48// ============================================================================
49// phase-456 W8 — one subscription registration, stated as one value
50// ============================================================================
51
52/// What a subscription registration STATES — phase-456 W8.
53///
54/// The thirteen `register_subscription_*` / `add_arena_subscription_*` entry
55/// points differ in their DELIVERY SHAPE (typed, raw, borrowed, with-info,
56/// validated) and used to differ in their LANGUAGE, and each re-derived the
57/// same prologue from positional parameters: node identity, topic info, the
58/// declared-depth check, the backend call. Twelve copies of it, and exactly
59/// ONE of them asked the backend whether it dispatches in place.
60///
61/// This is that prologue's argument, as one value. A struct rather than nine
62/// parameters because the fields are independently optional and a caller must
63/// be able to say "I state nothing here" without reordering a call — the same
64/// reason `DescriptorInputs` is a struct one layer up.
65///
66/// Two of its fields are the axes phase-456 W8 found under issue 1319's five
67/// rows: [`backend_hint`](Self::backend_hint) is "does this site know the
68/// type's bound", and [`in_place_capable`](Self::in_place_capable) is what
69/// lets `Executor::open_subscription` ask the third axis once, for every
70/// caller, in every language.
71pub(crate) struct SubscriptionRequest<'a> {
72    /// `None` is the legacy single-node path: identity comes from the
73    /// executor's own name and namespace and the session is slot 0.
74    pub(crate) node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
75    pub(crate) topic_name: &'a str,
76    pub(crate) type_name: &'a str,
77    pub(crate) type_hash: &'a str,
78    pub(crate) qos: QoSProfile,
79    /// Bytes the CALL SITE says it expects to receive, for the BACKEND's
80    /// payload size class (phase-231 / RFC-0038, phase-402 W2).
81    ///
82    /// `None` — and, for a C caller whose ABI spells it `0`, a zero — means
83    /// "this site stated nothing", which is a different claim from "zero
84    /// bytes": `with_rx_buffer_hint(0)` would be the second.
85    pub(crate) backend_hint: Option<usize>,
86    /// Bytes ONE receive slot claims from the arena, already derived by the
87    /// caller that has the type.
88    ///
89    /// Not the same number as [`Self::backend_hint`] — the typed Rust path
90    /// hints the type's bound and sizes the slot from
91    /// `default_subscription_rx_bytes`, which may differ — so both travel.
92    /// Ignored entirely when [`SubscriptionOpen::in_place`] comes back true.
93    pub(crate) slot_bytes: usize,
94    /// Can THIS delivery shape dispatch out of the backend's own receive slot?
95    ///
96    /// A property of the shape, not of the backend: `process_raw_in_place`
97    /// hands the callback borrowed BYTES and nothing else, so a shape that
98    /// must also deliver a wire attachment (`_info`), an integrity status
99    /// (`_validated` / `_safety`) or a `MessageInfo` cannot use it however
100    /// capable the backend is. Stated per call site so an omission is a line
101    /// someone wrote rather than a question nobody asked — which is exactly
102    /// what the C path was before W8.
103    pub(crate) in_place_capable: bool,
104}
105
106/// The result of `Executor::open_subscription`: a claimed slot, a live backend
107/// subscriber, and the ONE answer to the in-place question.
108pub(crate) struct SubscriptionOpen {
109    /// The claimed entry slot. Claimed BEFORE the fallible work, per
110    /// `Executor::emplace_entry`'s rule.
111    pub(crate) slot: usize,
112    pub(crate) handle: session::RmwSubscriber,
113    /// **The only place in this crate that
114    /// `Subscription::supports_process_in_place` is read.**
115    ///
116    /// Before phase-456 W8 the read lived inside
117    /// `register_subscription_buffered_on`, which is the Rust typed path and
118    /// only that: every C and C++ subscription on zenoh or XRCE therefore
119    /// allocated a receive region the backend does not need, at the same order
120    /// as issue 1340's ~9.7 KiB per subscription. The irony phase-456 W8
121    /// measured is that the C callback is the BETTER candidate —
122    /// `RawSubscriptionCallback` is already `(const uint8_t*, size_t, void*)`,
123    /// a borrowed-bytes signature, where the Rust typed path has to produce an
124    /// owned `&M` from somewhere.
125    pub(crate) in_place: bool,
126    /// [`SubscriptionRequest::slot_bytes`], carried through so a caller's arena
127    /// arithmetic reads ONE local rather than re-deriving it.
128    pub(crate) slot_bytes: usize,
129    /// The QoS the backend was actually given — phase-454 W13 through
130    /// phase-456 W8.
131    ///
132    /// NOT the caller's `req.qos`. `declared_qos::honour` REWRITES the depth
133    /// when the system declared one, and the twelve prologues this function
134    /// replaced each passed that rewritten value on to the entry they built.
135    /// Returning it is what keeps that true with one honouring site: a caller
136    /// that stored `req.qos` instead would size its entry from a depth the
137    /// backend never saw, and nothing would fail — the subscription would
138    /// simply hold a different number of samples than the build reserved for
139    /// it.
140    pub(crate) qos: QoSProfile,
141}

164// Executor::open() factory method

167/// phase-271 / phase-392 W6 — the `'static` `u64` backing the `alloc`
168/// convenience constructors borrow, sized to `sizing`.
169///
170/// **The named static first, the heap second.** phase-271 made this a
171/// `Box::leak`, and a leak has no symbol: `mem-report` reads an ELF's symbol
172/// table, so the largest single RAM consumer of every Rust image was the one
173/// thing the memory instrument could not see (RFC-0002 § 4.4b). It is served
174/// from `executor::backing::EXECUTOR_BACKING` now — same bytes, same
175/// executor-lifetime reservation, in `.bss` where the linker can print them and
176/// out of the allocator arena that used to pay for them.
177///
178/// The heap arm is still reached, and both cases are legitimate rather than
179/// degraded: a SECOND executor opened through an `alloc` convenience
180/// constructor, and an entry sized past the build-time default. A tiered boot's
181/// spawned tiers are NOT that second executor any more: they open over the
182/// entry's `TierExecutorBacking` slots (`open_with_session_slot`, issue 1571). Neither is an error, so neither
183/// warns — `report_arena_headroom` is where an over-provisioned executor gets
184/// told about itself, and a duplicate line here would just be noise.
185///
186/// `alloc`-only — no_std-no-alloc entries supply their own `static`/stack
187/// backing via `open_in` / `from_session_in`.
188#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
189fn default_backing(sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing) -> &'static mut [MaybeUninit<u64>] {
190    let words = sizing.u64_len();
191    match super::backing::take(words) {
192        Some(backing) => backing,
193        None => alloc::boxed::Box::leak(alloc::boxed::Box::new_uninit_slice(words)),
194    }
195}

197#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
198impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
199    /// phase-271 — open a new executor session over caller-supplied `backing`,
200    /// sized by `sizing` (per-entry sizing). The core, non-generic sized entry
201    /// point: the `alloc` [`open`](Self::open) convenience leaks a default
202    /// backing and delegates here, and the `nros::main!` macro emits a backing
203    /// sized to the entry's own entity count.
204    ///
205    /// Phase 115.M.4 — auto-registers the cffi vtable for whichever
206    /// backend the build was configured for, mirroring the C++ side's
207    /// `#ifdef NROS_RMW_<NAME>` fan-out in `<nros/node.hpp>`. The
208    /// runtime's atomic vtable slot is idempotent: a re-call of any
209    /// backend's `register()` is a no-op, so the fan-out below is safe
210    /// to invoke on every `Executor::open` (cheaper than a `Once` and
211    /// doesn't pull in `std::sync` for no_std targets).
212    ///
213    /// Connects to the middleware at the locator specified in `config`.
214    ///
215    /// # Safety
216    /// `backing` must be ≥ `sizing.u64_len()` words, live for `'s`, and be
217    /// otherwise untouched while the executor lives (see
218    /// [`from_session_in`](Self::from_session_in)).
219    pub unsafe fn open_in(
220        config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>,
221        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
222        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
223    ) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
224        use nros_rmw::Rmw;
225
226        // Phase 128.A.3 / 249 P4b.1 — manifest-driven backend selection.
227        //
228        // Every linked backend self-registered via its `.init_array`
229        // ctor before `main` (RFC-0042 §D3.3), so the registry is
230        // already populated — no runtime section walk.
231        //
232        // 1. Honour `config.rmw` — the caller's explicit backend selection,
233        //    mirroring ROS 2's `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION`. On a hosted build
234        //    `nros::ExecutorConfigEnvExt::from_env` / `nros::env::resolve_hosted`
235        //    fill it from `$NROS_RMW`; issue 0687 moved that read to the edge,
236        //    because reading a process environment is what kept `std` in this
237        //    crate and an RTOS image has no environment to read.
238        // 2. With no selector, pick the unique registered backend.
239        //    Zero registered → `NoBackend`; more than one →
240        //    `Ambiguous` (user must select one, or use
241        //    `Executor::open_multi`).
242        let selector = config.rmw;
243        match nros_rmw_cffi::resolve_backend(selector.map(str::as_bytes)) {
244            nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::Single(_) => {}
245            // Issue 0436 — these are SELECTION outcomes, not transport failures,
246            // and calling them `ConnectionFailed` actively misleads: a PX4 bridge
247            // that registered two backends reported "connection failed", which
248            // reads as a router/network problem and was chased as one. Nothing is
249            // connected at this point — the resolver has not chosen a backend yet.
250            //
251            // The variant still collapses into `NodeError::Transport` (the enum has
252            // no selection arm, and adding one is an ABI change across the C/C++
253            // seams), but `InvalidConfig` at least says "your configuration is
254            // unresolvable", and the std-gated line below names WHICH outcome.
255            other => {
256                {
257                    let why: &str = match other {
258                        nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::NoBackend => {
259                            "no RMW backend is registered"
260                        }
261                        nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::Ambiguous => {
262                            "more than one RMW backend is registered and no \
263                             $NROS_RMW selector was set — name one (e.g. \
264                             NROS_RMW=uorb), or open per-backend sessions"
265                        }
266                        nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::Unknown => {
267                            "$NROS_RMW names a backend that is not registered"
268                        }
269                        nros_rmw_cffi::BackendResolution::Single(_) => unreachable!(),
270                    };
271                    nros_log::log_error!(
272                        nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
273                        "cannot select an RMW backend — {why}"
274                    );
275                }
276                let _ = other;
277                return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::InvalidConfig));
278            }
279        }
280
281        let rmw_config = nros_rmw::RmwConfig {
282            locator: config.locator,
283            mode: config.mode,
284            domain_id: config.domain_id,
285            node_name: config.node_name,
286            namespace: config.namespace,
287            properties: &[],
288        };
289        let session = if let Some(name) = selector {
290            // Selector path: route to the specific named backend so
291            // the env-var-disambiguated outcome matches what the
292            // resolver above identified.
293            nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw::open_with_rmw(name, &rmw_config)
294        } else {
295            nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw.open(&rmw_config)
296        }
297        .map_err(|e| {
298            // Issue 0465 — do not relabel. This used to discard the backend's
299            // error and report `ConnectionFailed` for every open failure, so an
300            // exhausted session pool (`InvalidConfig`) and a router that is not
301            // there produced the same sentence. Same lesson as the selection
302            // arm above: say which failure happened.
303            nros_log::log_error!(
304                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
305                "RMW session open failed — {e:?}"
306            );
307            NodeError::Transport(e)
308        })?;
309        // SAFETY: forwarded from this fn's contract — `backing`/`sizing` sized
310        // + alive for `'s`.
311        let mut executor = unsafe { Self::from_session_in(session, backing, sizing) };
312        {
313            // `config.clock_us` overrides the constructor's platform default
314            // (issue: assigning `None` here clobbered it and re-enabled the
315            // credit-the-requested-timeout fallback).
316            if let Some(clock) = config.clock_us {
317                executor.clock_us_fn = Some(clock);
318                executor.last_spin_end_us = Some(clock());
319            }
320            // issue 0671 — the SAME rule as `clock_us` directly above, which is
321            // why that one is guarded: a config that does not SPECIFY an epoch
322            // must not be read as "this target HAS no epoch". Assigning `None`
323            // here clobbered the constructor's platform default
324            // (`Some(default_epoch_us)`), and `ExecutorConfig::new` — the path
325            // `nros::init_*` + `ctx.config()` takes — leaves `epoch_us: None`,
326            // so EVERY hosted node built that way silently lost its wall clock.
327            // With no epoch, `Node::subscription` never attaches the age cell
328            // (it needs `(STAMP_OFFSET, epoch)` both `Some`), so a baked
329            // `max_age_ms` contract becomes a silently-dead monitor — the exact
330            // outcome RFC-0052 says must never happen. The rate monitor rides
331            // the GUARDED `clock_us_fn` and kept working, which is why only the
332            // age half went quiet.
333            if let Some(epoch) = config.epoch_us {
334                executor.epoch_us_fn = Some(epoch);
335            }
336        }
337        executor.set_node_identity(config.node_name, config.namespace);
338        // Issue 0656 — beside the identity, for the same reason: an entity needs
339        // both to be addressable, and this half used to be dropped here.
340        executor.domain_id = config.domain_id;
341        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
342        executor.install_wake_signal_on_primary();
343        // Phase 277 W2.c — readiness marker for E2E harnesses. This is the
344        // single call-through `open()`/`open_sized()` share, so it fires on
345        // every platform that reaches here (native, freertos, zephyr,
346        // threadx, …) regardless of which RMW backend or board owns the
347        // boot path. It replaces the per-example synthetic
348        // `log::info!("Publishing messages")` markers W4 removes — those
349        // only proved a callback had fired at least once; this line proves
350        // the session itself is up, before any node/callback exists.
351        //
352        // STABILITY CONTRACT: the leading `"nros: session open"` text is
353        // load-bearing — test harnesses grep for it verbatim. Keep it
354        // stable even if the trailing `(rmw=...)` detail changes.
355        #[cfg(feature = "log")]
356        {
357            if let Some(name) = selector {
358                log::info!("nros: session open (rmw={name})");
359            } else {
360                log::info!("nros: session open");
361            }
362        }
363        Ok(executor)
364    }
365}

367#[cfg(all(feature = "rmw-cffi", feature = "alloc"))]
368impl Executor<'static> {
369    /// Open a new executor session using the active RMW backend, at the
370    /// build-time default sizing. Convenience over
371    /// [`open_in`](Self::open_in): leaks a default-sized backing (executor-
372    /// lifetime) so existing callers keep the zero-storage-arg signature.
373    /// Per-entry sizing goes through `open_in` / the `nros::main!` macro.
374    ///
375    /// # Example
376    ///
377    /// ```ignore
378    /// let config = ExecutorConfig::from_env().node_name("my_node");
379    /// let mut executor = Executor::open(&config)?;
380    /// ```
381    pub fn open(config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
382        Self::open_sized(config, super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT)
383    }
384
385    /// phase-271 — like [`open`](Self::open) but sized to a caller-supplied
386    /// `sizing` (its own declared topology) instead of the build-time default.
387    /// The `alloc` entry point the `nros::main!` macro's native board path uses
388    /// to size a fat entry (>default `MAX_CBS` callbacks) without a
389    /// workspace-global `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_CBS`. Leaks a `sizing`-sized backing
390    /// (executor-lifetime); no-alloc entries use `open_in` with their own static.
391    pub fn open_sized(
392        config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>,
393        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
394    ) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
395        // SAFETY: the backing is exactly `sizing.u64_len()` words, `'static`,
396        // uniquely owned by the returned executor.
397        unsafe { Self::open_in(config, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
398    }
399
400    /// Phase 128.F.1 — explicit per-backend session declaration for
401    /// bridge mode. `specs[0]` becomes the primary session; `specs[1..]`
402    /// open as extras keyed by RMW name. After construction, every
403    /// `create_node_on(name, rmw)` call dispatches to whichever
404    /// session was opened under that RMW name (or, when the rmw name
405    /// matches the primary, the primary session itself).
406    ///
407    /// Single-backend callers should keep using
408    /// [`open`](Self::open) — this entry costs an extra
409    /// `open_with_rmw` per spec and adds no value when only one
410    /// backend is linked.
411    ///
412    /// `$NROS_RMW` env is ignored: bridge mode wants explicit names.
413    ///
414    /// Default-sized `alloc` convenience over
415    /// [`open_multi_in`](Self::open_multi_in) (leaks a default backing).
416    #[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
417    pub fn open_multi(specs: &[SessionSpec<'_>]) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
418        let sizing = super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT;
419        // SAFETY: the backing is exactly `sizing.u64_len()` words, `'static`.
420        unsafe { Self::open_multi_in(specs, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
421    }
422
423    /// Phase 104.C.1 — open the Executor against a specific RMW
424    /// backend by name. Selects from the named registry (Phase
425    /// 104.B.2). `rmw_name` must match one of the names a backend
426    /// registered under (`"zenoh"`, `"cyclonedds"`, `"xrce"`, …).
427    ///
428    /// Equivalent to [`Executor::open`] when the registry has exactly
429    /// one backend (the default-backend fast path). Use this entry
430    /// point in multi-backend builds where `Executor::open` would
431    /// pick the first-registered slot.
432    ///
433    /// Single-Executor multi-Node multi-RMW (the long-term Design X
434    /// from `docs/roadmap/phase-104-multi-backend-bridges.md`) is
435    /// follow-up work — Phase 104.C.2 + C.3.
436    ///
437    /// Default-sized `alloc` convenience over
438    /// [`open_with_rmw_in`](Self::open_with_rmw_in) (leaks a default backing).
439    #[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
440    pub fn open_with_rmw(rmw_name: &str, config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
441        let sizing = super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT;
442        // SAFETY: the backing is exactly `sizing.u64_len()` words, `'static`.
443        unsafe { Self::open_with_rmw_in(rmw_name, config, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
444    }
445}
446
447// phase-271 — no-alloc sized cores for the bridge/named open paths. In
448// `impl<'s>` (not the `'static` alloc block) so they stay available in
449// `rmw-cffi`-without-`alloc` builds (e.g. the `nros-bridge` no_std default),
450// which is where `open_multi`/`open_with_rmw` lived before.
451#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
452impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
453    /// Per-entry-sized [`open_multi`](Self::open_multi): carves `backing` for
454    /// the executor's tables instead of leaking a default one.
455    ///
456    /// # Safety
457    /// `backing`/`sizing` as in [`from_session_in`](Self::from_session_in).
458    pub unsafe fn open_multi_in(
459        specs: &[SessionSpec<'_>],
460        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
461        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
462    ) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
463        // Phase 249 P4b.1 — backends self-registered via their
464        // `.init_array` ctor before `main`; no runtime section walk.
465        let primary = specs
466            .first()
467            .ok_or(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ConnectionFailed))?;
468        let primary_session =
469            nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw::open_with_rmw(primary.rmw, &primary.to_rmw_config())
470                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)?;
471        // SAFETY: forwarded from this fn's contract.
472        let mut executor = unsafe { Self::from_session_in(primary_session, backing, sizing) };
473        executor.set_node_identity("", "/");
474        // Phase 156 — see `Executor::open` for primary-identity
475        // recording rationale.
476        let _ = executor.primary_rmw_name.push_str(primary.rmw);
477        let _ = executor.primary_locator.push_str(primary.locator);
478        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
479        executor.install_wake_signal_on_primary();
480
481        for spec in specs.iter().skip(1) {
482            let session = nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw::open_with_rmw(spec.rmw, &spec.to_rmw_config())
483                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)?;
484            executor
485                .extra_sessions
486                .push(session)
487                .map_err(|_| NodeError::NodeTableFull)?;
488            // Issue 0436 — record WHICH backend/locator this extra is, so
489            // `NodeBuilder::rmw(name)` can find it instead of opening a second
490            // session against the same (singleton) backend.
491            {
492                let mut rmw_s = heapless::String::<32>::new();
493                let _ = rmw_s.push_str(spec.rmw);
494                let mut loc_s = heapless::String::<128>::new();
495                let _ = loc_s.push_str(spec.locator);
496                let _ = executor.extra_session_ids.push((rmw_s, loc_s));
497            }
498            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
499            {
500                let idx = executor.extra_sessions.len() - 1;
501                executor.install_wake_signal_on_extra(idx);
502            }
503        }
504
505        Ok(executor)
506    }
507
508    /// Per-entry-sized [`open_with_rmw`](Self::open_with_rmw): carves `backing`
509    /// for the executor's tables instead of leaking a default one.
510    ///
511    /// # Safety
512    /// `backing`/`sizing` as in [`from_session_in`](Self::from_session_in).
513    pub unsafe fn open_with_rmw_in(
514        rmw_name: &str,
515        config: &ExecutorConfig<'_>,
516        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
517        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
518    ) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
519        if !nros_rmw_cffi::backend_registered() {
520            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ConnectionFailed));
521        }
522
523        let rmw_config = nros_rmw::RmwConfig {
524            locator: config.locator,
525            mode: config.mode,
526            domain_id: config.domain_id,
527            node_name: config.node_name,
528            namespace: config.namespace,
529            properties: &[],
530        };
531        let session = nros_rmw_cffi::CffiRmw::open_with_rmw(rmw_name, &rmw_config)
532            .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ConnectionFailed))?;
533        // SAFETY: forwarded from this fn's contract.
534        let mut executor = unsafe { Self::from_session_in(session, backing, sizing) };
535        {
536            // `config.clock_us` overrides the constructor's platform default
537            // (issue: assigning `None` here clobbered it and re-enabled the
538            // credit-the-requested-timeout fallback).
539            if let Some(clock) = config.clock_us {
540                executor.clock_us_fn = Some(clock);
541                executor.last_spin_end_us = Some(clock());
542            }
543            // issue 0671 — the SAME rule as `clock_us` directly above, which is
544            // why that one is guarded: a config that does not SPECIFY an epoch
545            // must not be read as "this target HAS no epoch". Assigning `None`
546            // here clobbered the constructor's platform default
547            // (`Some(default_epoch_us)`), and `ExecutorConfig::new` — the path
548            // `nros::init_*` + `ctx.config()` takes — leaves `epoch_us: None`,
549            // so EVERY hosted node built that way silently lost its wall clock.
550            // With no epoch, `Node::subscription` never attaches the age cell
551            // (it needs `(STAMP_OFFSET, epoch)` both `Some`), so a baked
552            // `max_age_ms` contract becomes a silently-dead monitor — the exact
553            // outcome RFC-0052 says must never happen. The rate monitor rides
554            // the GUARDED `clock_us_fn` and kept working, which is why only the
555            // age half went quiet.
556            if let Some(epoch) = config.epoch_us {
557                executor.epoch_us_fn = Some(epoch);
558            }
559        }
560        executor.set_node_identity(config.node_name, config.namespace);
561        // Phase 156 — record primary identity for the session-
562        // cache hit path. See `Executor::open` for the rationale.
563        let _ = executor.primary_rmw_name.push_str(rmw_name);
564        let _ = executor.primary_locator.push_str(config.locator);
565        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
566        executor.install_wake_signal_on_primary();
567        Ok(executor)
568    }
569}

571/// Phase 128.F.1 — per-backend session declaration for
572/// [`Executor::open_multi`]. Each spec names an RMW backend (must
573/// match one a backend registered under via
574/// `nros_rmw_cffi_register_named` / the `RMW_INIT_ENTRIES` linker
575/// section) and the locator + domain id to open against it.
576#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
577#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
578pub struct SessionSpec<'cfg> {
579    pub rmw: &'cfg str,
580    pub locator: &'cfg str,
581    pub domain_id: u32,
582    pub node_name: &'cfg str,
583    pub namespace: &'cfg str,
584}
585
586#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
587impl<'cfg> SessionSpec<'cfg> {
588    /// Minimal spec — just RMW name + locator. Domain id defaults to
589    /// 0; node name and namespace are empty.
590    pub const fn new(rmw: &'cfg str, locator: &'cfg str) -> Self {
591        Self {
592            rmw,
593            locator,
594            domain_id: 0,
595            node_name: "",
596            namespace: "",
597        }
598    }
599
600    pub const fn domain_id(mut self, domain_id: u32) -> Self {
601        self.domain_id = domain_id;
602        self
603    }
604
605    pub const fn node_name(mut self, name: &'cfg str) -> Self {
606        self.node_name = name;
607        self
608    }
609
610    pub const fn namespace(mut self, ns: &'cfg str) -> Self {
611        self.namespace = ns;
612        self
613    }
614
615    fn to_rmw_config(self) -> nros_rmw::RmwConfig<'cfg> {
616        nros_rmw::RmwConfig {
617            locator: self.locator,
618            mode: nros_rmw::SessionMode::Client,
619            domain_id: self.domain_id,
620            node_name: self.node_name,
621            namespace: self.namespace,
622            properties: &[],
623        }
624    }
625}
626
627// Phase 128.A.3 — selector for the single-backend resolution path.
628//
629// On hosted (`std`) builds, read `$NROS_RMW`; mirrors ROS 2's
630// `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION`. Returns the name as a byte vector so the
631// caller can pass it to `nros_rmw_cffi::resolve_backend` and (when
632// `Some`) to `CffiRmw::open_with_rmw`.
633//
634// On `no_std` / bare-metal builds, environment variables are not
635// available; resolution always falls through to the single-backend
636// or ambiguous path. Embedded users with multiple backends use the
637// bridge surface `Executor::open_multi` instead.
638// phase-359 W10 / issue 0687 — the private reader that stood here is gone, and
639// so is the shared one that briefly replaced it. `ExecutorConfig::rmw` carries
640// the selection instead: `nros::rmw_selector` reads the variable ONCE, at the
641// hosted edge, and every consumer takes the value.
642
643// ============================================================================
644// SessionStore — owned or borrowed session
645// ============================================================================
646
647/// Session storage: owned or borrowed via raw pointer.
648///
649/// The C API creates a session in `nros_support_init()` before the
650/// executor. `Borrowed` lets the executor use that session without owning it.
651#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]
652pub(crate) enum SessionStore {
653    Owned(session::ConcreteSession),
654    Borrowed(*mut session::ConcreteSession),
655}
656
657impl core::ops::Deref for SessionStore {
658    type Target = session::ConcreteSession;
659    fn deref(&self) -> &session::ConcreteSession {
660        match self {
661            SessionStore::Owned(s) => s,
662            SessionStore::Borrowed(ptr) => unsafe { &**ptr },
663        }
664    }
665}
666
667impl core::ops::DerefMut for SessionStore {
668    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut session::ConcreteSession {
669        match self {
670            SessionStore::Owned(s) => s,
671            SessionStore::Borrowed(ptr) => unsafe { &mut **ptr },
672        }
673    }
674}
675
676/// Phase 228.E — an opaque, `Send` handle to an [`Executor`]'s RMW session.
677///
678/// In the per-tier model the boot executor opens the one session and hands each
679/// spawned tier task a handle (not a borrow) so the task opens its own
680/// [`Executor`] over that *same* session across the RTOS task boundary. Wrapping
681/// the `pub(crate)` session pointer lets board crates (`nros-board-linux`,
682/// `nros-board-freertos`, …) name + move the handle without naming the session
683/// type. Obtain via [`Executor::session_handle`]; consume via
684/// [`Executor::open_with_session_handle`].
685#[cfg(any(has_rmw, test))]
686pub struct SessionHandle(*mut session::ConcreteSession);
687
688// SAFETY: the per-tier model deliberately shares one session across RTOS tasks;
689// concurrent access is serialized by the RMW backend's internal locks (the RTOS
690// targets build zenoh-pico `Z_FEATURE_MULTI_THREAD=1` — RFC-0032 §5.0). The
691// boot executor owns the session and outlives every tier task.
692#[cfg(any(has_rmw, test))]
693unsafe impl Send for SessionHandle {}
694
695#[cfg(any(has_rmw, test))]
696impl SessionHandle {
697    /// Phase 274.W1 — convert to an opaque `*mut c_void` for C/C++ FFI.
698    ///
699    /// The returned pointer encodes the session address and is valid as long as
700    /// the owning executor lives. Reconstruct via [`Self::from_raw`].
701    pub fn into_raw(self) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
702        self.0 as *mut core::ffi::c_void
703    }
704
705    /// Phase 274.W1 — reconstruct a `SessionHandle` from an opaque pointer
706    /// returned by [`Self::into_raw`].
707    ///
708    /// # Safety
709    /// `ptr` must be a pointer obtained from `into_raw()` on a `SessionHandle`
710    /// whose underlying session is still live and owned by its original executor.
711    pub unsafe fn from_raw(ptr: *mut core::ffi::c_void) -> Self {
712        Self(ptr as *mut session::ConcreteSession)
713    }
714}
715
716/// Phase 228.C — pure callback-group filter decision. `None` = wildcard (accept
717/// every group); `Some` = accept only listed groups. Backs
718/// [`Executor::group_active`]; split out so the logic is unit-testable without a
719/// live session.
720pub(crate) fn group_filter_accepts(
721    active: Option<&[super::storage::ActiveGroup]>,
722    node: u64,
723    group: &str,
724) -> bool {
725    match active {
726        None => true,
727        Some(v) => v.iter().any(|(n, g)| *n == node && g.as_str() == group),
728    }
729}

731/// Bytes the parameter store asks the platform heap for, in ONE allocation.
732///
733/// Issue 1706 -- the size of THIS build's store, which folds every knob that
734/// shapes it (`MAX_PARAMETERS`, which a contract's `params:` derives, and the
735/// board's string/array capacities). No formula and no measured constant: the
736/// compiler's own answer, so the number reported below cannot drift from the
737/// allocation it describes.
738#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
739pub const PARAMETER_STORE_BYTES: usize = core::mem::size_of::<nros_params::ParameterStorage>();
740
741/// Issue 1706 -- a TEST seam standing in for a platform heap that returns NULL
742/// for the store's request, on the current thread only (tests run in
743/// parallel). Not a test `#[global_allocator]`: `check-feature-contract`
744/// clause (e) allows exactly one, `nros-platform`'s.
745#[cfg(all(test, feature = "std", feature = "param-services"))]
746pub(crate) struct RefuseParameterStore;
747
748#[cfg(all(test, feature = "std", feature = "param-services"))]
749std::thread_local! {
750    static REFUSE_PARAMETER_STORE: core::cell::Cell<bool> = const { core::cell::Cell::new(false) };
751}
752
753#[cfg(all(test, feature = "std", feature = "param-services"))]
754impl RefuseParameterStore {
755    pub(crate) fn arm() -> Self {
756        REFUSE_PARAMETER_STORE.with(|c| c.set(true));
757        Self
758    }
759
760    fn armed() -> bool {
761        REFUSE_PARAMETER_STORE.with(core::cell::Cell::get)
762    }
763}
764
765#[cfg(all(test, feature = "std", feature = "param-services"))]
766impl Drop for RefuseParameterStore {
767    fn drop(&mut self) {
768        REFUSE_PARAMETER_STORE.with(|c| c.set(false));
769    }
770}
771
772/// Issue 1706 -- say, once, that the parameter store did not fit.
773///
774/// The RFC-0100 D11 shape, one layer up from Cyclone's boot check: the
775/// failure is named where it is decided, with the number a reader needs to
776/// size the heap, instead of surfacing as an anonymous halt in the allocator.
777/// What it can name is the REQUEST; the heap's own report (Zephyr's `HEAP
778/// EXHAUSTED` line, the board's `nros: heap peak` line) carries the capacity.
779#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
780#[cold]
781fn report_parameter_store_refused() {
782    let slots = nros_params::MAX_PARAMETERS;
783    // THREE short lines, not one sentence: a log backend truncates a long
784    // line (Zephyr's cut the first draft at its slot count), and the number
785    // is the one part that must survive.
786    let logger = nros_log::get_logger("nros");
787    nros_log::log_error!(
788        logger,
789        "parameter store refused: needs {} bytes in one allocation ({} slots x {})",
790        PARAMETER_STORE_BYTES,
791        slots,
792        PARAMETER_STORE_BYTES / if slots == 0 { 1 } else { slots }
793    );
794    nros_log::log_error!(
795        logger,
796        "every parameter declaration on this executor is refused (issue 1706)"
797    );
798    // phase-382 W3' -- the remedy that takes the store OUT of the heap comes
799    // first: a build that knows the image builds a store carves it from the
800    // executor backing instead (`nros_params::IMPLIED_STORE_SLOTS`).
801    nros_log::log_error!(
802        logger,
803        "declare the parameters in the contract (params:) or state NROS_PARAM_STORE=1"
804    );
805    nros_log::log_error!(
806        logger,
807        "and the store is carved from the executor backing; or raise the image heap"
808    );
809}
810
811/// `text` typed as `declared`'s type — phase-482 W5. `None` when it does not
812/// parse as that type, or the type takes no override yet (arrays).
813///
814/// A `NotSet` declaration has no type to follow, so the text decides: `true` /
815/// `false`, then an integer, then a double, then a string — the order rcl's
816/// YAML reading gives an unquoted scalar.
817#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
818fn typed_param_override(
819    text: &str,
820    declared: &nros_params::ParameterValue,
821) -> Option<nros_params::ParameterValue> {
822    use nros_params::ParameterValue as V;
823    let boolean = |t: &str| match t {
824        "true" | "True" | "TRUE" => Some(true),
825        "false" | "False" | "FALSE" => Some(false),
826        _ => None,
827    };
828    let string = |t: &str| heapless::String::try_from(t).ok().map(V::String);
829    match declared {
830        V::Bool(_) => boolean(text).map(V::Bool),
831        V::Integer(_) => text.parse::<i64>().ok().map(V::Integer),
832        V::Double(_) => text.parse::<f64>().ok().map(V::Double),
833        V::String(_) => string(text),
834        V::NotSet => boolean(text)
835            .map(V::Bool)
836            .or_else(|| text.parse::<i64>().ok().map(V::Integer))
837            .or_else(|| text.parse::<f64>().ok().map(V::Double))
838            .or_else(|| string(text)),
839        _ => None,
840    }
841}

843#[cfg(test)]
844mod group_filter_tests {
845    use super::group_filter_accepts;
846    use crate::executor::storage::{ActiveGroup, node_identity_hash};
847
848    type Group = heapless::String<32>;
849
850    fn entry(node: &str, ns: &str, g: &str) -> ActiveGroup {
851        let mut s = Group::new();
852        s.push_str(g).unwrap();
853        (node_identity_hash(node, ns), s)
854    }
855
856    #[test]
857    fn wildcard_accepts_all() {
858        assert!(group_filter_accepts(
859            None,
860            node_identity_hash("n", "/"),
861            "anything"
862        ));
863    }
864
865    #[test]
866    fn set_accepts_only_listed_groups() {
867        let active = [entry("n", "/", "ctrl")];
868        let n = node_identity_hash("n", "/");
869        assert!(group_filter_accepts(Some(&active[..]), n, "ctrl"));
870        assert!(!group_filter_accepts(Some(&active[..]), n, "telem"));
871    }
872
873    /// issue 1172 — the SAME group id on a DIFFERENT node is not this tier's.
874    ///
875    /// This is the case the whole change exists for: two nodes may legitimately
876    /// declare `ctrl`, pinned to different tiers, and the old filter — keyed on
877    /// the group name alone — admitted both onto whichever tier asked first.
878    #[test]
879    fn the_same_group_on_another_node_is_not_accepted() {
880        let active = [entry("talker", "/", "ctrl")];
881        assert!(group_filter_accepts(
882            Some(&active[..]),
883            node_identity_hash("talker", "/"),
884            "ctrl"
885        ));
886        assert!(
887            !group_filter_accepts(
888                Some(&active[..]),
889                node_identity_hash("listener", "/"),
890                "ctrl"
891            ),
892            "another node's identically-named group must NOT be admitted"
893        );
894    }
895
896    /// The namespace is part of the identity, not decoration: two nodes may
897    /// share a bare name under different namespaces, which is legal in ROS.
898    #[test]
899    fn the_same_name_under_another_namespace_is_a_different_node() {
900        let active = [entry("talker", "/left", "ctrl")];
901        assert!(!group_filter_accepts(
902            Some(&active[..]),
903            node_identity_hash("talker", "/right"),
904            "ctrl"
905        ));
906    }
907
908    /// An empty namespace and `/` are the SAME node. Both ends normalise, and
909    /// if only one did, a filter would never match what it named.
910    #[test]
911    fn an_empty_namespace_normalises_to_root() {
912        assert_eq!(
913            node_identity_hash("talker", ""),
914            node_identity_hash("talker", "/")
915        );
916    }
917
918    /// The separator is load-bearing: without it `("ab","c")` and `("a","bc")`
919    /// would hash alike, and a node name may contain any namespace character.
920    #[test]
921    fn the_name_namespace_split_cannot_be_forged() {
922        assert_ne!(
923            node_identity_hash("ab", "/c"),
924            node_identity_hash("a", "b/c")
925        );
926    }
927
928    /// phase-409 — the wildcard and an EMPTY filter are different answers, and
929    /// the carved table cannot tell them apart on its own (the old
930    /// `Option<Vec>` could). `Executor::active_groups_filtering` is what keeps
931    /// them apart; this pins the distinction at the decision itself.
932    #[test]
933    fn an_empty_filter_is_not_the_wildcard() {
934        let empty: [ActiveGroup; 0] = [];
935        let n = node_identity_hash("n", "/");
936        assert!(!group_filter_accepts(Some(&empty[..]), n, "anything"));
937        assert!(group_filter_accepts(None, n, "anything"));
938    }
939}

941// ============================================================================
942// Executor
943// ============================================================================
944
945/// Backend-agnostic executor that owns a session.
946///
947/// Provides `create_node()` for entity creation and `drive_io()` for polling.
948///
949/// # Callback Mode
950///
951/// The executor supports arena-based callback registration via the
952/// `node_mut(id).subscription(t)` builder and
953/// [`register_service()`](Self::register_service), with dispatch via
954/// [`spin_once()`](Self::spin_once). No heap allocation is needed.
955///
956/// The sizes are set via `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_CBS` (default 4) and
957/// `NROS_EXECUTOR_ARENA_SIZE` (default 4096) environment variables at build time.
958///
959/// Phase 124.B.2 — opaque context handed to the runtime wake
960/// callback. Backends store the raw pointer + invoke the callback;
961/// the callback decodes back to `&WakeCtx`.
962#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
963pub(crate) struct WakeCtx {
964    pub(crate) flag: portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool>,
965    /// The wake primitive. Phase 130.3 added it beside a `std::sync::Condvar`
966    /// pair and noted that "a future migration to a single primitive flips one
967    /// branch instead of two"; phase-359 W10 is that migration, and this is the
968    /// one that survived.
969    pub(crate) node_wake: Option<portable_atomic_util::Arc<super::node_wake::NodeWake>>,
970}
971
972/// Phase 124.B.2 — runtime wake callback.
973///
974/// RT-context contract:
975///
976/// * **Thread-safe**: callable from any thread. The cb is lock-free
977///   on the cv path — no mutex held during `notify_all`. Lost-wakeup
978///   is prevented by the waiter checking `wake_flag` under
979///   `wake_mu` via the `wait_timeout_while` predicate.
980/// * **NOT async-signal-safe on POSIX**: `pthread_cond_signal`
981///   isn't on the POSIX async-signal-safe function list. For POSIX
982///   signal handler wake, use a `signalfd` + select pattern in a
983///   thread that owns the wake duty — that pattern is Linux-only
984///   (`signalfd`/`eventfd` are Linux syscalls, not POSIX), which is
985///   why the `WakeSignalFd` worker is gated `target_os = "linux"`.
986/// * **RTOS ISR**: per-RTOS platform layer wraps the cv with an
987///   ISR-safe primitive (`xSemaphoreGiveFromISR`,
988///   `tx_event_flags_set` from ISR, `k_sem_give` from ISR on
989///   Zephyr). Backend's ISR caller routes through the platform's
990///   `signal_from_isr` API instead of this cb directly.
991/// * **Bounded execution time**: O(1) — atomic store + cv notify.
992///   No allocation, no contended lock.
993///
994/// The cb is the symbol backends invoke from their async wake path
995/// (datagram arrival, worker-thread enqueue, etc.). It does
996/// flag-write + condvar-signal in that order, lock-free.
997#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
998pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb(ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void) {
999    if ctx.is_null() {
1000        return;
1001    }
1002    // Phase 141.B.2 — capture T0 at cb entry. No-op when the
1003    // probe feature is off or no cycle reader is installed.
1004    #[cfg(feature = "wake-latency-probe")]
1005    super::wake_probe::on_wake();
1006    // SAFETY: ctx points at a `WakeCtx` owned by an Executor still
1007    // alive at the time of the call. `Executor::clear_wake_signal`
1008    // discharges that obligation — `set_wake_callback(None, _)` on the
1009    // primary and every extra session — from `Executor::close` (before
1010    // the session closes) and from the end of `Executor::drop` (before
1011    // `wake_ctx` is dropped). Issue 1385: until then this comment named
1012    // an "`install_wake_*` teardown path" that did not exist, and
1013    // `set_wake_callback(None` occurred nowhere in the tree but here.
1014    let wake = unsafe { &*(ctx as *const WakeCtx) };
1015    // Lock-free: the `flag` store is SeqCst and therefore happens-before any
1016    // subsequent acquire in the waiter, so a wake cannot be missed even though
1017    // nothing is held here.
1018    wake.flag.store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
1019    // phase-359 W10 — ONE primitive. This used to signal both a
1020    // `std::sync::Condvar` and (since phase 130.3) the `NodeWake`, "so the cb
1021    // keeps working whichever wait primitive spin_once is using". `spin_once`
1022    // now has only one, so this has only one to signal.
1023    if let Some(nw) = wake.node_wake.as_ref() {
1024        nw.signal();
1025    }
1026}
1027
1028/// phase-467 Row 8 — the symbol a backend invokes when the ROS GRAPH changes.
1029///
1030/// `rmw_event_callback_t`'s shape, so it fits the ABI slot unchanged:
1031/// `user_data` plus a coalesced count, and no payload. The count is IGNORED on
1032/// purpose — a guard condition is a level, not a queue, so N changes observed
1033/// before the executor spins are one dispatch. That is the same collapse
1034/// `guard_try_process` already performs on a flag several `trigger()`s set.
1035///
1036/// RT-context contract: identical to [`nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`] and for the
1037/// same reason — a relaxed-store-plus-wake, O(1), no allocation, no lock. Both
1038/// are called from a transport or worker thread.
1039///
1040/// # Safety
1041///
1042/// `user_data` must be the pointer `Executor::install_graph_change_guard`
1043/// passed: a `GuardCondition` in a box that executor owns. The obligation is
1044/// discharged by `clear_graph_change_signal`, which retires the pointer from
1045/// the backend BEFORE the box is freed, from `close()` and from `drop`. Issue
1046/// 1385 is what the other ordering costs.
1047#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
1048pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn nros_rmw_runtime_graph_change_cb(
1049    user_data: *const core::ffi::c_void,
1050    _count: usize,
1051) {
1052    if user_data.is_null() {
1053        return;
1054    }
1055    // SAFETY: see this function's `# Safety`.
1056    let guard = unsafe { &*(user_data as *const GuardCondition) };
1057    guard.trigger();
1058}
1059
1060/// Phase 124.B.7.c — Linux signalfd worker.
1061///
1062/// Owns a Linux `eventfd` plus a worker task that `read()`s the
1063/// fd and forwards it as a wake. The eventfd
1064/// write side is async-signal-safe per the kernel contract
1065/// (`write(2)` to an eventfd is permitted from signal handlers),
1066/// closing the gap that `pthread_cond_signal` leaves open on POSIX.
1067///
1068/// Lifecycle:
1069///   * Constructed lazily in `Executor::signal_fd()` on first
1070///     caller request.
1071///   * `Drop` writes a shutdown sentinel + joins the worker.
1072///
1073/// Caller flow (signal handler):
1074///   1. Get fd via `Executor::signal_fd()` before installing the
1075///      handler.
1076///   2. Handler does `eventfd_write(fd, 1)` (equivalently,
1077///      `write(fd, &1u64, 8)`).
1078///   3. Worker thread reads the fd, signals wake_cv. spin_once
1079///      blocked in cv.wait_timeout_while sees flag=true and exits.
1080///
1081/// phase-359 W10 — the worker is a PLATFORM TASK, not a `std::thread`, and it
1082/// forwards through the same [`NodeWake`](super::node_wake::NodeWake) the
1083/// runtime wake callback uses rather than a `std::sync::Condvar`. The eventfd
1084/// itself is still Linux — that is what makes the write async-signal-safe — so
1085/// this stays `target_os = "linux"`; what it no longer is, is std-only.
1086#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1087pub struct WakeSignalFd {
1088    fd: core::ffi::c_int,
1089    ctx: portable_atomic_util::Arc<SignalFdCtx>,
1090    task: Option<nros_platform_api::task::PlatformTask>,
1091}
1092
1093/// What the signalfd worker task needs, reachable through one pointer.
1094#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1095struct SignalFdCtx {
1096    fd: core::ffi::c_int,
1097    shutdown: portable_atomic::AtomicBool,
1098    /// The executor's wake state — the same `WakeCtx` the runtime callback
1099    /// decodes, reached as an address so the context is plainly `Send`.
1100    wake_ctx: usize,
1101}
1102
1103/// Worker entry: read the eventfd, forward as a wake, until shut down.
1104///
1105/// # Safety
1106/// `arg` must point at a live [`SignalFdCtx`] whose `wake_ctx` addresses a
1107/// `WakeCtx` that outlives this task.
1108#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1109unsafe extern "C" fn signal_fd_worker(arg: *mut core::ffi::c_void) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
1110    // SAFETY: the spawn site passes `Arc::as_ptr` of a ctx it keeps alive until
1111    // after the join in `Drop`.
1112    let ctx = unsafe { &*(arg as *const SignalFdCtx) };
1113    loop {
1114        let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
1115        // SAFETY: reading 8 bytes from an eventfd into an 8-byte buffer.
1116        let n = unsafe { libc::read(ctx.fd, buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut core::ffi::c_void, 8) };
1117        if ctx.shutdown.load(portable_atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
1118            return core::ptr::null_mut();
1119        }
1120        if n <= 0 {
1121            // EINTR / EOF — shutdown was re-checked above, so loop.
1122            continue;
1123        }
1124        // Same effect as `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`, reached directly because
1125        // the shutdown check above plus `Drop`'s join is what guarantees the
1126        // `WakeCtx` is still alive.
1127        // SAFETY: `wake_ctx` addresses the executor's `WakeCtx`, which outlives
1128        // this task by that same guarantee.
1129        unsafe {
1130            let w = &*(ctx.wake_ctx as *const WakeCtx);
1131            w.flag.store(true, portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
1132            if let Some(wake) = w.node_wake.as_ref() {
1133                wake.signal();
1134            }
1135        }
1136    }
1137}
1138
1139#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1140impl WakeSignalFd {
1141    /// Spawn the worker. `wake_ctx_ptr` is the `*const WakeCtx`
1142    /// produced by `Executor::wake_ctx_ptr` — same value the
1143    /// runtime wake cb decodes.
1144    ///
1145    /// phase-359 W10 — returns `NodeError` rather than `std::io::Error`. The
1146    /// only caller is `Executor::signal_fd`, and the errno detail it used to
1147    /// carry had no consumer: the one failure a caller can act on is "this
1148    /// platform would not give me the worker", which is what
1149    /// `NotInitialized` says — the eventfd and the task are both subsystems
1150    /// this capability requires and neither is guaranteed.
1151    fn new(wake_ctx_ptr: *const WakeCtx) -> Result<Self, NodeError> {
1152        // SAFETY: `eventfd(2)` with a valid flag; returns -1 on failure.
1153        let fd = unsafe { libc::eventfd(0, libc::EFD_CLOEXEC) };
1154        if fd < 0 {
1155            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
1156        }
1157        let ctx = portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(SignalFdCtx {
1158            fd,
1159            shutdown: portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
1160            wake_ctx: wake_ctx_ptr as usize,
1161        });
1162        let arg = portable_atomic_util::Arc::as_ptr(&ctx) as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
1163        // SAFETY: `arg` points at a ctx this struct owns and keeps alive until
1164        // after the join in `Drop`.
1165        let Some(task) = (unsafe {
1166            nros_platform_api::task::PlatformTask::spawn(
1167                signal_fd_worker,
1168                arg,
1169                // A read(2) loop and one atomic store — the smallest stack any
1170                // port will honour is plenty.
1171                8192,
1172                c"nros-wakefd".as_ptr(),
1173            )
1174        }) else {
1175            // SAFETY: nothing else holds the fd — the task never started.
1176            unsafe { libc::close(fd) };
1177            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
1178        };
1179        Ok(Self {
1180            fd,
1181            ctx,
1182            task: Some(task),
1183        })
1184    }
1185
1186    /// Returns the writable eventfd. The caller (typically a POSIX
1187    /// signal handler) writes any non-zero 8-byte value to trigger
1188    /// a wake. `write(2)` on an eventfd is async-signal-safe per
1189    /// `eventfd(2)` man page.
1190    pub fn fd(&self) -> core::ffi::c_int {
1191        self.fd
1192    }
1193}
1194
1195#[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
1196impl Drop for WakeSignalFd {
1197    fn drop(&mut self) {
1198        self.ctx
1199            .shutdown
1200            .store(true, portable_atomic::Ordering::Release);
1201        // Wake the worker so it re-checks shutdown: it is blocked in `read`,
1202        // which only this write can release.
1203        let one: u64 = 1;
1204        // SAFETY: an 8-byte write to our own eventfd.
1205        unsafe {
1206            libc::write(self.fd, &one as *const u64 as *const core::ffi::c_void, 8);
1207        }
1208        if let Some(task) = self.task.take() {
1209            task.join();
1210        }
1211        // SAFETY: the worker has exited, so nothing else touches the fd.
1212        unsafe { libc::close(self.fd) };
1213    }
1214}
1215
1216/// Phase 124.B.7.b — ISR / interrupt-context wake callback.
1217///
1218/// Same semantics as [`nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`] but constrained to
1219/// async-signal-safe / ISR-safe primitives.
1220///
1221/// Per-platform routing:
1222///
1223/// * **POSIX (std)**: `pthread_cond_signal` is NOT on the POSIX
1224///   async-signal-safe function list. Calling from a SIGUSR1
1225///   handler is technically UB. Real fix (Phase 124.B.7.c) routes
1226///   via `signalfd`/`eventfd` + a runtime worker thread — Linux
1227///   only, since neither syscall is POSIX; until that lands,
1228///   signal-handler callers MUST use
1229///   `nros_guard_condition_trigger` from a **separate thread** (not
1230///   from the handler itself), OR set the wake_flag and rely on
1231///   the next poll deadline. This cb currently aliases the regular
1232///   `wake_cb` and is safe only from non-signal-handler ISR-like
1233///   contexts (e.g. timer thread, kernel callback).
1234///
1235/// * **RTOS no_std (Zephyr/FreeRTOS/ThreadX)**: routes through the
1236///   platform-cffi `condvar_signal_from_isr` slot. Each backend
1237///   uses its ISR-safe variant — `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR`,
1238///   `tx_semaphore_put`, `k_condvar_signal`.
1239///
1240/// `ctx` semantics identical to [`nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`].
1241#[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
1242#[allow(dead_code)] // Public exposure pending B.7.c signalfd worker.
1243pub(crate) unsafe extern "C" fn nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb_from_isr(ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void) {
1244    // Today: alias regular wake_cb. POSIX signal-handler safety
1245    // pending B.7.c (signalfd worker-thread forward). Documented in
1246    // the contract above so callers know the boundary.
1247    unsafe { nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb(ctx) };
1248}

1250/// Phase 216 follow-up — per-Node dispatch trampoline registered with
1251/// [`Executor::register_dispatch_slot`].
1252///
1253/// The board-side dispatch task (RTIC `__nros_run` / Embassy
1254/// `__nros_run_task`) dequeues a `nros_platform::SignaledCallback`
1255/// envelope and forwards `(cb_id, ctx_ptr)` into
1256/// [`Executor::dispatch_callback`]; that method linear-scans this
1257/// slot table and invokes every registered `on_callback` with the
1258/// owning Node's per-Node `state` blob. Each Node's
1259/// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` self-filters on its own
1260/// `CallbackId` tag set, so a slot whose Node doesn't own this
1261/// callback is a cheap no-op string compare.
1262///
1263/// The shape mirrors the per-pkg `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback`
1264/// extern "C" trampoline emitted by the `nros::node!()` macro
1265/// (see `packages/core/nros-macros/src/lib.rs` Phase 216.A.5).
1266///
1267/// # Why not `linkme`
1268///
1269/// `linkme::distributed_slice` hangs on bare-metal Cortex-M /
1270/// RISC-V because `cortex_m_rt`'s link script doesn't provide the
1271/// `__start_/__stop_` section anchors in a shape that lets the
1272/// iterator terminate (see
1273/// `packages/rmw/cffi/src/section.rs` Phase 142). Since
1274/// stm32f4 RTIC / Embassy boards are the whole point of Phase 216,
1275/// the registry uses the explicit `register()` pattern from Phase
1276/// 104.A.
1277#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
1278pub struct DispatchSlot {
1279    /// Owning Node's `State` blob — produced by the macro-emitted
1280    /// `i()` and round-tripped through
1281    /// `nros::__private_node_state_into_raw`. Opaque to the
1282    /// executor.
1283    pub state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
1284    /// Per-Node `extern "C"` trampoline; signature matches the
1285    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` symbol the `nros::node!()`
1286    /// macro emits.
1287    pub on_callback: unsafe extern "C" fn(
1288        state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
1289        cb_id_ptr: *const u8,
1290        cb_id_len: usize,
1291        ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
1292    ),
1293}
1294
1295// SAFETY: `DispatchSlot` carries two raw pointers (`state` + an
1296// extern "C" fn pointer). The fn pointer is `Send`/`Sync` by
1297// definition; the `state` pointer's `Send`/`Sync` story matches the
1298// owning `Executor` (which is `unsafe impl Send`). Treating the
1299// slot itself as `Send` keeps the existing `Executor` Send impl
1300// intact — see `unsafe impl Send for Executor {}` later in this
1301// file.
1302unsafe impl Send for DispatchSlot {}
1303unsafe impl Sync for DispatchSlot {}
1304
1305/// Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — executor-owned component tick slot.
1306///
1307/// The layering-clean half of the W0-B `install` seam's tick fix
1308/// (phase-257 D2). A `nros`-layer `install`/`register_node_borrowed`
1309/// builds an `Arc<ComponentCell>` (the typed/poll-driven component
1310/// state) and enrolls it here via [`Executor::enroll_component`]; the
1311/// executor then drives `tick` on every enrolled slot at the tail of
1312/// each [`spin_once`](Executor::spin_once) — so `install`'d nodes
1313/// (C, C++, **and Rust owned-spin**) tick, closing the
1314/// service-client/action poll gap that the callback-`Arc`-only
1315/// lifetime left open.
1316///
1317/// Like [`DispatchSlot`] the executor only sees raw pointers + `extern
1318/// "C"` fn pointers (no `nros` dep — `nros-node` is the lower layer):
1319///
1320/// * `state` — a *leaked* `Arc<ComponentCell>` (via `Arc::into_raw`),
1321///   re-borrowed by the `nros`-side `tick`/`drop` fns. Unlike a
1322///   pub/sub/timer component (kept alive by the executor's per-entity
1323///   callback `Arc` clones), a poll-only component has no callbacks, so
1324///   the slot must own a clone of the cell — hence the paired `drop`.
1325/// * `tick` — `nros`-side `extern "C"` fn that casts `state` back to
1326///   `&ComponentCell`, casts `exec_ctx` back to `*mut Executor`, and
1327///   runs that one cell's tick (mirrors `ExecutorNodeRuntime::run_ticks`).
1328/// * `drop` — `nros`-side `extern "C"` fn run on `Executor::drop` that
1329///   reconstitutes + drops the leaked `Arc`, so the executor owns the
1330///   cell's lifetime.
1331///
1332/// Kept a SEPARATE registry from [`DispatchSlot`] on purpose: framework
1333/// dispatch (RTIC / Embassy) is interrupt-driven, name-keyed, and has no
1334/// tick/own concern — mixing the two risks that path.
1335#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
1336pub struct ComponentSlot {
1337    /// Leaked `Arc<ComponentCell>` (opaque to the executor). Owned by
1338    /// this slot — dropped via `drop` on `Executor::drop`.
1339    pub state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
1340    /// `nros`-side tick trampoline: `(state, exec_ctx)` where `exec_ctx`
1341    /// is `*mut Executor`. Drives one component's `tick`.
1342    pub tick: unsafe extern "C" fn(state: *mut core::ffi::c_void, exec_ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void),
1343    /// `nros`-side drop trampoline: reconstitutes + drops the leaked
1344    /// `Arc<ComponentCell>` at `state`. Run once on `Executor::drop`.
1345    pub drop: unsafe extern "C" fn(state: *mut core::ffi::c_void),
1346}
1347
1348// SAFETY: same story as `DispatchSlot` — two raw pointers + two extern
1349// "C" fn pointers. The `state` pointer's Send/Sync matches the owning
1350// `Executor` (`unsafe impl Send for Executor`); the fn pointers are
1351// Send/Sync by definition.
1352unsafe impl Send for ComponentSlot {}
1353unsafe impl Sync for ComponentSlot {}

1355/// phase-271 — fixed capacity of the per-spin ready-sets (FIFO bitmap + EDF
1356/// heap) and the dispatch loop's upper bound. The executor's callback index is
1357/// carried in a `u64` active-mask (`1u64 << i`), so a callback table can hold at
1358/// most 64 entries regardless of per-entry sizing; the ready-sets are sized to
1359/// this ceiling (stack-transient) so any entry slice up to 64 dispatches
1360/// correctly. `EdfReadySet`'s presence bitmap independently asserts `N <= 64`.
1361pub(crate) const MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS: usize = 64;

1363/// Issue 1667 — the arena's allocation grain. Every region the arena hands out
1364/// starts on it and is a multiple of it, so a released region is always big
1365/// enough, and aligned enough, to hold its own free-list node.
1366pub(crate) const ARENA_GRAIN: usize = core::mem::align_of::<u64>();
1367
1368/// Issue 1667 — the smallest region the arena hands out: one free-list node
1369/// (`next`, `len`), rounded to the grain.
1370pub(crate) const ARENA_MIN_REGION: usize =
1371    (2 * core::mem::size_of::<usize>()).next_multiple_of(ARENA_GRAIN);
1372
1373/// Issue 1667 — the end of the free list.
1374const ARENA_FREE_NONE: usize = usize::MAX;

1376/// Issue 1496 — one arena region, as an allocation hands it out.
1377#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1378pub(crate) struct FreedRegion {
1379    pub(crate) offset: usize,
1380    pub(crate) len: usize,
1381}

1383/// Phase 305 W3 (issue 0255) — upper bound on launch remap rules held by one
1384/// executor (across all its nodes). Launch files carry a handful per node;
1385/// raise here if a plan legitimately outgrows it.
1386pub const MAX_REMAPS: usize = 16;

1388/// Which of [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`]'s two tiers a stored rule
1389/// belongs to.
1390#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1391pub(crate) enum RemapTier {
1392    /// Projected from the launch file (`declare_remap`, which the generated
1393    /// entry calls). AUTHORITATIVE, scoped to one `(name, namespace)`.
1394    Launch,
1395    /// Parsed from `--ros-args` (`crate::ros_args::install_argv_remaps`).
1396    /// FALLBACK — consulted only when no launch rule matched. Scoped to every
1397    /// node, or to the nodes of one NAME (rcl matches a `node:` prefix
1398    /// against the name alone).
1399    Argv,
1400}
1401
1402/// Phase 305 W3 (issue 0255) — one remap rule. `from`/`to` are stored RAW (as
1403/// written); the lookup in [`Executor::resolve_entity_name_for`] expands both
1404/// sides against the owning node's identity via `crate::names` (exact-FQN
1405/// match, no wildcards).
1406///
1407/// The table holds BOTH tiers, so each rule records which one it belongs to.
1408/// The tier is still decided at resolution, by
1409/// [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`]'s two parameters, never by where a
1410/// rule sits in this table — `tier_rules` splits the table into those two
1411/// arguments. That is what keeps declaration order from deciding between the
1412/// channels: an argv rule installed before a launch rule still loses to it.
1413pub(crate) struct RemapRule {
1414    /// For [`RemapTier::Launch`]: the owning node. For [`RemapTier::Argv`]:
1415    /// the node name a `name:from:=to` rule was restricted to, or EMPTY for a
1416    /// rule that applies to every node.
1417    pub(crate) node_name: heapless::String<64>,
1418    /// For [`RemapTier::Launch`] only (normalised, `/` for root). Unused by
1419    /// argv rules, whose node prefix carries no namespace.
1420    pub(crate) namespace: heapless::String<64>,
1421    pub(crate) from: heapless::String<{ crate::names::MAX_RESOLVED_NAME_LEN }>,
1422    pub(crate) to: heapless::String<{ crate::names::MAX_RESOLVED_NAME_LEN }>,
1423    pub(crate) tier: RemapTier,
1424}
1425
1426impl RemapRule {
1427    /// Does this rule belong to `tier` and apply to the node `(node_name, ns)`?
1428    /// `ns` must already be normalised (`/` for root).
1429    fn applies(&self, tier: RemapTier, node_name: &str, ns: &str) -> bool {
1430        self.tier == tier
1431            && match tier {
1432                RemapTier::Launch => {
1433                    self.node_name.as_str() == node_name && self.namespace.as_str() == ns
1434                }
1435                RemapTier::Argv => {
1436                    self.node_name.is_empty() || self.node_name.as_str() == node_name
1437                }
1438            }
1439    }
1440}
1441
1442/// The rules of one tier that apply to one node, in declaration order, as the
1443/// `(from, to)` pairs [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`] takes. The ONE
1444/// place a stored table is split into the two tiers — the executor's resolver,
1445/// `NodeHandle`, and the Rust component road (through
1446/// `crate::ros_args::argv_fallback`) all read through it.
1447pub(crate) fn tier_rules<'r>(
1448    table: &'r [Option<RemapRule>],
1449    tier: RemapTier,
1450    node_name: &'r str,
1451    namespace: &'r str,
1452) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&'r str, &'r str)> + 'r {
1453    let ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
1454    table
1455        .iter()
1456        .flatten()
1457        .filter(move |r| r.applies(tier, node_name, ns))
1458        .map(|r| (r.from.as_str(), r.to.as_str()))
1459}

1461/// The executor's halt flag, in the one shape each configuration can hold.
1462///
1463/// Issue 1177. With an allocator it is refcounted, because `halt_flag()` hands
1464/// a caller its own handle to set from a signal handler or another thread.
1465/// Without one there is no handle to hand out -- a C caller reaches the
1466/// executor through its own pointer and calls `cancel()` directly -- so a plain
1467/// atomic is the whole requirement.
1468///
1469/// `Arc<AtomicBool>` derefs to `AtomicBool`, so every `load`/`store` below is
1470/// written once and only construction and the getter are cfg'd.
1471#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
1472pub(crate) type HaltFlag = portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool>;
1473/// See [`HaltFlag`] above -- the no-allocator shape.
1474#[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
1475pub(crate) type HaltFlag = portable_atomic::AtomicBool;

1477pub struct Executor<'s> {
1478    /// Issue 0656 — the ROS domain this executor's entities belong to.
1479    ///
1480    /// Retained because it was NOT: `open_in` passed `config.domain_id` into
1481    /// `RmwConfig` and dropped it, so every entity built from the executor
1482    /// (rather than from a `Node`, which keeps its own) declared on domain 0
1483    /// whatever `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` said. The value was read, printed, and then not
1484    /// used where it counts — issue 0161's shape.
1485    pub(crate) domain_id: u32,
1486    pub(crate) session: SessionStore,
1487    /// phase-271 (issue 0110) — the six sized tables are no longer inline
1488    /// arrays baked to `nros-node`'s build-time consts; they borrow
1489    /// caller-owned, per-entry-sized storage (`&'s mut` slices carved from a
1490    /// raw `[MaybeUninit<u64>]` backing by [`super::storage::carve`]). Lets a
1491    /// fat native entry and a lean embedded entry in one shared-target
1492    /// workspace each size to its own topology. `Executor` stays non-generic
1493    /// (lifetime only) so the C/C++ FFI keeps wrapping one concrete type.
1494    pub(crate) arena: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u8>],
1495    pub(crate) arena_used: usize,
1496    /// Issue 1496 / 1667 — the head of the FREE LIST: arena regions given back
1497    /// by a released entry, reused first-fit by the next allocation that fits.
1498    ///

1876    /// sample or by the report. The policy, and the argument for its unit, are
1877    /// in [`crate::time_source::SilenceWatch`].
1878    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
1879    pub(crate) sim_time_silence: crate::time_source::SilenceWatch,
1880    #[cfg(feature = "lifecycle-services")]
1881    pub(crate) lifecycle:
1882        Option<alloc::boxed::Box<crate::lifecycle_services::LifecycleRuntimeState>>,

1886    /// explicit `thread::sleep`) counts toward timer accumulation just
1887    /// like time spent inside `drive_io`.
1888
1889    /// Monotonic clock endpoint for no_std timer accounting.
1890    // phase-359 W4 — ONE field. The std twin held an `Instant`; both now hold
1891    // µs from the single `now_us()` read.
1892    pub(crate) last_spin_end_us: Option<u64>,
1893    /// The executor's monotonic µs clock: `ExecutorConfig::clock_us` when the

1897    /// `Instant` through a separate field instead, which is how "what time is
1898    /// it" had two answers in one crate.
1899    pub(crate) clock_us_fn: Option<fn() -> u64>,
1900
1901    /// Consecutive `drive_io` failures on the PRIMARY session (issue 0324).
1902    ///
1903    /// Reset to 0 by any successful drive. A session that has died — router
1904    /// gone, lease expired, socket closed — used to keep returning `Ok(())`
1905    /// from `spin()` forever: the node looked alive, publishes went nowhere,
1906    /// and no callback fired. Nothing in the crate could report it; a
1907    /// `git grep` for a health surface found none, so every such
1908    /// investigation started from packet captures (issue 0268 burned days
1909    /// this way).

1911    /// A COUNTER rather than propagating the error out of `spin_once`,
1912    /// deliberately: `drive_io` returns `Err` for any non-OK backend code, and
1913    /// whether a benign poll timeout maps to one is backend-specific. Aborting
1914    /// the spin on a single failure would risk turning a transient into a dead
1915    /// node. A counter cannot regress behaviour and still makes the condition
1916    /// observable via [`Executor::session_io_failures`].
1917    pub(crate) consecutive_io_failures: u32,

1919    pub(crate) epoch_us_fn: Option<fn() -> u64>,

1924    /// below the crate that defines the frame. `None` outside a registration.
1925    pub(crate) component_frame: Option<core::ptr::NonNull<()>>,

1929    pub(crate) monitor_states: [super::monitor::MonitorState; super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS],
1930    /// Alive supervision, one record per SchedContext: dispatches are counted

1932    /// once per monitor tick. CARVED from the backing like `sporadic_states`.
1933    /// It began as an inline `[_; MAX_SC]` pair on the claim that `MAX_SC` is a
1934    /// build-time constant; it is a SIZING KNOB (`ExecutorSizing::sc`), so the
1935    /// header grew with it and `the_executor_value_does_not_scale_with_the_knobs`
