1946    /// Issue #515 — the spin cadence audit runs once, on the first spin
1947    /// that carries a non-zero timeout (which is where the tier's
1948    /// declared spin period becomes visible to the executor).
1949    pub(crate) spin_quantization_checked: bool,
1950    /// phase-436 W1 — the cadence the quantization audit (issue 0515) actually
1951    /// ran against. Recorded because the audit only LOGS: without this a
1952    /// regression that fed it the wrong number is invisible to a test, and
1953    /// capping the park by the timer deadline is exactly such a regression
1954    /// waiting to happen.
1955    pub(crate) spin_quantization_us: u64,
1956    /// Release jitter: worst observed lateness of a `spin_period` wake
1957    /// against its own nominal schedule, in microseconds.
1958    ///
1959    /// Issue #515 added a STATIC audit for one cause of cadence error --
1960    /// a period that is not a multiple of the spin period. Nothing measured
1961    /// the actual release instants, and `audit_spin_quantization` says so in
1962    /// as many words: "the rate is preserved and no activation is dropped,
1963    /// so every runtime rule is (correctly) silent -- the jitter stays
1964    /// invisible until someone measures cadence on target."
1965    ///
1966    /// This is that measurement, and it is the one `cyclictest` exists to
1967    /// report: the deviation between a timer's programmed wake-up and the
1968    /// instant the task actually resumed, whose MAXIMUM is the figure of
1969    /// merit for a real-time system.
1970    ///
1971    /// `spin_period` already holds both numbers -- `next_us` is the nominal
1972    /// deadline and `now_us()` the actual -- and when the loop is late it
1973    /// skips the sleep and discards the difference. That difference is the
1974    /// jitter.
1975    pub(crate) max_release_jitter_us: u64,
1976    /// Clock reading at the previous `spin_once` entry, for the interval the
1977    /// jitter is measured over. `None` until the first spin, and reset by
1978    /// `clear_release_jitter_stats` so a window starts clean.
1979    pub(crate) last_spin_entry_us: Option<u64>,
1980    /// Jitter high-water at the previous `release-jitter-runtime` check, so
1981    /// the rule reports the DELTA. Same shape as `overruns_reported` on a
1982    /// timer header, and for the same reason: a maximum that has not moved
1983    /// is the fault already reported, not a new one.
1984    pub(crate) jitter_reported_us: u64,
1985    /// Declared minimum stack headroom in bytes for the thread this executor
1986    /// spins on; `0` (default) disables the rule.
1987    ///
1988    /// An executor-level install rather than a contract field, because the
1989    /// bound cannot be derived from anything already declared -- see
1990    /// `check_stack_headroom`. The entry that spawned the thread is the one
1991    /// that knows what it gave it, so that is where the number comes from.
1992    pub(crate) min_stack_headroom_bytes: usize,
1993    /// Lowest headroom already reported, so the rule fires on new lows only.
1994    /// `usize::MAX` = nothing reported yet.
1995    pub(crate) stack_headroom_reported: usize,
1996    /// phase-436 E3 — a minimum is set but the port reports no stack data,
1997    /// so `check_stack_headroom_rule` will skip every tick. Recorded when the
1998    /// bound is set; see `stack_headroom_blind`.
1999    pub(crate) stack_headroom_blind: bool,
2000    /// phase-436 E4 — when the headroom query last ran (`None` = never; a
2001    /// clockless build stores `Some(0)` to mean "has run"), spins since, and
2002    /// how many queries actually reached the port.
2003    pub(crate) stack_headroom_last_check_us: Option<u64>,
2004    pub(crate) stack_headroom_spins_since_check: u32,
2005    pub(crate) stack_headroom_checks: u32,
2006    /// The pacing quantum the spin loop was last driven at, in microseconds.
2007    /// This is the bound the jitter rule judges against -- the caller's own
2008    /// declared cadence, so nothing further has to be declared.
2009    pub(crate) spin_nominal_us: u64,
2010    /// Cadence DECLARED by the driver, in microseconds; `0` = not declared.
2011    ///
2012    /// Takes precedence over the `spin_once` timeout when judging release
2013    /// jitter, because the two are not the same quantity. The timeout is how
2014    /// long a spin may BLOCK waiting for work; the cadence is how often the
2015    /// loop intends to come round. A driver that blocks up to 10 ms and then
2016    /// sleeps 30 ms has a 30 ms cadence and a 10 ms timeout, and judging it
2017    /// against the timeout reports a loop that is late on every single wake.
2018    pub(crate) spin_nominal_declared_us: u64,
2019    /// phase-436 — the bound the last park was computed with, in us, and the
2020    /// source that won it. See `WakeSourceId`.
2021    pub(crate) last_park_bound_us: u64,
2022    pub(crate) last_park_source: WakeSourceId,
2023    /// phase-436 W2 — the park bound after rounding UP to what the platform's
2024    /// wake primitive can express. Kept beside the request rather than
2025    /// replacing it: reporting both is what makes the rounding auditable
2026    /// instead of silent (issue 1194).
2027    pub(crate) last_park_achieved_us: u64,
2028    /// phase-436 W6 — registered platform deadline sources, and how many are
2029    /// live. Inline table: no allocator on the targets this exists for.
2030    pub(crate) wake_sources: [Option<WakeSourceSlot>; MAX_WAKE_SOURCES],
2031    pub(crate) wake_source_count: usize,
2032    /// The single thing that actually blocks. Many sources say WHEN; one
2033    /// primitive does the waiting.
2034    pub(crate) park_primitive: Option<(ParkUntilFn, *mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
2035    /// phase-436 W7.b (issue 1242) — the finest park the INSTALLED primitive
2036    /// can actually express, in microseconds. `0` = none installed, fall back
2037    /// to the `wake_wait_ms` ABI floor.
2038    pub(crate) park_granularity_declared_us: u64,
2039    /// Wakes that were already past their nominal deadline, and wakes total.
2040    ///
2041    /// The maximum alone cannot distinguish one bad wake from a loop that is
2042    /// late every single cycle, and those are different faults: the first is
2043    /// a glitch, the second means the period cannot be met at all.
2044    pub(crate) late_wakes: u32,
2045    pub(crate) total_wakes: u32,
2046    /// Issue 0514 / 1635 / phase-474 I1 -- what happens to a detected contract
2047    /// violation: the log switch, the drain-and-report hook, the image's sink,
2048    /// and the ring (CARVED, phase-409) with its total and dropped counters.
2049    /// See [`super::monitor::ViolationChannel`].
2050    pub(crate) violations: super::monitor::ViolationChannel<'s>,
2051    /// Issue 0790 — hooks that run BEFORE the session is closed, while every
2052    /// entity still works. The load-bearing half: a device releasing a bus or
2053    /// parking an actuator has to publish its final state / answer its last
2054    /// request from HERE, because after teardown it cannot.
2055    ///
2056    /// `[Option<_>; N]` rather than a `heapless::Vec`, deliberately: the handle
2057    /// a caller holds IS the slot index, so a removal must leave every other
2058    /// index where it was. A `Vec`'s `swap_remove` would silently re-point one
2059    /// live handle at a different callback, and its `remove` would re-point all
2060    /// of them. Clearing a slot to `None` also lets the next registration reuse
2061    /// it, which a fill cursor could not.
2062    pub(crate) pre_shutdown_hooks:
2063        [Option<super::types::ShutdownHook>; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS],
2064    /// Issue 0790 — hooks that run AFTER the session is closed. rclcpp's
2065    /// `add_on_shutdown_callback` / `rclcpp::on_shutdown`. See
2066    /// [`Self::pre_shutdown_hooks`] for why this is an array.
2067    pub(crate) on_shutdown_hooks:
2068        [Option<super::types::ShutdownHook>; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS],
2069}

2071impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
2072    /// phase-271 — assemble an executor over already-carved, caller-owned
2073    /// storage (`slices`, from [`super::storage::carve`]). Fills every
2074    /// non-storage field and reserves SC slot 0 for the default Fifo SC (carve
2075    /// left it `None`). The single builder shared by every constructor path.
2076    fn assemble(session: SessionStore, slices: super::storage::ExecutorSlices<'s>) -> Self {
2077        let super::storage::ExecutorSlices {
2078            arena,
2079            entries,
2080            sched_contexts,
2081            sched_context_bindings,
2082            sporadic_states,
2083            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2084            sporadic_atomic_states,
2085            remaps,
2086            nodes,
2087            extra_sessions,
2088            extra_session_ids,
2089            node_sched_table,
2090            dispatch_slots,
2091            component_slots,
2092            active_groups,
2093            group_sched_table,
2094            monitor_violations,
2095            alive_slots,
2096            slot_tags,
2097            params: param_slots,
2098        } = slices;
2099        // phase-382 W3' — only an executor that can build a store keeps the
2100        // carved slots; without `param-services` the region (sized by the
2101        // build, not by a feature, so the layout never depends on one) is
2102        // simply never initialised.
2103        #[cfg(not(feature = "param-services"))]
2104        let _ = param_slots;
2105        // Slot 0 = the auto-created default Fifo SC (see field doc). carve
2106        // initialised the whole table to `None`; populate the reserved slot.
2107        if let Some(slot0) = sched_contexts.first_mut() {
2108            *slot0 = Some(super::sched_context::SchedContext::default());
2109        }
2110        // phase-412 -- stamp the self-report before anything can fail. `init`
2111        // is idempotent, so an image with two executors need not decide which
2112        // one owns the record, and `note_arena_capacity` records the slice this
2113        // executor was actually handed rather than the compiled constant: the
2114        // arena's placement is the caller's choice (issue 0900), so the two can
2115        // legitimately differ and the difference is worth seeing.
2116        crate::boot_report::init();
2117        crate::boot_report::note_arena_capacity(arena.len());
2118        crate::boot_report::checkpoint(crate::boot_report::Stage::ExecutorReady);
2119        Self {
2120            // `assemble` is reached from session-only entry points that have no
2121            // config, so 0 is the floor rather than a choice; `open_in` and any
2122            // binding that knows better overwrite it via `set_domain_id`.
2123            domain_id: 0,
2124            session,
2125            arena,
2126            arena_used: 0,
2127            arena_free_head: ARENA_FREE_NONE,
2128            pending_region: None,
2129            entries,
2130            sched_contexts,
2131            sched_context_bindings,
2132            sporadic_states,
2133            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2134            sporadic_atomic_states,
2135            major_frame_us: 0,
2136            #[cfg(all(
2137                feature = "alloc",
2138                feature = "rmw-cffi",
2139                feature = "scheduler-os-priority"
2140            ))]
2141            os_priority_pool: super::os_priority::OsPriorityPool::new(),
2142            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "scheduler-os-priority"))]
2143            os_priority_apply_policy: None,
2144            trigger: Trigger::Any,
2145            semantics: ExecutorSemantics::RclcppExecutor,
2146            node_name: heapless::String::new(),
2147            active_groups,
2148            active_groups_filtering: false,
2149            nodes,
2150            node_sched_table,
2151            group_sched_table,
2152            remap_table: remaps,
2153            remap_len: 0,
2154            dispatch_slots,
2155            component_slots,
2156            extra_sessions,
2157            extra_session_ids,
2158            primary_rmw_name: heapless::String::new(),
2159            primary_locator: heapless::String::new(),
2160            namespace: {
2161                let mut ns = heapless::String::new();
2162                let _ = ns.push_str("/");
2163                ns
2164            },
2165            // Issue 1177 -- the only cfg the halt flag still needs. `HaltFlag`
2166            // is refcounted with an allocator and plain without one, and
2167            // nothing below this line can tell the difference.
2168            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2169            halt_flag: portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)),
2170            #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
2171            halt_flag: portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
2172            spinning: portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
2173            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2174            wake_flag: portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)),
2175            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2176            node_wake: super::node_wake::NodeWake::new().map(portable_atomic_util::Arc::new),
2177            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2178            wake_ctx: None,
2179            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2180            wake_cb_installed: false,
2181            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2182            graph_change_target: None,
2183            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
2184            has_async_wake: false,
2185            // Phase 141.A.3 — alloc-mode wake state init. Constructed
2186            // eagerly (NodeWake allocation) so the runtime cb can be
2187            // installed lazily on first session without a fallible
2188            // alloc inside spin_once. `None` when the platform
2189            // provider reports the primitive unavailable (matches
2190            // the std-RTOS path's `node_wake: Option<...>`).
2191            #[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", target_os = "linux"))]
2192            signal_fd: None,
2193            #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
2194            params: None,
2195            #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
2196            param_slots,
2197            #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
2198            param_store_refused: false,
2199            #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
2200            declared_params: nros_params::DeclaredParams::EMPTY,
2201            #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
2202            sim_time_source: None,
2203            #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
2204            sim_time_requested: false,
2205            #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
2206            sim_time_stated: false,
2207            #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
2208            sim_time_silence: crate::time_source::SilenceWatch::new(),
2209            #[cfg(feature = "lifecycle-services")]
2210            lifecycle: None,
2211            // Initialise the spin endpoint to construction time so the
2212            // very first `spin_once` credits time the caller spent
2213            // *before* it (e.g. setup, an explicit pre-spin sleep) just
2214            // like time spent between later calls.
2215            // One field, one seed now (phase-359 W10): the clock is absolute
2216            // on every flavour, so it is READ here rather than assumed to be
2217            // zero at construction. The std arm used to seed `Some(0)` because
2218            // its epoch WAS construction; with one provider that special case
2219            // is gone.
2220            last_spin_end_us: default_clock_us_fn().map(|clock| clock()),
2221            clock_us_fn: default_clock_us_fn(),
2222            consecutive_io_failures: 0,
2223            // RFC-0052 W3b.5 — a build with a wall clock gets one by default so
2224            // age monitors activate without extra wiring; a build with neither a
2225            // platform port nor a host gets `None`, and its board installs
2226            // `config.epoch_us` in `from_session_in`/`open`.
2227            //
2228            // phase-359 W10 — the cfg pair that used to be here moved into
2229            // `default_epoch_us_fn`, beside the `default_clock_us_fn` it
2230            // mirrors. (The old comment pointed at "the `not(std)` blocks
2231            // above" for the board install; those blocks are no longer
2232            // cfg-gated — the config override applies on every flavour now.)
2233            epoch_us_fn: super::types::default_epoch_us_fn(),
2234            component_frame: None,
2235            monitor_table: &[],
2236            monitor_states: [super::monitor::MonitorState::default(); super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS],
2237            age_table: &[],
2238            age_states: [super::monitor::AgeState::default(); super::monitor::MAX_AGE_MONITORS],
2239            fault_fn: None,
2240            spin_quantization_checked: false,
2241            spin_quantization_us: 0,
2242            max_release_jitter_us: 0,
2243            last_spin_entry_us: None,
2244            jitter_reported_us: 0,
2245            min_stack_headroom_bytes: 0,
2246            stack_headroom_reported: usize::MAX,
2247            stack_headroom_blind: false,
2248            stack_headroom_last_check_us: None,
2249            stack_headroom_spins_since_check: 0,
2250            stack_headroom_checks: 0,
2251            spin_nominal_us: 0,
2252            spin_nominal_declared_us: 0,
2253            last_park_bound_us: 0,
2254            last_park_source: WakeSourceId::CallerBudget,
2255            last_park_achieved_us: 0,
2256            wake_sources: [None; MAX_WAKE_SOURCES],
2257            wake_source_count: 0,
2258            park_primitive: None,
2259            park_granularity_declared_us: 0,
2260            late_wakes: 0,
2261            total_wakes: 0,
2262            violations: super::monitor::ViolationChannel::new(monitor_violations),
2263            alive_slots,
2264            slot_tags,
2265            // Issue 0790 — both phase tables start empty. An image that
2266            // registers nothing pays these `None`s and a two-slot scan at
2267            // teardown, and nothing else.
2268            pre_shutdown_hooks: [None; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS],
2269            on_shutdown_hooks: [None; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS],
2270        }
2271    }

2273    /// Create an owning executor over caller-supplied `backing`, sized by
2274    /// `sizing`. The core, non-generic, per-entry entry point (the `alloc`
2275    /// [`from_session`](Self::from_session) convenience leaks a default backing
2276    /// and calls this; the macro / C FFI pass an entry-sized backing).
2277    ///
2278    /// # Safety
2279    /// `backing` must be ≥ `sizing.u64_len()` words, stay alive for `'s`, and
2280    /// not be otherwise accessed while the executor lives (it aliases it).
2281    /// `sizing.cbs` must be ≤ 64 (the `u64` ready-set bitmask ceiling).
2282    pub unsafe fn from_session_in(
2283        session: session::ConcreteSession,
2284        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
2285        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
2286    ) -> Self {
2287        let slices = unsafe { super::storage::carve(backing, sizing) };
2288        Self::assemble(SessionStore::Owned(session), slices)
2289    }
2290
2291    /// Create a borrowing executor over caller-supplied `backing`, sized by
2292    /// `sizing`. Counterpart to [`from_session_in`](Self::from_session_in) for
2293    /// the per-tier / C model (the session is borrowed, not owned).
2294    ///
2295    /// # Safety
2296    /// - `session_ptr` must point to a valid session that outlives the executor
2297    ///   and is not moved/dropped while it exists.
2298    /// - `backing` obligations as in [`from_session_in`](Self::from_session_in).
2299    pub unsafe fn from_session_ptr_in(
2300        session_ptr: *mut session::ConcreteSession,
2301        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
2302        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
2303    ) -> Self {
2304        let slices = unsafe { super::storage::carve(backing, sizing) };
2305        Self::assemble(SessionStore::Borrowed(session_ptr), slices)
2306    }
2307}

2309impl Executor<'static> {
2310    /// Create an executor from an already-opened session, using the build-time
2311    /// default sizing (`MAX_CBS`/`MAX_SC`/`ARENA_SIZE`). Convenience for
2312    /// std/alloc callers that don't size per-entry: it leaks a default-sized
2313    /// backing (executor-lifetime, one-time) and calls
2314    /// [`from_session_in`](Self::from_session_in). Per-entry sizing goes through
2315    /// the macro / `open_in` instead.
2316    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2317    pub fn from_session(session: session::ConcreteSession) -> Self {
2318        let sizing = super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT;
2319        // SAFETY: the backing is exactly `sizing.u64_len()` words,
2320        // `'static`, and uniquely owned by this executor.
2321        unsafe { Self::from_session_in(session, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
2322    }
2323
2324    /// [`from_session`](Self::from_session) with an [`ExecutorConfig`], so a
2325    /// caller that brings its own session can also bring its own clock.
2326    ///
2327    /// issue 0709 / issue 0687 — `from_session` takes no config, and that is
2328    /// the path the no-port population uses: it accepts any `Session`, so a
2329    /// consumer with a non-cffi backend reaches the executor through it and had
2330    /// NO way to install `clock_us`. phase-359 W10 argued the `std`-without-a-
2331    /// port clock fallbacks could go because "a caller with a clock installs it
2332    /// through `ExecutorConfig::clock_us`" — true for `open`, false here, which
2333    /// is half of why that deletion was reverted.
2334    ///
2335    /// Only the timing sources are read from `config`; identity (locator,
2336    /// domain, names) belongs to the session the caller already opened. As in
2337    /// [`open_in`](Self::open_in), a `None` field does NOT clobber the
2338    /// platform default — it means "not specified" (the bug issue 0671
2339    /// records).
2340    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2341    pub fn from_session_with(
2342        session: session::ConcreteSession,
2343        config: &super::types::ExecutorConfig<'_>,
2344    ) -> Self {
2345        let mut executor = Self::from_session(session);
2346        if let Some(clock) = config.clock_us {
2347            executor.clock_us_fn = Some(clock);
2348            executor.last_spin_end_us = Some(clock());
2349        }
2350        if let Some(epoch) = config.epoch_us {
2351            executor.epoch_us_fn = Some(epoch);
2352        }
2353        executor
2354    }
2355
2356    /// Create an executor from a borrowed session pointer, default-sized. The
2357    /// `alloc` convenience wrapper over
2358    /// [`from_session_ptr_in`](Self::from_session_ptr_in) — leaks a default
2359    /// backing so existing callers keep the zero-storage-arg signature.
2360    ///
2361    /// # Safety
2362    /// - `session_ptr` must point to a valid, initialized session that lives at
2363    ///   least as long as this executor.
2364    /// - The caller must not move or drop the session while the executor exists.
2365    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2366    pub unsafe fn from_session_ptr(session_ptr: *mut session::ConcreteSession) -> Self {
2367        let sizing = super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT;
2368        // SAFETY: the backing as in `from_session`; session_ptr contract
2369        // forwarded to `from_session_ptr_in`.
2370        unsafe { Self::from_session_ptr_in(session_ptr, default_backing(sizing), sizing) }
2371    }
2372}
2373
2374/// The two cadences a `period_us` timer alternates between under a `spin_us`
2375/// spin period, or `None` when the audit (issue #515) has nothing to say.
2376///
2377/// Split out of `audit_spin_quantization` so the decision can be asserted:
2378/// the audit only LOGS, so a regression in what it decides is otherwise
2379/// invisible to a test.
2380///
2381/// `None` for a period of zero, for a period that divides the spin period —
2382/// and, since issue 1321, for a timer whose activations are NOT paced by the
2383/// spin period at all. The warning's arithmetic is wall microseconds on both
2384/// sides; a `Ros` timer's activations are quantised by the `/clock` STEP, so
2385/// the sentence it would print ("activations will alternate between X and Y
2386/// us") is about nothing.
2387pub(crate) fn spin_quantization_span(
2388    clock_source: TimerClockSource,
2389    period_us: u64,
2390    spin_us: u64,
2391) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
2392    if spin_us == 0 || period_us == 0 || period_us.is_multiple_of(spin_us) {
2393        return None;
2394    }
2395    if !clock_source.remaining_is_wall_time() {
2396        return None;
2397    }
2398    let early_us = (period_us / spin_us) * spin_us;
2399    Some((early_us, early_us.saturating_add(spin_us)))
2400}
2401
2402/// phase-436 — which deadline source bounded the last park.
2403///
2404/// Attribution is what turns "why did we wake" from a guess into a number.
2405/// Recording it costs one byte per spin and is the difference between a
2406/// schedulability argument you can audit and one you have to trust.
2407#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
2408#[repr(u8)]
2409pub enum WakeSourceId {
2410    /// The `spin_once` caller's own timeout — always a member of the source
2411    /// set, which is why the park is never unbounded.
2412    CallerBudget,
2413    /// A registered timer's next expiry (issue 1192).
2414    Timer,
2415    /// The backend's next internal event (lease keepalive, heartbeat,
2416    /// ACK-NACK). Folded into the same `min` as everything else rather than
2417    /// capping the budget separately upstream, so one rule decides the park
2418    /// and one attribution explains it.
2419    Session,
2420    /// A source the PLATFORM registered: a `k_poll` event set, an `epoll`
2421    /// group, a FreeRTOS queue set, a ThreadX event-flags group, or a
2422    /// bare-metal device ISR. The core never names an RTOS; it only asks each
2423    /// registered source when it will next need the executor.
2424    Platform(u8),
2425}
2426
2427/// How many platform sources one executor can carry. A plain const, not a
2428/// sizing knob: the table is inline, so no allocator is required on the no_std
2429/// targets this seam mainly exists for.
2430pub const MAX_WAKE_SOURCES: usize = 8;
2431
2432/// When this source will next need the executor, in the executor's clock,
2433/// as microseconds FROM NOW.
2434///
2435/// `u64::MAX` means "nothing pending" — the source does not shorten the park.
2436/// That is how an ASYNC source spells itself: a socket or a DDS listener
2437/// contributes no deadline and instead breaks the park by signalling the wake
2438/// primitive, so async and deadline sources compose without a second
2439/// mechanism.
2440pub type NextDeadlineFn = unsafe extern "C" fn(ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void) -> u64;
2441
2442/// Park until `deadline_us` from now, or until something signals, whichever
2443/// comes first.
2444///
2445/// Returns `0` when woken by an event, `1` when the deadline expired, and a
2446/// negative value when this build cannot park at all.
2447///
2448/// A DEADLINE, not a duration, and that distinction is what makes bare metal
2449/// work: `nros-baremetal-common`'s own note says `wfi` with no pending
2450/// interrupt deadlocks, so a board must arm a timer compare BEFORE waiting.
2451/// A `sleep(duration)` seam cannot express that — the sleeper does not know
2452/// whether anyone armed an interrupt. `park_until(deadline)` does, because the
2453/// deadline is exactly what the compare is armed to.
2454pub type ParkUntilFn = unsafe extern "C" fn(ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void, deadline_us: u64) -> i8;
2455
2456/// A registered deadline contributor.
2457#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
2458pub(crate) struct WakeSourceSlot {
2459    pub(crate) next: NextDeadlineFn,
2460    pub(crate) ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
2461}
2462
2463impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
2464    /// Phase 228.B (RFC-0015) — construct a tier task's executor that **shares**
2465    /// a session opened once by the orchestration `main()`.
2466    ///
2467    /// In the per-tier execution model `main()` opens one RMW session, then
2468    /// spawns one RTOS task per priority tier; each task calls this to get an
2469    /// [`Executor`] over the *same* session (the `Borrowed` session store — this
2470    /// executor neither owns nor closes it), registers its tier's callback
2471    /// groups, and spins. Thin alias over [`Executor::from_session_ptr`].
2472    ///
2473    /// # Safety
2474    /// `session` must outlive every executor/task built from it (the
2475    /// orchestration `main()` holds it and never returns / WFIs), and must not
2476    /// be mutated except through these executors' spin calls.
2477    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2478    pub unsafe fn open_with_session(session: *mut session::ConcreteSession) -> Executor<'static> {
2479        unsafe { Executor::<'static>::from_session_ptr(session) }
2480    }
2481
2482    /// phase-271 — per-tier borrowed-session constructor over caller-supplied,
2483    /// per-tier-sized `backing`. The sized counterpart to
2484    /// [`open_with_session`](Self::open_with_session): each RTOS tier task owns
2485    /// its own backing so tiers size independently.
2486    ///
2487    /// # Safety
2488    /// `session` obligations as in [`open_with_session`](Self::open_with_session);
2489    /// `backing`/`sizing` as in [`from_session_ptr_in`](Self::from_session_ptr_in).
2490    pub unsafe fn open_with_session_in(
2491        session: *mut session::ConcreteSession,
2492        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
2493        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
2494    ) -> Self {
2495        unsafe { Self::from_session_ptr_in(session, backing, sizing) }
2496    }
2497
2498    /// Raw pointer to this executor's RMW session, for the per-tier model:
2499    /// the boot task opens the one session via [`Executor::open`] (the RMW
2500    /// session is a process-wide singleton — opening twice fails), then hands
2501    /// this pointer to each spawned tier task's
2502    /// [`Executor::open_with_session`]. The boot task's executor owns the
2503    /// session and outlives every borrower, so the pointer stays valid for the
2504    /// program's life. Works for both `Owned` and `Borrowed` stores.
2505    ///
2506    /// # Safety
2507    /// The returned pointer aliases `self.session`. Callers must keep `self`
2508    /// alive (not moved/dropped) for as long as any tier executor uses the
2509    /// pointer, and must only touch the session through executor spin calls
2510    /// (the RMW backend serializes concurrent access through its own locks).
2511    pub fn session_ptr(&mut self) -> *mut session::ConcreteSession {
2512        &mut *self.session as *mut session::ConcreteSession
2513    }
2514
2515    /// Opaque, `Send` form of [`session_ptr`](Self::session_ptr) — the per-tier
2516    /// model hands this to each spawned tier task (it can cross the RTOS task /
2517    /// thread boundary, which a bare `*mut` cannot). See [`SessionHandle`].
2518    ///
2519    /// # Safety
2520    /// Same contract as [`session_ptr`](Self::session_ptr): `self` (the session
2521    /// owner) must outlive every executor built from the handle.
2522    pub fn session_handle(&mut self) -> SessionHandle {
2523        SessionHandle(self.session_ptr())
2524    }
2525
2526    /// Open an [`Executor`] over the session a [`SessionHandle`] refers to (the
2527    /// `Borrowed` store — neither owns nor closes it). The tier-task counterpart
2528    /// to [`session_handle`](Self::session_handle).
2529    ///
2530    /// # Safety
2531    /// The handle's session must still be alive (its owning executor not moved
2532    /// or dropped); access only through executor spin calls.
2533    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2534    pub unsafe fn open_with_session_handle(handle: SessionHandle) -> Executor<'static> {
2535        unsafe { Executor::<'static>::open_with_session(handle.0) }
2536    }
2537
2538    /// phase-271 — sized counterpart to
2539    /// [`open_with_session_handle`](Self::open_with_session_handle) (per-tier
2540    /// backing).
2541    ///
2542    /// # Safety
2543    /// As [`open_with_session_handle`](Self::open_with_session_handle) +
2544    /// [`from_session_ptr_in`](Self::from_session_ptr_in).
2545    pub unsafe fn open_with_session_handle_in(
2546        handle: SessionHandle,
2547        backing: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<u64>],
2548        sizing: super::storage::ExecutorSizing,
2549    ) -> Self {
2550        unsafe { Self::open_with_session_in(handle.0, backing, sizing) }
2551    }
2552
2553    /// issue 1571 — a SPAWNED tier's executor over its slot of the entry's
2554    /// [`TierExecutorBacking`](super::TierExecutorBacking) — the road every
2555    /// board's `run_tiers` takes for each tier but the boot one.
2556    ///
2557    /// The slot's TYPE is the size: it is `ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT.u64_len()`
2558    /// words and this opens with `ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT`, so the pairing is
2559    /// exact by construction and lives here, once, rather than at five boards.
2560    /// [`open_with_session`](Self::open_with_session) is the heap twin this
2561    /// replaced on those roads.
2562    ///
2563    /// # Safety
2564    /// `session` obligations as in [`open_with_session`](Self::open_with_session).
2565    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2566    pub unsafe fn open_with_session_slot(
2567        session: *mut session::ConcreteSession,
2568        slot: &'s mut super::TierExecutorBackingSlot,
2569    ) -> Self {
2570        unsafe {
2571            Self::open_with_session_in(
2572                session,
2573                &mut slot[..],
2574                super::storage::ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT,
2575            )
2576        }
2577    }
2578
2579    /// issue 1571 — [`open_with_session_slot`](Self::open_with_session_slot)
2580    /// over a [`SessionHandle`], for the boards whose tier tasks carry one.
2581    ///
2582    /// # Safety
2583    /// As [`open_with_session_handle`](Self::open_with_session_handle).
2584    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
2585    pub unsafe fn open_with_session_handle_slot(
2586        handle: SessionHandle,
2587        slot: &'s mut super::TierExecutorBackingSlot,
2588    ) -> Self {
2589        unsafe { Self::open_with_session_slot(handle.0, slot) }
2590    }
2591
2592    /// Phase 228.C — set this tier executor's active callback-group filter. The
2593    /// generated per-tier task calls this before registering nodes; afterwards
2594    /// only callbacks whose `.callback_group()` is in `groups` register here.
2595    /// An empty slice (or never calling it) leaves the wildcard — register all
2596    /// callbacks (the single-tier degenerate case + today's behaviour).
2597    pub fn set_active_groups(
2598        &mut self,
2599        groups: &[(&str, &str, &str)],
2600    ) -> Result<(), super::types::BindError> {
2601        // phase-409 — the table is CARVED and reused, so clear before refilling;
2602        // the old `Option<heapless::Vec>` got a fresh empty vector each call.
2603        self.active_groups.clear();
2604        if groups.is_empty() {
2605            self.active_groups_filtering = false;
2606            return Ok(());
2607        }
2608        for (name, ns, group) in groups {
2609            // issue 1172 — this used to be `if s.push_str(g).is_ok()`, which
2610            // DROPPED an oversized group name and left the tier filtering on a
2611            // set that silently lacked it. It fails closed (the entity is never
2612            // created), so the symptom is a missing entity with nothing to read
2613            // that says why. Same contract as `declare_remap` below: too long,
2614            // or table full, is the caller's error.
2615            let key = super::storage::node_identity_hash(name, ns);
2616            let mut s = heapless::String::new();
2617            let why = if s.push_str(group).is_err() {
2618                Some(super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)
2619            } else if self.active_groups.push((key, s)).is_err() {
2620                Some(super::types::BindError::TableFull)
2621            } else {
2622                None
2623            };
2624            if let Some(why) = why {
2625                // FAIL CLOSED, and say so. Returning here with a PARTIAL table
2626                // would leave the tier filtering on a subset — the same silent
2627                // narrowing, one step later. An empty table with filtering ON
2628                // accepts NOTHING (`group_filter_accepts` matches on an empty
2629                // slice), so the tier registers no entities at all: visible in
2630                // behaviour, where a missing entry is not. The `Err` is for the
2631                // caller that can report it; the state is safe for the one that
2632                // cannot.
2633                self.active_groups.clear();
2634                self.active_groups_filtering = true;
2635                return Err(why);
2636            }
2637        }
2638        self.active_groups_filtering = true;
2639        Ok(())
2640    }
2641
2642    /// The current callback-group filter, or `None` for the wildcard.
2643    fn active_group_filter(&self) -> Option<&[super::storage::ActiveGroup]> {
2644        self.active_groups_filtering
2645            .then(|| self.active_groups.as_slice())
2646    }
2647
2648    /// Phase 228.C — whether a callback in `group` should register in this
2649    /// executor under the current filter. The wildcard accepts everything.
2650    pub fn group_active(&self, node_name: &str, node_namespace: &str, group: &str) -> bool {
2651        group_filter_accepts(
2652            self.active_group_filter(),
2653            super::storage::node_identity_hash(node_name, node_namespace),
2654            group,
2655        )
2656    }
2657
2658    /// Set the node name and namespace used for liveliness tokens.
2659    ///
2660    /// Called by `open()` to propagate config values. When `register_subscription`
2661    /// or `register_service` creates entities, these values are attached to the
2662    /// Phase 156 — record the primary session's backend identity
2663    /// (rmw name + locator) so `NodeBuilder::resolve_session_slot`
2664    /// can detect when a `.rmw(name)` matches the primary instead
2665    /// of opening a SECOND backend session against the same
2666    /// singleton (zenoh-pico's `g_session` is process-wide;
2667    /// opening twice fails). `Executor::open*` calls this
2668    /// automatically; the C surface (`nros_executor_init`) calls
2669    /// it manually because it constructs via `from_session_ptr`
2670    /// which doesn't know the open metadata. Empty strings = "no
2671    /// primary identity tracked"; the cache check degrades to
2672    /// always-miss.
2673    pub fn set_primary_identity(&mut self, rmw_name: &str, locator: &str) {
2674        self.primary_rmw_name.clear();
2675        let _ = self.primary_rmw_name.push_str(rmw_name);
2676        self.primary_locator.clear();
2677        let _ = self.primary_locator.push_str(locator);
2678    }
2679
2680    /// `TopicInfo`/`ServiceInfo` so the zenoh backend can declare liveliness.
2681    /// Issue 0656 — set the ROS domain for entities this executor declares.
2682    ///
2683    /// For bindings that build an executor from an existing session
2684    /// (`from_session_ptr_in`), where no `ExecutorConfig` is available and the
2685    /// domain would otherwise stay at its 0 floor.
2686    pub fn set_domain_id(&mut self, domain_id: u32) {
2687        self.domain_id = domain_id;
2688    }
2689
2690    /// The ROS domain this executor declares entities on.
2691    pub fn domain_id(&self) -> u32 {
2692        self.domain_id
2693    }
2694
2695    pub fn set_node_identity(&mut self, node_name: &str, namespace: &str) {
2696        self.node_name.clear();
2697        let _ = self.node_name.push_str(node_name);
2698        if !namespace.is_empty() {
2699            self.namespace.clear();
2700            let _ = self.namespace.push_str(namespace);
2701        }
2702    }
2703
2704    // =========================================================================
2705    // Phase 305 W3 (issue 0255) — per-node launch remap table
2706    // =========================================================================
2707
2708    /// Record one launch `<remap from= to=/>` rule for the node identified by
2709    /// `(node_name, namespace)`. Rules are matched in declaration order (first
2710    /// wins) by [`Self::resolve_entity_name_for`]. Errors when a string
2711    /// overflows its slot or the table is at `MAX_REMAPS` — callers surface
2712    /// this rather than silently dropping a routing rule.
2713    ///
2714    /// **This declares an AUTHORITATIVE rule.** Declaration order settles
2715    /// which of two launch rules for one name wins; it is not how an argv rule
2716    /// is ranked against a launch rule. The `--ros-args` rules share this table
2717    /// but are tagged as the fallback tier, and resolution reads both tiers
2718    /// through [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`] — so an argv rule
2719    /// installed BEFORE a launch rule still loses to it.
2720    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
2721    pub fn declare_remap(
2722        &mut self,
2723        node_name: &str,
2724        namespace: &str,
2725        from: &str,
2726        to: &str,
2727    ) -> Result<(), ()> {
2728        let mut rule = RemapRule {
2729            node_name: heapless::String::new(),
2730            namespace: heapless::String::new(),
2731            from: heapless::String::new(),
2732            to: heapless::String::new(),
2733            tier: RemapTier::Launch,
2734        };
2735        rule.node_name.push_str(node_name)?;
2736        let ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
2737        rule.namespace.push_str(ns)?;
2738        rule.from.push_str(from)?;
2739        rule.to.push_str(to)?;
2740        // Same contract as the `heapless::Vec::push` this replaces: full table
2741        // is an error the caller surfaces, never a silently dropped rule.
2742        let slot = self.remap_table.get_mut(self.remap_len).ok_or(())?;
2743        *slot = Some(rule);
2744        self.remap_len += 1;
2745        Ok(())
2746    }
2747
2748    /// Resolve a source-level entity name for the node identified by
2749    /// `(node_name, namespace)`: ROS 2 name expansion (`~`/relative → FQN)
2750    /// plus this node's declared remap rules (exact-FQN match, first rule
2751    /// wins). Nodes with no rules still get expansion. Errors on an
2752    /// unexpandable name (see `crate::names::expand_name`).
2753    ///
2754    /// Two tiers, through [`crate::names::resolve_name_layered`]: the rules
2755    /// [`Self::declare_remap`] recorded for this node are AUTHORITATIVE (the
2756    /// generated entry declares the launch projection there), and the
2757    /// `--ros-args` rules `crate::ros_args::install_argv_remaps` put in the
2758    /// same table are the FALLBACK, consulted only when no launch rule
2759    /// matched. rcl does the same with its local and global arguments
2760    /// (`rcl_remap_topic_name`, Humble `rcl/remap.h`).
2761    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
2762    pub fn resolve_entity_name_for(
2763        &self,
2764        node_name: &str,
2765        namespace: &str,
2766        source: &str,
2767    ) -> Result<crate::names::ResolvedName, ()> {
2768        let ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
2769        let table = &self.remap_table[..self.remap_len];
2770        crate::names::resolve_name_layered(
2771            source,
2772            node_name,
2773            ns,
2774            tier_rules(table, RemapTier::Launch, node_name, ns),
2775            tier_rules(table, RemapTier::Argv, node_name, ns),
2776        )
2777    }
2778
2779    /// [`Self::resolve_entity_name_for`] against the executor's CURRENT node
2780    /// identity (`set_node_identity`) — the nros-c registration sites set that
2781    /// identity per node immediately before registering each entity.
2782    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
2783    pub fn resolve_entity_name(&self, source: &str) -> Result<crate::names::ResolvedName, ()> {
2784        self.resolve_entity_name_for(self.node_name.as_str(), self.namespace.as_str(), source)
2785    }
2786
2787    // =========================================================================
2788    // Phase 272 (RFC-0047) — node-name → sched-context table
2789    // =========================================================================
2790
2791    /// Seed a config-resolved tier binding by `(name, namespace)` before the
2792    /// node is built. `NodeBuilder::build` consults this table when no
2793    /// explicit `.sched()` override is given — the table entry then wins over
2794    /// the `SchedContextId(0)` default (precedence: explicit > table > 0).
2795    ///
2796    /// Call BEFORE `node_builder(name).build()`. An existing entry for the
2797    /// same `(name, namespace)` key is overwritten (last-write wins). Overflow
2798    /// past `MAX_NODES` is an `Err`, never a dropped binding — issue 1172. An
2799    /// empty `namespace` is normalised
2800    /// to `"/"` to match what `NodeBuilder::build` computes for a root-NS node.
2801    pub fn bind_node_name_sched(
2802        &mut self,
2803        name: &str,
2804        namespace: &str,
2805        sc: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
2806    ) -> Result<(), super::types::BindError> {
2807        let norm_ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
2808        // Overwrite if there is already an entry for this (name, ns) pair.
2809        for entry in self.node_sched_table.iter_mut() {
2810            if entry.0.as_str() == name && entry.1.as_str() == norm_ns {
2811                entry.2 = sc;
2812                return Ok(());
2813            }
2814        }
2815        // New entry. Too long, or table full, is an ERROR the caller surfaces
2816        // — never a dropped binding. A binding that vanishes leaves the node on
2817        // the wrong sched context with nothing to read that says so.
2818        let mut name_s = heapless::String::<64>::new();
2819        let mut ns_s = heapless::String::<64>::new();
2820        name_s
2821            .push_str(name)
2822            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
2823        ns_s.push_str(norm_ns)
2824            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
2825        self.node_sched_table
2826            .push((name_s, ns_s, sc))
2827            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::TableFull)?;
2828        Ok(())
2829    }

2831    /// Look up the seeded sched-context for `(name, namespace)`. Returns
2832    /// `None` when the table has no entry for this pair (unseed → default 0).
2833    /// `pub(super)` — visible only within the `executor` module (sibling
2834    /// `node_record` calls it from `NodeBuilder::build`).
2835    pub(super) fn lookup_node_sched(
2836        &self,
2837        name: &str,
2838        namespace: &str,
2839    ) -> Option<super::sched_context::SchedContextId> {
2840        for entry in self.node_sched_table.iter() {
2841            if entry.0.as_str() == name && entry.1.as_str() == namespace {
2842                return Some(entry.2);
2843            }
2844        }
2845        None
2846    }

2848    // =========================================================================
2849    // Phase 273 (RFC-0047) — per-callback-group → sched-context table
2850    // =========================================================================
2851
2852    /// Seed a config-resolved tier binding by `(name, namespace, group)` before
2853    /// entities are registered. `apply_node_default_sched` consults this table
2854    /// first (group table > node default > `SchedContextId(0)`).
2855    ///
2856    /// Call BEFORE entity creation. An existing entry for the same
2857    /// `(name, namespace, group)` key is overwritten (last-write wins). Overflow
2858    /// past `MAX_CBS` is an `Err`, never a dropped binding — issue 1172. An
2859    /// empty `namespace` is normalised to
2860    /// `"/"` to match `NodeBuilder::build`. Mirror of `bind_node_name_sched`.
2861    pub fn bind_group_sched(
2862        &mut self,
2863        name: &str,
2864        namespace: &str,
2865        group: &str,
2866        sc: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
2867    ) -> Result<(), super::types::BindError> {
2868        let norm_ns = if namespace.is_empty() { "/" } else { namespace };
2869        // Overwrite if there is already an entry for this (name, ns, group).
2870        for entry in self.group_sched_table.iter_mut() {
2871            if entry.0.as_str() == name && entry.1.as_str() == norm_ns && entry.2.as_str() == group
2872            {
2873                entry.3 = sc;
2874                return Ok(());
2875            }
2876        }
2877        // Same contract as the two above.
2878        let mut name_s = heapless::String::<64>::new();
2879        let mut ns_s = heapless::String::<64>::new();
2880        let mut grp_s = heapless::String::<32>::new();
2881        name_s
2882            .push_str(name)
2883            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
2884        ns_s.push_str(norm_ns)
2885            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
2886        grp_s
2887            .push_str(group)
2888            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::NameTooLong)?;
2889        self.group_sched_table
2890            .push((name_s, ns_s, grp_s, sc))
2891            .map_err(|_| super::types::BindError::TableFull)?;
2892        Ok(())
2893    }

2895    /// Look up the seeded sched-context for `(name, namespace, group)`. Returns
2896    /// `None` when the table has no entry for this triple.
2897    fn lookup_group_sched(
2898        &self,
2899        name: &str,
2900        namespace: &str,
2901        group: &str,
2902    ) -> Option<super::sched_context::SchedContextId> {
2903        for entry in self.group_sched_table.iter() {
2904            if entry.0.as_str() == name
2905                && entry.1.as_str() == namespace
2906                && entry.2.as_str() == group
2907            {
2908                return Some(entry.3);
2909            }
2910        }
2911        None
2912    }

2914    // =========================================================================
2915    // Phase 110.B — SchedContext API
2916    // =========================================================================
2917
2918    /// Identifier of the auto-created default `Fifo`-class scheduling
2919    /// context. Every callback registered without an explicit
2920    /// [`Self::bind_handle_to_sched_context`] binds to this SC.
2921    pub fn default_sched_context_id(&self) -> super::sched_context::SchedContextId {
2922        super::sched_context::SchedContextId(0)
2923    }
2924
2925    /// Register a new scheduling context. Returns a [`SchedContextId`](crate::executor::sched_context::SchedContextId)
2926    /// callers pass to [`Self::bind_handle_to_sched_context`] to attach
2927    /// callbacks. Phase 110.B.
2928    pub fn create_sched_context(
2929        &mut self,
2930        sc: super::sched_context::SchedContext,
2931    ) -> Result<super::sched_context::SchedContextId, NodeError> {
2932        // Slot 0 is reserved for the default Fifo SC; search 1..MAX_SC.
2933        for (i, slot) in self.sched_contexts.iter_mut().enumerate().skip(1) {
2934            if slot.is_none() {
2935                *slot = Some(sc);
2936                // Phase 110.E — Sporadic-class SCs get a sibling
2937                // `SporadicState` entry that the spin_once dispatch
2938                // path consults each cycle to refill the budget at
2939                // period boundaries and skip dispatch when budget
2940                // is exhausted.
2941                if matches!(sc.class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
2942                    let budget = sc.budget_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
2943                    let period = sc.period_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
2944                    self.sporadic_states[i] =
2945                        Some(super::sched_context::SporadicState::new(budget, period));
2946                }
2947                return Ok(super::sched_context::SchedContextId(i as u8));
2948            }
2949        }
2950        Err(NodeError::NoSchedContextSlot)
2951    }

2954    /// target has an epoch source (config `epoch_us`, defaulted from
2955    /// `SystemTime` on hosted configs). `None` = no wall clock; age
2956    /// monitors must not have been baked (the emitter refuses).
2957    pub fn epoch_now_us(&self) -> Option<u64> {

2961    /// RFC-0052 W3b.4 — install the baked contract-monitor table. Call
2962    /// BEFORE entity creation so `create_publisher` can attach each
2963    /// contracted endpoint's counter cell. Mirrors `set_qos_overrides`:
2964    /// `&'static`, codegen-baked, empty by default.
2965    ///
2966    /// phase-467 W1 -- the executor watches at most
2967    /// [`MAX_MONITORS`](super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS) rows
2968    /// (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_MONITORS`). A generated entry cannot reach this with
2969    /// more: its table carries a compile-time assertion that names the knob,
2970    /// and the C++ installer refuses at runtime. A hand-written longer table is
2971    /// a debug-build panic naming the knob, because in release the spin loop
2972    /// would inspect only the first `MAX_MONITORS` and leave the rest silently
2973    /// unwatched.
2974    pub fn set_monitor_table(&mut self, table: &'static [super::monitor::MonitorSpec]) {
2975        if let Err(full) = super::monitor::check_table_capacity(table.len(), 0)
2976            && cfg!(debug_assertions)
2977        {
2978            panic!("set_monitor_table: {full}");
2979        }
2980        self.monitor_table = table;
2981    }

2983    /// phase-467 W1 -- install BOTH baked monitor tables, or neither.
2984    ///
2985    /// The refusing installer: a table longer than this executor watches
2986    /// (`MAX_MONITORS` / `MAX_AGE_MONITORS`) is `Err`, and its `Display` names
2987    /// the knob to raise, before anything is installed. Nothing is truncated:
2988    /// the spin loop inspects only the first `MAX_*` specs, so accepting a
2989    /// longer table would boot with its tail silently unwatched. The C ABI's
2990    /// `nros_cpp_install_monitors` refuses on the same check.
2991    pub fn try_set_monitor_tables(
2992        &mut self,
2993        table: &'static [super::monitor::MonitorSpec],
2994        ages: &'static [super::monitor::AgeMonitorSpec],
2995    ) -> Result<(), super::monitor::MonitorTableFull> {
2996        super::monitor::check_table_capacity(table.len(), ages.len())?;
2997        self.monitor_table = table;
2998        self.age_table = ages;
2999        Ok(())
3000    }

3055    /// exact topic match against the baked age table, only for stamped
3056    /// types (`M::STAMP_OFFSET`) and only when an epoch source exists.
3057    fn age_lookup<M: RosMessage>(&self, topic: &str) -> Option<super::arena::AgeMon> {

3066    /// W3b.5 — install the `DeadlineAction::Fault` hook. Without one a
3067    /// fault-class deadline miss panics (watchdog-visible stop on
3068    /// embedded targets).
3069    /// Record one `spin_once` entry against the caller's intended cadence.
3070    ///
3071    /// Late is `(now - last_entry) - timeout`, clamped at zero: arriving early
3072    /// is not jitter, it is a poll that had nothing to wait for. A zero
3073    /// timeout claims no cadence and is skipped entirely, which keeps
3074    /// `Future::wait`-style busy spins out of the statistic.
3075    fn record_release_jitter(&mut self, timeout: core::time::Duration) {
3076        // phase-474 I7 -- the violation reporter's own time since the last
3077        // sample is not a late release (see `flush_violation_reports`). Taken
3078        // first, so a spin that judges nothing does not carry it forward.
3079        let report_us = core::mem::take(&mut self.violations.reports.debt_us);
3080        // A declared cadence wins over the timeout: see
3081        // `spin_nominal_declared_us` for why they are different quantities.
3082        let nominal_us = if self.spin_nominal_declared_us != 0 {
3083            self.spin_nominal_declared_us
3084        } else {
3085            timeout.as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64
3086        };
3087        if nominal_us == 0 {
3088            return;
3089        }
3090        let Some(now) = self.now_us() else {
3091            return;
3092        };
3093        self.spin_nominal_us = nominal_us;
3094        if let Some(last) = self.last_spin_entry_us {
3095            let interval = now.saturating_sub(last).saturating_sub(report_us);
3096            self.total_wakes = self.total_wakes.saturating_add(1);
3097            if let Some(late) = interval.checked_sub(nominal_us)
3098                && late > 0
3099            {
3100                self.late_wakes = self.late_wakes.saturating_add(1);
3101                if late > self.max_release_jitter_us {
3102                    self.max_release_jitter_us = late;
3103                }
3104            }
3105        }
3106        self.last_spin_entry_us = Some(now);
3107    }
3108
3109    /// Release-jitter statistics from the spin loop: worst lateness in
3110    /// microseconds, the number of wakes that were already late, and the
3111    /// number of wakes total.
3112    ///
3113    /// The maximum is the figure of merit, and the ratio is what tells the
3114    /// two failures apart: one late wake in ten thousand is a glitch, ten
3115    /// thousand in ten thousand means the period cannot be met at all.
3116    ///
3117    /// Zero on a build with no clock -- `spin_period` refuses to run at all
3118    /// there (issue 0709), so there is nothing to have measured.
3119    pub fn release_jitter(&self) -> (u64, u32, u32) {
3120        (
3121            self.max_release_jitter_us,
3122            self.late_wakes,
3123            self.total_wakes,
3124        )
3125    }
3126
3127    /// Reset the release-jitter statistics. For monitoring code that logs
3128    /// and clears per window, so a single early outlier does not pin the
3129    /// maximum for the life of the process.
3130    pub fn clear_release_jitter_stats(&mut self) {
3131        self.max_release_jitter_us = 0;
3132        self.late_wakes = 0;
3133        self.total_wakes = 0;
3134        self.last_spin_entry_us = None;
3135        self.jitter_reported_us = 0;
3136    }

3139        self.fault_fn = Some(f);

3142    /// Issue #515 — warn about periods the spin cadence cannot express.
3143    ///
3144    /// A timer fires on the first spin at or after its period elapses, so
3145    /// a period that is not an integer multiple of the executor's spin
3146    /// period lands on the spin grid instead of the declared cadence: a
3147    /// 33 ms timer on a 5 ms spin alternates 35 ms / 30 ms, mean 33.0.
3148    /// The rate is preserved and no activation is dropped, so every
3149    /// runtime rule is (correctly) silent — the jitter stays invisible
3150    /// until someone measures cadence on target.
3151    ///
3152    /// Runs ONCE, on the first spin carrying a non-zero timeout, because
3153    /// that timeout is where the tier's declared spin period becomes
3154    /// visible down here. A resolve-time diagnostic would be better
3155    /// still — the toolchain holds both numbers before the image is
3156    /// built — but this backstop needs no board or codegen change and
3157    /// catches hand-written spin loops too.
3158    /// phase-436 W1 (issue 1192) — how long the executor may park, in
3159    /// microseconds, given the caller's budget.
3160    ///
3161    /// The park used to be bounded by the caller's timeout narrowed by exactly
3162    /// one input, the BACKEND's `next_deadline_ms`. A registered timer is a
3163    /// deadline the EXECUTOR owns, and nothing let it shorten the sleep — so
3164    /// `spin_default`'s 50 ms slept straight past a 10 ms timer, and the
3165    /// activations then arrived in the burst issue 0505 describes.
3166    ///
3167    /// This is the `min` over the deadline sources phase-436 names. The
3168    /// caller's budget is always a member, so the result is never unbounded
3169    /// and never zero-by-omission: with no timers registered the budget
3170    /// stands, which keeps a long idle wait a wait rather than a poll.
3171    ///
3172    /// Distinct from issue 0515's audit, which warns that a period does not
3173    /// divide the spin grid. That takes the grid as given; this moves it.
3174    ///
3175    /// `#[cfg(test)]`-gated (matching `mod tests`'s own gate in `mod.rs`):
3176    /// production code calls `next_wake_bound_attributed_us` directly to get
3177    /// the source alongside the bound, so this `.0`-only convenience has no
3178    /// caller outside the test module and is dead code in any build that
3179    /// does not compile it (every `cargo check`/`cargo doc`, and `cargo test
3180    /// --features rmw-cffi`, which excludes `mod tests` too).
3181    #[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
3182    pub(crate) fn next_wake_bound_us(&self, budget_us: u64) -> u64 {
3183        self.next_wake_bound_attributed_us(budget_us, None).0
3184    }
3185
3186    /// phase-436 W6 — contribute a deadline source.
3187    ///
3188    /// The core never names an RTOS: a port registers `k_poll`, `epoll`, a
3189    /// queue set or a device ISR here, and the executor only ever asks "when
3190    /// will you next need me?".
3191    ///
3192    /// Refuses past capacity rather than dropping silently. A source that was
3193    /// quietly discarded would leave the executor sleeping past a deadline it
3194    /// had been told about, which is the failure this whole phase exists to
3195    /// remove.
3196    pub fn register_wake_source(
3197        &mut self,
3198        next: NextDeadlineFn,
3199        ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
3200    ) -> Result<WakeSourceId, NodeError> {
3201        if self.wake_source_count >= MAX_WAKE_SOURCES {
3202            return Err(NodeError::ExecutorFull);
3203        }
3204        let idx = self.wake_source_count;
3205        self.wake_sources[idx] = Some(WakeSourceSlot { next, ctx });
3206        self.wake_source_count += 1;
3207        Ok(WakeSourceId::Platform(idx as u8))
3208    }
3209
3210    /// Install THE thing that blocks. Singular by nature — only one primitive
3211    /// can actually wait — so this replaces whatever was there.
3212    /// `granularity_us` is the finest park this primitive can actually
3213    /// express. The port states it because only the port knows: the ABI
3214    /// signature is not the limit — an RTOS tick is a second, coarser one, and
3215    /// a timespec primitive is a finer one.
3216    pub fn set_park_primitive(
3217        &mut self,
3218        park: ParkUntilFn,
3219        ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
3220        granularity_us: u64,
3221    ) {
3222        self.park_primitive = Some((park, ctx));
3223        self.park_granularity_declared_us = granularity_us;
3224    }
3225
3226    /// The wake primitive a port must hand its `ParkUntilFn` as `ctx`, or NULL
3227    /// when this build has none.
3228    ///
3229    /// phase-436 W7 — a park that waits on its own fresh object is NOT
3230    /// breakable by the backend's listener, and installing one makes latency
3231    /// worse: once a port has parked, the transport drain drops to
3232    /// non-blocking, so an unbreakable park sleeps out its full deadline with
3233    /// data already waiting. Waiting on THIS object keeps the async break.
3234    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
3235    pub fn wake_raw_ptr(&self) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
3236        match self.node_wake.as_ref() {
3237            Some(w) => w.raw_ptr(),
3238            None => core::ptr::null_mut(),
3239        }
3240    }
3241
3242    /// Whether a platform park primitive is installed.
3243    pub fn has_park_primitive(&self) -> bool {
3244        self.park_primitive.is_some()
3245    }
3246
3247    /// The bound and the source that produced it: the `min` over every
3248    /// deadline source, with the caller's budget as an ordinary member.
3249    ///
3250    /// The budget being a member is what makes the result never unbounded and
3251    /// never zero-by-omission, and it is why "no sources registered" needs no
3252    /// special case.
3253    pub(crate) fn next_wake_bound_attributed_us(
3254        &self,
3255        budget_us: u64,
3256        session_us: Option<u64>,
3257    ) -> (u64, WakeSourceId) {
3258        let mut best = (budget_us, WakeSourceId::CallerBudget);
3259
3260        // The backend's next internal event is a MEMBER, not a pre-cap. It was
3261        // folded into the budget upstream, which meant a park the session
3262        // actually won reported `CallerBudget` — the attribution named the
3263        // wrong source, and "why did we wake" is the question attribution
3264        // exists to answer.
3265        if let Some(s) = session_us
3266            && s < best.0
3267        {
3268            best = (s, WakeSourceId::Session);
3269        }
3270
3271        if let Some(timer_us) = self.next_timer_deadline_us()
3272            && timer_us < best.0
3273        {
3274            best = (timer_us, WakeSourceId::Timer);
3275        }
3276
3277        for (i, slot) in self.wake_sources.iter().enumerate() {
3278            let Some(slot) = slot else { continue };
3279            // SAFETY: the callback and ctx were supplied together by the port
3280            // through `register_wake_source` and outlive the executor by its
3281            // contract; the call takes no ownership.
3282            let due = unsafe { (slot.next)(slot.ctx) };
3283            // `u64::MAX` is "nothing pending" — an async source spells itself
3284            // this way and breaks the park by signalling instead.
3285            if due != u64::MAX && due < best.0 {
3286                best = (due, WakeSourceId::Platform(i as u8));
3287            }
3288        }
3289
3290        best
3291    }
3292
3293    /// phase-436 — the bound the last park used, and which source won it.
3294    pub fn last_park(&self) -> (u64, WakeSourceId) {
3295        (self.last_park_bound_us, self.last_park_source)
3296    }
3297
3298    /// phase-436 W2 — the park the platform was actually asked for, after
3299    /// rounding the request up to an expressible value.
3300    ///
3301    /// Differs from `last_park().0` exactly when the request did not land on
3302    /// the platform's grid. Both are reported because a cadence that cannot be
3303    /// waited in must not be presented as if it were met.
3304    pub fn last_park_achieved_us(&self) -> u64 {
3305        self.last_park_achieved_us
3306    }
3307
3308    /// phase-436 W3 (issue 1194) — the granularity the release-jitter
3309    /// measurement was actually made at, in microseconds.
3310    ///
3311    /// The jitter statistic is reported in microseconds, but the mechanism
3312    /// that PACES the loop decides how fine it can honestly be, and there are
3313    /// two mechanisms:
3314    ///
3315    /// * **No declared cadence** — the loop is paced by the blocking wait
3316    ///   itself, so it cannot come round more precisely than one park granule.
3317    ///   Reporting µs there is precision the wait cannot deliver.
3318    /// * **A declared cadence** (`set_spin_nominal_us`) — the caller paces
3319    ///   itself, as nros-cpp's tiers do with `platform_sleep_us` between
3320    ///   spins. That sleep is finer than the wait, so the measurement really
3321    ///   is good to a microsecond and coarsening it would understate it.
3322    ///
3323    /// Reported rather than applied: this does not change what the monitor
3324    /// judges, because silently coarsening a bound could mask real lateness.
3325    /// It says what the number is worth.
3326    pub fn release_jitter_granularity_us(&self) -> u64 {
3327        if self.spin_nominal_declared_us != 0 {
3328            1
3329        } else {
3330            self.park_granularity_us()
3331        }
3332    }
3333
3334    /// The finest park this build can actually express, in microseconds.
3335    ///
3336    /// Comes from the INSTALLED primitive, because only the port knows. The
3337    /// exported ABI signature is not the limit in either direction (issue
3338    /// 1242):
3339    ///
3340    /// * an RTOS tick is a COARSER limit — ThreadX pins
3341    ///   `TX_TIMER_TICKS_PER_SECOND = 100`, a 10 ms tick, so a 1 ms park is not
3342    ///   achievable there however the ABI is spelled;
3343    /// * a timespec primitive is a FINER one — POSIX's `sem_timedwait` and
3344    ///   `pthread_cond_timedwait` are nanosecond-native, and only the
3345    ///   `uint32_t timeout_ms` signature floors them at a millisecond.
3346    ///
3347    /// This was a hardcoded `1_000` justified by "every `nros_platform_wake_*`
3348    /// port takes `uint32_t timeout_ms`". That was right for FreeRTOS by
3349    /// coincidence and wrong for the other two, and it made the W3 jitter
3350    /// report over-claim on ThreadX — the failure W3 exists to prevent,
3351    /// reproduced one layer below W3 in its own dependency.
3352    ///
3353    /// With nothing installed the fallback is 1 ms, which IS the honest floor
3354    /// of the `wake_wait_ms` ABI every port exports today.
3355    pub fn park_granularity_us(&self) -> u64 {
3356        if self.park_granularity_declared_us != 0 {
3357            self.park_granularity_declared_us
3358        } else {
3359            1_000
3360        }
3361    }
3362
3363    pub(crate) fn round_park_up_us(&self, requested_us: u64) -> u64 {
3364        if requested_us == 0 {
3365            return 0;
3366        }
3367        let g = self.park_granularity_us();
3368        if g <= 1 {
3369            return requested_us;
3370        }
3371        requested_us.div_ceil(g).saturating_mul(g)
3372    }
3373
3374    /// Microseconds until the soonest live timer is due, or `None` when no
3375    /// timer is pending.
3376    ///
3377    /// A timer that is cancelled, or a one-shot that already fired, owes
3378    /// nothing and must not hold the park short — otherwise the executor keeps
3379    /// waking on a deadline nobody is waiting for.
3380    ///
3381    /// So does a timer whose remainder is not WALL microseconds
3382    /// ([`TimerClockSource::remaining_is_wall_time`], issue 1321): the number
3383    /// this returns is handed to the port's park primitive, so a ROS-time
3384    /// timer's simulated remainder would be a units error — and on a paused
3385    /// `/clock` a frozen one, waking the image once per timer period forever.
3386    /// Its wake source is a `/clock` message, which reaches `drive_io` like
3387    /// any sample.
3388    pub(crate) fn next_timer_deadline_us(&self) -> Option<u64> {
3389        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
3390        let mut soonest: Option<u64> = None;
3391        for meta in self.entries.iter().flatten() {
3392            if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) {
3393                continue;
3394            }
3395            // SAFETY: a Timer entry's arena slot holds a `TimerEntry<F>`, whose
3396            // leading layout is `TimerHeader` — the same projection
3397            // `audit_spin_quantization` relies on.
3398            let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
3399            if header.cancelled || header.period_us == 0 {
3400                continue;
3401            }
3402            if header.oneshot && header.fired {
3403                continue;
3404            }
3405            // Issue 1321 — the park is WALL microseconds, so only a timer
3406            // whose own clock runs in them may bound it.
3407            if !header.clock_source.remaining_is_wall_time() {
3408                continue;
3409            }
3410            // Already due: the bound is zero, and no other timer can beat it.
3411            let remaining = header.period_us.saturating_sub(header.elapsed_us);
3412            soonest = Some(match soonest {
3413                Some(cur) => cur.min(remaining),
3414                None => remaining,
3415            });
3416            if remaining == 0 {
3417                break;
3418            }
3419        }
3420        soonest
3421    }
3422
3423    fn audit_spin_quantization(&mut self, spin_us: u64) {
3424        if spin_us == 0 {
3425            return;
3426        }
3427        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
3428        for i in 0..self.entries.len() {
3429            let Some(meta) = self.entries[i].as_ref() else {
3430                continue;
3431            };
3432            if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) {
3433                continue;
3434            }
3435            // SAFETY: a Timer entry's arena slot holds a `TimerEntry<F>`,
3436            // whose leading layout is `TimerHeader`.
3437            let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
3438            let period_us = header.period_us;
3439            let Some((early_us, late_us)) =
3440                spin_quantization_span(header.clock_source, period_us, spin_us)
3441            else {
3442                continue;
3443            };
3444            nros_log::log_warn!(
3445                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
3446                "timer period {} us is not a multiple of the {} us spin period: activations will alternate between {} us and {} us (mean cadence preserved)",
3447                period_us,
3448                spin_us,
3449                early_us,
3450                late_us
3451            );
3452        }
3453    }

3455    /// Issue #514 — whether the executor logs each violation as it is

3459    /// way via [`Self::drain_violations`]; the ring is unaffected

3465    /// phase-474 I1 -- the drain-and-report hook: at the end of every spin,
3466    /// drain the ring and log each entry with its sequence number and the
3467    /// `total` / `dropped` counters (`contract violation #N: <rule> <fqn>

3481    /// before any drain took them.

3493    /// `total - dropped - pending` is how many drains have taken.

3499    /// Draining clears the ring. Call between spins, never from a callback.
3500    pub fn drain_violations(&mut self, mut f: impl FnMut(&super::monitor::Violation)) {
3501        self.violations.drain(|_, v| f(v));
3502    }
