3511    /// phase-474 I2 -- choose when this executor's contract monitors arm,
3512    /// overriding the build default (`NROS_MONITOR_ARM_ON_CALL`,
3513    /// `NROS_MONITOR_ARM_GRACE_MS`). Call before the first spin (an
3514    /// `arm_monitors` made before it is undone by this); after the first spin
3515    /// an executor that already armed stays armed.
3516    ///
3517    /// `on_call`: wait for [`Self::arm_monitors`] or
3518    /// [`super::monitor::request_monitor_arming`] (`nros_monitors_arm()`).
3519    /// `grace_ms`: arm anyway that long after the first spin (0 = never by
3520    /// deadline; with `on_call == false`, 0 means "at the first spin").
3521    pub fn set_monitor_arming(&mut self, on_call: bool, grace_ms: u32) {
3522        let v = &mut self.violations.counts;
3523        v.arm_on_call = on_call;
3524        v.arm_grace_ms = grace_ms;
3525        if !v.spun {
3526            // Before the first spin, "armed" is just the policy's answer (no
3527            // rule has run yet); the first spin counts the arming once.
3528            v.armed = super::monitor::MonitorArming { on_call, grace_ms }.armed_at_first_spin();
3529        }
3530    }
3531
3532    /// phase-474 I2 -- the application says its start-up is over: this
3533    /// executor's monitors start judging now. Idempotent.
3534    ///
3535    /// Judgement restarts at arming: every rate/age/silence window reopens,
3536    /// a latency or age measured before arming is discarded, the release-
3537    /// jitter statistics are cleared (so the figure after RUN is RUN's), and a
3538    /// stack low-water mark already past the declared minimum is reported
3539    /// again, because stack depth reached at start-up is a real fault, not
3540    /// start-up noise.
3541    pub fn arm_monitors(&mut self) {
3542        self.arm_now("the application armed them");
3543    }
3544
3545    /// phase-474 I2 -- whether this executor's monitors are armed.
3546    pub fn monitors_armed(&self) -> bool {
3547        self.violations.counts.armed
3548    }
3549
3550    /// phase-474 I2 -- verdicts reached before the monitors armed: counted,
3551    /// never stored, logged, sunk or traced.
3552    pub fn violations_suppressed_before_arm(&self) -> u32 {
3553        self.violations.counts.suppressed_before_arm
3554    }
3555
3556    fn arm_now(&mut self, why: &str) {
3557        if self.violations.counts.armed {
3558            return;
3559        }
3560        self.violations.counts.armed = true;
3561        for st in self.monitor_states.iter_mut() {
3562            *st = super::monitor::MonitorState::default();
3563        }
3564        for st in self.age_states.iter_mut() {
3565            *st = super::monitor::AgeState::default();
3566        }
3567        for spec in self.monitor_table.iter() {
3568            spec.cell
3569                .max_latency_us
3570                .store(0, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
3571        }
3572        for spec in self.age_table.iter() {
3573            spec.cell
3574                .max_age_ms
3575                .store(0, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
3576            spec.cell
3577                .takes
3578                .store(0, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
3579        }
3580        self.clear_release_jitter_stats();
3581        self.stack_headroom_reported = usize::MAX;
3582        self.stack_headroom_last_check_us = None;
3583        // Counted once per executor: here once it has spun, else by the first
3584        // spin (which counts an executor that is armed by then either way).
3585        #[cfg(nros_boot_report)]
3586        if self.violations.counts.spun {
3587            super::monitor::NROS_VIOLATION_RECORD
3588                .armed
3589                .fetch_add(1, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
3590        }
3591        nros_log::log_info!(
3592            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
3593            "contract monitors armed ({}); {} verdict(s) before arming suppressed",
3594            why,
3595            self.violations.counts.suppressed_before_arm
3596        );
3597    }
3598
3599    /// phase-474 I2 -- once per spin, before any rule runs: note the first
3600    /// spin, and arm when the policy says so.
3601    fn update_monitor_arming(&mut self, now_us: Option<u64>) {
3602        // Milliseconds in a wrapping `u32`, like the silence rule's lease
3603        // (`AgeState::last_take_ms`): this state is inline in the `Executor`
3604        // value, whose size is budgeted (issue 0961).
3605        let now_ms = now_us.map(|us| (us / 1_000) as u32);
3606        let v = &mut self.violations.counts;
3607        if !v.spun {
3608            v.spun = true;
3609            v.first_spin_ms = now_ms.unwrap_or(0);
3610            if v.armed {
3611                // Armed from the start (the default), or by a call made before
3612                // the first spin: count it in the record so a reader sees how
3613                // many executors are judging.
3614                #[cfg(nros_boot_report)]
3615                super::monitor::NROS_VIOLATION_RECORD
3616                    .armed
3617                    .fetch_add(1, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
3618                return;
3619            }
3620            if (super::monitor::MonitorArming {
3621                on_call: v.arm_on_call,
3622                grace_ms: v.arm_grace_ms,
3623            })
3624            .armed_at_first_spin()
3625            {
3626                self.arm_now("at the first spin");
3627                return;
3628            }
3629        }
3630        if v.armed {
3631            return;
3632        }
3633        if super::monitor::arm_requests() != v.arm_requests_seen {
3634            self.arm_now("the application asked: nros_monitors_arm");
3635            return;
3636        }
3637        let grace_ms = v.arm_grace_ms;
3638        if grace_ms == 0 {
3639            return;
3640        }
3641        match now_ms {
3642            Some(now) if now.wrapping_sub(v.first_spin_ms) >= grace_ms => {
3643                self.arm_now("the grace period after the first spin elapsed");
3644            }
3645            // No clock: a grace period cannot elapse, and waiting forever would
3646            // leave the image unmonitored. Arm rather than guess a duration.
3647            None if !v.arm_on_call => {
3648                self.arm_now("no clock to time the grace period");
3649            }
3650            _ => {}
3651        }
3652    }
3653
3654    /// Issue 1635 -- hand every stored violation to `sink`, beside the log line
3655    /// (issue 0514's floor) and the ring push.
3656    ///
3657    /// phase-474 I7 -- not at detection any more: the verdict is queued and
3658    /// leaves from `Executor::flush_violation_reports` at the end of a spin with
3659    /// slack, so the report never costs the dispatch it judges.
3660    ///
3661    /// Before this nothing in a generated image drained the ring, so the log
3662    /// line was the only output and `/diagnostics` stayed silent on every C
3663    /// and C++ road. A report point the RUNTIME owns reaches every road at
3664    /// once — every board's spin loop goes through the executor — where one
3665    /// per entry template would have to be rebuilt for each board runner. The
3666    /// ring is still filled, so an application (or a fixture) that drains it
3667    /// with [`Self::drain_violations`] sees exactly what it did before.
3668    /// `None` removes the sink.
3669    ///
3670    /// # Safety
3671    /// `ctx` must stay valid for every call of the sink until it is replaced
3672    /// or this executor is dropped (see [`super::monitor::ViolationSink`]).
3673    pub unsafe fn set_violation_sink(
3674        &mut self,
3675        sink: Option<(super::monitor::ViolationSink, *mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
3676    ) {
3677        self.violations.sink = sink.map(|(f, ctx)| (f, ctx as usize));
3678        if self.violations.sink.is_none() {
3679            // Nothing is left to send them to.
3680            self.violations.reports.pending.clear();
3681            self.violations.reports.since_us = None;
3682        }
3683    }
3684
3685    /// phase-474 I7 -- hand the queued verdicts to the sink, if this is a slot
3686    /// for it. Called at the end of every spin, after its dispatches and its
3687    /// rules, so the report never runs inside the tick being judged.
3688    ///
3689    /// A slot is a spin end whose next timer is due no sooner than the last
3690    /// report took (`ReportQueue::last_cost_us`; 0 before the first report, so
3691    /// the first goes at the first spin end with no timer already due), or
3692    /// any spin end once the oldest pending verdict has waited
3693    /// [`REPORT_DEFER_MAX_US`](super::monitor::REPORT_DEFER_MAX_US). Without a
3694    /// clock there is nothing to measure slack with, so every spin end is a
3695    /// slot. The sink takes as many as it coalesces into one message; the rest
3696    /// wait for the next slot.
3697    ///
3698    /// The time the sink takes is the reporter's own and is stated by
3699    /// [`Self::violation_report_cost_us`]; the release-jitter rule does not
3700    /// charge it to the spin's cadence (it is not a late release of any
3701    /// application work), which is what used to turn one verdict into a
3702    /// `release-jitter-runtime` verdict of its own on the safety island.
3703    pub(crate) fn flush_violation_reports(&mut self) {
3704        let Some((sink, ctx)) = self.violations.sink else {
3705            return;
3706        };
3707        if self.violations.reports.pending.is_empty() {
3708            return;
3709        }
3710        let now = self.now_us();
3711        if let Some(now) = now {
3712            let since = *self.violations.reports.since_us.get_or_insert(now);
3713            let overdue = now.saturating_sub(since) >= super::monitor::REPORT_DEFER_MAX_US;
3714            let cost = self.violations.reports.last_cost_us as u64;
3715            let slack = match self.next_timer_deadline_us() {
3716                None => true,
3717                Some(remaining) => remaining > 0 && remaining >= cost,
3718            };
3719            if !slack && !overdue {
3720                return;
3721            }
3722        }
3723        // SAFETY: `Executor::set_violation_sink`'s contract -- `ctx` is valid
3724        // for every call until the sink is replaced or the executor dropped.
3725        let taken = unsafe {
3726            sink(
3727                ctx as *mut core::ffi::c_void,
3728                &self.violations.reports.pending[..],
3729            )
3730        };
3731        let q = &mut self.violations.reports;
3732        if taken == 0 {
3733            // The sink counted its failure; drop the oldest so a report that
3734            // can never be sent does not stall the queue. It stays in the ring
3735            // and the record.
3736            q.pending.remove(0);
3737            q.failed = q.failed.saturating_add(1);
3738        } else {
3739            let n = taken.min(q.pending.len());
3740            for _ in 0..n {
3741                q.pending.remove(0);
3742            }
3743        }
3744        q.since_us = None;
3745        if let (Some(t0), Some(t1)) = (now, self.now_us()) {
3746            let q = &mut self.violations.reports;
3747            let cost = t1.saturating_sub(t0);
3748            q.last_cost_us = cost.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32;
3749            q.max_cost_us = q.max_cost_us.max(q.last_cost_us);
3750            q.debt_us = q.debt_us.saturating_add(cost);
3751        }
3752    }
3753
3754    /// phase-474 I7 -- what handing verdicts to the violation sink has cost
3755    /// this executor: `(last_us, max_us, pending, overflowed)`. `overflowed`
3756    /// counts verdicts evicted from the report queue by newer ones before a
3757    /// slot came (they are still in the ring and the SWD record).
3758    pub fn violation_report_cost_us(&self) -> (u32, u32, usize, u32) {
3759        let q = &self.violations.reports;
3760        (q.last_cost_us, q.max_cost_us, q.pending.len(), q.overflowed)
3761    }
3762
3763    /// THE monotonic-µs read. phase-359 W4 — every consumer goes through here.
3764    ///
3765    /// Before this there were FIVE spellings of "what time is it": this one,
3766    /// `last_spin_end: Instant`, and two ad-hoc `static EPOCH: OnceLock<Instant>`
3767    /// blocks — plus `PlatformClock`, which nothing called because `Executor` is
3768    /// deliberately non-generic and the trait's methods are associated fns.
3769    ///
3770    /// `None` means no clock is available (no_std with no injected hook).
3771    /// Callers must degrade, not guess: a missing clock is why the sporadic
3772    /// refill and the major-frame phase behaved differently on no_std.
3773    fn now_us(&mut self) -> Option<u64> {
3774        self.clock_us_fn.map(|clock| clock())
3775    }
3776
3777    /// Run the rate/latency/age checks over the baked tables (single
3778    /// branch each when empty).
3779    fn run_contract_monitors(&mut self) {
3780        if !self.monitor_table.is_empty()
3781            && let Some(now_us) = self.now_us()
3782        {
3783            {
3784                for (i, spec) in self
3785                    .monitor_table
3786                    .iter()
3787                    .take(super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS)
3788                    .enumerate()
3789                {
3790                    if let Some(v) =
3791                        super::monitor::check_rate(spec, &mut self.monitor_states[i], now_us)
3792                    {
3793                        self.violations.record(v);
3794                    }
3795                    if let Some(v) =
3796                        super::monitor::check_latency(spec, &mut self.monitor_states[i])
3797                    {
3798                        self.violations.record(v);
3799                    }
3800                }
3801            }
3802        }
3803        if !self.age_table.is_empty() {
3804            // phase-462 W2 -- the age loop needs the clock now: `silence-runtime`
3805            // judges how long an endpoint has taken NOTHING, and `None` (a
3806            // build with no clock) makes that rule abstain rather than guess.
3807            // Read before the loop because the borrow of `age_states` below
3808            // outlives the `&mut self` the reader wants.
3809            let now_us = self.now_us();
3810            for (i, spec) in self
3811                .age_table
3812                .iter()
3813                .take(super::monitor::MAX_AGE_MONITORS)
3814                .enumerate()
3815            {
3816                if let Some(v) = super::monitor::check_age(spec, &mut self.age_states[i], now_us) {
3817                    self.violations.record(v);
3818                }
3819            }
3820        }
3821    }
3822
3823    /// Issue #505 — report activations dropped by
3824    /// [`TimerOverrunPolicy::Skip`](super::arena::TimerOverrunPolicy)
3825    /// since the last check.
3826    ///
3827    /// Unlike the rate/age/latency rules this needs no baked spec table:
3828    /// every periodic timer counts its own overruns, and a dropped
3829    /// activation is a contract failure for any declared period. It runs
3830    /// on the same tick so violations land in the same ring the entry
3831    /// glue drains.
3832    /// Declare the minimum stack headroom this executor's thread must keep,
3833    /// in bytes. `0` (the default) disables the `stack-headroom-runtime`
3834    /// rule.
3835    ///
3836    /// Set by the entry that spawned the thread, because it is the only
3837    /// party that knows what stack it handed over: the executor never sees
3838    /// `stack_bytes`, and no portable query returns a task's total stack, so
3839    /// neither an absolute floor nor a percentage can be inferred here.
3840    /// Declare how often this executor's loop intends to come round, in
3841    /// microseconds. `0` (the default) falls back to the `spin_once` timeout.
3842    ///
3843    /// Needed because a driver's pacing and its blocking bound are separate
3844    /// numbers. nros-cpp's tier loops sleep `spin_period_us` between spins but
3845    /// pass a fixed 10 ms timeout, so the release-jitter rule judged every
3846    /// tier against 10 ms regardless of what the contract declared -- too lax
3847    /// for a 1 ms tier and far too strict for a 30 ms one.
3848    pub fn set_spin_nominal_us(&mut self, us: u64) {
3849        self.spin_nominal_declared_us = us;
3850    }
3851
3852    pub fn set_min_stack_headroom_bytes(&mut self, bytes: usize) {
3853        self.min_stack_headroom_bytes = bytes;
3854        // phase-436 E4 — a new bound is checked on the next spin, not up to an
3855        // interval later.
3856        self.stack_headroom_last_check_us = None;
3857        // phase-436 E3 — `check_stack_headroom_rule` treats a 0 from the port as
3858        // "not instrumented" and skips, which is right for the rule and wrong
3859        // for the reader: an armed rule that can never judge reports nothing,
3860        // exactly like one that judged and found the stack healthy. Ask the
3861        // port once, here. Entries set the bound at boot on the thread it
3862        // describes, so the answer is about the right stack and the warning
3863        // lands once per tier, next to the tier's other boot lines.
3864        self.stack_headroom_blind = bytes != 0 && nros_platform_api::stack_unused_bytes() == 0;
3865        if self.stack_headroom_blind {
3866            nros_log::log_warn!(
3867                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
3868                "stack-headroom-runtime: a {} B minimum is set but this port reports no stack \
3869                 data, so the rule will never check (Zephyr: enable CONFIG_INIT_STACKS)",
3870                bytes
3871            );
3872        }
3873    }
3874
3875    /// phase-436 E3 — whether `stack-headroom-runtime` is armed on a port that
3876    /// cannot measure, and so will never report a violation.
3877    ///
3878    /// `true` means the rule's silence is not evidence of headroom. Zephyr
3879    /// answers only with `CONFIG_INIT_STACKS && CONFIG_THREAD_STACK_INFO`;
3880    /// POSIX never does.
3881    pub fn stack_headroom_blind(&self) -> bool {
3882        self.stack_headroom_blind
3883    }
3884
3885    /// Report a spin thread that has come closer to the end of its stack
3886    /// than `set_min_stack_headroom_bytes` allows.
3887    ///
3888    /// Runs on the same tick as the other rules and feeds the same ring.
3889    /// Queries the port at most once per `STACK_HEADROOM_CHECK_INTERVAL_US`
3890    /// (phase-436 E4): on a painted Zephyr stack the query scans every unused
3891    /// byte, so an every-spin query put that scan inside the control loop.
3892    /// Nothing at all when no minimum was declared.
3893    fn check_stack_headroom_rule(&mut self) {
3894        if self.min_stack_headroom_bytes == 0 {
3895            return;
3896        }
3897        self.stack_headroom_spins_since_check =
3898            self.stack_headroom_spins_since_check.saturating_add(1);
3899        let now_us = self.now_us();
3900        if !super::monitor::stack_headroom_check_due(
3901            now_us,
3902            self.stack_headroom_last_check_us,
3903            self.stack_headroom_spins_since_check,
3904        ) {
3905            return;
3906        }
3907        self.stack_headroom_last_check_us = Some(now_us.unwrap_or(0));
3908        self.stack_headroom_spins_since_check = 0;
3909        self.stack_headroom_checks = self.stack_headroom_checks.saturating_add(1);
3910        let unused = nros_platform_api::stack_unused_bytes();
3911        // 0 means the port does not instrument stacks, not that the stack is
3912        // full. Reporting a violation there would be a fault invented from an
3913        // absence of data.
3914        if unused == 0 {
3915            return;
3916        }
3917        if let Some(v) = super::monitor::check_stack_headroom(
3918            unused,
3919            self.min_stack_headroom_bytes,
3920            &mut self.stack_headroom_reported,
3921        ) {
3922            self.violations.record(v);
3923        }
3924    }
3925
3926    /// AUTOSAR-style ALIVE supervision: report a SchedContext that produced
3927    /// no dispatch at all over a full window while declaring a period.
3928    ///
3929    /// Every other rule here fires when something happens and is wrong. This
3930    /// one fires when nothing happens, which is the failure a watchdog
3931    /// exists for and the one `rate-hierarchy-runtime` cannot see: that rule
3932    /// counts publishes on an endpoint, so a callback that stops firing while
3933    /// its topic is published from elsewhere leaves it satisfied.
3934    fn check_alive_supervision(&mut self) {
3935        let Some(now_us) = self.now_us() else {
3936            // No clock, no windows. Silence here is honest: the rule cannot
3937            // tell a stalled context from a fast one without time.
3938            return;
3939        };
3940        let n = self.alive_slots.len().min(self.sched_contexts.len());
3941        for i in 0..n {
3942            let period_us = match self.sched_contexts[i].as_ref() {
3943                Some(sc) => sc.period_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get() as u64).unwrap_or(0),
3944                None => continue,
3945            };
3946            let slot = &mut self.alive_slots[i];
3947            if let Some(v) =
3948                super::monitor::check_alive(period_us, slot.dispatches, &mut slot.state, now_us)
3949            {
3950                self.violations.record(v);
3951            }
3952        }
3953    }
3954
3955    /// Issue #515 — report a spin wake a whole period late.
3956    ///
3957    /// Runs on the same tick as `check_timer_overruns` and feeds the same
3958    /// ring, so the entry glue drains it with the other rules and no caller
3959    /// needs to know this one exists. Like that rule it needs no spec table:
3960    /// the bound is the spin period the caller already passes in.
3961    fn check_release_jitter_rule(&mut self) {
3962        let (max_us, _late, _total) = self.release_jitter();
3963        let period_us = self.spin_nominal_us;
3964        if let Some(v) =
3965            super::monitor::check_release_jitter(max_us, &mut self.jitter_reported_us, period_us)
3966        {
3967            self.violations.record(v);
3968        }
3969    }
3970
3971    fn check_timer_overruns(&mut self) {
3972        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
3973        for i in 0..self.entries.len() {
3974            let Some(meta) = self.entries[i].as_ref() else {
3975                continue;
3976            };
3977            if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) {
3978                continue;
3979            }
3980            // SAFETY: a Timer entry's arena slot holds a `TimerEntry<F>`,
3981            // which shares its leading layout with `TimerHeader`. The
3982            // baseline lives in the header too, so this needs no state
3983            // parallel to `entries` (whose capacity is a runtime slice
3984            // length, not a const).
3985            let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
3986            if let Some(v) = super::monitor::check_timer_overrun(
3987                header.overruns,
3988                &mut header.overruns_reported,
3989                0,
3990            ) {
3991                self.violations.record(v);
3992            }
3993        }
3994    }
3995
3996    /// RFC-0052 / phase-296 W3a — replace the DEFAULT scheduling context
3997    /// (slot 0, the SC every unbound callback dispatches through).
3998    ///
3999    /// The run_tiers model runs one Executor per tier, so a tier-wide
4000    /// scheduling policy (`[tiers.<t>] class/budget_us/period_us` and the
4001    /// TT window) is exactly "this executor's default SC". Boards call
4002    /// this once, before entity creation; explicit per-handle/per-group
4003    /// bindings still take precedence (they never resolve to slot 0).
4004    ///
4005    /// Sporadic-class SCs get the same sibling `SporadicState` the
4006    /// `create_sched_context` path builds, so budget refill/exhaustion
4007    /// applies to the default queue too.
4008    pub fn set_default_sched_context(&mut self, sc: super::sched_context::SchedContext) {
4009        self.sched_contexts[0] = Some(sc);
4010        if matches!(sc.class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
4011            let budget = sc.budget_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
4012            let period = sc.period_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
4013            self.sporadic_states[0] =
4014                Some(super::sched_context::SporadicState::new(budget, period));
4015        } else {
4016            self.sporadic_states[0] = None;
4017        }
4018    }
4019
4020    /// Bind a registered callback to a scheduling context. The next
4021    /// `spin_once` cycle dispatches the callback through that SC's
4022    /// queue (FIFO bitmap or EDF heap). Phase 110.B.
4023    pub fn bind_handle_to_sched_context(
4024        &mut self,
4025        handle: HandleId,
4026        sc_id: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
4027    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
4028        let i = self.live_slot(handle);
4029        if i >= self.entries.len() {
4030            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
4031        }
4032        if self.entries[i].is_none() {
4033            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
4034        }
4035        let sc_idx = sc_id.0 as usize;
4036        if sc_idx >= self.sched_contexts.len() || self.sched_contexts[sc_idx].is_none() {
4037            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
4038        }
4039        self.sched_context_bindings[i] = sc_id;
4040        Ok(())
4041    }
4042
4043    /// Phase 110.F — opt in to per-callback OS-priority dispatch.
4044    /// Once registered, every `spin_once` cycle routes ready entries
4045    /// whose bound SC has `os_pri > 0` onto a worker thread the OS
4046    /// scheduler has elevated to that numeric priority. Workers are
4047    /// spawned lazily on first use and self-halt when the Executor
4048    /// drops.
4049    ///
4050    /// `apply_policy` is the same `fn(SchedPolicy) -> Result<(),
4051    /// SchedError>` shape `open_threaded` takes — keeps the
4052    /// Executor non-generic over Platform.
4053    ///
4054    /// Calling this with `apply_policy = noop` is fine for testing
4055    /// (workers spawn but don't actually elevate priority); real
4056    /// hard-RT use needs `CAP_SYS_NICE` on Linux or the equivalent
4057    /// kernel config on RTOSes.
4058    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "scheduler-os-priority"))]
4059    pub fn register_os_priority_dispatcher(
4060        &mut self,
4061        apply_policy: fn(
4062            nros_platform_api::SchedPolicy,
4063        ) -> Result<(), nros_platform_api::SchedError>,
4064    ) {
4065        self.os_priority_apply_policy = Some(apply_policy);
4066    }
4067
4068    /// Phase 110.G — enable time-triggered dispatch by setting the
4069    /// executor's major-frame length. Once set, every `spin_once`
4070    /// cycle gates dispatch through each entry's bound SC's
4071    /// `tt_window_offset_us` / `tt_window_duration_us` fields:
4072    /// dispatch only fires when the current monotonic time falls
4073    /// inside the window `[off, off + duration) mod major_frame`.
4074    ///
4075    /// `major_frame_us = 0` disables the TT gate (default state).
4076    /// Setting a non-zero major frame after callbacks are already
4077    /// registered is allowed — TT gates take effect on the next
4078    /// `spin_once` cycle.
4079    pub fn register_time_triggered_dispatcher(&mut self, major_frame_us: u32) {
4080        self.major_frame_us = major_frame_us;
4081    }
4082
4083    /// Phase 110.G — apply a declarative cyclic schedule.
4084    ///
4085    /// One-shot helper that wraps the underlying primitives:
4086    /// validates the schedule (`major_frame > 0`, no overlapping
4087    /// windows, every window fits inside the major frame), sets the
4088    /// executor's major-frame length, then materialises one
4089    /// `SchedContext` per window with `class = TimeTriggered` +
4090    /// the window's offset / duration. Returns the per-window
4091    /// [`SchedContextId`](crate::executor::sched_context::SchedContextId) array so callers can immediately
4092    /// `bind_handle_to_sched_context(handle, sc_id)` for their
4093    /// subscription / timer handles.
4094    ///
4095    /// `N` is the schedule's *declared* maximum window count;
4096    /// `schedule.window_count` gates how many SCs are actually
4097    /// created. Unused trailing slots return
4098    /// `SchedContextId::default()` (sentinel — callers must respect
4099    /// `window_count`).
4100    pub fn apply_time_triggered_schedule<const N: usize>(
4101        &mut self,
4102        schedule: &super::sched_context::TimeTriggeredSchedule<N>,
4103    ) -> Result<
4104        [super::sched_context::SchedContextId; N],
4105        super::sched_context::TimeTriggeredScheduleError,
4106    > {
4107        schedule.validate()?;
4108        self.major_frame_us = schedule.major_frame_us;
4109        // SC slot 0 is the auto-created default; reusing it as a
4110        // sentinel for unused trailing slots is safe because the
4111        // caller respects `schedule.window_count`.
4112        let mut ids: [super::sched_context::SchedContextId; N] =
4113            [super::sched_context::SchedContextId(0); N];
4114        for (i, window) in schedule.windows[..schedule.window_count].iter().enumerate() {
4115            // TT is not a scheduling class (phase-482 W6 deleted the
4116            // `SchedClass::TimeTriggered` variant): it is a per-SC *window gate* on top of
4117            // the existing class-based dispatch (Fifo here keeps
4118            // the EDF / Sporadic budgets out of the picture for
4119            // pure cyclic schedules). The window-gate fields set
4120            // below are what `spin_once`'s 110.G runtime gate
4121            // actually reads.
4122            let sc = super::sched_context::SchedContext {
4123                tt_window_offset_us: super::sched_context::OptUs::from_us(window.offset_us),
4124                tt_window_duration_us: super::sched_context::OptUs::from_us(window.duration_us),
4125                ..super::sched_context::SchedContext::new_fifo()
4126            };
4127            ids[i] = self.create_sched_context(sc).map_err(|_| {
4128                super::sched_context::TimeTriggeredScheduleError::WindowCountOverflow
4129            })?;
4130        }
4131        Ok(ids)
4132    }
4133
4134    /// Phase 110.E.b — register an ISR-driven refill timer for an
4135    /// already-created Sporadic SC. The caller invokes their
4136    /// platform's `PlatformTimer::create_periodic` with the returned
4137    /// `Arc<AtomicSporadicState>` as `user_data` and the
4138    /// `atomic_sporadic_refill_thunk` as the callback, then hands
4139    /// the resulting platform handle to this method via
4140    /// `OpaqueTimerHandle::new(handle, destroy_fn)`.
4141    ///
4142    /// The Executor stores both the Arc and the handle so Drop can
4143    /// clean them up. Calling this on a non-Sporadic SC returns
4144    /// `Err(InvalidSchedContextBinding)`.
4145    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
4146    pub fn register_sporadic_timer(
4147        &mut self,
4148        sc_id: super::sched_context::SchedContextId,
4149        timer: OpaqueTimerHandle,
4150    ) -> Result<portable_atomic_util::Arc<super::sched_context::AtomicSporadicState>, NodeError>
4151    {
4152        let i = sc_id.0 as usize;
4153        if i >= self.sched_contexts.len() {
4154            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
4155        }
4156        let sc = self.sched_contexts[i]
4157            .as_ref()
4158            .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
4159        if !matches!(sc.class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
4160            return Err(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding);
4161        }
4162        let budget = sc.budget_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
4163        let period = sc.period_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
4164        let state = portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(super::sched_context::AtomicSporadicState::new(
4165            budget, period,
4166        ));
4167        self.sporadic_atomic_states[i] = Some((portable_atomic_util::Arc::clone(&state), timer));
4168        Ok(state)
4169    }

4176        self.sched_contexts.get(sc_id.0 as usize)?.as_ref()

4244    /// Issue #52 — install the baked QoS-override table on one node. Every

4263    /// Phase 104.C.3 — resolve a session-slot index to a mutable
4264    /// session reference. Slot 0 = the Executor's primary session;
4265    /// slots 1..=N = the `extra_sessions` vec opened by
4266    /// `node_builder.rmw(name)` calls that named a backend
4267    /// different from the primary.
4268    pub(crate) fn session_at_mut(&mut self, idx: u8) -> Option<&mut session::ConcreteSession> {
4269        if idx == 0 {
4270            Some(&mut *self.session)
4271        } else {
4272            self.extra_sessions.get_mut((idx - 1) as usize)
4273        }
4274    }

4276    /// [`Self::session_at_mut`] plus a shared borrow of the remap table, for
4277    /// building a [`NodeHandle`] — which needs both at once, and gets them
4278    /// here as two disjoint field borrows rather than through two `&mut self`
4279    /// calls the borrow checker could not split.
4280    pub(crate) fn session_and_remaps_at_mut(
4281        &mut self,
4282        idx: u8,
4283    ) -> Option<(&mut session::ConcreteSession, &[Option<RemapRule>])> {
4284        let remaps = &self.remap_table[..self.remap_len];
4285        let session = if idx == 0 {
4286            Some(&mut *self.session)
4287        } else {
4288            self.extra_sessions.get_mut((idx - 1) as usize)
4289        };
4290        session.map(|s| (s, remaps))
4291    }

4306    /// Phase 189.M1 — create a typed publisher bound to a node's session.
4307    /// Backs `node.publisher(t).typed::<M>().build()` on the
4308    /// executor-borrowing [`Node`](super::node::Node); the returned
4309    /// handle is owned and outlives the `Node`.
4310    pub fn create_publisher_on<M: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw>(
4311        &mut self,
4312        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
4313        topic_name: &str,
4314        qos: QoSProfile,
4315    ) -> Result<crate::executor::handles::EmbeddedPublisher<M>, NodeError> {
4316        // RFC-0088 / phase-421 W1 — the message's declared format must be the
4317        // one the linked backend speaks. Universal: the const lives on
4318        // `RosMessage`, which `MessageForRmw` requires under every backend.
4319        crate::format_check::assert_message_format::<M>();
4320        // Phase 212.K.7.6.b — register `M`'s cyclonedds descriptor before
4321        // creating the underlying publisher handle. No-op for other RMWs.
4322        crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<M>()?;
4323        let handle = self.create_raw_publisher_handle_on(
4324            node_id,
4325            topic_name,
4326            <M as RosMessage>::TYPE_NAME,
4327            <M as RosMessage>::TYPE_HASH,
4328            qos,
4329        )?;
4330        // RFC-0052 W3b.4 — attach the contracted endpoint's counter cell.
4331        let monitor = self
4332            .monitor_table
4333            .iter()
4334            .find(|m| m.topic == topic_name)
4335            .map(|m| m.cell);
4336        Ok(crate::executor::handles::EmbeddedPublisher {
4337            handle,
4338            event_regs: crate::executor::handles::empty_event_regs(),
4339            monitor,
4340            epoch: self.epoch_us_fn,
4341            _phantom: PhantomData,
4342        })
4343    }
4344
4345    /// Phase 189.M1 — create a generic (type-erased) publisher bound to a
4346    /// node's session. Backs `node.publisher(t).generic(ty, hash).build()`;
4347    /// the bridge re-publishes through this handle on the dest session.
4348    pub fn create_publisher_raw_on(
4349        &mut self,
4350        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
4351        topic_name: &str,
4352        type_name: &str,
4353        type_hash: &str,
4354        qos: QoSProfile,
4355    ) -> Result<crate::executor::handles::EmbeddedRawPublisher, NodeError> {
4356        let handle =
4357            self.create_raw_publisher_handle_on(node_id, topic_name, type_name, type_hash, qos)?;
4358        Ok(crate::executor::handles::EmbeddedRawPublisher {
4359            handle,
4360            arena: crate::executor::handles::TxArena::new(),
4361            event_regs: crate::executor::handles::empty_event_regs(),
4362            // Issue 1676 — attach the contracted endpoint's counter cell by
4363            // exact topic match against the installed table, the rule
4364            // `NodeHandle::create_publisher` applies. This is the publisher
4365            // the Rust component road creates, so without it no contracted
4366            // Rust publisher was ever counted.
4367            monitor: self.publisher_monitor_cell(topic_name),
4368        })
4369    }
4370
4371    /// Shared prelude for the publisher-on-node paths: resolve the node's
4372    /// identity + session slot, build the [`TopicInfo`], validate QoS, and
4373    /// create the backend publisher handle. Mirrors
4374    /// `register_subscription_buffered_raw_on`'s session resolution so a
4375    /// bridge's source sub + dest pub agree on topic construction.
4376    fn create_raw_publisher_handle_on(
4377        &mut self,
4378        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
4379        topic_name: &str,
4380        type_name: &str,
4381        type_hash: &str,
4382        qos: QoSProfile,
4383    ) -> Result<session::RmwPublisher, NodeError> {
4384        let (node_name, ns, session_idx, overrides) = {
4385            let r = self
4386                .nodes
4387                .get(node_id.index())
4388                .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
4389            (
4390                r.name.clone(),
4391                r.namespace.clone(),
4392                r.session_idx,
4393                r.qos_overrides,
4394            )
4395        };
4396        // Issue #52 — fold the node's baked overrides for this topic BEFORE
4397        // `validate_against`, so an override the backend cannot honour errors
4398        // loudly instead of being silently dropped.
4399        let qos = super::node_record::apply_qos_override_codes(
4400            qos,
4401            topic_name,
4402            nros_rmw::QoSOverrideRole::Publisher,
4403            overrides,
4404        );
4405        let mut topic = TopicInfo::new(topic_name, type_name, type_hash)
4406            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
4407            .with_namespace(&ns);
4408        if !node_name.is_empty() {
4409            topic = topic.with_node_name(&node_name);
4410        }
4411        // issue 1608 -- the publisher half of the declared-QoS check, before
4412        // validation so a policy the contract raises this publisher to is one
4413        // the backend is asked about. See `declared_qos::honour_publisher`.
4414        let qos = crate::declared_qos::honour_publisher(topic.type_name, topic.name, qos)?;
4415        let session = self
4416            .session_at_mut(session_idx)
4417            .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
4418        super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
4419            &qos,
4420            Session::supported_qos_policies(session),
4421            "publisher",
4422            topic_name,
4423        )?;
4424        session
4425            .create_publisher(&topic, qos)
4426            .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::PublisherCreationFailed))
4427    }
4428
4429    /// Phase 124.B.1 — install the executor's wake callback onto the
4430    /// primary session. Best-effort: backends that don't override
4431    /// `Session::set_wake_callback` (poll-only XRCE, bare-metal)
4432    /// ignore the call and continue to be drained on the executor's
4433    /// deadline-bound cv-wait boundary.
4434    ///
4435    /// `pub` for issue 1385, and for the same reason
4436    /// [`set_primary_identity`](Self::set_primary_identity) is: the three
4437    /// `Executor::open*` paths call this automatically, and a binding that
4438    /// builds its executor over a session it BORROWS
4439    /// ([`from_session_ptr_in`](Self::from_session_ptr_in)) reaches none of
4440    /// them, so it has to call it itself. `nros_executor_init` is that
4441    /// binding, and until 1385 it did not — leaving `has_async_wake` false
4442    /// for the life of every C executor on every backend.
4443    ///
4444    /// Pairs with `clear_wake_signal`, which the
4445    /// executor runs from `close()` and from `drop`. A caller that installs
4446    /// owes nothing further: the teardown is the executor's.
4447    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4448    pub fn install_wake_signal_on_primary(&mut self) {
4449        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
4450        let ctx = self.wake_ctx_ptr();
4451        // SAFETY: `ctx` points at executor-owned wake state that outlives
4452        // the session callback installation and is cleared by
4453        // `clear_wake_signal` on `close()`/drop.
4454        unsafe {
4455            self.session
4456                .set_wake_callback(Some(nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb), ctx);
4457        }
4458        // Issue 1385 — record that WE are the executor whose ctx the backend
4459        // now holds. The clear reads this and nothing else: a tier executor
4460        // over a BORROWED session (`open_with_session*`) installs nothing, so
4461        // it must not clear the boot executor's callback out from under it
4462        // when the tier task ends.
4463        self.wake_cb_installed = true;
4464        if self.session.supports_wake_callback() {
4465            self.has_async_wake = true;
4466        }
4467    }
4468
4469    /// Phase 124.B.1 — install the wake callback onto an extra
4470    /// session opened by `node_builder.rmw(...)`. Called from
4471    /// `NodeBuilder::build()` right after `extra_sessions.push(...)`.
4472    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4473    pub(crate) fn install_wake_signal_on_extra(&mut self, idx: usize) {
4474        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
4475        let ctx = self.wake_ctx_ptr();
4476        if let Some(s) = self.extra_sessions.get_mut(idx) {
4477            // SAFETY: same executor-owned wake state as the primary session;
4478            // the extra session is owned by this executor.
4479            unsafe {
4480                s.set_wake_callback(Some(nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb), ctx);
4481            }
4482            // Issue 1385 — as on the primary.
4483            self.wake_cb_installed = true;
4484            if s.supports_wake_callback() {
4485                self.has_async_wake = true;
4486            }
4487        }
4488    }
4489
4490    /// Issue 1385 — the teardown half of `install_wake_signal_on_*`, and the
4491    /// obligation `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb`'s own SAFETY comment has asserted
4492    /// since phase 124: *"Executor::drop must clear the callback via
4493    /// `set_wake_callback(None, _)` on all sessions before dropping
4494    /// wake_ctx"*. Nothing did. The string `set_wake_callback(None` occurred
4495    /// exactly once in the tree — in that comment.
4496    ///
4497    /// The context the backend holds is `Arc::as_ptr(&self.wake_ctx)`, freed
4498    /// with this executor. Leaving it installed is a dangling callback the
4499    /// backend may invoke from a worker thread or an ISR. On the Rust `open*`
4500    /// paths the session is `SessionStore::Owned` and dies in the same drop,
4501    /// so the window is narrow; on the C path it is arbitrary —
4502    /// `rclc_executor_fini` drops the executor and zero-fills `_opaque` while
4503    /// the session lives on in `nros_support_t` until `rclc_support_fini`.
4504    ///
4505    /// Clears the primary and every extra session, then latches off, so
4506    /// `close()` followed by drop clears once.
4507    ///
4508    /// Only fires when THIS executor installed (see
4509    /// `install_wake_signal_on_primary`). Two executors sharing one session
4510    /// is still last-writer-wins on the backend's single slot: the first to
4511    /// tear down clears the second's wake and the second degrades to
4512    /// `drive_io(full timeout)`. That is a lost optimisation where the
4513    /// alternative is a freed pointer, which is the trade this direction of
4514    /// the fix makes deliberately.
4515    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4516    pub(crate) fn clear_wake_signal(&mut self) {
4517        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
4518        if !self.wake_cb_installed {
4519            return;
4520        }
4521        self.wake_cb_installed = false;
4522        // SAFETY: clearing takes no context, and both sessions are still live
4523        // here — this runs BEFORE `Session::close` in `close()` and before the
4524        // session field is dropped in `Drop`.
4525        unsafe {
4526            self.session.set_wake_callback(None, core::ptr::null_mut());
4527            for s in self.extra_sessions.iter_mut() {
4528                s.set_wake_callback(None, core::ptr::null_mut());
4529            }
4530        }
4531        self.has_async_wake = false;
4532    }
4533
4534    /// phase-467 Row 8 — hand the PRIMARY session a graph-change target it may
4535    /// trigger from a worker thread, and take ownership of that target.
4536    ///
4537    /// The install half of the pair; [`clear_graph_change_signal`] is the
4538    /// other and the executor owes it. `guard` is CLONED, so the caller keeps
4539    /// its own handle to the same arena flag — that is the whole point: the
4540    /// pointer the backend receives is the executor's box, never the caller's
4541    /// storage. Issue 1385 is the same hazard on the wake slot, found after
4542    /// the fact; this is the shape that cannot reach it.
4543    ///
4544    /// PRIMARY only, deliberately. A graph is a property of a session, and the
4545    /// extra sessions of `node_builder.rmw(...)` each have their own — feeding
4546    /// several into one guard would make "the graph changed" unattributable
4547    /// while costing the caller the ability to ask which. A caller wanting a
4548    /// second backend's graph asks that session for its own.
4549    ///
4550    /// Returns `Err(Unsupported)` from a backend with no graph. A previously
4551    /// installed target is retired first, so an executor never has two.
4552    ///
4553    /// [`clear_graph_change_signal`]: Self::clear_graph_change_signal
4554    ///
4555    /// `pub(crate)`, not `pub`: the public verb is
4556    /// [`register_graph_change_guard_on`], which does the probe, the
4557    /// registration and this in the one order that cannot hand back a guard
4558    /// nothing fires. Exposing the install alone would let a caller reach the
4559    /// second step without the first.
4560    ///
4561    /// [`register_graph_change_guard_on`]: Self::register_graph_change_guard_on
4562    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4563    pub(crate) fn install_graph_change_guard(
4564        &mut self,
4565        guard: &GuardCondition,
4566    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
4567        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
4568        self.clear_graph_change_signal();
4569        let boxed = alloc::boxed::Box::new(guard.clone());
4570        let ptr = (&*boxed) as *const GuardCondition as *const core::ffi::c_void;
4571        // SAFETY: `ptr` names heap storage this executor owns and which
4572        // `clear_graph_change_signal` retires from the backend before it is
4573        // freed. `GuardCondition` is `Send + Sync` and its `trigger()` is a
4574        // relaxed store plus the runtime wake hook, which is what a foreign
4575        // thread is allowed to do here.
4576        let rc = unsafe {
4577            self.session
4578                .set_graph_change_callback(Some(nros_rmw_runtime_graph_change_cb), ptr)
4579        };
4580        match rc {
4581            Ok(()) => {
4582                self.graph_change_target = Some(boxed);
4583                Ok(())
4584            }
4585            // `boxed` drops here, and nothing holds its pointer: the backend
4586            // either refused or failed, so there is no installed callback to
4587            // retire first.
4588            Err(e) => Err(NodeError::Transport(e)),
4589        }
4590    }
4591
4592    /// phase-467 Row 8 — can the primary session deliver a graph-change edge?
4593    ///
4594    /// Asked by CLEARING, which is the one probe that costs nothing and cannot
4595    /// lie: a backend with no graph answers `Unsupported` to a `None` install
4596    /// just as it does to a real one, and an idempotent clear on a backend
4597    /// that HAS a graph is a no-op. Nullity of the vtable slot cannot answer
4598    /// it — `rust_adapter.rs` fills the slot for every Rust backend whether or
4599    /// not that backend overrides the trait method, which
4600    /// `check-rmw-slot-producers`'s own report says in as many words.
4601    ///
4602    /// The caller is `register_graph_change_guard_on`, which asks BEFORE it
4603    /// consumes an executor handle slot, so an unsupported backend costs
4604    /// nothing and the caller is never handed a guard nothing fires.
4605    /// `pub(crate)` for the same reason the install is: asking costs a CLEAR,
4606    /// so a caller that asks and then does nothing has silently retired a live
4607    /// target. The public verb asks once, on the caller's behalf.
4608    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4609    pub(crate) fn supports_graph_change_callback(&mut self) -> bool {
4610        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
4611        // Retire whatever is installed first — the probe IS a clear, so doing
4612        // it without this would silently drop a live target.
4613        self.clear_graph_change_signal();
4614        // SAFETY: a `None` install takes no context and installs nothing.
4615        unsafe {
4616            self.session
4617                .set_graph_change_callback(None, core::ptr::null())
4618                .is_ok()
4619        }
4620    }
4621
4622    /// phase-467 Row 8 — the teardown half of
4623    /// [`install_graph_change_guard`](Self::install_graph_change_guard), and
4624    /// the reason that install cannot recreate issue 1385.
4625    ///
4626    /// Order is the whole content: tell the backend to stop FIRST, then drop
4627    /// the box it was pointing at. Reversed, the window between the free and
4628    /// the clear is exactly 1385's dangling callback — and on the C path that
4629    /// window is arbitrary, because the session outlives the executor.
4630    ///
4631    /// Latched on `graph_change_target.is_some()`, not on a separate flag: the
4632    /// box IS the record of having installed, so `close()` followed by drop
4633    /// clears once and an executor that never installed clears nothing. That
4634    /// is the same predicate `clear_wake_signal` needs a bool for only because
4635    /// its context is shared with `signal_fd()` and every guard condition.
4636    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4637    pub(crate) fn clear_graph_change_signal(&mut self) {
4638        use nros_rmw::Session as _;
4639        if self.graph_change_target.is_none() {
4640            return;
4641        }
4642        // SAFETY: clearing takes no context, and the session is still live
4643        // here — this runs BEFORE `Session::close` in `close()` and before the
4644        // session field is dropped in `Drop`.
4645        unsafe {
4646            let _ = self
4647                .session
4648                .set_graph_change_callback(None, core::ptr::null());
4649        }
4650        // Only now. The backend has been told, so nothing can be holding this
4651        // pointer when it is freed.
4652        self.graph_change_target = None;
4653    }
4654
4655    /// Phase 124.B.2 — opaque context pointer the runtime wake
4656    /// callback receives. Encodes `(flag, mu, cv)` as a borrowed
4657    /// `&WakeCtx` reference; the callback decodes via
4658    /// `*const WakeCtx`.
4659    ///
4660    /// Lifetime: tied to the Executor instance. WakeCtx storage
4661    /// lives inside Executor (lazy-allocated on first install), so
4662    /// the pointer stays valid as long as the Executor is.
4663    /// Phase 124.B.7.c — POSIX signal-handler-safe wake fd.
4664    ///
4665    /// Returns a Linux `eventfd` that callers (typically POSIX
4666    /// signal handlers) can `write(fd, &1u64, 8)` to from any
4667    /// context, including signal handlers. A runtime-owned worker
4668    /// thread reads the fd and signals `wake_cv`, unblocking
4669    /// `spin_once`.
4670    ///
4671    /// The worker thread is spawned lazily on first call and
4672    /// joined on Executor drop. Linux-only and gated behind
4673    /// `feature = "signal-fd-wake"`; binaries that don't install
4674    /// signal handlers shouldn't enable it.
4675    ///
4676    /// Returns the raw fd. The Executor retains ownership; do not
4677    /// `close()` it from the caller.
4678    #[cfg(all(feature = "signal-fd-wake", feature = "rmw-cffi", target_os = "linux"))]
4679    /// phase-359 W10 — was `std::io::Result`. Same values, an error type that
4680    /// does not require `std`.
4681    pub fn signal_fd(&mut self) -> Result<core::ffi::c_int, NodeError> {
4682        let ctx_ptr = self.wake_ctx_ptr() as *const WakeCtx;
4683        if self.signal_fd.is_none() {
4684            self.signal_fd = Some(WakeSignalFd::new(ctx_ptr)?);
4685        }
4686        Ok(self.signal_fd.as_ref().expect("just set").fd())
4687    }
4688
4689    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
4690    fn wake_ctx_ptr(&mut self) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
4691        if self.wake_ctx.is_none() {
4692            self.wake_ctx = Some(portable_atomic_util::Arc::new(WakeCtx {
4693                flag: self.wake_flag.clone(),
4694                node_wake: self.node_wake.clone(),
4695            }));
4696        }
4697        let arc = self.wake_ctx.as_ref().expect("just set");
4698        portable_atomic_util::Arc::as_ptr(arc) as *mut core::ffi::c_void
4699    }
4700
4701    /// Phase 104.C.4 — apply a Node's default SchedContext to a
4702    /// freshly-registered handle. Called from every `_inner`
4703    /// register variant after the entry slot is committed. No-op
4704    /// when `node_id` is None (legacy path), when the Node is
4705    /// out of range, or when the Node's `default_sched` is the
4706    /// auto-created Fifo slot (0) which matches the executor's
4707    /// default binding already.
4708    ///
4709    /// Phase 273 (RFC-0047) — extends with an optional `group` name.
4710    /// Precedence: **group table > node default > no binding** (SC 0).
4711    /// When `group` is `Some(g)`, consults `group_sched_table` first;
4712    /// if no entry exists for `(name, namespace, g)` falls back to the
4713    /// node's `default_sched`. When `group` is `None` the group table
4714    /// is not consulted (unchanged phase-272 path).
4715    ///
4716    /// Handles can still override per-call via
4717    /// `bind_handle_to_sched_context(handle, sc_id)` post-register.
4718    pub(crate) fn apply_node_default_sched(
4719        &mut self,
4720        slot: usize,
4721        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
4722        group: Option<&str>,
4723    ) {
4724        let Some(id) = node_id else { return };
4725        // Copy name, namespace, and default_sched out so the borrow on
4726        // `self.nodes` is released before the immutable `lookup_group_sched`
4727        // borrow and the mutable `sched_context_bindings` write below.
4728        let (name, namespace, node_sc) = {
4729            let Some(rec) = self.nodes.get(id.index()) else {
4730                return;
4731            };
4732            (rec.name.clone(), rec.namespace.clone(), rec.default_sched)
4733        };
4734        // Phase 273: group table > node default.
4735        let sc = match group {
4736            Some(g) => self
4737                .lookup_group_sched(name.as_str(), namespace.as_str(), g)
4738                .unwrap_or(node_sc),
4739            None => node_sc,
4740        };
4741        if sc.0 == 0 {
4742            return;
4743        }
4744        if slot >= self.entries.len() {
4745            return;
4746        }
4747        let sc_idx = sc.0 as usize;
4748        if sc_idx >= self.sched_contexts.len() || self.sched_contexts[sc_idx].is_none() {
4749            return;
4750        }
4751        self.sched_context_bindings[slot] = sc;
4752    }
4753
4754    /// Phase 104.C.3.2 — scoped Node-handle access. The closure
4755    /// receives a [`NodeHandle`](crate::executor::NodeHandle) bound to the
4756    /// requested [`NodeId`](crate::executor::NodeId)'s
4757    /// session + identity. Use the standard `Node::create_publisher`,
4758    /// `create_subscription`, etc. APIs inside.
4759    ///
4760    /// rclcpp-aligned bridge pattern:
4761    ///
4762    /// ```ignore
4763    /// let node_in = exec.node_builder("ingress").rmw("zenoh").build()?;
4764    /// let node_out = exec.node_builder("egress").rmw("xrce").build()?;
4765    ///
4766    /// let pub_out = exec.with_node(node_out, |n| {
4767    ///     n.create_publisher::<Int32>("/fwd")
4768    /// })??;
4769    ///
4770    /// exec.with_node(node_in, |n| {
4771    ///     n.create_subscription_buffered::<Int32, _, 1024>(
4772    ///         "/src", qos(), move |m| { let _ = pub_out.publish(m); }
4773    ///     )
4774    /// })??;
4775    /// ```
4776    ///
4777    /// The closure can return any type; double-`?` unwraps the
4778    /// outer `Result<R, NodeError>` from `with_node` and the inner
4779    /// result returned by the closure.
4780    /// Phase 104.C.3.3.d — flat-Result variant of
4781    /// [`with_node`](Self::with_node). When the closure already
4782    /// returns `Result<R, NodeError>`, this avoids the double-`?`:
4783    ///
4784    /// ```ignore
4785    /// // Without `with_node_try`:
4786    /// let pub_ = exec.with_node(id, |n| n.create_publisher(...))??;
4787    ///
4788    /// // With `with_node_try`:
4789    /// let pub_ = exec.with_node_try(id, |n| n.create_publisher(...))?;
4790    /// ```
4791    pub fn with_node_try<R>(
4792        &mut self,
4793        id: super::node_record::NodeId,
4794        f: impl FnOnce(&mut NodeHandle<'_>) -> Result<R, NodeError>,
4795    ) -> Result<R, NodeError> {
4796        self.with_node(id, f)?
4797    }
4798
4799    pub fn with_node<R>(
4800        &mut self,
4801        id: super::node_record::NodeId,
4802        f: impl FnOnce(&mut NodeHandle<'_>) -> R,
4803    ) -> Result<R, NodeError> {
4804        let (name, ns, session_idx) = {
4805            let r = self
4806                .nodes
4807                .get(id.index())
4808                .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
4809            (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
4810        };
4811        let monitors = self.monitor_table;
4812        let age_monitors = self.age_table;
4813        let epoch = self.epoch_us_fn;
4814        let domain_id = self.domain_id;
4815        let (session, remaps) = self
4816            .session_and_remaps_at_mut(session_idx)
4817            .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
4818        // SAFETY: short-lived scoped reference. `Node::new` takes
4819        // `&mut ConcreteSession`; lifetime is bound to this fn's
4820        // body via the closure's borrow of `node`.
4821        // issue 0801 (second half) — the executor's domain, NOT a literal 0.
4822        // 429d5a581 fixed the ELEVEN arena `TopicInfo`s and left the THREE
4823        // `NodeHandle::new` sites, so an entity created through a node HANDLE
4824        // (`with_node`, `node`, `node_on`) still declared on domain 0 while the
4825        // arena path declared on the configured one. Same split the issue is
4826        // about, one constructor over: `loan_e2e` publishes through a handle and
4827        // subscribes through the arena, so it delivered on domain 0 and on
4828        // nothing else.
4829        let mut node = NodeHandle::new(name, ns, session, remaps, domain_id);
4830        // RFC-0052 W3b.4/.5 — seed the baked monitor tables so contracted
4831        // publishers/subscribers attach their cells without entry glue.
4832        node.set_monitors(monitors);
4833        node.set_age_monitors(age_monitors, epoch);
4834        Ok(f(&mut node))
4835    }
4836
4837    /// Find a registered executor node by final name and namespace.
4838    pub fn node_id_by_name(
4839        &self,
4840        name: &str,
4841        namespace: &str,
4842    ) -> Option<super::node_record::NodeId> {
4843        self.nodes
4844            .iter()
4845            .enumerate()
4846            .find(|(_, node)| node.name.as_str() == name && node.namespace.as_str() == namespace)
4847            .map(|(index, _)| super::node_record::NodeId::from_raw(index as u8))
4848    }
4849
4850    /// Create a node on this executor.
4851    ///
4852    /// Registers the node in the executor's table, deduplicating on
4853    /// `(name, namespace)` — phase-376 W5/B1.
4854    ///
4855    /// # This is `rclrs::Executor::create_node`
4856    ///
4857    /// phase-427 W10 (RFC-0089 "Context and `init`, settled"). Same name, same
4858    /// place in the sequence — `Context` → executor → node — so a ported rclrs
4859    /// `main` lands here unchanged:
4860    ///
4861    /// ```ignore
4862    /// let context = nros::Context::default_from_env()?;
4863    /// let mut executor = context.create_executor()?;
4864    /// let mut node = executor.create_node("talker")?;
4865    /// ```
4866    ///
4867    /// Two differences from upstream, both structural and both named in the
4868    /// ledger row (`rust:Executor::create_node`): ours takes `&mut self`,
4869    /// because the node is registered in the executor's compile-time-sized
4870    /// table rather than allocated, and it hands back a borrowing
4871    /// [`NodeHandle`] rather than an `Arc<Node>`, because there is no
4872    /// allocator. Neither is silent — the compiler names both.
4873    ///
4874    /// The name comes from HERE, not from
4875    /// [`ExecutorConfig::node_name`](crate::ExecutorConfig::node_name), whose
4876    /// builder spelling is deprecated for exactly this reason: one executor
4877    /// holds several named nodes (RFC-0047), so a name on the session config
4878    /// can only ever describe the first of them.
4879    ///
4880    /// Until 2026-08-24 this path registered NOTHING. It built a `NodeHandle`
4881    /// and returned it, so `node_id_by_name` could not find a node the caller
4882    /// had just created, and two calls with one name handed out two handles the
4883    /// executor had never heard of. `create_node_on_with_domain` had the dedup
4884    /// (phase-267 added it there when N bridge endpoints overflowed the table);
4885    /// the plain path never got it.
4886    ///
4887    /// That is a prerequisite for the `create_node` vtable slot, whose contract
4888    /// is that the runtime calls it ONCE per distinct `(name, namespace)`:
4889    /// without a registry to check, the runtime would call it once per
4890    /// `create_node` and every backend would need its own dedup — which is the
4891    /// registry the slot exists to delete (zenoh's `ensure_node_liveliness`
4892    /// linear-scans `per_node_liveliness` for exactly this reason).
4893    ///
4894    /// The table is bounded by `MAX_NODES` (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_NODES`, default
4895    /// 4), so a caller creating a fifth DISTINCT node now gets
4896    /// `NodeError::NodeTableFull` where it previously got a handle. That is the
4897    /// bound doing its job: a node the executor does not know about cannot
4898    /// carry a sched context, a QoS override, or a graph identity. Repeated
4899    /// calls with the SAME name are free.
4900    pub fn create_node(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<super::node::Node<'_, 's>, NodeError> {
4901        if name.len() > 64 {
4902            return Err(NodeError::NameTooLong);
4903        }
4904        // Dedup against the executor's own namespace, which is the namespace
4905        // `node_builder` gives a node when none is named. phase-483 W2: this
4906        // returns THE node type (`Node`, re-exported as `nros::Node`), the
4907        // same handle `node_mut` gives a component, where it used to return a
4908        // session-borrowing `NodeHandle` with a different method set.
4909        let id = match self.node_id_by_name(name, self.namespace.clone().as_str()) {
4910            Some(id) => id,
4911            None => self.node_builder(name).build()?,
4912        };
4913        Ok(super::node::Node::new(self, id))
4914    }
4915
4916    /// Phase 128.F.2 — bridge-mode node factory. Registers a Node
4917    /// bound to the named RMW backend by opening (or reusing) an
4918    /// extra session via `node_builder().rmw(rmw).build()`, then
4919    /// returns a [`NodeHandle`](crate::executor::NodeHandle) borrowing that
4920    /// session. Use when the
4921    /// binary intentionally links more than one backend and a Node
4922    /// must speak a specific one.
4923    ///
4924    /// The single-backend common case should keep using
4925    /// [`create_node`](Self::create_node) — this entry costs an
4926    /// extra session lookup and serves no purpose when only one
4927    /// backend is registered.
4928    #[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
4929    pub fn create_node_on(
4930        &mut self,
4931        name: &str,
4932        rmw: &str,
4933    ) -> Result<super::node::Node<'_, 's>, NodeError> {
4934        self.create_node_on_with_domain(name, rmw, None, None)
4935    }
4936
4937    /// Like [`create_node_on`](Self::create_node_on) but pins the extra
4938    /// session's domain id. Required for a multi-domain config-driven bridge:
4939    /// an extra RMW session's participant domain follows the **node builder's**
4940    /// `domain_id` (`resolve_session_slot` → `domain_id.unwrap_or(0)`), NOT the
4941    /// `SessionSpec`'s — so without this an egress on a non-zero domain silently
4942    /// opens on domain 0 and never matches its receiver (phase-267 issue 0109).
4943    /// `None` domain preserves the legacy domain-0 default. `locator` pins the
4944    /// extra session's address — REQUIRED for an agent-based backend (xrce: the
4945    /// Micro-XRCE-DDS Agent addr) whose session can't be opened locator-less;
4946    /// `None` keeps the rmw-default (cyclonedds is domain-discovered, no locator).
4947    pub fn create_node_on_with_domain(
4948        &mut self,
4949        name: &str,
4950        rmw: &str,
4951        domain_id: Option<u32>,
4952        locator: Option<&str>,
4953    ) -> Result<super::node::Node<'_, 's>, NodeError> {
4954        if name.len() > 64 {
4955            return Err(NodeError::NameTooLong);
4956        }
4957        // Reuse an existing Node of this name rather than growing the node table
4958        // (phase-267 non-flat): a config-driven bridge calls this once per bridge
4959        // ENDPOINT, and the same session node (`s0`/`s1`) recurs across every
4960        // `[[bridge]]`. Without dedup, N bridges push 2N records and overflow
4961        // `MAX_NODES`. Names are unique per session in a generated bridge config,
4962        // so matching by name is unambiguous.
4963        let id = if let Some(i) = self.nodes.iter().position(|n| n.name.as_str() == name) {
4964            super::node_record::NodeId::from_raw(i as u8)
4965        } else {
4966            let mut builder = self.node_builder(name).rmw(rmw);
4967            if let Some(d) = domain_id {
4968                builder = builder.domain_id(d);
4969            }
4970            if let Some(loc) = locator {
4971                builder = builder.locator(loc);
4972            }
4973            builder.build()?
4974        };
4975        Ok(super::node::Node::new(self, id))
4976    }

4978    /// Drive transport I/O (poll network, dispatch callbacks).
4979    #[allow(dead_code)]
4980    pub(crate) fn drive_io(&mut self, timeout_ms: i32) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
4981        self.session
4982            .drive_io(timeout_ms)
4983            .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::PollFailed))
4984    }
