4986    /// Close the underlying session, running the shutdown hooks around it.
4987    ///
4988    /// Issue 0790. The order is the feature:
4989    ///
4990    /// 1. every registered PRE-shutdown hook, while the session is still open
4991    ///    and every entity still works — this is where a node publishes a final
4992    ///    state, answers a last request, parks an actuator or releases a bus;
4993    /// 2. the session close;
4994    /// 3. every registered ON-shutdown hook.
4995    ///
4996    /// A hook runs EXACTLY ONCE: each phase table is emptied before its first
4997    /// hook is invoked, so a second `close()` — or the [`Drop`] sweep after one
4998    /// — finds nothing left to run. Step 2 runs even
4999    /// if a pre-shutdown hook was registered and step 3 even if the close
5000    /// failed — a hook cannot strand the session, and a dead session must not
5001    /// strand the hooks.
5002    ///
5003    /// # This is a CLEAN-STOP facility and nothing more
5004    ///
5005    /// A watchdog reset, a hard fault or a panic does not come through here, so
5006    /// these hooks do not run then. Nothing in a fixed static table can promise
5007    /// otherwise, and an API that implied it would be worse than none: hardware
5008    /// that must be safe across an abnormal stop needs a hardware answer (a
5009    /// pull-down, a watchdog-driven output disable), not a callback.
5010    pub fn close(&mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
5011        self.run_shutdown_hooks(super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre);
5012        // Issue 1385 — hand the callback back BEFORE closing the session that
5013        // holds it. `close()` leaves the executor alive, so without this a
5014        // later `set_wake_callback` from the drop sweep would reach a session
5015        // the backend has already torn down.
5016        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
5017        self.clear_wake_signal();
5018        // phase-467 Row 8 — the same obligation on the graph-change slot, and
5019        // it has to be discharged in the same place for the same reason.
5020        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
5021        self.clear_graph_change_signal();
5022        let result = self
5023            .session
5024            .close()
5025            .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ConnectionFailed));
5026        self.run_shutdown_hooks(super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post);
5027        result
5028    }
5029
5030    /// Register a hook to run BEFORE the session is closed (issue 0790).
5031    ///
5032    /// rclcpp's `Context::add_pre_shutdown_callback`. Returns the handle
5033    /// [`Self::remove_pre_shutdown_callback`] takes, or
5034    /// [`NodeError::ShutdownCallbacksFull`] when the phase table is full —
5035    /// raise `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS` (default 2) at build time.
5036    ///
5037    /// # Safety
5038    /// `callback` must be safe to invoke exactly once with `context`, and
5039    /// `context` must stay valid until the hook runs or is removed. The hook
5040    /// runs on whichever task calls [`Self::close`] (or drops the executor),
5041    /// which is not necessarily the task that registered it.
5042    pub unsafe fn add_pre_shutdown_callback(
5043        &mut self,
5044        callback: super::types::ShutdownCallbackFn,
5045        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
5046    ) -> Result<super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle, NodeError> {
5047        Self::claim_shutdown_slot(
5048            &mut self.pre_shutdown_hooks,
5049            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre,
5050            callback,
5051            context,
5052        )
5053    }
5054
5055    /// Register a hook to run AFTER the session is closed (issue 0790).
5056    ///
5057    /// rclcpp's `Context::add_on_shutdown_callback` / `rclcpp::on_shutdown`.
5058    /// Entities are gone by the time it runs, so anything that needs the wire
5059    /// belongs in [`Self::add_pre_shutdown_callback`] instead.
5060    ///
5061    /// # Safety
5062    /// Same contract as [`Self::add_pre_shutdown_callback`].
5063    pub unsafe fn add_on_shutdown_callback(
5064        &mut self,
5065        callback: super::types::ShutdownCallbackFn,
5066        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
5067    ) -> Result<super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle, NodeError> {
5068        Self::claim_shutdown_slot(
5069            &mut self.on_shutdown_hooks,
5070            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post,
5071            callback,
5072            context,
5073        )
5074    }
5075
5076    /// Remove a pre-shutdown hook. `true` if `handle` named a live one.
5077    ///
5078    /// rclcpp's `Context::remove_pre_shutdown_callback`, and `bool` for the
5079    /// same reason: "it was not there" is an ordinary answer (the hook may
5080    /// already have run), not an error. A handle issued for the OTHER phase
5081    /// returns `false` and removes nothing — that is what the phase tag in
5082    /// [`ShutdownCallbackHandle`] buys.
5083    ///
5084    /// [`ShutdownCallbackHandle`]: super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle
5085    pub fn remove_pre_shutdown_callback(
5086        &mut self,
5087        handle: super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle,
5088    ) -> bool {
5089        Self::release_shutdown_slot(
5090            &mut self.pre_shutdown_hooks,
5091            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre,
5092            handle,
5093        )
5094    }
5095
5096    /// Remove an on-shutdown hook. See [`Self::remove_pre_shutdown_callback`].
5097    pub fn remove_on_shutdown_callback(
5098        &mut self,
5099        handle: super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle,
5100    ) -> bool {
5101        Self::release_shutdown_slot(
5102            &mut self.on_shutdown_hooks,
5103            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post,
5104            handle,
5105        )
5106    }
5107
5108    /// How many hooks are currently registered for `phase`. Diagnostic /
5109    /// test surface, and what a "did my registration land?" assertion reads.
5110    pub fn shutdown_callback_count(&self, phase: super::types::ShutdownPhase) -> usize {
5111        let table = match phase {
5112            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre => &self.pre_shutdown_hooks,
5113            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post => &self.on_shutdown_hooks,
5114        };
5115        table.iter().flatten().count()
5116    }
5117
5118    /// Claim the first free slot of a phase table.
5119    fn claim_shutdown_slot(
5120        table: &mut [Option<super::types::ShutdownHook>],
5121        phase: super::types::ShutdownPhase,
5122        callback: super::types::ShutdownCallbackFn,
5123        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
5124    ) -> Result<super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle, NodeError> {
5125        for (index, slot) in table.iter_mut().enumerate() {
5126            if slot.is_some() {
5127                continue;
5128            }
5129            let handle = super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle::new(phase, index)
5130                .ok_or(NodeError::ShutdownCallbacksFull)?;
5131            *slot = Some(super::types::ShutdownHook { callback, context });
5132            return Ok(handle);
5133        }
5134        Err(NodeError::ShutdownCallbacksFull)
5135    }
5136
5137    /// Clear a slot of a phase table, rejecting a handle from the other phase.
5138    fn release_shutdown_slot(
5139        table: &mut [Option<super::types::ShutdownHook>],
5140        phase: super::types::ShutdownPhase,
5141        handle: super::types::ShutdownCallbackHandle,
5142    ) -> bool {
5143        if handle.phase() != Some(phase) {
5144            return false;
5145        }
5146        match table.get_mut(handle.index()) {
5147            Some(slot) => slot.take().is_some(),
5148            None => false,
5149        }
5150    }
5151
5152    /// Run — and consume — every hook registered for `phase`, in registration
5153    /// order.
5154    ///
5155    /// The table is EMPTIED BEFORE the first callback runs, not slot by slot as
5156    /// the loop walks it, and both halves of that matter:
5157    ///
5158    /// * "exactly once" becomes a property of the table rather than of the
5159    ///   caller — a second `close()`, or the `Drop` sweep after one, finds
5160    ///   nothing left to run;
5161    /// * the `&mut self` borrow ENDS before any foreign code is invoked. A hook
5162    ///   is an `extern "C" fn` that may hold a raw pointer back to this
5163    ///   executor (the C and C++ shims hand out exactly that), so a hook that
5164    ///   registers or removes another one must not be running inside a live
5165    ///   `&mut` into the table it is touching.
5166    pub(crate) fn run_shutdown_hooks(&mut self, phase: super::types::ShutdownPhase) {
5167        let table = match phase {
5168            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre => &mut self.pre_shutdown_hooks,
5169            super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post => &mut self.on_shutdown_hooks,
5170        };
5171        // `ShutdownHook` is `Copy` (a fn pointer and a raw pointer), so this is
5172        // a register-width move of a table whose default size is two slots —
5173        // not a reason to keep the borrow open across the calls.
5174        let hooks = *table;
5175        *table = [None; crate::config::MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS];
5176        for hook in hooks.iter().flatten() {
5177            // SAFETY: the `add_*_shutdown_callback` caller promised `callback`
5178            // is safe to invoke once with `context`, and that `context` stays
5179            // valid until the hook runs or is removed. This is that one call,
5180            // and the table is already cleared so it cannot happen again.
5181            unsafe {
5182                (hook.callback)(hook.context);
5183            }
5184        }
5185    }
5186
5187    /// Phase 216 follow-up — register a per-Node dispatch trampoline.
5188    ///
5189    /// The board-side Entry pkg (or the macro-emitted
5190    /// `register_dispatch(executor)` wrapper, once wired) calls this
5191    /// once per deployed Node pkg, handing in the
5192    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` symbol + the Node's per-pkg
5193    /// `state` blob. [`Executor::dispatch_callback`] then linear-scans
5194    /// the registered slots when the dispatch task hands off a
5195    /// `SignaledCallback`.
5196    ///
5197    /// Returns `Err(())` when the registry is full (`MAX_NODES`
5198    /// entries — raise via `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_NODES` at build time).
5199    ///
5200    /// # Safety
5201    ///
5202    /// `state` must outlive the executor (the typical shape is a
5203    /// `*mut State` produced by
5204    /// `nros::__private_node_state_into_raw` from the
5205    /// macro-emitted `i()`; that pointer's lifetime IS the
5206    /// `Executor`'s by construction). `on_callback` must be safe to
5207    /// invoke with `(state, cb_id_ptr, cb_id_len, ctx)` matching the
5208    /// per-Node `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` ABI emitted by the
5209    /// `nros::node!()` macro (Phase 216.A.5).
5210    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
5211    pub fn register_dispatch_slot(
5212        &mut self,
5213        state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
5214        on_callback: unsafe extern "C" fn(
5215            *mut core::ffi::c_void,
5216            *const u8,
5217            usize,
5218            *mut core::ffi::c_void,
5219        ),
5220    ) -> Result<(), ()> {
5221        self.dispatch_slots
5222            .push(DispatchSlot { state, on_callback })
5223            .map_err(|_| ())
5224    }

5226    /// Phase 216 follow-up — current registered dispatch-slot count.

5229        self.dispatch_slots.len()

5232    /// Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — enroll a component into the executor-owned
5233    /// tick registry. Called by `nros`'s `install`/`register_node_borrowed`
5234    /// after it builds the `Arc<ComponentCell>`: `state` is the leaked
5235    /// `Arc<ComponentCell>` (the slot takes ownership), `tick`/`drop` are the
5236    /// `nros`-side trampolines (see `ComponentSlot`). The slot's `tick`
5237    /// runs at the tail of every [`spin_once`](Self::spin_once); its `drop`
5238    /// runs once on `Executor::drop`.
5239    ///
5240    /// Returns `Err(())` when the registry is full (`MAX_NODES` — raise via
5241    /// `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_NODES` at build time). On error the caller still
5242    /// owns `state` (the slot was not stored) and must drop it.
5243    ///
5244    /// # Safety
5245    /// `state` must be a `*mut` produced by leaking the component cell the
5246    /// `tick`/`drop` trampolines expect (an `Arc<ComponentCell>` via
5247    /// `Arc::into_raw` in the canonical `nros` caller), and must remain valid
5248    /// until the matching `drop` runs. `tick` must be safe to invoke with
5249    /// `(state, exec_ctx = *mut Executor)` each spin; `drop` must be safe to
5250    /// invoke exactly once with `state`.
5251    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
5252    pub unsafe fn enroll_component(
5253        &mut self,
5254        state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
5255        tick: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void, *mut core::ffi::c_void),
5256        drop: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void),
5257    ) -> Result<(), ()> {
5258        self.component_slots
5259            .push(ComponentSlot { state, tick, drop })
5260            .map_err(|_| ())
5261    }

5263    /// Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — current enrolled component-slot count.

5269    /// issue #140 — the enrolled components' opaque `state` pointers, in enroll

5275    /// `ExecutorNodeRuntime::components`, so the hosted-spin counts read zero

5281    /// Phase 216 final dispatch hook — stable entry point the
5282    /// framework's dispatch task (RTIC `__nros_run` /
5283    /// Embassy `__nros_run_task`) calls for each `SignaledCallback`
5284    /// envelope it dequeues from the board-side SPSC / Embassy
5285    /// channel.
5286    ///
5287    /// ## Signature shape
5288    ///
5289    /// `nros-node` sits below `nros` in the dep graph, so the typed
5290    /// `nros::CallbackId<'_>` / `nros::CallbackCtx<'_>` types
5291    /// referenced in the Phase 216 design notes cannot appear in the
5292    /// signature here. The macro emit translates the dequeued
5293    /// envelope to the layer-clean `(cb_id: &str, ctx: *mut c_void)`
5294    /// pair before calling this method; the per-Node `on_callback`
5295    /// trampoline ABI (Phase 216.A.5,
5296    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback(state, cb_id_ptr, cb_id_len,
5297    /// ctx)`) uses the same untyped shape on the other side of the
5298    /// fence, so the round-trip stays type-consistent.
5299    ///
5300    /// ## Body — linear scan of the dispatch registry
5301    ///
5302    /// Each registered `DispatchSlot` holds an
5303    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` fn pointer + the owning Node's
5304    /// `state` blob. The macro-emitted trampoline body
5305    /// `match`es on `CallbackId` tags the Node declared and is a
5306    /// no-op for non-matching `cb_id`s — at most one Node per
5307    /// `cb_id` actually acts, the rest are cheap string-compare
5308    /// no-ops. This mirrors the strategy
5309    /// `ExecutorNodeRuntime::dispatch_callback` uses in
5310    /// `packages/api/nros/src/node_runtime.rs:470`.
5311    ///
5312    /// ## What's NOT auto-wired today
5313    ///
5314    /// The `nros::node!()` macro doesn't yet emit a
5315    /// `register_dispatch(executor)` wrapper that pushes the per-pkg
5316    /// `(state, on_callback)` into this registry. Until that wiring
5317    /// lands (Phase 216 follow-up — see commit msg), downstream
5318    /// consumers (board's `init_hardware`, or the codegen-emitted
5319    /// `run_plan`) must call
5320    /// [`Executor::register_dispatch_slot`] explicitly with the
5321    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` symbol + a `state` blob from
5322    /// the macro-emitted `i()`.
5323    //
5324    // `ctx` is an opaque FFI cookie forwarded verbatim to each slot's
5325    // `on_callback`; this fn never dereferences it (the registered callback
5326    // does, under the `register_dispatch_slot` safety contract), so it is sound
5327    // to call from safe code.
5328    #[allow(clippy::not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref)]
5329    pub fn dispatch_callback(&mut self, cb_id: &str, ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void) {
5330        let cb_id_ptr = cb_id.as_ptr();
5331        let cb_id_len = cb_id.len();
5332        // Snapshot pointer + length to avoid an outstanding borrow
5333        // across the unsafe fn calls below; each `DispatchSlot` is
5334        // `Copy`, so iterating by value sidesteps any aliasing
5335        // worry the borrow checker would flag if a slot's
5336        // `on_callback` re-entered the executor.
5337        for slot in self.dispatch_slots.iter().copied() {
5338            // SAFETY: caller of `register_dispatch_slot` guaranteed
5339            // `state` outlives the executor + `on_callback` matches
5340            // the per-Node `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` ABI;
5341            // `cb_id_ptr`/`cb_id_len` describe the live `&str` the
5342            // caller passed in.
5343            unsafe {
5344                (slot.on_callback)(slot.state, cb_id_ptr, cb_id_len, ctx);
5345            }
5346        }
5347    }

5362    /// state required).

5367    /// backend can't probe.

5371    /// `ping(100)` periodically and tear down / re-open the session
5372    /// on timeout.

5376            .ping_session(timeout_ms)

5380    /// phase-381 W4 — every node on the graph, with its namespace.
5381    ///
5382    /// `visit(name, namespace, enclave)` is called once per node and returns
5383    /// `false` to stop early. A VISITOR rather than a returned collection
5384    /// because there is no allocator at this layer and the graph has no bound
5385    /// the caller can know; peak extra memory is one entry. Every string is
5386    /// BORROWED for the duration of the call.
5387    ///
5388    /// `enclave` is `None` where the backend does not track one, which is what
5389    /// lets one call answer both `rmw_get_node_names` and
5390    /// `rmw_get_node_names_with_enclaves`.
5391    ///
5392    /// **This reports what has already been DISCOVERED, and never blocks.** The
5393    /// first call after startup legitimately sees a partial graph — the backend
5394    /// keeps a standing query fed by `spin`, so the view fills in over
5395    /// successive calls. Code that waits for a peer should poll, not call once
5396    /// and conclude. An empty result is "nobody seen yet", never "nobody
5397    /// exists".
5398    ///
5399    /// `Err(Transport(Unsupported))` from a backend with no graph — distinct
5400    /// from an empty graph, deliberately.
5401    pub fn get_node_names(
5402        &mut self,
5403        visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&str, &str, Option<&str>) -> bool,
5404    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
5405        use nros_rmw::Session;
5406        self.session
5407            .get_node_names(visit)
5408            .map_err(NodeError::Transport)
5409    }

5569    /// phase-444 — block until at least `count` publishers are visible on
5570    /// `topic_name`, or `timeout` elapses. Upstream's `rcl_wait_for_publishers`.
5571    ///
5572    /// Returns `Ok(true)` when the graph showed at least `count` inside the
5573    /// budget, `Ok(false)` on timeout. The startup-ordering primitive one
5574    /// entity kind over from [`EmbeddedServiceClient::wait_for_service`](super::handles::EmbeddedServiceClient::wait_for_service),
5575    /// and built the same way: a spin on a discovery read, so other
5576    /// subscriptions and timers keep making progress while it waits.
5577    ///
5578    /// **This is the one blocking member of the graph family, and it does not
5579    /// weaken the family's contract — it composes it.** The query underneath
5580    /// ([`count_publishers`](Self::count_publishers)) still reports only what
5581    /// has been DISCOVERED and still never blocks; what waits is this loop,
5582    /// and it waits by POLLING that query. RFC-0021 is the rule that governs
5583    /// it, and that rule does not forbid blocking: it requires a blocking
5584    /// helper to take an executor and drive it, which is what makes the
5585    /// timeout reliable on a single-threaded transport and what makes the
5586    /// reentrancy visible at the call site.
5587    ///
5588    /// **`Unsupported` is propagated IMMEDIATELY, not waited out** — and this
5589    /// is the one place it deliberately differs from `wait_for_service`, which
5590    /// treats a backend that cannot answer as "keep waiting" and reports
5591    /// `Ok(false)` at the deadline (issue 1087). That is right for a service
5592    /// probe, where not-yet-answerable is a transient. It is wrong here: a
5593    /// backend with no graph (XRCE) can never answer, so spending the budget
5594    /// to return `Ok(false)` would report "no publishers appeared" for a
5595    /// backend that cannot see publishers at all — collapsing "cannot tell
5596    /// you" into "not there", which is exactly the distinction RFC-0036 exists
5597    /// to keep and which every other method in this family promises to keep.
5598    ///
5599    /// `count == 0` is satisfied immediately and without asking the backend —
5600    /// including on a backend with no graph, because "at least zero" is true
5601    /// of every graph and needs no discovery to establish.
5602    pub fn wait_for_publishers(
5603        &mut self,
5604        topic_name: &str,
5605        count: usize,
5606        timeout: core::time::Duration,
5607    ) -> Result<bool, NodeError> {
5608        self.wait_for_endpoints(true, topic_name, count, timeout)
5609    }
5610
5611    /// phase-444 — block until at least `count` subscribers are visible on
5612    /// `topic_name`. Upstream's `rcl_wait_for_subscribers`. See
5613    /// [`wait_for_publishers`](Self::wait_for_publishers) for the contract,
5614    /// and for why `Unsupported` returns rather than waits.
5615    pub fn wait_for_subscribers(
5616        &mut self,
5617        topic_name: &str,
5618        count: usize,
5619        timeout: core::time::Duration,
5620    ) -> Result<bool, NodeError> {
5621        self.wait_for_endpoints(false, topic_name, count, timeout)
5622    }
5623
5624    /// The one loop both `wait_for_*` verbs run — a shared helper rather than
5625    /// a second spelling, because the pair differs only in which counter it
5626    /// polls and a copied loop is how the two drift.
5627    fn wait_for_endpoints(
5628        &mut self,
5629        publishers: bool,
5630        topic_name: &str,
5631        count: usize,
5632        timeout: core::time::Duration,
5633    ) -> Result<bool, NodeError> {
5634        if count == 0 {
5635            return Ok(true);
5636        }
5637        // `?`, not a swallow: a backend that cannot see the graph says so now.
5638        if self.count_endpoints(publishers, topic_name)? >= count {
5639            return Ok(true);
5640        }
5641        let spin_interval =
5642            core::time::Duration::from_millis(super::handles::DEFAULT_SPIN_INTERVAL_MS);
5643        let max_spins =
5644            (timeout.as_millis() as u64 / super::handles::DEFAULT_SPIN_INTERVAL_MS).max(1);
5645        let mut budget = super::handles::WaitBudget::new(max_spins, timeout);
5646        loop {
5647            self.spin_once(budget.next_spin_interval(spin_interval));
5648            if self.count_endpoints(publishers, topic_name)? >= count {
5649                return Ok(true);
5650            }
5651            if !budget.tick() {
5652                return Ok(false);
5653            }
5654        }
5655    }
5656
5657    /// Which counter a `wait_for_*` polls. Keeps the boolean's meaning in ONE
5658    /// place instead of at both call sites.
5659    fn count_endpoints(&mut self, publishers: bool, topic_name: &str) -> Result<usize, NodeError> {
5660        if publishers {
5661            self.count_publishers(topic_name)
5662        } else {
5663            self.count_subscribers(topic_name)
5664        }
5665    }

5667    /// Get a mutable reference to an action client core in the arena by entry index.
5668    ///
5669    /// # Safety
5670    /// The caller must ensure that `entry_index` refers to an `ActionClientRawArenaEntry`.
5671    pub unsafe fn action_client_core_mut(
5672        &mut self,
5673        entry_index: usize,
5674    ) -> Option<&mut super::action_core::ActionClientCore> {
5675        let meta = self.entries.get(self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?)?.as_ref()?;
5676        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::ActionClient) {
5677            return None;
5678        }
5679        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
5680        unsafe {
5681            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(meta.offset)
5682                as *mut super::arena::ActionClientRawArenaEntry<
5683                    { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
5684                    { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
5685                    { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
5686                >;
5687            Some(&mut (*entry_ptr).core)
5688        }
5689    }
5690
5691    /// Get a mutable reference to a service-client arena entry (Phase 82).
5692    ///
5693    /// Returns `None` if `entry_index` doesn't refer to a service client
5694    /// entry. The default reply buffer size is assumed because the C API
5695    /// always uses the default — the entry was registered via
5696    /// `register_service_client_raw_sized::<DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE>`.
5697    ///
5698    /// # Safety
5699    /// `entry_index` must refer to a `ServiceClientRawArenaEntry`.
5700    pub unsafe fn service_client_entry_mut(
5701        &mut self,
5702        entry_index: usize,
5703    ) -> Option<&mut super::arena::ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<{ crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE }>>
5704    {
5705        let meta = self.entries.get(self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?)?.as_ref()?;
5706        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::ServiceClient) {
5707            return None;
5708        }
5709        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
5710        unsafe {
5711            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(meta.offset)
5712                as *mut super::arena::ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<
5713                    { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
5714                >;
5715            Some(&mut *entry_ptr)
5716        }
5717    }

5719    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
5720    // issue 1437 / phase-444 — the ARENA half of the granted-QoS read-back.
5721    //
5722    // An entity registered with a callback lives in the executor arena, and
5723    // the C / C++ handle the user holds is then bookkeeping: its inline
5724    // storage is untouched and the only identity it carries is the entry
5725    // index. So an accessor that reads the user's own storage answers for
5726    // the POLL road and returns an absence on the CALLBACK road — which is
5727    // the road a ported `rclcpp` node takes, i.e. the common one. These
5728    // three close that reach.
5729    //
5730    // Each reads the entry's HANDLE and nothing else, which is why one
5731    // function per kind serves every entry SHAPE of that kind: every arena
5732    // entry is `#[repr(C)]` with its handle as the first field (12
5733    // subscription shapes, 2 service-server, 2 service-client), so
5734    // `arena_base + offset` IS the handle pointer whatever buffer sizes and
5735    // callback types the shape was monomorphised with.
5736    // `service_client_entry_mut` above has to name ONE shape because it
5737    // reaches past the handle; these do not, and that is the whole
5738    // difference. `arena::tests::every_arena_entry_begins_with_its_handle`
5739    // pins the invariant.
5740
5741    /// The `RmwSubscriber` of an arena-registered subscription, by entry index.
5742    ///
5743    /// `None` when `entry_index` names no entry, or names one that is not a
5744    /// subscription.
5745    ///
5746    /// # Safety
5747    /// `entry_index` must be an index this executor handed out. The borrow is
5748    /// valid only while the arena is not re-entered.
5749    pub unsafe fn subscription_handle(
5750        &self,
5751        entry_index: usize,
5752    ) -> Option<&session::RmwSubscriber> {
5753        let meta = self.entries.get(self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?)?.as_ref()?;
5754        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Subscription) {
5755            return None;
5756        }
5757        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
5758        // SAFETY: `meta.offset` is inside the arena by construction, and every
5759        // subscription entry shape begins with its `RmwSubscriber`.
5760        Some(unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const session::RmwSubscriber) })
5761    }
5762
5763    /// The `RmwServiceServer` of an arena-registered service, by entry index.
5764    ///
5765    /// # Safety
5766    /// See [`Executor::subscription_handle`].
5767    pub unsafe fn service_server_handle(
5768        &self,
5769        entry_index: usize,
5770    ) -> Option<&session::RmwServiceServer> {
5771        let meta = self.entries.get(self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?)?.as_ref()?;
5772        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Service) {
5773            return None;
5774        }
5775        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
5776        // SAFETY: as above; every service-server entry shape begins with its
5777        // `RmwServiceServer`.
5778        Some(unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const session::RmwServiceServer) })
5779    }
5780
5781    /// The `RmwServiceClient` of an arena-registered client, by entry index.
5782    ///
5783    /// # Safety
5784    /// See [`Executor::subscription_handle`].
5785    pub unsafe fn service_client_handle(
5786        &self,
5787        entry_index: usize,
5788    ) -> Option<&session::RmwServiceClient> {
5789        let meta = self.entries.get(self.slot_of_raw(entry_index)?)?.as_ref()?;
5790        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::ServiceClient) {
5791            return None;
5792        }
5793        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
5794        // SAFETY: as above; both service-client entry shapes begin with their
5795        // `RmwServiceClient` — the typed one through `ServiceClientSendHeader`,
5796        // itself `#[repr(C)]` and handle-first.
5797        Some(unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const session::RmwServiceClient) })
5798    }

5810    /// Choose between `Direct` (process in place) and `LET`
5811    /// (snapshot-then-process) semantics. See [`ExecutorSemantics`].
5812    pub fn set_semantics(&mut self, semantics: ExecutorSemantics) {

5816    /// Set the invocation mode for a specific handle.
5817    ///
5818    /// Controls whether the callback fires on every spin
5819    /// ([`Always`](InvocationMode::Always)) or only when new data
5820    /// arrives ([`OnNewData`](InvocationMode::OnNewData), the default).
5821    pub fn set_invocation(&mut self, id: HandleId, mode: InvocationMode) {
5822        let slot = self.live_slot(id);
5823        if let Some(Some(meta)) = self.entries.get_mut(slot) {
5824            meta.invocation = mode;
5825        }
