5828    // ========================================================================
5829    // Arena-based callback registration
5830    // ========================================================================
5831
5832    /// Arena bytes claimed by registered entities so far.
5833    ///
5834    /// EXACT, not a worst case: the arena is a bump allocator and every
5835    /// `arena_alloc` charges `size_of::<T>()`, so nothing is reserved per slot.
5836    /// `ARENA_SIZE` itself is derived the other way — every slot budgeted at
5837    /// the ActionClient worst case — which is issue 0900, and this accessor is
5838    /// how an image can find out what it actually needs.
5839    pub fn arena_used(&self) -> usize {
5840        self.arena_used
5841    }
5842
5843    /// Total arena bytes this executor was given.
5844    ///
5845    /// The arena is a borrowed slice; where its storage lives is the caller's
5846    /// choice, not a property of this type. Three answers are real — a `.bss`
5847    /// static (the C/C++ entries, and the `alloc` constructors since phase-392
5848    /// W6), the heap (those constructors' fallback), and a stack-declared
5849    /// `nros_executor_t`. See `super::backing` and `report_arena_headroom`.
5850    pub fn arena_capacity(&self) -> usize {
5851        self.arena.len()
5852    }
5853
5854    /// Bump-allocate space for `T` in the arena. Returns the byte offset.
5855    pub(crate) fn arena_alloc<T>(&mut self) -> Result<usize, NodeError> {
5856        // Issue 1667 — every region is grain-aligned and at least one free-list
5857        // node long, so it can be listed when it is released.
5858        let align = core::mem::align_of::<T>().max(ARENA_GRAIN);
5859        let size = Self::arena_region_len(core::mem::size_of::<T>());
5860        if let Some((offset, granted)) = self.arena_take_freed(size, align) {
5861            crate::boot_report::note_alloc(size, self.arena_used);
5862            self.note_entry_region(offset, granted);
5863            return Ok(offset);
5864        }
5865        let aligned_offset = (self.arena_used + align - 1) & !(align - 1);
5866        let new_used = aligned_offset + size;
5867        if new_used > self.arena.len() {
5868            // issue 0900 — `BufferTooSmall` is returned by a dozen other paths,
5869            // so on a target where a return code is all you get, arena
5870            // exhaustion is indistinguishable from a message that did not fit.
5871            return Err(self.arena_exhausted(
5872                core::any::type_name::<T>(),
5873                size,
5874                new_used - self.arena.len(),
5875            ));
5876        }
5877        self.arena_used = new_used;
5878        crate::boot_report::note_alloc(size, new_used);
5879        self.note_entry_region(aligned_offset, size);
5880        Ok(aligned_offset)
5881    }
5882
5883    /// Issue 1631 — remember the region an ENTRY allocation handed out, for
5884    /// `emplace_entry` to record. Only the two entry allocators call this; a
5885    /// callback capture rides inside the entry's trailing region (phase-476
5886    /// W0), so it is part of what they record.
5887    fn note_entry_region(&mut self, offset: usize, len: usize) {
5888        self.pending_region = Some(FreedRegion { offset, len });
5889    }
5890
5891    /// Issue 1667 — the length a region of `len` requested bytes occupies:
5892    /// rounded up to the grain, and never shorter than a free-list node.
5893    const fn arena_region_len(len: usize) -> usize {
5894        let len = len.next_multiple_of(ARENA_GRAIN);
5895        if len < ARENA_MIN_REGION {
5896            ARENA_MIN_REGION
5897        } else {
5898            len
5899        }
5900    }
5901
5902    /// Bytes a callback CAPTURE takes in an entry's trailing region: its length
5903    /// rounded up to the arena's `u64` grain. 0 for no capture.
5904    ///
5905    /// phase-476 W0 — a capture used to be a SEPARATE arena allocation
5906    /// (`stow_capture` over `arena_alloc_bytes`), which `release_entry` never
5907    /// gave back: it frees exactly the region `emplace_entry` recorded, and that
5908    /// was the entry's. Placing the capture at the END of the entry's own
5909    /// trailing region puts it inside the recorded region, so releasing the
5910    /// entry releases its capture.
5911    pub(crate) fn capture_trailing_len(capture: Option<&[u8]>) -> usize {
5912        match capture {
5913            Some(b) if !b.is_empty() => b.len().next_multiple_of(core::mem::align_of::<u64>()),
5914            _ => 0,
5915        }
5916    }
5917
5918    /// Copy a caller's callback CAPTURE to arena offset `at` and return the
5919    /// context pointer the entry should dispatch with — phase-456 W1, made a
5920    /// runtime length by W8, made part of the entry's region by phase-476 W0.
5921    ///
5922    /// `context` is one pointer. That carries a C++ `[this]` capture and not a
5923    /// `[this, state]` (two) or a `[obj, method]` (three, because a
5924    /// pointer-to-member-function is two words on the Itanium ABI) — the
5925    /// distribution phase-442 W0 measured over this tree and the porting corpus.
5926    /// So the capture lives in the arena beside the registration that uses it:
5927    /// arena bytes never move once allocated, and the returned pointer is into
5928    /// them rather than into anything of the caller's, so the C++ side keeps
5929    /// nothing.
5930    ///
5931    /// `at` must start [`capture_trailing_len`](Self::capture_trailing_len)
5932    /// bytes the caller's entry allocation reserved for it. `None` and an empty
5933    /// slice both mean "no capture", and both give the caller's own `context`
5934    /// straight back, which is every pre-W1 caller.
5935    pub(crate) fn place_capture(
5936        &mut self,
5937        at: usize,
5938        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
5939        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
5940    ) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
5941        let bytes = match capture {
5942            Some(b) if !b.is_empty() => b,
5943            _ => return context,
5944        };
5945        debug_assert!(at + bytes.len() <= self.arena.len());
5946        // SAFETY: the caller's entry allocation reserved
5947        // `capture_trailing_len(capture)` bytes at `at` for exactly this, and
5948        // `bytes` is a caller slice that cannot alias the arena (the arena is
5949        // borrowed mutably by `self` for the whole call).
5950        unsafe {
5951            let dst = (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(at);
5952            core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), dst, bytes.len());
5953            dst as *mut core::ffi::c_void
5954        }
5955    }
5956
5957    /// Bump-allocate space for `T` plus `trailing_bytes` extra bytes.
5958    ///
5959    /// Returns `(entry_offset, trailing_offset)`. The trailing region starts
5960    /// immediately after `T` (aligned to 8 bytes).
5961    pub(crate) fn arena_alloc_with_trailing<T>(
5962        &mut self,
5963        trailing_bytes: usize,
5964    ) -> Result<(usize, usize), NodeError> {
5965        let align = core::mem::align_of::<T>().max(ARENA_GRAIN);
5966        let entry_size = core::mem::size_of::<T>();
5967        // Issue 1496 — a released region that holds the entry AND its trailing
5968        // region is reused whole. The trailing region keeps its rule: it starts
5969        // on a `u64` boundary after the entry, so the request is sized by that.
5970        let u64_align = core::mem::align_of::<u64>();
5971        let whole = Self::arena_region_len(entry_size.next_multiple_of(u64_align) + trailing_bytes);
5972        if let Some((entry_offset, granted)) = self.arena_take_freed(whole, align) {
5973            let trailing_offset = (entry_offset + entry_size).next_multiple_of(u64_align);
5974            crate::boot_report::note_alloc(whole, self.arena_used);
5975            self.note_entry_region(entry_offset, granted);
5976            return Ok((entry_offset, trailing_offset));
5977        }
5978        let entry_offset = self.arena_used.next_multiple_of(align);
5979        // Trailing region starts on an 8-byte (u64) boundary after the entry.
5980        let trailing_offset =
5981            (entry_offset + entry_size).next_multiple_of(core::mem::align_of::<u64>());
5982        // Issue 1667 — the region ends on the grain and is at least a node.
5983        let new_used = entry_offset + whole;
5984        debug_assert!(new_used >= trailing_offset + trailing_bytes);
5985        if new_used > self.arena.len() {
5986            // This path reported NOTHING until phase-412's self-report went in,
5987            // while its sibling `arena_alloc` has named the knob since issue
5988            // 0900. Half of arena exhaustion was therefore silent -- and it is
5989            // the half carrying buffered subscriptions and action entries,
5990            // which is what an island image actually allocates.
5991            return Err(self.arena_exhausted(
5992                core::any::type_name::<T>(),
5993                new_used - entry_offset,
5994                new_used - self.arena.len(),
5995            ));
5996        }
5997        self.arena_used = new_used;
5998        crate::boot_report::note_alloc(new_used - entry_offset, new_used);
5999        self.note_entry_region(entry_offset, new_used - entry_offset);
6000        Ok((entry_offset, trailing_offset))
6001    }
6002
6003    /// The ONE exhaustion path every arena allocator goes through — issues
6004    /// 0900, 1036, 1496.
6005    ///
6006    /// It names the knob (`report_arena_exhausted`), writes the first failure
6007    /// and its shortfall to the boot record (the only channel a console-less
6008    /// board has), says whether the failure is a SHAPE problem rather than a
6009    /// size one (released regions that together hold the request, none of
6010    /// which alone does), and — where the image asked for it — halts through
6011    /// the platform's fatal hook, so the record survives instead of the board
6012    /// running on with an entity missing. Three spellings of this existed, and
6013    /// the `_with_trailing` one reported nothing until phase-412.
6014    fn arena_exhausted(&self, entity: &'static str, request: usize, shortfall: usize) -> NodeError {
6015        super::arena::report_arena_exhausted(
6016            entity,
6017            shortfall,
6018            self.arena_used,
6019            self.arena.len(),
6020            self.arena_released(),
6021            request,
6022        );
6023        crate::boot_report::note_alloc_failed(request, shortfall);
6024        super::arena::arena_exhaustion_is_fatal();
6025        NodeError::BufferTooSmall
6026    }
6027
6028    /// Issue 1667 — read the free-list node at `offset`: `(next, len)`.
6029    fn arena_hole(&self, offset: usize) -> (usize, usize) {
6030        // SAFETY: `offset` is a listed free region: in bounds, grain-aligned and
6031        // at least `ARENA_MIN_REGION` long, written by `arena_set_hole`.
6032        unsafe {
6033            let p = (self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8).add(offset) as *const usize;
6034            (p.read_unaligned(), p.add(1).read_unaligned())
6035        }
6036    }
6037
6038    /// Issue 1667 — write the free-list node at `offset`.
6039    fn arena_set_hole(&mut self, offset: usize, next: usize, len: usize) {
6040        debug_assert!(len >= ARENA_MIN_REGION && offset + len <= self.arena.len());
6041        // SAFETY: as `arena_hole`; the region is free, so nothing else reads it.
6042        unsafe {
6043            let p = (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(offset) as *mut usize;
6044            p.write_unaligned(next);
6045            p.add(1).write_unaligned(len);
6046        }
6047    }
6048
6049    /// Point `prev`'s node (or the head, for `ARENA_FREE_NONE`) at `next`.
6050    fn arena_link(&mut self, prev: usize, next: usize) {
6051        if prev == ARENA_FREE_NONE {
6052            self.arena_free_head = next;
6053        } else {
6054            let (_, len) = self.arena_hole(prev);
6055            self.arena_set_hole(prev, next, len);
6056        }
6057    }
6058
6059    /// Issue 1496 / 1667 — first-fit over the free list. Returns the offset and
6060    /// the length GRANTED, which is the request plus any tail too short to list
6061    /// on its own: that tail belongs to the allocation, so its release gives it
6062    /// back. A hole whose alignment slack would be too short to list is skipped
6063    /// rather than split, for the same reason — no byte is ever orphaned.
6064    fn arena_take_freed(&mut self, size: usize, align: usize) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
6065        let mut prev = ARENA_FREE_NONE;
6066        let mut cur = self.arena_free_head;
6067        while cur != ARENA_FREE_NONE {
6068            let (next, len) = self.arena_hole(cur);
6069            let start = cur.next_multiple_of(align);
6070            let head = start - cur;
6071            let fits = start + size <= cur + len;
6072            if fits && (head == 0 || head >= ARENA_MIN_REGION) {
6073                let tail = cur + len - (start + size);
6074                let granted = if tail < ARENA_MIN_REGION {
6075                    size + tail
6076                } else {
6077                    size
6078                };
6079                // What stays listed: the head slack, the tail, both, or neither.
6080                let mut after = next;
6081                if tail >= ARENA_MIN_REGION {
6082                    let t = start + size;
6083                    self.arena_set_hole(t, after, tail);
6084                    after = t;
6085                }
6086                if head > 0 {
6087                    self.arena_set_hole(cur, after, head);
6088                } else {
6089                    self.arena_link(prev, after);
6090                }
6091                return Some((start, granted));
6092            }
6093            prev = cur;
6094            cur = next;
6095        }
6096        None
6097    }
6098
6099    /// Issue 1496 / 1667 — give a region back. It is inserted in address order
6100    /// and coalesced with both neighbours, so a loop that frees what it
6101    /// allocated returns the arena to the shape it had; a hole that then ends
6102    /// at `arena_used` is handed back to the bump pointer.
6103    pub(crate) fn arena_release(&mut self, offset: usize, len: usize) {
6104        debug_assert!(len >= ARENA_MIN_REGION && len.is_multiple_of(ARENA_GRAIN));
6105        // `pprev` -> `prev` -> [offset] -> `cur`, in address order.
6106        let mut pprev = ARENA_FREE_NONE;
6107        let mut prev = ARENA_FREE_NONE;
6108        let mut cur = self.arena_free_head;
6109        while cur != ARENA_FREE_NONE && cur < offset {
6110            pprev = prev;
6111            prev = cur;
6112            cur = self.arena_hole(cur).0;
6113        }
6114        let (mut start, mut size) = (offset, len);
6115        let mut next = cur;
6116        if next != ARENA_FREE_NONE && start + size == next {
6117            let (after, next_len) = self.arena_hole(next);
6118            size += next_len;
6119            next = after;
6120        }
6121        if prev != ARENA_FREE_NONE {
6122            let (_, prev_len) = self.arena_hole(prev);
6123            if prev + prev_len == start {
6124                start = prev;
6125                size += prev_len;
6126                // `prev` is absorbed: link from ITS predecessor.
6127                prev = pprev;
6128            }
6129        }
6130        if start + size == self.arena_used {
6131            // The top of the arena: give it back to the bump pointer.
6132            self.arena_used = start;
6133            self.arena_link(prev, next);
6134            return;
6135        }
6136        self.arena_set_hole(start, next, size);
6137        self.arena_link(prev, start);
6138    }
6139
6140    /// Issue 1496 — bytes released back to the arena and not yet reused.
6141    /// Bytes handed back to the bump pointer are not counted: `arena_used`
6142    /// already went down by them.
6143    pub fn arena_released(&self) -> usize {
6144        let mut total = 0;
6145        let mut cur = self.arena_free_head;
6146        while cur != ARENA_FREE_NONE {
6147            let (next, len) = self.arena_hole(cur);
6148            total += len;
6149            cur = next;
6150        }
6151        total
6152    }
6153
6154    /// Issue 1667 — how many separate holes the free list holds. For tests and
6155    /// diagnostics.
6156    pub fn arena_holes(&self) -> usize {
6157        let mut count = 0;
6158        let mut cur = self.arena_free_head;
6159        while cur != ARENA_FREE_NONE {
6160            count += 1;
6161            cur = self.arena_hole(cur).0;
6162        }
6163        count
6164    }
6165
6166    /// Issue 1496 — RELEASE one callback entry: drop the entry in place (its
6167    /// RMW handles' `Drop`s destroy the backend entities, so nothing stays
6168    /// advertised), free its callback slot, and give its arena bytes back for
6169    /// reuse. `false`, touching nothing, when `index` is not a live entry of
6170    /// `kind`.
6171    ///
6172    /// Issue 1631 — the bytes released are the ones `emplace_entry` RECORDED
6173    /// from the allocator (`CallbackMeta::arena_len`), entry and trailing
6174    /// region together. 1496's form took the size from the caller, which had
6175    /// to restate the concrete entry type — impossible for a buffered
6176    /// subscription (its trailing region is sized at runtime) or a timer (its
6177    /// closure type is the registering crate's).
6178    ///
6179    /// # Safety
6180    /// No handle naming `index` may be used afterwards: the slot and its bytes
6181    /// go to the next registration.
6182    pub(crate) unsafe fn release_entry(&mut self, index: usize, kind: EntryKind) -> bool {
6183        let live = self
6184            .entries
6185            .get(index)
6186            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
6187            .is_some_and(|m| m.kind == kind);
6188        if !live {
6189            return false;
6190        }
6191        // Issue 1667 — the entry's own callback is running (it, or something it
6192        // called, asked for this release). Mark it and let `finish_dispatch` do
6193        // the release when the callback returns. The handle stops resolving
6194        // now, so a second request answers `false` and nothing dispatches it.
6195        //
6196        // Issue 1705 — the same for an entry an OS-priority WORKER holds
6197        // (`WORKER_QUEUED`): its callback may be running on the worker task, or
6198        // its item may still be queued. The worker skips an item whose release
6199        // is pending, and `reap_deferred_releases` completes the release once
6200        // the worker has let go. This is also the whole of what a release
6201        // requested FROM the worker thread does: one atomic flag, nothing the
6202        // spin thread is touching.
6203        if let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get(index)
6204            && tag.flags() & super::types::SlotTag::IN_FLIGHT != 0
6205        {
6206            let was = tag.set(super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING);
6207            return was & super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING == 0;
6208        }
6209        let Some(meta) = self.entries[index].take() else {
6210            return false;
6211        };
6212        // SAFETY: the entry was written by its registration and not yet
6213        // dropped; `drop_fn` matches its concrete type.
6214        unsafe {
6215            let data_ptr = (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(meta.offset);
6216            (meta.drop_fn)(data_ptr);
6217        }
6218        self.sched_context_bindings[index] = super::sched_context::SchedContextId(0);
6219        if let Some(st) = self.sporadic_states.get_mut(index) {
6220            *st = None;
6221        }
6222        if let Some(len) = meta.arena_len.get() {
6223            self.arena_release(meta.offset, len);
6224        }
6225        if let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get_mut(index) {
6226            tag.owner = 0;
6227            tag.reset_flags();
6228        }
6229        true
6230    }
6231
6232    /// Issue 1667 — mark `slot`'s callback as running, so a release it requests
6233    /// is deferred rather than dropping the entry under it.
6234    #[inline]
6235    fn begin_dispatch(slot_tags: &[super::types::SlotTag], slot: usize) {
6236        if let Some(tag) = slot_tags.get(slot) {
6237            tag.set(super::types::SlotTag::IN_DISPATCH);
6238        }
6239    }
6240
6241    /// Issue 1705 — `slot`'s entry is not to be touched by the spin thread
6242    /// this pass: an OS-priority worker holds it (`WORKER_QUEUED` — its item
6243    /// is queued or its callback is running, so even READING its state for
6244    /// readiness races the worker), or its release is pending (it is never
6245    /// dispatched again).
6246    #[inline]
6247    fn slot_held(slot_tags: &[super::types::SlotTag], slot: usize) -> bool {
6248        slot_tags.get(slot).is_some_and(|t| {
6249            t.flags()
6250                & (super::types::SlotTag::WORKER_QUEUED | super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING)
6251                != 0
6252        })
6253    }
6254
6255    /// Issue 1667 — `slot`'s callback has returned. Complete a release it
6256    /// requested while running.
6257    fn finish_dispatch(&mut self, slot: usize) {
6258        let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get(slot) else {
6259            return;
6260        };
6261        let was = tag.clear(super::types::SlotTag::IN_DISPATCH);
6262        if was & super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING != 0 {
6263            self.complete_deferred_release(slot);
6264        }
6265    }
6266
6267    /// Issue 1667 / 1705 — finish a release that was deferred while a dispatch
6268    /// of the entry was in flight, if none is any more. A no-op while one still
6269    /// is (a worker holding the entry): `reap_deferred_releases` retries.
6270    fn complete_deferred_release(&mut self, slot: usize) {
6271        let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get(slot) else {
6272            return;
6273        };
6274        let f = tag.flags();
6275        if f & super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING == 0
6276            || f & super::types::SlotTag::IN_FLIGHT != 0
6277        {
6278            return;
6279        }
6280        if let Some(kind) = self
6281            .entries
6282            .get(slot)
6283            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
6284            .map(|m| m.kind)
6285        {
6286            // SAFETY: the release was requested through a generation-checked
6287            // handle, and `resolve_handle` has refused the slot since; no
6288            // dispatch holds the entry (`IN_FLIGHT` is clear, read Acquire, so
6289            // a worker's writes before it let go are visible).
6290            let _ = unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, kind) };
6291        }
6292    }
6293
6294    /// Issue 1705 — complete every deferred release whose last dispatch has
6295    /// finished. A release deferred behind an OS-priority WORKER cannot be
6296    /// completed by the worker (it may not touch the executor), so the spin
6297    /// thread picks it up here, at the top of every `spin_once`.
6298    pub(crate) fn reap_deferred_releases(&mut self) {
6299        for slot in 0..self.slot_tags.len() {
6300            if self.slot_tags[slot].flags() & super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING != 0 {
6301                self.complete_deferred_release(slot);
6302            }
6303        }
6304    }
6305
6306    /// Issue 1631 — release a SUBSCRIPTION entry, whatever registration shape
6307    /// made it (typed, raw, in-place, buffered, with-info). See
6308    /// `release_entry` (crate-private): the entry is dropped, so its
6309    /// subscriber leaves the graph; its slot and arena bytes are reused by the
6310    /// next registration. `false`, touching nothing, when `handle` is not a
6311    /// live subscription.
6312    ///
6313    /// # Safety
6314    /// No copy of `handle` may be used afterwards — the slot is handed to the
6315    /// next registration, which may be of any kind.
6316    pub unsafe fn release_subscription(&mut self, handle: HandleId) -> bool {
6317        match self.resolve_handle(handle) {
6318            Some(slot) => unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, EntryKind::Subscription) },
6319            None => false,
6320        }
6321    }
6322
6323    /// Issue 1631 — release a TIMER entry; the timer's callback (and anything
6324    /// its closure captured) is dropped and never fires again. As
6325    /// [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
6326    ///
6327    /// # Safety
6328    /// As [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
6329    pub unsafe fn release_timer(&mut self, handle: HandleId) -> bool {
6330        match self.resolve_handle(handle) {
6331            Some(slot) => unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, EntryKind::Timer) },
6332            None => false,
6333        }
6334    }
6335
6336    /// Issue 1631 — release a SERVICE SERVER entry; the server leaves the
6337    /// graph. As [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
6338    ///
6339    /// # Safety
6340    /// As [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
6341    pub unsafe fn release_service(&mut self, handle: HandleId) -> bool {
6342        match self.resolve_handle(handle) {
6343            Some(slot) => unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, EntryKind::Service) },
6344            None => false,
6345        }
6346    }
6347
6348    /// Issue 1631 — release a SERVICE CLIENT entry; the client leaves the
6349    /// graph and any reply it was waiting for is abandoned with it. As
6350    /// [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
6351    ///
6352    /// # Safety
6353    /// As [`release_subscription`](Self::release_subscription).
6354    pub unsafe fn release_service_client(&mut self, handle: HandleId) -> bool {
6355        match self.resolve_handle(handle) {
6356            Some(slot) => unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, EntryKind::ServiceClient) },
6357            None => false,
6358        }
6359    }
6360
6361    /// Issue 1667 — release a GUARD CONDITION entry: its callback is dropped and
6362    /// `spin_once` stops polling it; the slot and its arena bytes go to the next
6363    /// registration.
6364    ///
6365    /// Unlike the other release verbs this one has a contract a generation
6366    /// cannot discharge. The [`GuardCondition`] trigger handle holds a pointer
6367    /// to the flag INSIDE the entry, and it is `Clone` + `Send`, so a clone on
6368    /// another thread (an ISR, a worker) would write into whatever reuses those
6369    /// bytes. The C++ `GuardCondition` is non-copyable and the one holder of its
6370    /// trigger handle, which is why its destructor can call this.
6371    ///
6372    /// # Safety
6373    /// No [`GuardCondition`] trigger handle for this entry — the one
6374    /// registration returned, or any clone of it — may be used afterwards.
6375    pub unsafe fn release_guard_condition(&mut self, handle: HandleId) -> bool {
6376        match self.resolve_handle(handle) {
6377            Some(slot) => unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, EntryKind::GuardCondition) },
6378            None => false,
6379        }
6380    }
6381
6382    /// Find the next free entry slot index.
6383    pub(crate) fn next_entry_slot(&self) -> Result<usize, NodeError> {
6384        self.entries
6385            .iter()
6386            .position(|e| e.is_none())
6387            // Issue 0095 — the callback-entry table (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_CBS`,
6388            // default 4) is full. Distinct from `BufferTooSmall` so the register
6389            // seam can tell the user to raise the knob.
6390            .ok_or(NodeError::ExecutorFull)
6391    }
6392
6393    /// Install a finished [`CallbackMeta`] into its slot.
6394    ///
6395    /// phase-8 (`docs/design/callback_tracing.rst`) — the ONE choke point
6396    /// every registration site funnels through, so the
6397    /// `nros_callback_register(handle, kind, name)` event is emitted once,
6398    /// here, rather than at the 25 sites that build a `CallbackMeta`. The
6399    /// design's registration half is deliberately EXHAUSTIVE across every
6400    /// `EntryKind` even though the leaf hooks are staged: a callback that was
6401    /// registered but never observed then prints as "registered, not
6402    /// instrumented" instead of being silently absent, so an incomplete hook
6403    /// set announces itself in the output rather than looking like a
6404    /// measurement.
6405    ///
6406    /// It is the assignment — not [`next_entry_slot`](Self::next_entry_slot)
6407    /// — because a slot is claimed BEFORE the fallible work (session lookup,
6408    /// arena allocation, handle creation) that can still return `Err`.
6409    /// Emitting at slot-claim time would announce callbacks that do not
6410    /// exist.
6411    pub(crate) fn emplace_entry(
6412        &mut self,
6413        slot: usize,
6414        mut meta: CallbackMeta,
6415        name: TraceName<'_>,
6416    ) {
6417        // Issue 1631 — record the region the entry's allocation handed out,
6418        // so `release_entry` gives back exactly that. Matched on the OFFSET so
6419        // a stale region (a registration that failed after allocating) is
6420        // never attributed to a different entry.
6421        meta.arena_len = match self.pending_region.take() {
6422            Some(r) if r.offset == meta.offset => super::arena::ArenaLen::new(r.len),
6423            _ => super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
6424        };
6425        trace_register(slot, meta.kind, name);
6426        // phase-463 W7 — the slot's identity for the host profile, keyed on the
6427        // arena base the dispatch sees (stable for the executor's life).
6428        #[cfg(feature = "profile-mode")]
6429        super::profile::on_register(self.arena.as_ptr() as usize, slot, meta.kind, name);
6430        self.entries[slot] = Some(meta);
6431        // phase-476 W0 — a new occupant gets a new generation, so every handle
6432        // issued for the slot's previous occupant stops resolving. Owner is
6433        // cleared; a registration made for a node sets it after this
6434        // (`set_entry_owner`).
6435        if let Some(tag) = self.slot_tags.get_mut(slot) {
6436            tag.generation = tag.next_generation();
6437            tag.owner = 0;
6438            tag.reset_flags();
6439        }
6440    }
6441
6442    /// phase-476 W0 — the handle for the CURRENT occupant of `slot`. Every
6443    /// registration returns this, after `emplace_entry` has stamped the slot.
6444    pub(crate) fn handle_for(&self, slot: usize) -> HandleId {
6445        let generation = self.slot_tags.get(slot).map_or(0, |t| t.generation);
6446        HandleId::new(slot, generation)
6447    }
6448
6449    /// phase-476 W0 (issue 1667) — the slot `id` names, if and only if `id` was
6450    /// issued for the entry that occupies it NOW. A handle whose entry was
6451    /// released, or whose slot has since been taken by another registration of
6452    /// any kind, answers `None`, never the next occupant.
6453    pub fn resolve_handle(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<usize> {
6454        let slot = id.slot();
6455        let live = self.entries.get(slot).is_some_and(|e| e.is_some())
6456            && self
6457                .slot_tags
6458                .get(slot)
6459                .is_none_or(|t| t.flags() & super::types::SlotTag::RELEASE_PENDING == 0);
6460        // Generation 0 is `HandleId::for_owned_slot`: a uniquely-owned holder
6461        // naming its own live slot. Every ISSUED handle carries >= 1.
6462        let current = id.generation() == 0
6463            || self
6464                .slot_tags
6465                .get(slot)
6466                .is_some_and(|t| t.generation == id.generation());
6467        (live && current).then_some(slot)
6468    }
6469
6470    /// Issue 1703 — the slot behind a by-index accessor's `entry_index`
6471    /// argument, which callers hand in in TWO spellings: a bare slot (nros-c's
6472    /// stored `arena_entry_index`, `node_runtime`'s resolved slot, an action's
6473    /// owned slot) or the PACKED handle an FFI issued (`HandleId::to_raw`,
6474    /// what nros-cpp's `handle_id_` and nros-c's `subscription.handle_id`
6475    /// hold since phase-476 W0). A bare slot has generation 0, so both decode
6476    /// through [`HandleId::from_raw`] and resolve here: the slot for a live
6477    /// entry, generation-checked when one was issued, `None` for a stale or
6478    /// foreign handle.
6479    ///
6480    /// The five accessors indexed `entries` with the argument as given. W0 made
6481    /// the FFI value a packed `(generation << 16) | slot`, so every packed
6482    /// caller read past the table and got `None` — `async_send_request` on a
6483    /// C++ callback client returned `INVALID_ARGUMENT` on every call, and the
6484    /// granted-QoS read-backs answered for no entity.
6485    fn slot_of_raw(&self, entry_index: usize) -> Option<usize> {
6486        self.resolve_handle(HandleId::from_raw(entry_index))
6487    }
6488
6489    /// phase-476 W0 — [`resolve_handle`](Self::resolve_handle) as an index that
6490    /// is OUT OF RANGE for a stale handle, so an existing `entries.get(..)`
6491    /// chain answers `None` for it with no further change.
6492    pub(crate) fn live_slot(&self, id: HandleId) -> usize {
6493        self.resolve_handle(id).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
6494    }
6495
6496    /// phase-476 W0 — record that `node` registered the entry `id` names, so
6497    /// [`release_node`](Self::release_node) can find it. `false` when `id` is
6498    /// stale.
6499    pub fn set_entry_owner(&mut self, id: HandleId, node: crate::executor::NodeId) -> bool {
6500        let Some(slot) = self.resolve_handle(id) else {
6501            return false;
6502        };
6503        let Ok(biased) = u8::try_from(node.index() + 1) else {
6504            return false;
6505        };
6506        self.slot_tags[slot].owner = biased;
6507        true
6508    }
6509
6510    /// phase-476 W0 — release every entry `node` registered, whatever its kind.
6511    /// Returns how many were released.
6512    ///
6513    /// This is what a node's destruction calls. A C++ callback's capture is
6514    /// copied into the arena and commonly holds the node's `this`, so an entry
6515    /// that outlived its node would dispatch into freed memory.
6516    ///
6517    /// # Safety
6518    /// No handle to any of those entries may be used afterwards except through
6519    /// a lookup that checks the generation ([`resolve_handle`](Self::resolve_handle)),
6520    /// which every public lookup on this type does.
6521    pub unsafe fn release_node(&mut self, node: crate::executor::NodeId) -> usize {
6522        let Ok(biased) = u8::try_from(node.index() + 1) else {
6523            return 0;
6524        };
6525        let mut released = 0;
6526        for slot in 0..self.entries.len() {
6527            if self.slot_tags.get(slot).is_some_and(|t| t.owner == biased) {
6528                let kind = match self.entries[slot].as_ref() {
6529                    Some(m) => m.kind,
6530                    None => continue,
6531                };
6532                // SAFETY: forwarded from this function's contract.
6533                if unsafe { self.release_entry(slot, kind) } {
6534                    released += 1;
6535                }
6536            }
6537        }
6538        released
6539    }
6540
6541    /// Open a subscription: claim a slot, resolve the node's identity, create
6542    /// the backend subscriber, and answer the in-place question ONCE.
6543    ///
6544    /// **phase-456 W8 — the one prologue.** Every registration that creates its
6545    /// own subscriber goes through here, in every language. The two callers
6546    /// that do not are the two that cannot: `add_arena_subscription_callback`
6547    /// is handed a subscriber someone else built (uORB needs a
6548    /// `&'static orb_metadata`, which no `TopicInfo` can express), so there is
6549    /// no topic to resolve and no session to reach — a fourth axis under issue
6550    /// 1319's rows that W8's three-axis decomposition did not predict: WHO
6551    /// CREATED THE SUBSCRIBER. It is a real axis, it is orthogonal to the other
6552    /// three, and it has exactly one member.
6553    ///
6554    /// Everything downstream of this function differs per delivery shape: the
6555    /// arena entry's type, its `try_process`, and whether it has a receive
6556    /// region at all. That part is irreducible and stays at the call site.
6557    pub(crate) fn open_subscription(
6558        &mut self,
6559        req: &SubscriptionRequest<'_>,
6560    ) -> Result<SubscriptionOpen, NodeError> {
6561        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
6562        let (node_name, ns, session_idx) = match req.node_id {
6563            Some(id) => {
6564                let r = self
6565                    .nodes
6566                    .get(id.index())
6567                    .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
6568                (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
6569            }
6570            None => (self.node_name.clone(), self.namespace.clone(), 0u8),
6571        };
6572        let mut topic = TopicInfo::new(req.topic_name, req.type_name, req.type_hash)
6573            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
6574            .with_namespace(&ns);
6575        if !node_name.is_empty() {
6576            topic = topic.with_node_name(&node_name);
6577        }
6578        // Phase 231 (RFC-0038) / phase-402 W2 — hand the backend a
6579        // receive-buffer size so it can size-class its receive storage
6580        // (zenoh-pico: small vs large). Only when the caller actually stated
6581        // one: `with_rx_buffer_hint(0)` would be a claim of "zero bytes", not
6582        // "no opinion".
6583        if let Some(hint) = req.backend_hint {
6584            if hint != 0 {
6585                topic = topic.with_rx_buffer_hint(hint);
6586            }
6587        }
6588        // phase-454 W10/W13 — the depth this registration asks for against the
6589        // depth this system DECLARED for the topic. Before the backend call AND
6590        // before the arena claim, so the region this registration takes and the
6591        // one the build reserved are the same number; unchanged when nothing
6592        // was declared, which is every image with no contract sidecar. See
6593        // `declared_qos::honour` for why Rust TAKES the declared depth where C
6594        // and C++ assert it at the call site.
6595        //
6596        // phase-456 W8 — this used to be `declared_qos::check` here and
6597        // `honour` in each of the twelve hand-rolled prologues this function
6598        // replaced. Collapsing them onto `check` would have silently reverted
6599        // W13 for every Rust registration: `check` validates and returns, while
6600        // `honour` REWRITES the depth the backend is then given. One consulting
6601        // site is the point of this function, and it has to be the honouring
6602        // one.
6603        let qos = crate::declared_qos::honour(topic.type_name, topic.name, req.qos)?;
6604        let handle = {
6605            let session = self
6606                .session_at_mut(session_idx)
6607                .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
6608            session
6609                .create_subscription(&topic, qos)
6610                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)?
6611        };
6612        // Phase 231 Wave 0.2 (RFC-0038), phase-456 W8 — THE consulting site.
6613        // Deliberately `&&`-guarded by the delivery shape rather than by the
6614        // language: a shape that must hand the callback more than borrowed
6615        // bytes cannot use the capability however capable the backend is.
6616        let in_place = req.in_place_capable && {
6617            use nros_rmw::Subscription as _;
6618            handle.supports_process_in_place()
6619        };
6620        // phase-457 W3 — tell a metadata probe what this CALL SITE answered.
6621        //
6622        // `req.in_place_capable` and NOT `in_place`: the conjunction above
6623        // includes the backend a probe links, which is the RECORDING backend and
6624        // not the one the image ships. The sizing descriptor knows the shipped
6625        // backend from the image's `rmw` name and composes the two halves
6626        // itself; what it cannot see is this half, which is why nine of the
6627        // eleven registration entry points were previously credited with a
6628        // capability they do not have (issue 1340).
6629        //
6630        // AFTER the backend call, so a registration that failed reports
6631        // nothing — a row for a subscription that does not exist would raise the
6632        // probe's count, and an over-count of subscriptions is a real cost in
6633        // every pool that derives from it.
6634        #[cfg(feature = "registration-observer")]
6635        super::registration_observer::observe(super::registration_observer::ObservedRegistration {
6636            topic: topic.name,
6637            type_name: topic.type_name,
6638            in_place_capable: req.in_place_capable,
6639            // Issue 1648 -- the slot this registration is about to claim, read
6640            // off the request rather than inferred: `DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE`
6641            // (`RX_BUF`) is the closure buffer (`unbounded`), anything else a
6642            // stated bound.
6643            claims_closure_buffer: req.slot_bytes == crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE,
6644        });
6645        Ok(SubscriptionOpen {
6646            slot,
6647            handle,
6648            qos,
6649            in_place,
6650            slot_bytes: req.slot_bytes,
6651        })
6652    }
6653
6654    /// Typed buffered subscription core (the `node_mut(id).subscription(t)
6655    /// .typed::<M>()` builder lowers here). Routes the typed subscription
6656    /// through the [`NodeId`]'s session + identity (rclcpp `add_node` pattern).
6657    ///
6658    /// Phase 403 W2 -- `rx_bytes` says how many bytes each buffer slot claims
6659    /// from the arena.
6660    ///
6661    /// phase-392 W3c -- `Some(n)` is verbatim; **`None` now means DERIVE from
6662    /// `M`**, falling back to `RX_BUF` only where no bound is reachable (an
6663    /// unbounded type, or a backend whose `MessageForRmw` carries no schema).
6664    /// It used to mean `RX_BUF` unconditionally, so a subscription that named no
6665    /// number was charged the global for every slot and a consumer who did not
6666    /// know `.rx_buffer_from_type()` existed paid it silently. The opt-out is
6667    /// now the explicit one: `.rx_buffer::<N>()` passes `Some(N)`.
6668    ///
6669    /// It is a RUNTIME `usize` and not a second const generic because on THIS
6670    /// path `RX_BUF` was never an array length -- it reaches
6671    /// `buffered_region_size`, `TripleBuffer::init` and `SpscRing::init`, all of
6672    /// which take a plain `usize`. That is the only reason W2's per-type sizing
6673    /// is expressible here at all: `Sub<{ M::BOUND }>` is
6674    /// `error: generic parameters may not be used in const operations` on stable
6675    /// (rustc 1.97.1), so the sibling `register_subscription_with_info_sized_inner`
6676    /// / `..._with_safety_sized_inner`, whose entries really do hold
6677    /// `[u8; RX_BUF]`, still need `nros::rx_buffer_for!` at the call site.
6678    pub(crate) fn register_subscription_buffered_on<M, F, const RX_BUF: usize>(
6679        &mut self,
6680        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
6681        topic_name: &str,
6682        qos: QoSProfile,
6683        callback: F,
6684        group: Option<&str>,
6685        rx_bytes: Option<usize>,
6686    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
6687    where
6688        M: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw + 'static,
6689        F: FnMut(&M) + 'static,
6690    {
6691        type Entry<M, F> = SubBufferedEntry<M, F>;
6692
6693        // RFC-0088 / phase-421 W1 — the message's declared format must be the
6694        // one the linked backend speaks. Universal: the const lives on
6695        // `RosMessage`, which `MessageForRmw` requires under every backend.
6696        crate::format_check::assert_message_format::<M>();
6697        // Phase 212.K.7.6.b — see `create_publisher_on`.
6698        crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<M>()?;
6699
6700        // W3b.5 — contracted-endpoint age hook (None = free).
6701        let age_mon = self.age_lookup::<M>(topic_name);
6702
6703        // Phase 403 W2 -- one number for the whole allocation. The region size,
6704        // the strategy's slot size and the pointer arithmetic must agree, so
6705        // they read the same local rather than each spelling `RX_BUF`.
6706        //
6707        // phase-392 W3c -- and `None` no longer means `RX_BUF`, it means DERIVE.
6708        // This is the one choke point every default registration funnels
6709        // through, so putting the derivation here is what makes it the default
6710        // at all four of them (`create_subscription`, `create_subscription_in_group`,
6711        // the builder's `build()`, and the `/clock` time source) instead of at
6712        // whichever one a wave happened to touch. An explicit `Some(n)` -- what
6713        // `.rx_buffer::<N>()` and `.rx_buffer_from_type()` pass -- is still
6714        // verbatim, so the opt-out and the opt-in both bypass this line.
6715        let slot_bytes = match rx_bytes {
6716            Some(n) => n,
6717            None => crate::rmw_type_registry::default_subscription_rx_bytes::<M>(RX_BUF)
6718                .unwrap_or(RX_BUF),
6719        };
6720
6721        let open = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
6722            node_id: Some(node_id),
6723            topic_name,
6724            type_name: <M as RosMessage>::TYPE_NAME,
6725            type_hash: <M as RosMessage>::TYPE_HASH,
6726            qos,
6727            // Phase 392 W3a — the TYPE's bound, not `RX_BUF`. The arena slot
6728            // size says nothing about the message: a 64-byte type and a 4 KiB
6729            // type both hinted the same number, so the class was chosen from a
6730            // value unrelated to what arrives. Falls back to `RX_BUF` for an
6731            // unbounded type, where no bound exists to state (phase 380).
6732            backend_hint: Some(crate::rmw_type_registry::subscription_rx_hint::<M>(RX_BUF)),
6733            slot_bytes,
6734            // A typed Rust callback takes `&M` and nothing else, so borrowed
6735            // bytes are enough: deserialize straight from the backend's slot.
6736            in_place_capable: true,
6737        })?;
6738        let SubscriptionOpen {
6739            slot,
6740            handle,
6741            qos,
6742            in_place,
6743            slot_bytes,
6744        } = open;
6745
6746        // Phase 231 Wave 0.2 (RFC-0038) — in-place dispatch when the backend
6747        // advertises it: deserialize straight from the borrowed receive slot,
6748        // no arena buffer (copy #1 removed). Else the buffered path below.
6749        if in_place {
6750            let entry_offset = self.arena_alloc::<SubInplaceEntry<M, F>>()?;
6751            unsafe {
6752                let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
6753                let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut SubInplaceEntry<M, F>;
6754                core::ptr::write(
6755                    entry_ptr,
6756                    SubInplaceEntry {
6757                        handle,
6758                        callback,
6759                        age_mon,
6760                        _phantom: PhantomData,
6761                    },
6762                );
6763            }
6764            let meta = CallbackMeta {
6765                offset: entry_offset,
6766                kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
6767                arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
6768                try_process: sub_inplace_try_process::<M, F>,
6769                has_data: sub_inplace_has_data::<M, F>,
6770                pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
6771                invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
6772                drop_fn: drop_entry::<SubInplaceEntry<M, F>>,
6773            };
6774            self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
6775            self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, Some(node_id), group);
6776            return Ok(self.handle_for(slot));
6777        }
6778
6779        let (_slot_count, trailing_bytes) = buffered_region_size(qos.depth, slot_bytes);
6780
6781        let (entry_offset, trailing_offset) =
6782            self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<Entry<M, F>>(trailing_bytes)?;
6783
6784        let buf_ptr = unsafe { (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(trailing_offset) };
6785
6786        let buffer = if qos.depth <= 1 {
6787            BufferStrategy::Triple(unsafe { TripleBuffer::init(buf_ptr, slot_bytes) })
6788        } else {
6789            BufferStrategy::Ring(unsafe { SpscRing::init(buf_ptr, slot_bytes, qos.depth as usize) })
6790        };
6791
6792        unsafe {
6793            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
6794            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut Entry<M, F>;
6795            core::ptr::write(
6796                entry_ptr,
6797                Entry {
6798                    handle,
6799                    buffer,
6800                    callback,
6801                    age_mon,
6802                    _phantom: PhantomData,
6803                },
6804            );
6805        }
6806
6807        let meta = CallbackMeta {
6808            offset: entry_offset,
6809            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
6810            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
6811            try_process: sub_buffered_try_process::<M, F>,
6812            has_data: sub_buffered_has_data::<M, F>,
6813            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
6814            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
6815            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<M, F>>,
6816        };
6817        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
6818        // Phase 104.C.4 — apply Node's default SchedContext.
6819        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, Some(node_id), group);
6820        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
6821    }
6822
6823    /// Generic (type-erased) buffered subscription core (the
6824    /// `node_mut(id).subscription(t).generic(ty, hash)` builder lowers here).
6825    /// Routes the subscriber creation through the [`NodeId`]'s
6826    /// session + identity (rclcpp `add_node` pattern).
6827    ///
6828    /// Use this in bridge code where two Nodes bind to different RMW
6829    /// backends:
6830    ///
6831    /// ```ignore
6832    /// let node_in = exec.node_builder("ingress").rmw("zenoh").build()?;
6833    /// let pub_out = exec.with_node(node_out, |n| {
6834    ///     n.create_publisher_raw("/fwd", TYPE, HASH)
6835    /// })??;
6836    /// exec.register_subscription_buffered_raw_on::<_, 1024>(
6837    ///     node_in, "/src", TYPE, HASH, qos(),
6838    ///     move |bytes: &[u8]| { let _ = pub_out.publish_raw(bytes); },
6839    /// )?;
6840    /// ```
6841    pub(crate) fn register_subscription_buffered_raw_on<F, const RX_BUF: usize>(
6842        &mut self,
6843        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
6844        topic_name: &str,
6845        type_name: &str,
6846        type_hash: &str,
6847        qos: QoSProfile,
6848        callback: F,
6849    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
6850    where
6851        F: FnMut(&[u8]) + 'static,
6852    {
6853        // Issue #52 — fold the node's baked overrides for this topic before the
6854        // backend-compat check runs inside `create_subscription`.
6855        //
6856        // **This is the one registration that does it**, which phase-456 W8
6857        // noticed while collapsing the twelve prologues into one and did NOT
6858        // change: the other eleven reach `create_subscription` with the QoS
6859        // their caller passed. Whether that is a defect or a deliberate limit
6860        // of the generic bridge path is a question with a measurable answer and
6861        // no answer here, so the asymmetry stays where it was, stated.
6862        let overrides = self
6863            .nodes
6864            .get(node_id.index())
6865            .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?
6866            .qos_overrides;
6867        let qos = super::node_record::apply_qos_override_codes(
6868            qos,
6869            topic_name,
6870            nros_rmw::QoSOverrideRole::Subscription,
6871            overrides,
6872        );
6873
6874        let SubscriptionOpen {
6875            slot,
6876            handle,
6877            qos,
6878            in_place,
6879            slot_bytes,
6880        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
6881            node_id: Some(node_id),
6882            topic_name,
6883            type_name,
6884            type_hash,
6885            qos,
6886            backend_hint: None,
6887            slot_bytes: RX_BUF,
6888            // Issue 1340 — `FnMut(&[u8])` IS a borrowed-bytes callback, which is
6889            // exactly what `process_raw_in_place` hands over, so this shape takes
6890            // the in-place row the way the C raw path does.
6891            //
6892            // This used to be `false` because the buffered entry is shared with
6893            // `Self::add_arena_subscription_callback` and "an in-place twin would
6894            // have to serve both". It does not: that caller supplies its own
6895            // subscriber and never reaches `open_subscription`, so no in-place
6896            // report can arrive there. The branch below is local to this entry
6897            // point, and the shared buffered emplace is untouched.
6898            //
6899            // phase-457 W5 (issue 1522) — spelled as the SHAPE rather than as a
6900            // literal, because the declarative registrar lowers here and the
6901            // metadata probe must state the same bool without registering. One
6902            // definition (`DeclaredSubscriptionShape::in_place_capable`), two
6903            // readers, so the row the build prices and the claim made here
6904            // moved together when it flipped.
6905            in_place_capable: super::declared_shape::DeclaredSubscriptionShape::BufferedRaw
6906                .in_place_capable(),
6907        })?;
6908
6909        if in_place {
6910            // No receive region: the backend's slot is the buffer for the
6911            // duration of the callback. This is the whole of issue 1340's saving
6912            // on the generic path — `buffered_region_size(depth, RX_BUF)` is
6913            // never reserved.
6914            type Entry<F> = super::arena::SubInplaceRawEntry<F>;
6915            let entry_offset = self.arena_alloc::<Entry<F>>()?;
6916            unsafe {
6917                let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
6918                let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut Entry<F>;
6919                core::ptr::write(entry_ptr, Entry { handle, callback });
6920            }
6921            let meta = CallbackMeta {
6922                offset: entry_offset,
6923                kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
6924                arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
6925                try_process: super::arena::sub_inplace_raw_try_process::<F>,
6926                has_data: super::arena::sub_inplace_raw_has_data::<F>,
6927                pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
6928                invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
6929                drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<F>>,
6930            };
6931            // Same trace name as the buffered arm, so a trace reads the same
6932            // whichever dispatch the backend chose.
6933            self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Slot("sub", slot));
6934        } else {
6935            self.emplace_raw_buffered_subscription(slot, handle, qos, slot_bytes, callback)?;
6936        }
6937        // Phase 104.C.4 — apply Node's default SchedContext.
6938        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, Some(node_id), None);
6939        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
6940    }
6941
6942    /// Register a borrowed (zero-copy) buffered subscription (Phase 229.6,
6943    /// issue 0007 / RFC-0033 `borrowed` mode).
6944    ///
6945    /// `B` is the code-generated borrowed-message marker (e.g. `ImageViewable`)
6946    /// implementing [`ViewableMessage`](nros_core::ViewableMessage); the
6947    /// callback receives `&B::View<'a>` — a lifetime-carrying message whose
6948    /// unbounded sequence/string fields borrow directly from the receive buffer
6949    /// (no `heapless::Vec` copy). The view is valid only for the callback's
6950    /// duration.
6951    ///
6952    /// **Triple-buffer only.** A borrowed view must reference exactly one
6953    /// well-defined buffer slot for the callback's duration; an SPSC ring
6954    /// (`qos.depth > 1`) keeps several samples in flight with no single such
6955    /// slot. `qos.depth > 1` is therefore rejected with
6956    /// [`TransportError::Unsupported`].
6957    pub(crate) fn register_subscription_buffered_borrowed_on<B, F, const RX_BUF: usize>(
6958        &mut self,
6959        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
6960        topic_name: &str,
6961        qos: QoSProfile,
6962        callback: F,
6963    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
6964    where
6965        B: nros_core::ViewableMessage + 'static,
6966        F: for<'a> FnMut(&B::View<'a>) + 'static,
6967    {
6968        type Entry<B, F> = SubBufferedViewEntry<B, F>;
6969
6970        // Borrowed views require a single well-defined slot (triple buffer).
6971        if qos.depth > 1 {
6972            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::Unsupported));
6973        }
6974
6975        let SubscriptionOpen { slot, handle, .. } =
6976            self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
6977                node_id: Some(node_id),
6978                topic_name,
6979                type_name: <B as ViewableMessage>::TYPE_NAME,
6980                type_hash: <B as ViewableMessage>::TYPE_HASH,
6981                qos,
6982                backend_hint: None,
6983                slot_bytes: RX_BUF,
6984                // The view borrows the arena's own triple-buffer slot for the
6985                // callback's duration and `ViewableMessage::deserialize_view` is
6986                // what produces it, so there is no `FnMut(&[u8])` here to hand a
6987                // backend slot to. Making this shape in-place is a real option and
6988                // a separate change: it would move the borrow from the arena to the
6989                // backend's ring, which is a lifetime argument this item did not
6990                // make.
6991                in_place_capable: false,
6992            })?;
6993
6994        let (_slot_count, trailing_bytes) = buffered_region_size(qos.depth, RX_BUF);
6995        let (entry_offset, trailing_offset) =
6996            self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<Entry<B, F>>(trailing_bytes)?;
6997        let buf_ptr = unsafe { (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(trailing_offset) };
6998
6999        // depth <= 1 guaranteed above → always triple buffer.
7000        let buffer = BufferStrategy::Triple(unsafe { TripleBuffer::init(buf_ptr, RX_BUF) });
7001
7002        unsafe {
7003            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7004            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut Entry<B, F>;
7005            core::ptr::write(
7006                entry_ptr,
7007                Entry {
7008                    handle,
7009                    buffer,
7010                    callback,
7011                    _phantom: PhantomData,
7012                },
7013            );
7014        }
7015
7016        let meta = CallbackMeta {
7017            offset: entry_offset,
7018            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
7019            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
7020            try_process: sub_buffered_view_try_process::<B, F>,
7021            has_data: sub_buffered_view_has_data::<B, F>,
7022            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
7023            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
7024            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<B, F>>,
7025        };
7026        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
7027        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, Some(node_id), None);
7028        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
7029    }
7030
7031    /// Register a raw (type-erased) buffered subscription whose callback
7032    /// also receives a [`RawMessageInfo`](nros_core::RawMessageInfo)
7033    /// carrying the sample's wire **attachment** (Phase 189.M1).
7034    ///
7035    /// Backs the `node.subscription(t).generic(..).message_info().build(cb)`
7036    /// builder — the cross-RMW bridge reads the `bridge_origin` tag from
7037    /// `info.attachment()` for echo suppression. One sample per
7038    /// `spin_once`; the attachment is staged in a flat per-entry buffer
7039    /// (cap `RAW_INFO_ATT_CAP`).
7040    pub fn register_subscription_buffered_raw_info_on<F, const RX_BUF: usize>(
7041        &mut self,
7042        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
7043        topic_name: &str,
7044        type_name: &str,
7045        type_hash: &str,
7046        qos: QoSProfile,
7047        callback: F,
7048    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7049    where
7050        F: FnMut(&[u8], &nros_core::RawMessageInfo) + 'static,
7051    {
7052        type Entry<F, const N: usize> = SubBufferedRawInfoEntry<F, N>;
7053
7054        let SubscriptionOpen { slot, handle, .. } =
7055            self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
7056                node_id: Some(node_id),
7057                topic_name,
7058                type_name,
7059                type_hash,
7060                qos,
7061                backend_hint: None,
7062                slot_bytes: RX_BUF,
7063                // The callback also receives the sample's wire ATTACHMENT, which
7064                // `process_raw_in_place` does not carry: it hands over borrowed
7065                // payload bytes and nothing else. Not a limitation of the backend.
7066                in_place_capable: false,
7067            })?;
7068
7069        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<Entry<F, RX_BUF>>()?;
7070        unsafe {
7071            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7072            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry<F, RX_BUF>;
7073            core::ptr::write(
7074                entry_ptr,
7075                Entry {
7076                    handle,
7077                    buffer: [0u8; RX_BUF],
7078                    att: [0u8; super::arena::RAW_INFO_ATT_CAP],
7079                    callback,
7080                },
7081            );
7082        }
7083
7084        let meta = CallbackMeta {
7085            offset,
7086            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
7087            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
7088            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_info_try_process::<F, RX_BUF>,
7089            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_info_has_data::<F, RX_BUF>,
7090            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
7091            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
7092            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<F, RX_BUF>>,
7093        };
7094        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
7095        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, Some(node_id), None);
7096        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
7097    }

7099    /// Phase 250 (Wave 2) — register a generic (type-erased) raw subscription
7100    /// that surfaces E2E [`IntegrityStatus`](nros_rmw::IntegrityStatus) (CRC +
7101    /// sequence gap/dup) alongside the raw CDR bytes
7102    /// (`FnMut(&[u8], &IntegrityStatus)`). The type-erased analog of
7103    /// `register_subscription_with_safety_sized_inner`: the validator lives in
7104    /// the `RmwSubscriber` (`take_validated`), so the subscriber is created
7105    /// plainly and no `register_type::<M>()` is needed (the declarative `Node`
7106    /// path is generic). Used by the declarative runtime's `.safety()` opt-in.
7107    #[cfg(feature = "safety-e2e")]
7108    pub fn register_subscription_buffered_raw_safety_on<F, const RX_BUF: usize>(
7109        &mut self,
7110        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
7111        topic_name: &str,
7112        type_name: &str,
7113        type_hash: &str,
7114        qos: QoSProfile,
7115        callback: F,
7116    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7117    where
7118        F: FnMut(&[u8], &nros_rmw::IntegrityStatus) + 'static,
7119    {
7120        use super::arena::{
7121            SubBufferedRawSafetyEntry, sub_buffered_raw_safety_has_data,
7122            sub_buffered_raw_safety_try_process,
7123        };
7124        type Entry<F, const N: usize> = SubBufferedRawSafetyEntry<F, N>;
7125
7126        let SubscriptionOpen { slot, handle, .. } =
7127            self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
7128                node_id: Some(node_id),
7129                topic_name,
7130                type_name,
7131                type_hash,
7132                qos,
7133                backend_hint: None,
7134                slot_bytes: RX_BUF,
7135                // The sample is taken through `take_validated`, which computes the
7136                // integrity status as it copies. `process_raw_in_place` has no
7137                // validating form, so this shape cannot use it.
7138                //
7139                // phase-457 W5 (issue 1522) — as the SHAPE, for the reason its
7140                // sibling in `register_subscription_buffered_raw_on` gives.
7141                in_place_capable:
7142                    super::declared_shape::DeclaredSubscriptionShape::BufferedRawSafety
7143                        .in_place_capable(),
7144            })?;
7145
7146        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<Entry<F, RX_BUF>>()?;
7147        unsafe {
7148            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7149            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry<F, RX_BUF>;
7150            core::ptr::write(
7151                entry_ptr,
7152                Entry {
7153                    handle,
7154                    buffer: [0u8; RX_BUF],
7155                    callback,
7156                },
7157            );
7158        }
7159
7160        let meta = CallbackMeta {
7161            offset,
7162            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
7163            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
7164            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_safety_try_process::<F, RX_BUF>,
7165            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_safety_has_data::<F, RX_BUF>,
7166            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
7167            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
7168            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<F, RX_BUF>>,
7169        };
7170        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
7171        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, Some(node_id), None);
7172        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
7173    }

7175    /// Register a raw byte-shaped callback against a pre-built
7176    /// `RmwSubscriber` handle.
7177    ///
7178    /// Backend-agnostic primitive — the caller is responsible for
7179    /// obtaining the handle by whatever route the active backend
7180    /// supports:
7181    ///
7182    /// - **Generic ROS-typed flow**: call `Session::create_subscription`
7183    ///   on `self.session_mut()` with a [`TopicInfo`]. The
7184    ///   `node_mut(id).subscription(t).generic(ty, hash)` builder is the
7185    ///   convenience wrapper for this path.
7186    /// - **Backend-specific flow** (e.g. uORB needs `&'static orb_metadata`):
7187    ///   reach into the concrete session via [`Self::session_mut`] and
7188    ///   call its backend-specific create method, then hand the handle
7189    ///   here. `nros-px4::uorb::create_subscription_with_callback` is
7190    ///   the example.
7191    ///
7192    /// The arena-store + vtable wiring is identical to
7193    /// `register_subscription_buffered_raw`; the only thing that varies is
7194    /// where the handle came from. Callback fires on every message
7195    /// delivery during [`spin_once`](Self::spin_once); bytes are
7196    /// passed as `&[u8]`.
7197    pub fn add_arena_subscription_callback<F, const RX_BUF: usize>(
7198        &mut self,
7199        handle: session::RmwSubscriber,
7200        qos: QoSProfile,
7201        callback: F,
7202    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7203    where
7204        F: FnMut(&[u8]) + 'static,
7205    {
7206        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
7207        self.emplace_raw_buffered_subscription(slot, handle, qos, RX_BUF, callback)?;
7208        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
7209    }
7210
7211    /// Write a raw buffered subscription entry into an already-claimed slot —
7212    /// phase-456 W8.
7213    ///
7214    /// The shared tail of [`Self::add_arena_subscription_callback`] and
7215    /// `register_subscription_buffered_raw_on`, which differ only in where the
7216    /// subscriber came from: one is handed a live `RmwSubscriber`, the other
7217    /// resolves a topic through [`Self::open_subscription`] and gets one back.
7218    /// Both then build exactly this entry, and they used to build it twice —
7219    /// the bridge path by CALLING the other, which meant it claimed a slot,
7220    /// resolved a topic, and then let the callee claim a second slot it did not
7221    /// need.
7222    fn emplace_raw_buffered_subscription<F>(
7223        &mut self,
7224        slot: usize,
7225        handle: session::RmwSubscriber,
7226        qos: QoSProfile,
7227        slot_bytes: usize,
7228        callback: F,
7229    ) -> Result<(), NodeError>
7230    where
7231        F: FnMut(&[u8]) + 'static,
7232    {
7233        type Entry<F> = SubBufferedRawEntry<F>;
7234
7235        let (_slot_count, trailing_bytes) = buffered_region_size(qos.depth, slot_bytes);
7236
7237        let (entry_offset, trailing_offset) =
7238            self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<Entry<F>>(trailing_bytes)?;
7239
7240        let buf_ptr = unsafe { (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(trailing_offset) };
7241
7242        let buffer = if qos.depth <= 1 {
7243            BufferStrategy::Triple(unsafe { TripleBuffer::init(buf_ptr, slot_bytes) })
7244        } else {
7245            BufferStrategy::Ring(unsafe { SpscRing::init(buf_ptr, slot_bytes, qos.depth as usize) })
7246        };
7247
7248        unsafe {
7249            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7250            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut Entry<F>;
7251            core::ptr::write(
7252                entry_ptr,
7253                Entry {
7254                    handle,
7255                    buffer,
7256                    callback,
7257                },
7258            );
7259        }
7260
7261        let meta = CallbackMeta {
7262            offset: entry_offset,
7263            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
7264            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
7265            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_try_process::<F>,
7266            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_has_data::<F>,
7267            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
7268            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
7269            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<F>>,
7270        };
7271        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Slot("sub", slot));
7272        Ok(())
7273    }

7275    pub(crate) fn register_subscription_with_info_sized_inner<M, F, const RX_BUF: usize>(
7276        &mut self,
7277        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
7278        topic_name: &str,
7279        qos: QoSProfile,
7280        callback: F,
7281    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7282    where
7283        M: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw + 'static,
7284        F: FnMut(&M, Option<&nros_core::MessageInfo>) + 'static,
7285    {
7286        type Entry<M, F, const N: usize> = SubInfoEntry<M, F, N>;
7287
7288        // Phase 212.K.7.6.b — see `create_publisher_on`.
7289        crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<M>()?;
7290
7291        let SubscriptionOpen { slot, handle, .. } =
7292            self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
7293                node_id,
7294                topic_name,
7295                type_name: <M as RosMessage>::TYPE_NAME,
7296                type_hash: <M as RosMessage>::TYPE_HASH,
7297                qos,
7298                backend_hint: None,
7299                slot_bytes: RX_BUF,
7300                // The entry's `pre_sample` hook stages a `MessageInfo` beside the
7301                // payload before the callback runs; an in-place drain has no
7302                // pre-sample step to hang it on.
7303                in_place_capable: false,
7304            })?;
7305
7306        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<Entry<M, F, RX_BUF>>()?;
7307
7308        unsafe {
7309            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7310            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry<M, F, RX_BUF>;
7311            core::ptr::write(
7312                entry_ptr,
7313                Entry {
7314                    handle,
7315                    buffer: [0u8; RX_BUF],
7316                    sampled_len: 0,
7317                    callback,
7318                    _phantom: PhantomData,
7319                },
7320            );
7321        }
7322
7323        let meta = CallbackMeta {
7324            offset,
7325            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
7326            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
7327            try_process: sub_info_try_process::<M, F, RX_BUF>,
7328            has_data: sub_info_has_data::<M, F, RX_BUF>,
7329            pre_sample: sub_info_pre_sample::<M, F, RX_BUF>,
7330            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
7331            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<M, F, RX_BUF>>,
7332        };
7333        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
7334        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
7335        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
7336    }
