7401    /// Register a service callback with the default buffer size.
7402    ///
7403    /// The callback is stored in the arena and invoked during [`spin_once()`](Self::spin_once).
7404    pub fn register_service<Svc, F>(
7405        &mut self,
7406        service_name: &str,
7407        callback: F,
7408    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7409    where
7410        Svc: RosService + 'static,
7411        Svc::Request: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
7412        Svc::Reply: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
7413        F: FnMut(&Svc::Request) -> Svc::Reply + 'static,
7414    {
7415        self.register_service_sized::<Svc, F, { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE }, { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE }>(service_name, callback)
7416    }
7417
7418    /// Register a service callback with custom request/reply buffer sizes.
7419    pub fn register_service_sized<Svc, F, const REQ_BUF: usize, const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
7420        &mut self,
7421        service_name: &str,
7422        callback: F,
7423    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7424    where
7425        Svc: RosService + 'static,
7426        Svc::Request: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
7427        Svc::Reply: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
7428        F: FnMut(&Svc::Request) -> Svc::Reply + 'static,
7429    {
7430        type Entry<Svc, F, const RQ: usize, const RP: usize> = SrvEntry<Svc, F, RQ, RP>;
7431
7432        // Phase 212.K.7.7.b — register both halves of the service round-trip
7433        // under cyclonedds. No-op for other RMWs. Mirrors the K.7.6.b hook
7434        // on `Node::create_service_sized`.
7435        crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Request>()?;
7436        crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Reply>()?;
7437
7438        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
7439        let node_name: heapless::String<64> = self.node_name.clone();
7440        let ns: heapless::String<64> = self.namespace.clone();
7441        let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(service_name, Svc::SERVICE_NAME, Svc::SERVICE_HASH)
7442            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
7443            .with_namespace(&ns);
7444        if !node_name.is_empty() {
7445            info = info.with_node_name(&node_name);
7446        }
7447        let handle = self
7448            .session
7449            .create_service(&info, QoSProfile::services_default())
7450            .map_err(NodeError::Transport)?;
7451
7452        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<Entry<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>>()?;
7453
7454        // SAFETY: same guarantees as register_subscription_sized.
7455        unsafe {
7456            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7457            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>;
7458            core::ptr::write(
7459                entry_ptr,
7460                Entry {
7461                    handle,
7462                    req_buffer: [0u8; REQ_BUF],
7463                    reply_buffer: [0u8; REPLY_BUF],
7464                    callback,
7465                    _phantom: PhantomData,
7466                },
7467            );
7468        }
7469
7470        let meta = CallbackMeta {
7471            offset,
7472            kind: EntryKind::Service,
7473            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
7474            try_process: srv_try_process::<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>,
7475            has_data: srv_has_data::<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>,
7476            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
7477            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
7478            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>>,
7479        };
7480        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(service_name));
7481        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
7482    }
7483
7484    /// Phase 104.C.3.3.a — Node-aware variant of
7485    /// [`register_service_sized`](Self::register_service_sized).
7486    pub fn register_service_sized_on<Svc, F, const REQ_BUF: usize, const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
7487        &mut self,
7488        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
7489        service_name: &str,
7490        qos: QoSProfile,
7491        callback: F,
7492    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7493    where
7494        Svc: RosService + 'static,
7495        Svc::Request: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
7496        Svc::Reply: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
7497        F: FnMut(&Svc::Request) -> Svc::Reply + 'static,
7498    {
7499        type Entry<Svc, F, const RQ: usize, const RP: usize> = SrvEntry<Svc, F, RQ, RP>;
7500
7501        // Phase 212.K.7.7.b — see `register_service_sized`.
7502        crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Request>()?;
7503        crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Reply>()?;
7504
7505        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
7506        let (node_name, ns, session_idx) = {
7507            let r = self
7508                .nodes
7509                .get(node_id.index())
7510                .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
7511            (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
7512        };
7513        let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(service_name, Svc::SERVICE_NAME, Svc::SERVICE_HASH)
7514            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
7515            .with_namespace(&ns);
7516        if !node_name.is_empty() {
7517            info = info.with_node_name(&node_name);
7518        }
7519        let handle = {
7520            let session = self
7521                .session_at_mut(session_idx)
7522                .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
7523            // Phase 193.5 — validate against the backend's supported policies
7524            // (no silent downgrade); request/reply effectively requires RELIABLE.
7525            super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
7526                &qos,
7527                session.supported_qos_policies(),
7528                "service",
7529                service_name,
7530            )?;
7531            session
7532                .create_service(&info, qos)
7533                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)?
7534        };
7535
7536        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<Entry<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>>()?;
7537        unsafe {
7538            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7539            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>;
7540            core::ptr::write(
7541                entry_ptr,
7542                Entry {
7543                    handle,
7544                    req_buffer: [0u8; REQ_BUF],
7545                    reply_buffer: [0u8; REPLY_BUF],
7546                    callback,
7547                    _phantom: PhantomData,
7548                },
7549            );
7550        }
7551
7552        let meta = CallbackMeta {
7553            offset,
7554            kind: EntryKind::Service,
7555            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
7556            try_process: srv_try_process::<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>,
7557            has_data: srv_has_data::<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>,
7558            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
7559            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
7560            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry<Svc, F, REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>>,
7561        };
7562        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(service_name));
7563        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, Some(node_id), None);
7564        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
7565    }
7566
7567    /// Phase 104.C.3.3.a — Node-aware variant of
7568    /// [`register_service`](Self::register_service).
7569    pub fn register_service_on<Svc, F>(
7570        &mut self,
7571        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
7572        service_name: &str,
7573        callback: F,
7574    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7575    where
7576        Svc: RosService + 'static,
7577        Svc::Request: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
7578        Svc::Reply: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
7579        F: FnMut(&Svc::Request) -> Svc::Reply + 'static,
7580    {
7581        self.register_service_sized_on::<
7582            Svc,
7583            F,
7584            { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
7585            { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
7586        >(node_id, service_name, QoSProfile::services_default(), callback)
7587    }
7588
7589    // ========================================================================
7590    // Timer registration
7591    // ========================================================================
7592
7593    /// The ONE timer registration in the tree (phase-430 W4).
7594    ///
7595    /// Every timer verb — the four `Executor::register_timer*` entry points
7596    /// below, `Node::create_timer_in_group` / `create_timer_on_clock*`, the
7597    /// declarative `nros::Node` timer, and the C/C++ FFI that lower to them —
7598    /// constructs its arena entry HERE. Until W4 there were four copies of this
7599    /// body differing only in `oneshot`, `clock_source` and whether the sched
7600    /// binding was applied, and phase-425's clock axis reached exactly one of
7601    /// them; that is how a `nros::main!` component could declare a timer but
7602    /// not a ROS-time one.
7603    ///
7604    /// `node_id` / `group` feed `apply_node_default_sched` (phase 273: group
7605    /// table > node default > SC 0). `node_id == None` is the legacy unscoped
7606    /// path and makes that call a no-op.
7607    pub(crate) fn register_timer_entry<F>(
7608        &mut self,
7609        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
7610        period: TimerDuration,
7611        source: TimerClockSource,
7612        oneshot: bool,
7613        group: Option<&str>,
7614        callback: F,
7615    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7616    where
7617        F: FnMut() + 'static,
7618    {
7619        self.register_timer_entry_with(
7620            node_id,
7621            period,
7622            source,
7623            oneshot,
7624            group,
7625            None,
7626            core::ptr::null_mut(),
7627            move |_| callback,
7628        )
7629    }
7630
7631    /// [`register_timer_entry`](Self::register_timer_entry), with a CAPTURE
7632    /// the arena holds — phase-476 W2.
7633    ///
7634    /// The callback is BUILT after the allocation, by `make`, from the context
7635    /// pointer the entry should dispatch with: `place_capture`'s copy of
7636    /// `capture` when there is one, otherwise `context` unchanged. That is what
7637    /// lets the capture ride in the timer entry's own trailing region (so a
7638    /// release frees it) while the closure that reads it is still a plain
7639    /// `TimerEntry<F>`.
7640    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
7641    pub(crate) fn register_timer_entry_with<F, M>(
7642        &mut self,
7643        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
7644        period: TimerDuration,
7645        source: TimerClockSource,
7646        oneshot: bool,
7647        group: Option<&str>,
7648        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
7649        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
7650        make: M,
7651    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7652    where
7653        F: FnMut() + 'static,
7654        M: FnOnce(*mut core::ffi::c_void) -> F,
7655    {
7656        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
7657        let capture_len = Self::capture_trailing_len(capture);
7658        // No capture keeps the exact pre-W2 allocation, so a timer that captures
7659        // nothing costs what it always did.
7660        let (offset, context) = if capture_len == 0 {
7661            (self.arena_alloc::<TimerEntry<F>>()?, context)
7662        } else {
7663            let (offset, at) = self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<TimerEntry<F>>(capture_len)?;
7664            (offset, self.place_capture(at, capture, context))
7665        };
7666        let callback = make(context);
7667
7668        unsafe {
7669            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7670            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut TimerEntry<F>;
7671            core::ptr::write(
7672                entry_ptr,
7673                TimerEntry {
7674                    period_us: period.as_micros(),
7675                    elapsed_us: 0,
7676                    overruns: 0,
7677                    overruns_reported: 0,
7678                    oneshot,
7679                    fired: false,
7680                    cancelled: false,
7681                    overrun_policy: TimerOverrunPolicy::default(),
7682                    clock_source: source,
7683                    // Seeded HERE rather than on the first poll: a zero would
7684                    // make the first delta the whole epoch, which `Skip` would
7685                    // then coalesce into one immediate activation and `CatchUp`
7686                    // into a replay burst of ~10^9 periods. `Steady` reads no
7687                    // clock at all, so its seed is 0 and is never read.
7688                    last_clock_ns: source.now_ns(),
7689                    callback,
7690                },
7691            );
7692        }
7693
7694        let meta = CallbackMeta {
7695            offset,
7696            kind: EntryKind::Timer,
7697            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
7698            try_process: timer_try_process::<F>,
7699            has_data: always_ready,
7700            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
7701            invocation: InvocationMode::Always,
7702            drop_fn: drop_entry::<TimerEntry<F>>,
7703        };
7704        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::TimerPeriod(period.as_micros()));
7705        // Phase 273 — apply group sched binding (group > node default > SC 0).
7706        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, group);
7707        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
7708    }
7709
7710    /// Register a repeating timer callback.
7711    ///
7712    /// The callback fires every `period` milliseconds during [`spin_once()`](Self::spin_once).
7713    /// The timer delta is approximated by the `timeout_ms` argument to `spin_once`.
7714    pub fn register_timer<F>(
7715        &mut self,
7716        period: TimerDuration,
7717        callback: F,
7718    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7719    where
7720        F: FnMut() + 'static,
7721    {
7722        self.register_timer_entry(
7723            None,
7724            period,
7725            TimerClockSource::Steady,
7726            false,
7727            None,
7728            callback,
7729        )
7730    }
7731
7732    /// Register a repeating timer driven by a CLOCK rather than by the spin
7733    /// delta — phase-425 W4, the shape rclcpp spells
7734    /// `create_timer(node, clock, period, cb)`.
7735    ///
7736    /// [`register_timer`](Self::register_timer) is the wall timer: it consumes
7737    /// the executor's monotonic spin delta and no simulator can slow it down.
7738    /// This one reads `source` on every poll and advances by the difference, so
7739    /// a [`TimerClockSource::Ros`] timer follows `/clock` — it stops while the
7740    /// simulator is paused, halves with a bag replayed at 0.5x, and restarts
7741    /// its period on a backwards jump instead of stalling for the length of it.
7742    ///
7743    /// With no `/clock` source installed, a `Ros` timer reads system time and
7744    /// behaves like a wall timer with NTP steps, which is the same fallback
7745    /// `rclcpp::Clock` has: a node written for simulation still runs standalone.
7746    ///
7747    /// The node-level spellings of this are `Node::create_timer_on_clock`
7748    /// and the declarative `DeclaredNode::create_timer_on_clock` (phase-430 W4);
7749    /// all of them reach `register_timer_entry`, which is the only place a
7750    /// timer entry is built.
7751    pub fn register_timer_on_clock<F>(
7752        &mut self,
7753        period: TimerDuration,
7754        source: TimerClockSource,
7755        callback: F,
7756    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7757    where
7758        F: FnMut() + 'static,
7759    {
7760        self.register_timer_entry(None, period, source, false, None, callback)
7761    }
7762
7763    /// Register a one-shot timer callback.
7764    ///
7765    /// The callback fires once after `delay` milliseconds, then becomes inert.
7766    pub fn register_timer_oneshot<F>(
7767        &mut self,
7768        delay: TimerDuration,
7769        callback: F,
7770    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7771    where
7772        F: FnMut() + 'static,
7773    {
7774        self.register_timer_entry(None, delay, TimerClockSource::Steady, true, None, callback)
7775    }
7776
7777    /// phase-476 W2 — register a timer whose callback is a C function pointer
7778    /// and whose CAPTURE the arena holds: the `nros-cpp` road for a C++
7779    /// lambda, the timer twin of
7780    /// [`add_arena_subscription_c_callback_with_capture`](Self::add_arena_subscription_c_callback_with_capture).
7781    ///
7782    /// `capture`'s bytes are copied into the timer entry's trailing region and
7783    /// `callback` is called with a pointer to that copy, so the caller keeps
7784    /// nothing — which is what lets the C++ side hand back a two-word handle
7785    /// instead of a heap cell the node had to keep alive. Releasing the timer
7786    /// releases the capture with it.
7787    ///
7788    /// `source` picks the clock: [`TimerClockSource::Steady`] is the wall timer
7789    /// that advances with the spin delta.
7790    ///
7791    /// `capture_drop`, when given, is called with the same pointer when the
7792    /// entry is dropped (released, or the executor torn down), BEFORE its bytes
7793    /// go back to the arena. A C++ capture is a callable that may own something
7794    /// (a `std::shared_ptr`, a `std::string`), and its bytes were MOVED here by
7795    /// copy, so this is the only place its destructor can run.
7796    pub fn register_timer_c_capturing(
7797        &mut self,
7798        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
7799        period: TimerDuration,
7800        source: TimerClockSource,
7801        callback: unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void),
7802        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
7803        capture_drop: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
7804    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
7805        self.register_timer_entry_with(
7806            node_id,
7807            period,
7808            source,
7809            false,
7810            None,
7811            capture,
7812            core::ptr::null_mut(),
7813            move |ctx| {
7814                let held = super::arena::CapturedCallback {
7815                    callback,
7816                    guard: super::arena::CaptureGuard {
7817                        ctx,
7818                        drop: capture_drop,
7819                    },
7820                };
7821                move || held.call()
7822            },
7823        )
7824    }
7825
7826    /// Phase 273 (RFC-0047) — register a repeating timer callback bound to a
7827    /// specific node and optional callback group. The group name is threaded to
7828    /// `apply_node_default_sched` so the seeded `group_sched_table` assigns
7829    /// the timer's callback to the group's `SchedContext`. When `group` is
7830    /// `None` the node's `default_sched` applies (phase-272 behavior).
7831    ///
7832    /// This is the executor-level primitive called by the Rust `_in_group` API
7833    /// (`Node::create_timer_in_group`) and the C/C++ group-aware timer FFI.
7834    pub fn register_timer_on<F>(
7835        &mut self,
7836        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
7837        period: TimerDuration,
7838        callback: F,
7839        group: Option<&str>,
7840    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError>
7841    where
7842        F: FnMut() + 'static,
7843    {
7844        self.register_timer_entry(
7845            node_id,
7846            period,
7847            TimerClockSource::Steady,
7848            false,
7849            group,
7850            callback,
7851        )
7852    }
7853
7854    // ========================================================================
7855    // Raw callback registration (for C API)
7856    // ========================================================================
7857
7858    /// The kept C-FFI subscription core (Phase 189.M2.b): registers a
7859    /// raw `RawSubscriptionCallback` fn-ptr + `context` against an
7860    /// optional node's session. The Rust ergonomic surface is the
7861    /// `node.subscription(t)` builder (closures); this is the single
7862    /// primitive the `nros-c` thin wrapper lowers to. `node_id == None`
7863    /// is the legacy single-node path.
7864    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
7865    pub fn add_arena_subscription_c_callback<const RX_BUF: usize>(
7866        &mut self,
7867        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
7868        topic_name: &str,
7869        type_name: &str,
7870        type_hash: &str,
7871        qos: QoSProfile,
7872        callback: RawSubscriptionCallback,
7873        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
7874        group: Option<&str>,
7875        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
7876    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
7877        self.add_arena_subscription_c_callback_with_capture::<RX_BUF>(
7878            node_id,
7879            topic_name,
7880            type_name,
7881            type_hash,
7882            qos,
7883            callback,
7884            context,
7885            group,
7886            rx_buffer_hint,
7887            None,
7888            None,
7889        )
7890    }
7891
7892    /// The same registration, with the caller's CAPTURE held by the arena —
7893    /// phase-456 W1.
7894    ///
7895    /// `context` is one pointer, which carries a C++ `[this]` capture and not a
7896    /// `[this, state]` or a `[obj, method]`. When `capture` is `Some`, its
7897    /// bytes are copied into the arena and `context` is repointed at that copy,
7898    /// so the caller keeps nothing and nothing the caller owns is referenced
7899    /// after this returns. When it is `None` the behaviour is exactly the
7900    /// pre-existing one, which is why the plain entry point above is a wrapper
7901    /// rather than a second implementation.
7902    ///
7903    /// **phase-456 W8 changed two things here.** The capture is a RUNTIME
7904    /// length — see `Self::place_capture` — so there is no constant the C++
7905    /// side has to match and no `BufferTooSmall` reachable only by drifting
7906    /// from it. And this path now reaches the in-place dispatch that the Rust
7907    /// typed path has had since phase-231: `RawSubscriptionCallback` is
7908    /// `(const uint8_t*, size_t, void*)`, so the backend's borrowed receive
7909    /// slot IS the argument, and a C or C++ subscription on zenoh or XRCE
7910    /// claims no receive region at all.
7911    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
7912    pub fn add_arena_subscription_c_callback_with_capture<const RX_BUF: usize>(
7913        &mut self,
7914        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
7915        topic_name: &str,
7916        type_name: &str,
7917        type_hash: &str,
7918        qos: QoSProfile,
7919        callback: RawSubscriptionCallback,
7920        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
7921        group: Option<&str>,
7922        // phase-402 W2 / issue 0896 — bytes the caller expects to receive; 0 =
7923        // no opinion. A size-classing backend (zenoh-pico) routes on this, and
7924        // a subscription that states nothing takes the SMALL class whatever its
7925        // message type. The C path had no way to say it until the options
7926        // struct existed.
7927        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
7928        capture: Option<&[u8]>,
7929        // phase-476 W2 — called on the arena's copy of `capture` when the entry
7930        // is dropped; see `CaptureGuard`. `None` when the capture owns nothing.
7931        capture_drop: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void)>,
7932    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
7933        // phase-403 W3/W5 -- size the arena slot from the TYPE, not from the
7934        // image-wide default. `rx_buffer_hint` already arrives here (phase-402
7935        // routed it to the backend's payload class and stopped); spending it on
7936        // the allocation as well is what makes the buffer per-type.
7937        //
7938        // This is the whole saving on the raw path. `RX_BUF` is
7939        // DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE, so every slot -- publishers and timers included --
7940        // was charged the largest subscription's buffer. Measured on
7941        // mr-canhubk344: 36 handles at the correct 2052-byte bound wanted a
7942        // 242096-byte arena of a 77968-byte region; only 13 of those handles
7943        // receive anything.
7944        //
7945        // 0 keeps the old behaviour, and it means "this CALLER stated nothing"
7946        // rather than "this type is unbounded" -- an unbounded type is a build
7947        // error now, so a zero here is a caller that did not ask, never a type
7948        // that could not answer.
7949        let slot_bytes = if rx_buffer_hint != 0 {
7950            rx_buffer_hint
7951        } else {
7952            RX_BUF
7953        };
7954
7955        let SubscriptionOpen {
7956            slot,
7957            handle,
7958            qos,
7959            in_place,
7960            slot_bytes,
7961        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
7962            node_id,
7963            topic_name,
7964            type_name,
7965            type_hash,
7966            qos,
7967            backend_hint: Some(rx_buffer_hint),
7968            slot_bytes,
7969            // phase-456 W8 — `RawSubscriptionCallback` takes borrowed bytes and
7970            // a context, which is exactly what `process_raw_in_place` hands it.
7971            in_place_capable: true,
7972        })?;
7973
7974        // The capture is placed AFTER the backend call and BEFORE either entry
7975        // is written, so both dispatch shapes get the same context and a failed
7976        // `create_subscription` costs no arena bytes. phase-476 W0 — it rides
7977        // at the end of the entry's own trailing region, so releasing the entry
7978        // gives it back.
7979        let capture_len = Self::capture_trailing_len(capture);
7980
7981        if in_place {
7982            let (entry_offset, capture_at) =
7983                self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry>(capture_len)?;
7984            let context = self.place_capture(capture_at, capture, context);
7985            unsafe {
7986                let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
7987                let entry_ptr =
7988                    arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry;
7989                core::ptr::write(
7990                    entry_ptr,
7991                    super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry {
7992                        handle,
7993                        callback,
7994                        context,
7995                        capture: super::arena::CaptureGuard {
7996                            ctx: context,
7997                            drop: capture_drop,
7998                        },
7999                    },
8000                );
8001            }
8002            let meta = CallbackMeta {
8003                offset: entry_offset,
8004                kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
8005                arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
8006                try_process: super::arena::sub_inplace_raw_c_try_process,
8007                has_data: super::arena::sub_inplace_raw_c_has_data,
8008                pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
8009                invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
8010                drop_fn: drop_entry::<super::arena::SubInplaceRawCEntry>,
8011            };
8012            self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
8013            self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, group);
8014            return Ok(self.handle_for(slot));
8015        }
8016
8017        let (_slot_count, trailing_bytes) = buffered_region_size(qos.depth, slot_bytes);
8018
8019        // The ring first, then the capture on the next `u64` boundary after it.
8020        let ring_len = trailing_bytes.next_multiple_of(core::mem::align_of::<u64>());
8021        let (entry_offset, trailing_offset) =
8022            self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<SubBufferedRawCEntry>(ring_len + capture_len)?;
8023        let context = self.place_capture(trailing_offset + ring_len, capture, context);
8024
8025        let buf_ptr = unsafe { (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(trailing_offset) };
8026
8027        let buffer = if qos.depth <= 1 {
8028            BufferStrategy::Triple(unsafe { TripleBuffer::init(buf_ptr, slot_bytes) })
8029        } else {
8030            BufferStrategy::Ring(unsafe { SpscRing::init(buf_ptr, slot_bytes, qos.depth as usize) })
8031        };
8032
8033        unsafe {
8034            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8035            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut SubBufferedRawCEntry;
8036            core::ptr::write(
8037                entry_ptr,
8038                SubBufferedRawCEntry {
8039                    handle,
8040                    buffer,
8041                    callback,
8042                    context,
8043                    capture: super::arena::CaptureGuard {
8044                        ctx: context,
8045                        drop: capture_drop,
8046                    },
8047                },
8048            );
8049        }
8050
8051        let meta = CallbackMeta {
8052            offset: entry_offset,
8053            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
8054            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
8055            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_c_try_process,
8056            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_c_has_data,
8057            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
8058            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
8059            drop_fn: drop_entry::<SubBufferedRawCEntry>,
8060        };
8061        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
8062        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, group);
8063        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
8064    }

8066    /// phase-417 W5.a (RFC-0089 stage 5) — the TYPED C-FFI subscription core:
8067    /// the same registration as [`Self::add_arena_subscription_c_callback`],
8068    /// plus caller-owned message storage and the erased deserialiser for its
8069    /// type, so the callback receives a DESERIALISED message instead of CDR
8070    /// bytes.
8071    ///
8072    /// This is the Rust half of rclc's
8073    /// `rclc_executor_add_subscription(executor, subscription, msg, callback,
8074    /// invocation)`. rclc has no allocator on that path either — it makes the
8075    /// CALLER own the storage, which is exactly what `msg` is here. The C
8076    /// ledger recorded our byte-oriented delivery as forced by "no allocator";
8077    /// the compared surface operates under the same constraint, so the reason
8078    /// was false and the divergence was avoidable (issue 1022 / W-C3).
8079    ///
8080    /// The raw path is untouched and stays: a byte-oriented subscriber is a
8081    /// legitimate thing to want, and this is additive.
8082    ///
8083    /// # Contract on failure
8084    /// If `deserialize` returns non-zero the callback is **not** invoked, the
8085    /// sample is dropped, `try_process` reports
8086    /// `TransportError::DeserializationError` (so it lands in
8087    /// `SpinOnceResult::subscription_errors`), and a rate-limited `nros_log`
8088    /// error names the length and the return code. A message that does not fit
8089    /// the caller's storage arrives here as exactly that failure: both the
8090    /// bounded-string and bounded-sequence decoders refuse rather than
8091    /// truncate, so there is no silent short read.
8092    ///
8093    /// # Safety
8094    /// `msg` must point to storage of the type `deserialize` writes, valid for
8095    /// as long as the subscription is registered. Nothing here drops it.
8096    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
8097    pub unsafe fn add_arena_subscription_c_typed_callback<const RX_BUF: usize>(
8098        &mut self,
8099        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
8100        topic_name: &str,
8101        type_name: &str,
8102        type_hash: &str,
8103        qos: QoSProfile,
8104        msg: core::ptr::NonNull<core::ffi::c_void>,
8105        deserialize: RawMessageDeserializeFn,
8106        callback: TypedSubscriptionCallback,
8107        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
8108        group: Option<&str>,
8109        // Same meaning as on the raw path: bytes the caller expects to receive,
8110        // 0 = no opinion. A typed caller normally HAS an answer — the generated
8111        // `<Msg>_RX_MAX_SERIALIZED_SIZE` — which is why the C entry point takes
8112        // it rather than defaulting.
8113        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
8114    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
8115        let SubscriptionOpen {
8116            slot,
8117            handle,
8118            qos,
8119            slot_bytes: rx_bytes,
8120            ..
8121        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
8122            node_id,
8123            topic_name,
8124            type_name,
8125            type_hash,
8126            qos,
8127            backend_hint: Some(rx_buffer_hint),
8128            // phase-403 W3/W5, unchanged: the hint sizes the arena slot, and 0
8129            // means "this caller stated nothing", never "this type is zero
8130            // bytes".
8131            slot_bytes: if rx_buffer_hint != 0 {
8132                rx_buffer_hint
8133            } else {
8134                RX_BUF
8135            },
8136            // The callback receives the caller's DESERIALISED storage, written
8137            // by `deserialize` from the sample's bytes, so borrowed bytes would
8138            // be enough and this shape could take the in-place row. It does not
8139            // yet: `SubBufferedTypedCEntry` also owns the `msg` pointer and the
8140            // deserialiser, so an in-place twin is a second entry type rather
8141            // than a flag, and phase-456 W8's acceptance is the RAW C path.
8142            // Stated here rather than left blank because a `false` nobody wrote
8143            // down is what this whole item is about.
8144            in_place_capable: false,
8145        })?;
8146
8147        let (_slot_count, trailing_bytes) = buffered_region_size(qos.depth, rx_bytes);
8148
8149        let (entry_offset, trailing_offset) =
8150            self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<SubBufferedTypedCEntry>(trailing_bytes)?;
8151
8152        let buf_ptr = unsafe { (self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8).add(trailing_offset) };
8153
8154        let buffer = if qos.depth <= 1 {
8155            BufferStrategy::Triple(unsafe { TripleBuffer::init(buf_ptr, rx_bytes) })
8156        } else {
8157            BufferStrategy::Ring(unsafe { SpscRing::init(buf_ptr, rx_bytes, qos.depth as usize) })
8158        };
8159
8160        unsafe {
8161            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8162            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(entry_offset) as *mut SubBufferedTypedCEntry;
8163            core::ptr::write(
8164                entry_ptr,
8165                SubBufferedTypedCEntry {
8166                    handle,
8167                    buffer,
8168                    msg: msg.as_ptr(),
8169                    deserialize,
8170                    callback,
8171                    context,
8172                },
8173            );
8174        }
8175
8176        let meta = CallbackMeta {
8177            offset: entry_offset,
8178            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
8179            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
8180            try_process: sub_buffered_typed_c_try_process,
8181            has_data: sub_buffered_typed_c_has_data,
8182            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
8183            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
8184            drop_fn: drop_entry::<SubBufferedTypedCEntry>,
8185        };
8186        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
8187        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, group);
8188        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
8189    }

8191    /// Phase 189.M3.4 — register a raw C-fn-ptr subscription whose callback
8192    /// also receives the sample's wire **attachment**
8193    /// ([`RawSubscriptionInfoCallback`]: `(data, len, attachment, att_len,
8194    /// context)`) — the C analog of the Rust
8195    /// `node.subscription(t).generic(..).message_info()` builder. Backs the C
8196    /// FFI `nros_executor_add_subscription_raw_with_info`. Flat per-entry
8197    /// payload + attachment buffers (cap `RAW_INFO_ATT_CAP`);
8198    /// one sample per `spin_once`.
8199    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
8200    pub fn add_arena_subscription_c_info_callback<const RX_BUF: usize>(
8201        &mut self,
8202        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
8203        topic_name: &str,
8204        type_name: &str,
8205        type_hash: &str,
8206        qos: QoSProfile,
8207        callback: RawSubscriptionInfoCallback,
8208        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
8209        // phase-408 W5a/W5b — bytes the caller expects to receive; 0 = no
8210        // opinion. It now buys BOTH halves: the BACKEND's payload size-class
8211        // routing (W5a, below) and the ARENA slot (W5b, further down). `RX_BUF`
8212        // survives only as the fallback for a caller that states nothing, which
8213        // is exactly its role on the plain C path.
8214        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
8215    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
8216        type Entry = SubBufferedRawInfoCEntry;
8217
8218        let SubscriptionOpen {
8219            slot,
8220            handle,
8221            slot_bytes: rx_bytes,
8222            ..
8223        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
8224            node_id,
8225            topic_name,
8226            type_name,
8227            type_hash,
8228            qos,
8229            backend_hint: Some(rx_buffer_hint),
8230            // phase-408 W5b — the hint sizes the ARENA too, not just the
8231            // backend's size class. 0 still means "this caller stated nothing",
8232            // so `RX_BUF` -- `DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE` at every call site -- is what
8233            // it falls back to, and an unhinted registration claims the same
8234            // bytes it always did.
8235            slot_bytes: if rx_buffer_hint != 0 {
8236                rx_buffer_hint
8237            } else {
8238                RX_BUF
8239            },
8240            // Carries the wire attachment — see the Rust `_raw_info_on` twin.
8241            in_place_capable: false,
8242        })?;
8243
8244        let (offset, trailing_offset) = self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<Entry>(rx_bytes)?;
8245        unsafe {
8246            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8247            let buf = super::arena::TrailingBuf::init(arena_ptr.add(trailing_offset), rx_bytes);
8248            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry;
8249            core::ptr::write(
8250                entry_ptr,
8251                Entry {
8252                    handle,
8253                    buffer: buf,
8254                    att: [0u8; super::arena::RAW_INFO_ATT_CAP],
8255                    callback,
8256                    context,
8257                },
8258            );
8259        }
8260
8261        let meta = CallbackMeta {
8262            offset,
8263            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
8264            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
8265            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_info_c_try_process,
8266            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_info_c_has_data,
8267            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
8268            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
8269            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry>,
8270        };
8271        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
8272        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
8273        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
8274    }

8276    /// Phase 269 W3 — register a raw C-fn-ptr subscription whose callback
8277    /// ALSO surfaces the sample's E2E integrity status (CRC + sequence gap/dup)
8278    /// alongside the CDR bytes — the C/C++ component-callback analog of Rust's
8279    /// `register_subscription_buffered_raw_safety_on` (`FnMut(&[u8], &IntegrityStatus)`).
8280    ///
8281    /// The executor validates the sample via `take_validated` and unpacks the
8282    /// [`nros_rmw::IntegrityStatus`] into three plain scalars (gap, duplicate,
8283    /// crc_valid) before calling `callback`. This avoids introducing a
8284    /// cbindgen-visible struct at the executor layer; the C/C++ headers pack them
8285    /// back into their local integrity-status typedef.
8286    ///
8287    /// Requires the `safety-e2e` feature. Backed by `SubBufferedRawSafetyCEntry`.
8288    #[cfg(feature = "safety-e2e")]
8289    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
8290    pub fn add_arena_subscription_c_validated_callback<const RX_BUF: usize>(
8291        &mut self,
8292        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
8293        topic_name: &str,
8294        type_name: &str,
8295        type_hash: &str,
8296        qos: QoSProfile,
8297        callback: super::types::RawSubscriptionSafetyCallback,
8298        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
8299        // phase-408 W5a/W5b — bytes the caller expects to receive; 0 = no
8300        // opinion. It now buys BOTH halves: the BACKEND's payload size-class
8301        // routing (W5a, below) and the ARENA slot (W5b, further down). `RX_BUF`
8302        // survives only as the fallback for a caller that states nothing, which
8303        // is exactly its role on the plain C path.
8304        rx_buffer_hint: usize,
8305    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
8306        use super::arena::{
8307            SubBufferedRawSafetyCEntry, TrailingBuf, sub_buffered_raw_safety_c_has_data,
8308            sub_buffered_raw_safety_c_try_process,
8309        };
8310        type Entry = SubBufferedRawSafetyCEntry;
8311
8312        let SubscriptionOpen {
8313            slot,
8314            handle,
8315            slot_bytes: rx_bytes,
8316            ..
8317        } = self.open_subscription(&SubscriptionRequest {
8318            node_id,
8319            topic_name,
8320            type_name,
8321            type_hash,
8322            qos,
8323            backend_hint: Some(rx_buffer_hint),
8324            // phase-408 W5b — same as the info sibling: one flat slot in the
8325            // trailing region, sized from the hint, `RX_BUF` only as the
8326            // stated-nothing fallback.
8327            slot_bytes: if rx_buffer_hint != 0 {
8328                rx_buffer_hint
8329            } else {
8330                RX_BUF
8331            },
8332            // Carries the integrity status, which comes from `take_validated`.
8333            in_place_capable: false,
8334        })?;
8335
8336        let (offset, trailing_offset) = self.arena_alloc_with_trailing::<Entry>(rx_bytes)?;
8337        unsafe {
8338            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8339            let buf = TrailingBuf::init(arena_ptr.add(trailing_offset), rx_bytes);
8340            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut Entry;
8341            core::ptr::write(
8342                entry_ptr,
8343                Entry {
8344                    handle,
8345                    buffer: buf,
8346                    callback,
8347                    context,
8348                },
8349            );
8350        }
8351
8352        let meta = CallbackMeta {
8353            offset,
8354            kind: EntryKind::Subscription,
8355            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
8356            try_process: sub_buffered_raw_safety_c_try_process,
8357            has_data: sub_buffered_raw_safety_c_has_data,
8358            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
8359            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
8360            drop_fn: drop_entry::<Entry>,
8361        };
8362        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(topic_name));
8363        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
8364        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
8365    }

8418    /// Phase 104.C.3.3.a — Node-aware variant of
8419    /// [`Self::register_service_raw_sized`]. C-FFI path.
8420    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
8421    pub fn register_service_raw_sized_on<const REQ_BUF: usize, const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
8422        &mut self,
8423        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
8424        service_name: &str,
8425        service_type: &str,
8426        service_hash: &str,
8427        qos: QoSProfile,
8428        callback: RawServiceCallback,
8429        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
8430    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
8431        self.register_service_raw_sized_inner::<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>(
8432            Some(node_id),
8433            service_name,
8434            service_type,
8435            service_hash,

8437            callback,

8439        )

8441
8442    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
8443    fn register_service_raw_sized_inner<const REQ_BUF: usize, const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
8444        &mut self,
8445        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
8446        service_name: &str,
8447        service_type: &str,
8448        service_hash: &str,
8449        qos: QoSProfile,
8450        callback: RawServiceCallback,
8451        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
8452    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
8453        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
8454        let (node_name, ns, session_idx) = match node_id {
8455            Some(id) => {
8456                let r = self
8457                    .nodes
8458                    .get(id.index())
8459                    .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
8460                (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
8461            }
8462            None => (self.node_name.clone(), self.namespace.clone(), 0u8),
8463        };
8464        let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(service_name, service_type, service_hash)
8465            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
8466            .with_namespace(&ns);
8467        if !node_name.is_empty() {
8468            info = info.with_node_name(&node_name);
8469        }
8470        let handle = {
8471            let session = self
8472                .session_at_mut(session_idx)
8473                .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
8474            // Phase 193.5 — validate against the backend's supported policies
8475            // (no silent downgrade); request/reply effectively requires RELIABLE.
8476            super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
8477                &qos,
8478                session.supported_qos_policies(),
8479                "service",
8480                service_name,
8481            )?;
8482            session
8483                .create_service(&info, qos)
8484                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)?
8485        };
8486
8487        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<SrvRawEntry<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>>()?;
8488
8489        unsafe {
8490            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8491            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut SrvRawEntry<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>;
8492            core::ptr::write(
8493                entry_ptr,
8494                SrvRawEntry {
8495                    handle,
8496                    req_buffer: [0u8; REQ_BUF],
8497                    reply_buffer: [0u8; REPLY_BUF],
8498                    callback,
8499                    context,
8500                },
8501            );
8502        }
8503
8504        let meta = CallbackMeta {
8505            offset,
8506            kind: EntryKind::Service,
8507            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
8508            try_process: srv_raw_try_process::<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>,
8509            has_data: srv_raw_has_data::<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>,
8510            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
8511            invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
8512            drop_fn: drop_entry::<SrvRawEntry<REQ_BUF, REPLY_BUF>>,
8513        };
8514        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(service_name));
8515        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
8516        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
8517    }
8518
8519    // ========================================================================
8520    // Raw service client registration (Phase 82)
8521    // ========================================================================
8522
8523    /// Register a raw (untyped) service client with the default reply
8524    /// buffer size.
8525    ///
8526    /// The client is owned by the executor's arena. Each `spin_once`
8527    /// dispatch polls the in-flight reply slot via `take_response_raw`
8528    /// and fires the registered callback when the response arrives.
8529    /// Used by the C API thin wrapper — see Phase 82.
8530    pub fn register_service_client_raw(
8531        &mut self,
8532        service_name: &str,
8533        service_type: &str,
8534        service_hash: &str,
8535        callback: Option<RawResponseCallback>,
8536        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
8537    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
8538        self.register_service_client_raw_sized::<{ crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE }>(
8539            service_name,
8540            service_type,
8541            service_hash,
8542            QoSProfile::services_default(),
8543            callback,
8544            context,
8545        )
8546    }
8547
8548    /// Register a raw service client with a custom reply buffer size + QoS.
8549    ///
8550    /// `qos` applies to the client's request + reply endpoints (Phase 193.3b);
8551    /// defaults to [`QoSProfile::services_default`] via the convenience
8552    /// wrapper.
8553    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
8554    pub fn register_service_client_raw_sized<const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
8555        &mut self,
8556        service_name: &str,
8557        service_type: &str,
8558        service_hash: &str,
8559        qos: QoSProfile,
8560        callback: Option<RawResponseCallback>,
8561        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
8562    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
8563        self.register_service_client_raw_sized_inner::<REPLY_BUF>(
8564            None,
8565            service_name,
8566            service_type,
8567            service_hash,
8568            qos,
8569            callback,
8570            context,
8571        )
8572    }
8573
8574    /// Phase 104.C.3.3.a — Node-aware variant of
8575    /// [`Self::register_service_client_raw_sized`]. Routes the client
8576    /// creation through the named Node's session.
8577    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
8578    pub fn register_service_client_raw_sized_on<const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
8579        &mut self,
8580        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
8581        service_name: &str,
8582        service_type: &str,
8583        service_hash: &str,
8584        qos: QoSProfile,
8585        callback: Option<RawResponseCallback>,
8586        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
8587    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
8588        self.register_service_client_raw_sized_inner::<REPLY_BUF>(
8589            Some(node_id),
8590            service_name,
8591            service_type,
8592            service_hash,
8593            qos,
8594            callback,
8595            context,
8596        )
8597    }
8598
8599    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
8600    fn register_service_client_raw_sized_inner<const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
8601        &mut self,
8602        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
8603        service_name: &str,
8604        service_type: &str,
8605        service_hash: &str,
8606        qos: QoSProfile,
8607        callback: Option<RawResponseCallback>,
8608        context: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
8609    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
8610        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
8611        let (node_name, ns, session_idx) = match node_id {
8612            Some(id) => {
8613                let r = self
8614                    .nodes
8615                    .get(id.index())
8616                    .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
8617                (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
8618            }
8619            None => (self.node_name.clone(), self.namespace.clone(), 0u8),
8620        };
8621        let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(service_name, service_type, service_hash)
8622            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
8623            .with_namespace(&ns);
8624        if !node_name.is_empty() {
8625            info = info.with_node_name(&node_name);
8626        }
8627        let handle = {
8628            let session = self
8629                .session_at_mut(session_idx)
8630                .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
8631            // Phase 193.5 — validate against the backend's supported policies
8632            // (no silent downgrade); request/reply effectively requires RELIABLE.
8633            super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
8634                &qos,
8635                session.supported_qos_policies(),
8636                "client",
8637                service_name,
8638            )?;
8639            session
8640                .create_client(&info, qos)
8641                .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ServiceClientCreationFailed))?
8642        };
8643
8644        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<REPLY_BUF>>()?;
8645        unsafe {
8646            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8647            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<REPLY_BUF>;
8648            core::ptr::write(
8649                entry_ptr,
8650                ServiceClientRawArenaEntry {
8651                    handle,
8652                    reply_buffer: [0u8; REPLY_BUF],
8653                    pending: false,
8654                    reply_ready: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
8655                    callback,
8656                    context,
8657                },
8658            );
8659        }
8660
8661        let meta = CallbackMeta {
8662            offset,
8663            kind: EntryKind::ServiceClient,
8664            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
8665            try_process: service_client_raw_try_process::<REPLY_BUF>,
8666            has_data: always_ready,
8667            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
8668            invocation: InvocationMode::Always,
8669            drop_fn: drop_entry::<ServiceClientRawArenaEntry<REPLY_BUF>>,
8670        };
8671        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(service_name));
8672        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
8673        Ok(self.handle_for(slot))
8674    }
8675
8676    /// RFC-0041 / Phase 239.1 — register a **typed callback** service client.
8677    /// The reply is eager-drained at `spin_once` and dispatched to `callback` as
8678    /// a deserialized `Svc::Reply`. Returns the scheduling [`HandleId`] and a
8679    /// `*mut` to the arena entry's send header (used to build the typed
8680    /// [`ServiceClientCallback`](super::handles::ServiceClientCallback)).
8681    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
8682    pub(crate) fn register_service_client_callback<Svc, F, const REPLY_BUF: usize>(
8683        &mut self,
8684        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
8685        service_name: &str,
8686        service_type: &str,
8687        service_hash: &str,
8688        qos: QoSProfile,
8689        callback: F,
8690    ) -> Result<(HandleId, *mut ServiceClientSendHeader<REPLY_BUF>), NodeError>
8691    where
8692        Svc: nros_core::RosService + 'static,
8693        F: FnMut(&Svc::Reply) + 'static,
8694    {
8695        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
8696        let (node_name, ns, session_idx) = match node_id {
8697            Some(id) => {
8698                let r = self
8699                    .nodes
8700                    .get(id.index())
8701                    .ok_or(NodeError::InvalidSchedContextBinding)?;
8702                (r.name.clone(), r.namespace.clone(), r.session_idx)
8703            }
8704            None => (self.node_name.clone(), self.namespace.clone(), 0u8),
8705        };
8706        let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(service_name, service_type, service_hash)
8707            .with_domain(self.domain_id)
8708            .with_namespace(&ns);
8709        if !node_name.is_empty() {
8710            info = info.with_node_name(&node_name);
8711        }
8712        let handle = {
8713            let session = self
8714                .session_at_mut(session_idx)
8715                .ok_or(NodeError::BackendMismatch)?;
8716            super::node::validate_qos_or_report(
8717                &qos,
8718                session.supported_qos_policies(),
8719                "client",
8720                service_name,
8721            )?;
8722            session
8723                .create_client(&info, qos)
8724                .map_err(|_| NodeError::Transport(TransportError::ServiceClientCreationFailed))?
8725        };
8726
8727        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<ServiceClientCallbackEntry<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>>()?;
8728        let hdr_ptr = unsafe {
8729            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8730            let entry_ptr =
8731                arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut ServiceClientCallbackEntry<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>;
8732            core::ptr::write(
8733                entry_ptr,
8734                ServiceClientCallbackEntry {
8735                    hdr: ServiceClientSendHeader {
8736                        handle,
8737                        reply_buffer: [0u8; REPLY_BUF],
8738                        pending: false,
8739                        reply_ready: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
8740                    },
8741                    callback,
8742                    _phantom: core::marker::PhantomData,
8743                },
8744            );
8745            &mut (*entry_ptr).hdr as *mut ServiceClientSendHeader<REPLY_BUF>
8746        };
8747
8748        let meta = CallbackMeta {
8749            offset,
8750            kind: EntryKind::ServiceClient,
8751            arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
8752            try_process: service_client_callback_try_process::<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>,
8753            has_data: always_ready,
8754            pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
8755            invocation: InvocationMode::Always,
8756            drop_fn: drop_entry::<ServiceClientCallbackEntry<Svc, F, REPLY_BUF>>,
8757        };
8758        self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Text(service_name));
8759        self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
8760        Ok((self.handle_for(slot), hdr_ptr))
8761    }
8762
8763    // ========================================================================
8764    // Guard condition registration
8765    // ========================================================================
8766
8767    /// Register a guard condition with a callback, on no particular node.
8768    ///
8769    /// Returns both the [`HandleId`] for trigger configuration and a
8770    /// [`GuardCondition`] for triggering from other threads.
8771    ///
8772    /// **This is the ours-only PRIMITIVE, not the verb a user reaches for.**
8773    /// phase-417 W4.e settled that the NODE owns a guard condition in all three
8774    /// languages, so the spelling an application writes is
8775    /// [`Node::create_guard_condition`](crate::executor::Node::create_guard_condition)
8776    /// — which is this function with a node bound, so the guard inherits that
8777    /// node's `SchedContext` like every other entity the node creates. This one
8778    /// stays because the executor is what owns the arena the flag lives in, and
8779    /// because an image with no node at all (a bare `Executor::open` plus a
8780    /// wake source) still has to be able to make one.
8781    pub fn register_guard_condition<F>(
8782        &mut self,
8783        callback: F,
8784    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
8785    where
8786        F: FnMut() + 'static,
8787    {
8788        self.register_guard_condition_on(None, callback)
8789    }
8790
8791    /// The node-bound form of [`register_guard_condition`](Self::register_guard_condition)
8792    /// — phase-417 W4.e.
8793    ///
8794    /// `node_id == None` is the legacy nodeless path and behaves exactly as
8795    /// `register_guard_condition` always did. With a node, the registered slot
8796    /// takes that node's default `SchedContext`, which is what "the node owns
8797    /// it" has to mean for a callback that shares one executor with every other
8798    /// tier in the image (RFC-0047).
8799    pub fn register_guard_condition_on<F>(
8800        &mut self,
8801        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
8802        callback: F,
8803    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
8804    where
8805        F: FnMut() + 'static,
8806    {
8807        let slot = self.next_entry_slot()?;
8808        let offset = self.arena_alloc::<GuardConditionEntry<F>>()?;
8809
8810        unsafe {
8811            let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8812            let entry_ptr = arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut GuardConditionEntry<F>;
8813            core::ptr::write(
8814                entry_ptr,
8815                GuardConditionEntry {
8816                    flag: portable_atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
8817                    callback,
8818                },
8819            );
8820
8821            // Create a handle pointing to the flag in the arena
8822            let flag_ptr = &(*entry_ptr).flag as *const portable_atomic::AtomicBool;
8823            #[allow(unused_mut)]
8824            let mut guard_handle = GuardCondition::new(flag_ptr);
8825            // Phase 124.B.5 — wire the wake callback so trigger()
8826            // also signals the executor's wake_cv.
8827            #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
8828            {
8829                let ctx = self.wake_ctx_ptr();
8830                guard_handle.set_wake_cb(nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb, ctx);
8831            }
8832
8833            let meta = CallbackMeta {
8834                offset,
8835                kind: EntryKind::GuardCondition,
8836                arena_len: super::arena::ArenaLen::UNRECORDED,
8837                try_process: guard_try_process::<F>,
8838                has_data: guard_has_data::<F>,
8839                pre_sample: no_pre_sample,
8840                invocation: InvocationMode::OnNewData,
8841                drop_fn: drop_entry::<GuardConditionEntry<F>>,
8842            };
8843            self.emplace_entry(slot, meta, TraceName::Slot("guard", slot));
8844            self.apply_node_default_sched(slot, node_id, None);
8845
8846            Ok((self.handle_for(slot), guard_handle))
8847        }
8848    }
8849
8850    /// phase-467 Row 8 — a guard condition the BACKEND triggers when the ROS
8851    /// graph changes. Upstream's `rcl_node_get_graph_guard_condition`, under
8852    /// this project's guard-condition shape.
8853    ///
8854    /// **The verb is upstream's, the shape is ours, and the difference is
8855    /// stated rather than silent.** `rcl_node_get_graph_guard_condition`
8856    /// RETURNS a borrowed handle to a guard the node owns, which the caller
8857    /// then adds to a wait set. RFC-0018/0019 forbids returning an owned
8858    /// handle across the C seam, we decline wait sets (RFC-0002: one executor
8859    /// per RTOS task), and a guard condition here is created into CALLER
8860    /// storage with its callback bound at creation. So this CREATES one —
8861    /// exactly as [`register_guard_condition_on`] does — and differs from it
8862    /// only in who pulls the trigger.
8863    ///
8864    /// Order matters and is the reason this is one verb rather than two. The
8865    /// backend is asked whether it HAS a graph before a handle slot is
8866    /// consumed, so a caller on XRCE or uORB gets `Unsupported` and an
8867    /// unchanged executor, never a guard condition nothing will ever fire.
8868    ///
8869    /// [`register_guard_condition_on`]: Self::register_guard_condition_on
8870    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
8871    pub fn register_graph_change_guard_on<F>(
8872        &mut self,
8873        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
8874        callback: F,
8875    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
8876    where
8877        F: FnMut() + 'static,
8878    {
8879        // The probe FIRST — see the doc comment. `supports_*` asks by
8880        // clearing, which is idempotent and costs nothing.
8881        if !self.supports_graph_change_callback() {
8882            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::Unsupported));
8883        }
8884        let (handle_id, guard) = self.register_guard_condition_on(node_id, callback)?;
8885        self.install_graph_change_guard(&guard)?;
8886        Ok((handle_id, guard))
8887    }
8888
8889    /// The nodeless form of
8890    /// [`register_graph_change_guard_on`](Self::register_graph_change_guard_on),
8891    /// for an image with a session and no node — the same pairing
8892    /// [`register_guard_condition`](Self::register_guard_condition) has.
8893    #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
8894    pub fn register_graph_change_guard<F>(
8895        &mut self,
8896        callback: F,
8897    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
8898    where
8899        F: FnMut() + 'static,
8900    {
8901        self.register_graph_change_guard_on(None, callback)
8902    }
8903
8904    /// The same two verbs on a build with no `rmw-cffi` backend seam, or no
8905    /// allocator — they REFUSE rather than disappear.
8906    ///
8907    /// The cfg'd-out spelling was the first shape and it was wrong in a way
8908    /// `just check fast` cannot see: `nros_node_get_graph_guard_condition` is
8909    /// a C ABI symbol and calls this unconditionally, so a feature
8910    /// combination without the seam stopped `nros-c` from COMPILING
8911    /// (`check-build`'s `workspace-features`, which is the lane that unifies
8912    /// nothing and therefore sees each combination as a user would).
8913    ///
8914    /// Refusing is also the honest answer rather than a compile fix. The
8915    /// graph-change edge is installed on a SESSION through the backend seam;
8916    /// without that seam there is no backend to install it on, and the
8917    /// executor-owned target needs an allocator for the box the backend holds
8918    /// a pointer to. `Unsupported` is what a caller gets from a backend with
8919    /// no graph too, so the C entry point answers `NROS_RET_UNSUPPORTED` in
8920    /// both cases and a ported program sees one behaviour, not two.
8921    #[cfg(not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
8922    pub fn register_graph_change_guard_on<F>(
8923        &mut self,
8924        node_id: Option<super::node_record::NodeId>,
8925        callback: F,
8926    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
8927    where
8928        F: FnMut() + 'static,
8929    {
8930        let _ = (node_id, callback);
8931        Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::Unsupported))
8932    }
8933
8934    /// The nodeless form on a build with no backend seam — see
8935    /// [`register_graph_change_guard_on`](Self::register_graph_change_guard_on).
8936    #[cfg(not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
8937    pub fn register_graph_change_guard<F>(
8938        &mut self,
8939        callback: F,
8940    ) -> Result<(HandleId, GuardCondition), NodeError>
8941    where
8942        F: FnMut() + 'static,
8943    {
8944        self.register_graph_change_guard_on(None, callback)
8945    }
8946
8947    // ========================================================================
8948    // Timer control methods
8949    // ========================================================================
8950
8951    /// Cancel a timer. A cancelled timer will not fire but still accumulates
8952    /// elapsed time. The timer can be restarted with [`reset_timer()`](Self::reset_timer).
8953    pub fn cancel_timer(&mut self, id: HandleId) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
8954        let meta = self
8955            .entries
8956            .get(self.live_slot(id))
8957            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
8958            .ok_or(NodeError::BufferTooSmall)?;
8959        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) {
8960            return Err(NodeError::BufferTooSmall);
8961        }
8962        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8963        // SAFETY: meta.offset points to a valid TimerEntry<F> which shares
8964        // layout with TimerHeader for its initial fields (both #[repr(C)]).
8965        let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
8966        header.cancelled = true;
8967        Ok(())
8968    }
8969
8970    /// Reset a timer. Clears the cancelled state and resets the elapsed time
8971    /// to zero, so the timer starts a fresh period.
8972    pub fn reset_timer(&mut self, id: HandleId) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
8973        let meta = self
8974            .entries
8975            .get(self.live_slot(id))
8976            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
8977            .ok_or(NodeError::BufferTooSmall)?;
8978        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) {
8979            return Err(NodeError::BufferTooSmall);
8980        }
8981        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
8982        let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
8983        header.cancelled = false;
8984        header.elapsed_us = 0;
8985        Ok(())
8986    }
8987
8988    /// Check if a timer is cancelled.
8989    pub fn timer_is_canceled(&self, id: HandleId) -> bool {
8990        let meta = match self
8991            .entries
8992            .get(self.live_slot(id))
8993            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
8994        {
8995            Some(m) if matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer) => m,
8996            _ => return false,
8997        };
8998        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
8999        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
9000        header.cancelled
9001    }
9002
9003    /// Get the period of a timer in milliseconds (truncated — see
9004    /// [`Self::timer_period_us`]), or `None` if the handle is not a
9005    /// valid timer.
9006    pub fn timer_period_ms(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<u64> {
9007        let meta = self
9008            .entries
9009            .get(self.live_slot(id))
9010            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
9011            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
9012        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
9013        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
9014        Some(header.period_us / 1000)
9015    }
9016
9017    /// Get the period of a timer in microseconds, or `None` if the
9018    /// handle is not a valid timer.
9019    pub fn timer_period_us(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<u64> {
9020        let meta = self
9021            .entries
9022            .get(self.live_slot(id))
9023            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
9024            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
9025        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
9026        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `timer_period_ms`.
9027        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
9028        Some(header.period_us)
9029    }
9030
9031    /// Swap a registered timer's period, in microseconds, returning the one
9032    /// it had — or `None` if the handle is not a valid timer.
9033    ///
9034    /// `TimerHeader::period_us` is the number `arena::timer_try_process`
9035    /// compares `elapsed_us` against, so this writes the period the
9036    /// DISPATCHER honours rather than a second copy of it (RFC-0019). The C
9037    /// entry point `rcl_timer_exchange_period` also keeps
9038    /// `nros_timer_t::period_ns` in step, because that field is the
9039    /// registration input a later `rclc_executor_add_timer` would re-read.
9040    ///
9041    /// `elapsed_us` is deliberately NOT rewound, which is rcl's own behaviour:
9042    /// `rcl_timer_exchange_period` swaps the period and touches nothing else,
9043    /// so a timer shortened below its accumulated elapsed time becomes ready
9044    /// at once and one lengthened past it simply waits longer. A caller that
9045    /// wants the new period to start fresh calls
9046    /// [`reset_timer`](Self::reset_timer) after it.
9047    ///
9048    /// phase-417 W5.c — the Rust half of `c:timer_exchange_period`, the last
9049    /// timer row the C ledger filed as `gap`. The answer lives here and only
9050    /// the spelling lives in the wrapper, the same split
9051    /// [`timer_elapsed_us`](Self::timer_elapsed_us) made.
9052    pub fn exchange_timer_period_us(&mut self, id: HandleId, new_period_us: u64) -> Option<u64> {
9053        let offset = self
9054            .entries
9055            .get(self.live_slot(id))
9056            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
9057            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?
9058            .offset;
9059        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
9060        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `timer_period_us`.
9061        let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
9062        let old_period_us = header.period_us;
9063        header.period_us = new_period_us;
9064        Some(old_period_us)
9065    }
9066
9067    /// Set a timer's overrun policy (issue #505). Timers default to
9068    /// [`TimerOverrunPolicy::Skip`]; switch to
9069    /// [`TimerOverrunPolicy::CatchUp`] for timers whose every activation
9070    /// is a unit of work that must not be lost.
9071    pub fn set_timer_overrun_policy(
9072        &mut self,
9073        id: HandleId,
9074        policy: TimerOverrunPolicy,
9075    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
9076        let meta = self
9077            .entries
9078            .get(self.live_slot(id))
9079            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
9080            .ok_or(NodeError::BufferTooSmall)?;
9081        if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) {
9082            return Err(NodeError::BufferTooSmall);
9083        }
9084        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
9085        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `cancel_timer`.
9086        let header = unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
9087        header.overrun_policy = policy;
9088        Ok(())
9089    }
9090
9091    /// Periods this timer missed and dropped under
9092    /// [`TimerOverrunPolicy::Skip`] (issue #505), or `None` if the handle
9093    /// is not a valid timer.
9094    ///
9095    /// Monotonic and saturating. A growing count is the on-target signal
9096    /// that a tier is not keeping up with its declared cadence — the
9097    /// symptom an external observer would otherwise have to infer by
9098    /// differencing timestamps.
9099    pub fn timer_overruns(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<u32> {
9100        let meta = self
9101            .entries
9102            .get(self.live_slot(id))
9103            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
9104            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
9105        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
9106        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
9107        Some(header.overruns)
9108    }
9109
9110    /// Microseconds accumulated since this timer last fired, or `None` if the
9111    /// handle is not a valid timer.
9112    ///
9113    /// This is `TimerHeader::elapsed_us` — the SAME counter
9114    /// `arena::timer_try_process` compares against the period and rewinds on
9115    /// every activation, so it is the executor's own answer rather than a
9116    /// second one derived from a clock. `None` is not "zero elapsed": a caller
9117    /// that cannot tell them apart reports a timer that has just fired and a
9118    /// handle that is not a timer identically.
9119    ///
9120    /// phase-417 W5.c — added because the state was already here and nothing
9121    /// exposed it, which is why `c:timer_get_time_since_last_call` and
9122    /// `c:timer_is_ready` were both filed as gaps. The C forwarders
9123    /// (`nros_timer_get_time_since_last_call`, `nros_timer_is_ready`) read
9124    /// this; RFC-0019 puts the answer in Rust and only the spelling in the
9125    /// wrapper.
9126    pub fn timer_elapsed_us(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<u64> {
9127        let meta = self
9128            .entries
9129            .get(self.live_slot(id))
9130            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
9131            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
9132        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
9133        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `timer_period_us`.
9134        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
9135        Some(header.elapsed_us)
9136    }
9137
9138    /// Would this timer fire on the next dispatch pass? `None` if the handle
9139    /// is not a valid timer.
9140    ///
9141    /// The predicate is `arena::timer_try_process`'s own guard, in the same
9142    /// order: a cancelled timer is never ready, a one-shot that already fired
9143    /// is never ready again, and otherwise readiness is `elapsed >= period`.
9144    /// Keeping the two in one shape is the point — a readiness answer that
9145    /// disagrees with the dispatcher is worse than no answer at all.
9146    pub fn timer_is_ready(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<bool> {
9147        let meta = self
9148            .entries
9149            .get(self.live_slot(id))
9150            .and_then(|e| e.as_ref())
9151            .filter(|m| matches!(m.kind, EntryKind::Timer))?;
9152        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_ptr() as *const u8;
9153        // SAFETY: same layout invariant as `timer_period_us`.
9154        let header = unsafe { &*(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const TimerHeader) };
9155        if header.cancelled || (header.oneshot && header.fired) {
9156            return Some(false);
9157        }
9158        Some(header.elapsed_us >= header.period_us)
9159    }
9160
9161    /// Nanoseconds until this timer next fires — NEGATIVE when it is overdue.
9162    /// `None` if the handle is not a valid timer.
9163    ///
9164    /// phase-417 G6. THE computation, and it has to be: rcl's own pair are
9165    /// `next_call_time` and `next_call_time - now`, so upstream cannot have
9166    /// them disagree either. Before this it lived in `nros-c`
9167    /// (`remaining_period_ns` + `time_until_next_call_ns_of`), and the C++
9168    /// half of `cpp:Timer::time_until_trigger` would have been a second
9169    /// derivation of the same subtraction in a second crate — the shape
9170    /// CLAUDE.md's "fix the CLASS, add ONE shared helper rather than a second
9171    /// spelling" rule names. `nros-c` forwards here now; so does `nros-cpp`.
9172    ///
9173    /// **The unit is nanoseconds and the RESOLUTION is microseconds.** The
9174    /// arena's timer accounting is microsecond-based (issue #505), so this is a
9175    /// microsecond quantity scaled by 1000. The unit is rcl's; the resolution
9176    /// is ours.
9177    ///
9178    /// Saturating rather than wrapping: `period_us` and `elapsed_us` are both
