9179    /// `u64`, so their difference in nanoseconds can leave `i64` in either
9180    /// direction, and a wrap would turn "overdue by a lot" into "due in a
9181    /// long time" — the sign is the whole answer here.
9182    pub fn timer_time_until_next_call_ns(&self, id: HandleId) -> Option<i64> {
9183        let period_us = self.timer_period_us(id)?;
9184        let elapsed_us = self.timer_elapsed_us(id)?;
9185        let delta_ns = (period_us as i128 - elapsed_us as i128).saturating_mul(1_000);
9186        Some(if delta_ns > i64::MAX as i128 {
9187            i64::MAX
9188        } else if delta_ns < i64::MIN as i128 {
9189            i64::MIN
9190        } else {
9191            delta_ns as i64
9192        })
9193    }
9194
9195    // ========================================================================
9196    // spin_once (three-phase: readiness -> trigger -> dispatch)
9197    // ========================================================================
9198
9199    /// Drive I/O and dispatch registered callbacks once.
9200    ///
9201    /// Three-phase execution:
9202    /// 1. **Readiness scan** — query each handle's `has_data()`.
9203    /// 2. **Trigger evaluation** — check if the executor-level trigger passes.
9204    /// 3. **Dispatch** — invoke callbacks according to their `InvocationMode`.
9205    ///
9206    /// Returns a [`SpinOnceResult`] with counts of processed items and errors.
9207    ///
9208    /// # Arguments
9209    /// * `timeout` — upper bound on the I/O wait. Saturated at
9210    ///   `i32::MAX` ms (~24 days) for the underlying transport call.
9211    ///
9212    /// Phase 84.D7: unified on `core::time::Duration`. The previous
9213    /// `timeout_ms: i32` signature had a latent footgun where
9214    /// `spin_once(-1)` silently froze timers while still polling I/O;
9215    /// `Duration` has no negative sentinel.
9216    /// Consecutive `drive_io` failures on the primary session (issue 0324).
9217    ///
9218    /// `0` means the last drive succeeded. A value that keeps climbing across
9219    /// spins is a session that is no longer doing I/O — router gone, lease
9220    /// expired, socket closed — which otherwise presents as a node that spins
9221    /// `Ok(())` forever while publishing nowhere and firing no callbacks.
9222    ///
9223    /// Transient failures happen, so a single non-zero reading is not a fault;
9224    /// a threshold (say, "more than a few consecutive spins") is the useful
9225    /// signal. Extra (bridge / multi-domain) sessions are best-effort and are
9226    /// deliberately NOT counted here.
9227    pub fn session_io_failures(&self) -> u32 {
9228        self.consecutive_io_failures
9229    }
9230
9231    /// Whether the primary session drove I/O successfully on the last spin.
9232    ///
9233    /// Convenience over [`Self::session_io_failures`] for the common
9234    /// "is my transport alive?" check.
9235    pub fn session_io_healthy(&self) -> bool {
9236        self.consecutive_io_failures == 0
9237    }
9238
9239    /// Drive I/O once, then dispatch EVERY callback that is ready — the tick
9240    /// primitive the rest of the family is built from.
9241    ///
9242    /// OURS-ONLY (RFC-0089): rclcpp's `spin_once` executes the NEXT ready item
9243    /// and has no timeout; rclpy's is `spin_once(node, timeout_sec)`. Ours is a
9244    /// blocking wait with a budget, which an RTOS task that must not spin-poll
9245    /// needs and which neither upstream has a verb for. What it DOES when work
9246    /// is ready is rclcpp's `spin_some` — the whole ready set, one pass
9247    /// (RFC-0002 §3) — so [`spin_some`](Self::spin_some) is the drain verb and
9248    /// this is the waiting one.
9249    ///
9250    /// `timeout` is the upper bound on the I/O wait. Since phase-436 W2 it is
9251    /// carried in MICROSECONDS all the way to the park (issue 1193 — an
9252    /// `as_millis()` here truncated `from_micros(500)` to `0`, and a zero
9253    /// timeout selects the non-blocking path, so a sub-millisecond `spin()`
9254    /// was a 100 % CPU loop with no warning); the conversion to whatever the
9255    /// platform primitive accepts happens once, at the park, and rounds UP.
9256    /// `Duration` has no negative sentinel, which is what the pre-phase-84
9257    /// `timeout_ms: i32` signature used to silently mean "freeze the timers
9258    /// and poll I/O forever".
9259    pub fn spin_once(&mut self, timeout: core::time::Duration) -> SpinOnceResult {
9260        let mut discarded = None;
9261        self.spin_once_capturing(timeout, &mut discarded)
9262    }
9263
9264    /// [`spin_once`](Self::spin_once), plus the FIRST failing callback's
9265    /// error.
9266    ///
9267    /// phase-427 — [`SpinOnceResult`] counts errors and drops their values,
9268    /// and `SpinOnceResult` is `Copy`, so widening it to carry a
9269    /// (non-`Copy`, `alloc`-variant-bearing) [`TransportError`] would change a
9270    /// public type every consumer copies. The value is needed in exactly one
9271    /// place — `SpinOptions::stop_on_first_error`, where `spin` has to return
9272    /// the first error rather than a count — so it is threaded out through an
9273    /// out-parameter that lives in the caller's frame. Nothing is added to
9274    /// `Executor`, so a no-alloc image pays nothing for it.
9275    ///
9276    /// `first_error` is written at most once: subsequent failures in the same
9277    /// pass are counted in the result and their values dropped, exactly as
9278    /// before.
9279    fn spin_once_capturing(
9280        &mut self,
9281        timeout: core::time::Duration,
9282        first_error: &mut Option<TransportError>,
9283    ) -> SpinOnceResult {
9284        // Issue 1705 — releases deferred behind a dispatch that has since
9285        // finished (an OS-priority worker's) are completed here, before this
9286        // pass looks at the entries.
9287        self.reap_deferred_releases();
9288        // phase-436 W2 (issue 1193) — the budget is carried in MICROSECONDS.
9289        // This was `as_millis()`, which truncates: `from_micros(500)` became
9290        // `0`, and a zero timeout selects the non-blocking path — so a
9291        // sub-millisecond `spin()` was a 100 % CPU loop with no warning. The
9292        // conversion to whatever the platform primitive accepts happens once,
9293        // at the park, and rounds UP.
9294        let timeout_us = timeout.as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;
9295
9296        // phase-425 W3b — bring the `/clock` subscription in line with
9297        // `use_sim_time`. One bool comparison in the settled case; the work only
9298        // happens on a transition, or while a request is waiting for its first
9299        // node to exist.
9300        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
9301        self.reconcile_ros_time_source();
9302
9303        // phase-426 W3 — attach the six parameter services to any node that
9304        // does not have them yet. Same reason as the reconcile above: the
9305        // request routinely arrives before there is a node to publish under
9306        // (`nros::main!` emits `apply_param_services` ahead of its per-node
9307        // `register` calls, by design). One length comparison once settled.
9308        //
9309        // Issue 1271 -- a failure is LOGGED, once, rather than discarded. On
9310        // Cyclone this fails on every spin with `Transport(Unsupported)`
9311        // (issue 1268), and with the result dropped "this node has no
9312        // parameter services" was a fact nothing on the image stated.
9313        #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
9314        if self.parameter_services_pending()
9315            && let Err(e) = self.reconcile_parameter_services()
9316        {
9317            self.report_parameter_service_reconcile_failure(e);
9318        }
9319
9320        // Release jitter, measured HERE rather than in `spin_period`, because
9321        // this is the function every driver goes through.
9322        //
9323        // The first version instrumented `spin_period` only, and that was the
9324        // same mistake issue 0736 records one layer down: a measurement placed
9325        // on a path no shipped image takes. `nros-cpp`'s tier trampoline paces
9326        // itself with a `spin_once` loop at `spin_period_us` (see its
9327        // `run_components` docs, step 4), so `spin_period` is not what the C++
9328        // entry -- and therefore not what the Zephyr lane -- actually calls.
9329        // The field recorded zero forever while claiming to measure cadence.
9330        //
9331        // `timeout` is the caller's intended pacing quantum: `spin_period`
9332        // passes its period, and the tier loop passes `spin_period_us`. A wake
9333        // that arrives later than that is late by the difference, which is the
9334        // `cyclictest` quantity. A zero timeout means "poll, no cadence
9335        // claimed", so it is not judged.
9336        self.record_release_jitter(timeout);
9337
9338        // issue 0900 — one-shot advisory when the arena is far larger than what
9339        // registered. First spin rather than "end of registration", because
9340        // there is no such point: an app may register lazily.
9341        super::arena::maybe_report_arena_headroom(self.arena_used, self.arena.len());
9342
9343        // phase-412 -- the same moment, recorded where a board with no log sink
9344        // can still be asked. Reaching this stage is the positive result the
9345        // advisory above cannot deliver on the island: registration completed.
9346        crate::boot_report::checkpoint(crate::boot_report::Stage::FirstSpin);
9347
9348        // Phase 110.0 — the backend's next internal-event deadline (lease
9349        // keepalive, heartbeat, ACK-NACK timeout, ...). Default backend impl
9350        // returns `None`, so this contributes nothing unless the active
9351        // backend opts in.
9352        //
9353        // phase-436 W6 — a CANDIDATE now, not a pre-cap. Folding it into the
9354        // budget here meant a park the session won was attributed to
9355        // `CallerBudget`, so the one number that explains a wake named the
9356        // wrong source.
9357        let session_us = self
9358            .session
9359            .next_deadline_ms()
9360            .map(|next| (next as u64).saturating_mul(1000));
9361
9362        // phase-436 W1 (issue 1192) — and by the next TIMER deadline, which is
9363        // the one class of deadline the executor itself owns. Before this the
9364        // park was bounded by the caller's budget narrowed only by the
9365        // BACKEND's next event, so `spin_default`'s 50 ms slept straight past
9366        // a registered 10 ms timer.
9367        //
9368        // Attribution is recorded here rather than derived later: this is the
9369        // only point where the losing candidates are still in hand.
9370        let (park_bound_us, park_source) =
9371            self.next_wake_bound_attributed_us(timeout_us, session_us);
9372        self.last_park_bound_us = park_bound_us;
9373        self.last_park_source = park_source;
9374        // phase-436 W2 (issue 1193) — round UP to what the primitive can
9375        // express. The old `as_millis()` truncated, so a sub-millisecond
9376        // request became a zero park: the non-blocking path, a busy loop.
9377        let park_achieved_us = self.round_park_up_us(park_bound_us);
9378        self.last_park_achieved_us = park_achieved_us;
9379
9380        // phase-436 W6 — a port that installed a park primitive does its
9381        // waiting HERE, on the bound every source agreed on, and the transport
9382        // is then drained non-blockingly.
9383        //
9384        // This is the path bare metal needs: `park_until(deadline)` can arm a
9385        // timer compare before `wfi`, which `sleep(duration)` cannot express —
9386        // and `nros-baremetal-common` notes that `wfi` with no pending
9387        // interrupt deadlocks, so arming first is not optional there.
9388        //
9389        // Additive by construction: with no primitive installed this is a
9390        // no-op and every existing port keeps the behaviour it has.
9391        let parked = match self.park_primitive {
9392            Some((park, ctx)) if park_achieved_us > 0 => {
9393                // SAFETY: `park` and `ctx` were supplied together by the port
9394                // through `set_park_primitive` and outlive the executor by its
9395                // contract.
9396                let _ = unsafe { park(ctx, park_achieved_us) };
9397                true
9398            }
9399            _ => false,
9400        };
9401
9402        // Having already waited, the transport drain must not block again —
9403        // otherwise the park and the drive would sum, and the cadence would be
9404        // up to twice what was asked. Same trap as passing a period to
9405        // `spin_once` instead of declaring it (#648).
9406        let timeout_ms = if parked {
9407            0
9408        } else {
9409            (park_achieved_us / 1000).min(i32::MAX as u64) as i32
9410        };
9411
9412        // Wall-clock-accurate timer accumulation. Measure real time
9413        // since the previous `spin_once` exited (or, on the first call,
9414        // since `drive_io` started). Two failure modes the requested
9415        // `timeout_ms` doesn't capture:
9416        //  1. `drive_io` returns early — e.g. zenoh-pico's condvar wakes
9417        //     on data arrival, well under 1 ms.
9418        //  2. The caller spends time outside `spin_once` (explicit sleep,
9419        //     ROS-2 cooperative scheduling, etc.) and that time should
9420        //     still count toward timers.
9421        // Crediting the requested timeout to timers in either case ticks
9422        // them faster than wall-clock — observed as a 30 Hz control loop
9423        // overshooting to >200 Hz under sustained traffic. Carry the
9424        // sub-ms remainder across calls so precision is preserved.
9425        // phase-359 W4 — the spin-ENTRY read, one spelling. Kept distinct from
9426        // the post-IO read below because the first spin's delta is measured from
9427        // entry; collapsing them would make that delta 0 on the first call only.
9428        let spin_start_us = self.now_us();
9429
9430        // phase-474 I2 -- arm the monitors when the policy says start-up is over,
9431        // before any rule of this spin can judge.
9432        self.update_monitor_arming(spin_start_us);
9433
9434        // RFC-0052 W3b.4 — contract monitors tick once per spin (window
9435        // logic inside; single branch when the baked table is empty).
9436        self.run_contract_monitors();
9437
9438        // Phase 104.C.6 — shared executor wake. Swap-and-clear the
9439        // wake flag; if it was set before this `spin_once` entered,
9440        // skip the blocking wait on the primary session and poll
9441        // every session non-blockingly. Lets a wake signal from any
9442        // thread (or, post-104.C.6.b, any backend's vtable hook)
9443        // pre-empt whichever session the executor would otherwise
9444        // sleep on. Cost on the no-wake path is one atomic swap.
9445        // phase-359 W10 — ONE swap, at `alloc` scope.
9446        //
9447        // This was `#[cfg(feature = "std")]` while the alloc wait arm did its
9448        // own swap further down. Merging the two arms made that two swaps of
9449        // one flag per spin, the first consuming what the second tested, so the
9450        // arm would have read `was_woken == false` forever. Deleting the outer
9451        // one instead broke a different thing: `wake_flag` is `alloc`-gated and
9452        // "spin_once consumes the wake flag" is an invariant of every alloc
9453        // build, but the merged arm only runs with `rmw-cffi` — so a
9454        // `std`-without-`rmw-cffi` build stopped clearing it, which
9455        // `test_wake_cleared_each_spin` catches. It belongs here, at the scope
9456        // of the field it reads.
9457        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
9458        #[allow(unused_variables)]
9459        let was_woken = self
9460            .wake_flag
9461            .swap(false, portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
9462
9463        // Phase 124.B.4 — condvar-blocked wait.
9464        //
9465        // RT contract:
9466        //  * cv.wait_timeout_while: bounded by `timeout_ms`.
9467        //    Predicate is O(1) — one atomic swap + Instant::now.
9468        //    No allocation. PI-mutex consideration: wake_mu held
9469        //    only during predicate check (microseconds);
9470        //    contended worst-case = notify_all execution time
9471        //    (~10s of µs).
9472        //  * Backend's `set_wake_callback`-installed cb is called
9473        //    on async data arrival from its transport-notify path
9474        //    (worker thread, ISR-safe variant via 124.B.7). The
9475        //    runtime cb writes wake_flag + signals wake_cv,
9476        //    unblocking this loop sub-poll-period.
9477        //  * Poll-only backends (XRCE, bare-metal) leave the slot
9478        //    NULL; the cv wait still fires on its deadline, then
9479        //    drive_io(0) drains whatever the backend's internal
9480        //    poll has buffered. Equivalent to their pre-124
9481        //    behaviour minus the blocking wait inside drive_io.
9482        //
9483        // Lost-wakeup safe: SeqCst flag write happens-before
9484        // notify, and the waiter checks the flag under wake_mu in
9485        // the predicate. If wake fires between drain and cv.wait
9486        // entry, the predicate sees flag=true on first eval and
9487        // exits immediately.
9488        // Phase 130.4 — only sleep in the wake wait when a backend actually
9489        // installed `set_wake_callback`. Poll-only backends (XRCE) leave the
9490        // vtable slot NULL → `has_async_wake == false` →
9491        // drive_io for the caller's full timeout instead of sleeping in a
9492        // never-signaled wait that starves reliable retransmission (Phase
9493        // 127.C.4 root cause: the server's `send_response` flushes 100 ms once,
9494        // then a blind `wait_ms(100)` sleeps with zero session activity, so the
9495        // agent's ACK arrives into a stalled session and reliable redelivery
9496        // never fires).
9497        //
9498        // Phase 248 (C2) — which primitive is a RUNTIME choice from the
9499        // platform vtable's wake probe, not a compile-time per-RTOS `cfg`:
9500        // `node_wake.is_some()` means `nros_platform_wake_*` is linked and
9501        // `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb` signals it on transport arrival.
9502        // phase-359 W10 — ONE arm. This was a `std` arm and an `alloc` arm with
9503        // the same body: block on the platform wake primitive when a backend
9504        // installed the callback and nothing has woken us yet, else drive the
9505        // transport for the caller's full timeout. They stopped differing when
9506        // the condvar fallback was deleted — the std arm's `else` branch had
9507        // already become "drive for the full timeout", which is what the alloc
9508        // arm always did — so keeping two was keeping a fork that agreed.
9509        // phase-417 W4.e — the FIRST arm is what the swap-and-clear above says
9510        // it is for, and it was missing: a wake that landed BETWEEN two spins
9511        // set the flag, and this expression then took the `else` and drove the
9512        // transport for the caller's FULL timeout, so the pending work waited
9513        // out the very budget the wake exists to cut short. Measured with a
9514        // guard condition triggered from another thread just before a 400 ms
9515        // spin: 400 ms to dispatch, against 50 ms for the same trigger issued
9516        // while the spin was already parked in `wait_ms`. Being woken means
9517        // there IS work, so the right timeout is 0 — poll every session
9518        // non-blockingly and go dispatch it, which is what the comment at the
9519        // swap has claimed since Phase 104.C.6.
9520        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
9521        let primary_drive_timeout_ms = {
9522            if was_woken {
9523                // Issue 1385 — drain the wake PRIMITIVE too.
9524                //
9525                // `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb` sets both halves of one signal:
9526                // the flag, and the platform primitive. The swap above
9527                // consumed the flag and this arm returns without entering the
9528                // wait, so a primitive left posted makes the NEXT spin's
9529                // `wait_ms` return instantly on a signal already acted on —
9530                // that spin does not wait at all, and whatever it should have
9531                // waited for is dispatched a whole spin late.
9532                //
9533                // `wait_ms(0)` is the non-blocking take: every port's wait is a
9534                // deadline (`sem_timedwait`, `k_sem_take`, `xSemaphoreTake`),
9535                // so zero means "take it if it is there", never "wait
9536                // forever".
9537                //
9538                // Measured, not reasoned: with the C executor installing a
9539                // callback (the other half of 1385), an arrival taken by this
9540                // arm left the spin after it returning in 0 ms where it owed
9541                // 60 ms of waiting — which is what `node_guard_condition.c`'s
9542                // mid-spin case caught, and what `executor_backend_wake.c`'s
9543                // second lower bound now pins. Latent until then only because
9544                // no C spin had ever entered the wait arm.
9545                if let Some(wake) = self.node_wake.as_ref() {
9546                    let _ = wake.wait_ms(0);
9547                }
9548                0
9549            } else if self.has_async_wake
9550                && let Some(wake) = self.node_wake.as_ref()
9551            {
9552                let _ = wake.wait_ms(timeout_ms as u32);
9553                // Drain any flag the cb set while we were waiting.
9554                let _ = self
9555                    .wake_flag
9556                    .swap(false, portable_atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
9557                0
9558            } else {
9559                // No wake primitive linked, or a poll-only backend: drive the
9560                // transport for the full timeout. It still BLOCKS — in the
9561                // transport's own recv — which is where every flavour ended up
9562                // anyway.
9563                timeout_ms
9564            }
9565        };
9566
9567        // std builds without rmw-cffi (mock-session tests, future alternative
9568        // backends) keep the original "drive_io is non-blocking" assumption.
9569        // `std` implies `alloc`, so this is the only std configuration the arm
9570        // above does not cover.
9571        #[cfg(all(feature = "std", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
9572        let primary_drive_timeout_ms = 0;
9573
9574        // no_std without (alloc + rmw-cffi) keeps the legacy
9575        // full-timeout drive_io call.
9576        #[cfg(all(
9577            not(feature = "std"),
9578            not(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))
9579        ))]
9580        let primary_drive_timeout_ms = timeout_ms;
9581
9582        // issue 0324 — the primary session's I/O result is TRACKED, not
9583        // discarded. See `consecutive_io_failures` for why this is a counter
9584        // rather than an early return.
9585        match self.session.drive_io(primary_drive_timeout_ms) {
9586            Ok(()) => self.consecutive_io_failures = 0,
9587            Err(_) => self.consecutive_io_failures = self.consecutive_io_failures.saturating_add(1),
9588        }
9589        for extra in self.extra_sessions.iter_mut() {
9590            // Best-effort BY DESIGN: extra sessions are bridge / multi-domain
9591            // attachments, and one of them failing must not stall the primary
9592            // spin. The old code expressed this the same way it expressed the
9593            // primary's discarded error — identically — so the intent was
9594            // invisible. It is now the only `let _ =` of the two.
9595            let _ = extra.drive_io(0);
9596        }
9597
9598        // phase-359 W4 — ONE clock read per spin, shared by the delta below and
9599        // every consumer further down. Replaces the std/no_std delta pair AND
9600        // two ad-hoc `static EPOCH: OnceLock<Instant>` blocks that each kept
9601        // their own std-only epoch.
9602        let now_us_this_spin = self.now_us();
9603
9604        // Same rule on both flavours: measure elapsed when a clock exists, else
9605        // credit the REQUESTED timeout. That fallback was previously reachable
9606        // only on no_std; on std `Instant` always answered. It stays unreachable
9607        // on std for the same reason — `now_us()` is infallible there — so this
9608        // is one expression, not a behaviour change.
9609        let delta_us = match now_us_this_spin {
9610            Some(now) => {
9611                let prev = self
9612                    .last_spin_end_us
9613                    .unwrap_or_else(|| spin_start_us.unwrap_or(now));
9614                self.last_spin_end_us = Some(now);
9615                now.saturating_sub(prev)
9616            }
9617            None => (timeout_ms as u64).saturating_mul(1000),
9618        };
9619
9620        // phase-430 W1 — the silence watch is credited the SAME `delta_us` the
9621        // wall timers below are, which is the whole of its unit argument: the
9622        // diagnostic arrives after as much time as this image's own wall timers
9623        // believe has passed, on whatever clock it actually has.
9624        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
9625        self.note_sim_time_silence(delta_us);
9626
9627        if !self.spin_quantization_checked && timeout_ms > 0 {
9628            self.spin_quantization_checked = true;
9629            // The TIER's declared cadence, not the capped park bound. Since
9630            // phase-436 W1 the two differ whenever a timer is due sooner than
9631            // the budget, and auditing the cap would compare the timer period
9632            // against itself — an exact multiple every time, so issue 0515's
9633            // warning would go silent on precisely the images that have a
9634            // timer to quantize. `spin_nominal_us` is the declared cadence
9635            // (`set_spin_nominal_us`, else the caller's timeout), recorded at
9636            // the top of this spin before any capping.
9637            self.spin_quantization_us = self.spin_nominal_us;
9638            self.audit_spin_quantization(self.spin_quantization_us);
9639        }
9640
9641        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
9642
9643        // Phase 1: Readiness scan (Phase 110.A.b — backed by FifoReadySet).
9644        //
9645        // `bits` carries data-readiness only (used by trigger eval +
9646        // by `InvocationMode::OnNewData`). `always_mask` carries the
9647        // `InvocationMode::Always` entries that fire regardless of
9648        // data presence. The dispatcher drains
9649        // `FifoReadySet(bits | always_mask)` after the trigger
9650        // passes; `pop_next` yields registration order (lowest bit
9651        // first) so behavior is bit-identical to the pre-refactor
9652        // `for (i, meta) in entries.iter().enumerate()` loop.
9653        let mut bits: u64 = 0;
9654        let mut count: usize = 0;
9655        let mut non_timer_mask: u64 = 0;
9656        let mut always_mask: u64 = 0;
9657
9658        for (i, meta) in self.entries.iter().enumerate() {
9659            if let Some(meta) = meta
9660                && !Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i)
9661            {
9662                let data_ptr = unsafe { arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *const u8 };
9663                if unsafe { (meta.has_data)(data_ptr) } {
9664                    bits |= 1u64 << i;
9665                }
9666                if !matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer | EntryKind::GuardCondition) {
9667                    non_timer_mask |= 1u64 << i;
9668                }
9669                if matches!(meta.invocation, InvocationMode::Always) {
9670                    always_mask |= 1u64 << i;
9671                }
9672                count += 1;
9673            }
9674        }
9675
9676        let snapshot = ReadinessSnapshot { bits, count };
9677
9678        // Phase 2: Trigger evaluation
9679        let trigger_passes = match &self.trigger {
9680            Trigger::Any => bits & non_timer_mask != 0 || non_timer_mask == 0,
9681            Trigger::All => bits & non_timer_mask == non_timer_mask,
9682            Trigger::One(id) => snapshot.is_ready(*id),
9683            Trigger::AllOf(set) => snapshot.all_ready(*set),
9684            Trigger::AnyOf(set) => snapshot.any_ready(*set),
9685            Trigger::Always => true,
9686            Trigger::Predicate(f) => f(&snapshot),
9687            Trigger::RawPredicate { callback, context } => {
9688                // Convert ReadinessSnapshot bitmask to a bool array for the C callback
9689                let mut ready_array = [false; 64];
9690                for (i, slot) in ready_array
9691                    .iter_mut()
9692                    .enumerate()
9693                    .take(snapshot.count.min(64))
9694                {
9695                    *slot = snapshot.bits & (1u64 << i) != 0;
9696                }
9697                // SAFETY: The callback and context are provided by the C API caller.
9698                // The ready_array is valid for snapshot.count elements.
9699                unsafe { callback(ready_array.as_ptr(), snapshot.count, *context) }
9700            }
9701        };
9702
9703        if !trigger_passes {
9704            // Timers still need delta accumulation even when trigger doesn't pass
9705            //
9706            // phase-8 — `.enumerate()` (rather than a bare `.flatten()`) because
9707            // `try_process` now carries the entry's slot index for the callback
9708            // trace hooks. This sweep FIRES timer callbacks, so it is a real
9709            // dispatch path and must attribute them like the drain below does.
9710            //
9711            // phase-474 I6 -- and it must TIME them like the drain does. This
9712            // is the path every timer takes on a node that also subscribes
9713            // (the default `Trigger::Any` fails whenever no subscription has
9714            // a sample), and it measured nothing, so `max-latency-runtime`
9715            // never judged a timer path: the safety island's 250 ms overrun of
9716            // a 206 ms path stored no verdict. One clock read before and one
9717            // after each timer's `try_process`, only when a latency contract
9718            // exists and a clock is injected; the publish-count snapshot is a
9719            // fixed array on the stack, nothing allocates. The measured span
9720            // is callback entry to exit, as in the drains; release jitter is
9721            // `release-jitter-runtime`'s.
9722            let mon_table = self.monitor_table;
9723            let lat_clock = self
9724                .clock_us_fn
9725                .filter(|_| mon_table.iter().any(|m| m.max_latency_ms > 0));
9726            for i in 0..self.entries.len() {
9727                let Some(meta) = self.entries[i].as_ref() else {
9728                    continue;
9729                };
9730                if matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer) && !Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i) {
9731                    let data_ptr = unsafe { arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) };
9732                    let try_process = meta.try_process;
9733                    let counts_before = snapshot_pub_counts(mon_table, lat_clock.is_some());
9734                    let start_us = lat_clock.map(|c| c());
9735                    Self::begin_dispatch(self.slot_tags, i);
9736                    // phase-463 W7 -- the host profile times this sweep too:
9737                    // it is the path every timer of a node that also
9738                    // subscribes takes (see above), so missing it measured
9739                    // the talker's timer at zero invocations.
9740                    //
9741                    // The OFF arm is the original `let _ =`, untouched, and
9742                    // that is MEASURED rather than tidy: every binding tried
9743                    // in its place (`let _p`, `let p; drop(p)`) moved
9744                    // `spin_once_capturing` by 49-64 B in the Zephyr image
9745                    // (phase-463 W5 I3c). Hence the second `unsafe` block,
9746                    // recorded in the unsafe census.
9747                    #[cfg(not(feature = "profile-mode"))]
9748                    let _ = unsafe { try_process(data_ptr, delta_us, i as u8) };
9749                    #[cfg(feature = "profile-mode")]
9750                    {
9751                        super::profile::dispatch_begin(arena_ptr as usize, i);
9752                        let processed = unsafe { try_process(data_ptr, delta_us, i as u8) };
9753                        super::profile::dispatch_end(matches!(processed, Ok(true)));
9754                    }
9755                    if let (Some(clock), Some(t0)) = (lat_clock, start_us) {
9756                        let elapsed_us = clock().saturating_sub(t0).min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32;
9757                        attribute_latency(mon_table, true, &counts_before, elapsed_us);
9758                    }
9759                    self.finish_dispatch(i);
9760                }
9761            }
9762
9763            // Parameter services live outside the arena and must be processed
9764            // regardless of trigger state, otherwise ROS 2 param queries time out.
9765            #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
9766            {
9767                let mut handled = 0usize;
9768                if let Some(params) = &mut self.params {
9769                    {
9770                        let crate::parameter_services::ParamState {
9771                            server,
9772                            services,
9773                            buffers,
9774                            ..
9775                        } = &mut **params;
9776                        // phase-426 W3 — one set per node; every set is pumped,
9777                        // because `ros2 param list` addresses each node's own
9778                        // six and a set nobody polls times out.
9779                        //
9780                        // Issue 1270 -- all of them through ONE buffer pair.
9781                        // Issue 1271 -- a request that got no reply is logged
9782                        // inside, once per service; there is no error to drop.
9783                        if let Some(buffers) = buffers {
9784                            for set in services.iter_mut() {
9785                                handled += set.process_services(server, buffers);
9786                            }
9787                        }
9788                    }
9789                }
9790                // phase-425 W3b — a `ros2 param set … use_sim_time true` arrives
9791                // through this path.
9792                self.note_param_services_ran(handled);
9793            }
9794
9795            // Same treatment for lifecycle services — `ros2 lifecycle get`
9796            // must succeed even when no callbacks fired this tick.
9797            //
9798            // Issue 1587 — `process` also drains the state machine's
9799            // announcement queue onto `~/transition_event`, so a transition
9800            // triggered from application code between two spins (autostart is
9801            // the common one) reaches a watching supervisor here.
9802            // SAFETY: see the matching invariant on the later call site.
9803            #[cfg(feature = "lifecycle-services")]
9804            if let Some(lc) = &mut self.lifecycle {
9805                let _ = unsafe { lc.process() };
9806            }
9807
9808            // phase-474 I7 -- an idle spin is the natural slot for the queued
9809            // reports.
9810            self.flush_violation_reports();
9811
9812            return SpinOnceResult::new();
9813        }
9814
9815        // Phase 2.5: LET pre-sample (only when LogicalExecutionTime)
9816        //
9817        // Sample all subscription data into entry buffers BEFORE dispatching
9818        // any callbacks. This ensures all callbacks in this cycle see a
9819        // consistent snapshot of data from the same point in time.
9820        // Services are NOT pre-sampled (request-reply is sequential).
9821        if matches!(self.semantics, ExecutorSemantics::LogicalExecutionTime) {
9822            for (i, meta) in self.entries.iter().enumerate() {
9823                let Some(meta) = meta else { continue };
9824                if matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Subscription)
9825                    && !Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i)
9826                {
9827                    let data_ptr = unsafe { arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) };
9828                    unsafe { (meta.pre_sample)(data_ptr) };
9829                }
9830            }
9831        }
9832
9833        // Phase 3: Dispatch (Phase 110.C — bucketed by SC.priority).
9834        //
9835        // Two ready-set families, each split across `Priority::COUNT`
9836        // buckets (Critical / Normal / BestEffort). Per-entry SC
9837        // `class` selects FIFO bitmap vs EDF heap; SC `priority`
9838        // selects the bucket within. Drain order:
9839        //   for each bucket in priority order (Critical first):
9840        //     drain EDF heap (deadline-priority), then FIFO bitmap
9841        //     (registration-order)
9842        // Default workloads — every entry on the auto-default Fifo SC
9843        // (Normal priority) — populate only `fifo[Normal]`, so
9844        // dispatch order is bit-identical to 110.B.b for those.
9845        const NB: usize = super::sched_context::Priority::COUNT;
9846        let mut result = SpinOnceResult::new();
9847        let mut fifo: super::ready_set::BucketedFifoSet<NB, { MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS }> =
9848            super::ready_set::BucketedFifoSet::new();
9849        let mut edf: super::ready_set::BucketedEdfSet<NB, { MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS }> =
9850            super::ready_set::BucketedEdfSet::new();
9851        let active_mask = bits | always_mask;
9852
9853        // Phase 110.E — refill any Sporadic SC budgets at period
9854        // boundaries before deciding what to dispatch this cycle.
9855        // Refill is polled (not ISR-driven) — coarse but correct
9856        // upper-bound bandwidth limiter.
9857        // phase-359 W4 — was `#[cfg(feature = "std")]` with NO no_std arm, so
9858        // polled Sporadic budgets never refilled on embedded: they exhausted
9859        // once and stayed exhausted. That was a consequence of "no clock on
9860        // no_std", which is false whenever a `clock_us` hook is injected. Now it
9861        // runs on either flavour when a clock exists, and is skipped when none
9862        // does — identical to today's behaviour in that case.
9863        if let Some(now_us) = now_us_this_spin {
9864            let now_ms = now_us / 1000;
9865            // issue 0736 — REFILL only. This used to also charge the cycle's
9866            // `delta_us` as the per-SC consumption estimate ("worst-case
9867            // attribution", pending a higher-precision clock hook). That hook
9868            // landed, and the attribution was not merely coarse: `delta_us` is
9869            // the wall-clock gap between spins, not CPU the callbacks spent, so
9870            // wherever the gap exceeds the budget the SC is exhausted on every
9871            // spin regardless of what it ran. Consumption is charged from
9872            // measured callback runtime in `consume_dispatch_runtime_us`.
9873            for slot in self.sporadic_states.iter_mut().flatten() {
9874                let _ = slot.refill(now_ms);
9875            }
9876        }
9877
9878        for i in 0..self.entries.len() {
9879            if active_mask & (1u64 << i) == 0 {
9880                continue;
9881            }
9882            let sc_idx = self.sched_context_bindings[i].0 as usize;
9883            let sc_class_priority_deadline = self
9884                .sched_contexts
9885                .get(sc_idx)
9886                .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
9887                .map(|sc| {
9888                    (
9889                        sc.class,
9890                        sc.priority.index(),
9891                        sc.deadline_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
9892                    )
9893                });
9894            let (sc_class, bucket, deadline_us) = sc_class_priority_deadline.unwrap_or((
9895                super::sched_context::SchedClass::Fifo,
9896                super::sched_context::Priority::Normal.index(),
9897                u32::MAX,
9898            ));
9899            // Phase 110.E — Sporadic SC dispatch is suppressed when
9900            // its budget is exhausted. Atomic path (110.E.b PlatformTimer
9901            // refill) takes precedence when registered; polled path
9902            // (cycle-level delta_us attribution) handles the unregistered
9903            // case. Either way, exhausted budget skips dispatch.
9904            if matches!(sc_class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
9905                #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
9906                let atomic_has_budget = self
9907                    .sporadic_atomic_states
9908                    .get(sc_idx)
9909                    .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
9910                    .map(|(state, _)| state.has_budget());
9911                #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
9912                let atomic_has_budget: Option<bool> = None;
9913                let has_budget = match atomic_has_budget {
9914                    Some(b) => b,
9915                    None => self
9916                        .sporadic_states
9917                        .get(sc_idx)
9918                        .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
9919                        .map(|s| s.budget_remaining_us > 0)
9920                        .unwrap_or(true),
9921                };
9922                if !has_budget {
9923                    // issue 0736 — keep the TIMER'S CLOCK honest even while the
9924                    // budget gates its dispatch.
9925                    //
9926                    // A timer's `elapsed_us` only advances inside
9927                    // `timer_try_process`, which is reached only when the entry
9928                    // is DISPATCHED, and each dispatch is handed just THIS
9929                    // cycle's `delta_us`. So every cycle skipped here was
9930                    // dropped from the timer's sense of time: it did not fire,
9931                    // it did not learn that its period had passed, and — because
9932                    // the overrun counter is driven by that same `elapsed_us` —
9933                    // it did not count the activation it missed.
9934                    //
9935                    // That is why the throttle was invisible. Measured on
9936                    // nuttx-arm/rust: ~238 activations lost against ~40
9937                    // reported, so five in six missed firings were unaccounted
9938                    // ANYWHERE. The tier ran at a quarter of its declared rate
9939                    // and the only honest signal was the delivery count itself.
9940                    //
9941                    // Advancing the clock here does not dispatch anything and
9942                    // does not defeat the budget. It makes the entry's own
9943                    // accounting independent of whether the executor CHOSE to
9944                    // run it, which is the property every "did this meet its
9945                    // declaration?" question needs, and it lets the existing
9946                    // `Skip` policy count the backlog and the existing
9947                    // `timer-overrun-runtime` rule report it.
9948                    if let Some(meta) = self.entries[i].as_ref()
9949                        && matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Timer)
9950                    {
9951                        // SAFETY: a Timer entry's arena slot holds a
9952                        // `TimerEntry<F>`, whose leading layout IS
9953                        // `TimerHeader` — the same cast the overrun reporter
9954                        // one screen up already relies on.
9955                        let header =
9956                            unsafe { &mut *(arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) as *mut TimerHeader) };
9957                        // Issue 1321 — on the TIMER'S clock, not the
9958                        // executor's. This line read
9959                        // `header.elapsed_us += delta_us`, which is wall
9960                        // microseconds: for a `Ros` timer that advanced a
9961                        // simulated-time counter by wall time, so a paused
9962                        // `/clock` no longer paused the timer — the one
9963                        // property a ROS-time timer has. Unbounded, unlike
9964                        // 1321's park bound, because it can fire a callback
9965                        // that no clock step earned.
9966                        super::arena::timer_advance_without_dispatch(header, delta_us);
9967                    }
9968                    // issue 0736 — a budget skip used to be a bare `continue`,
9969                    // which is the silent-drop shape 0737 gated one layer out:
9970                    // the entry is simply not dispatched and nothing anywhere
9971                    // says so, so a permanently starved tier is
9972                    // indistinguishable from an idle one. It took a hand-run
9973                    // 45 s image and a per-executor probe to learn that this
9974                    // line was skipping 96 % of one tier's spins.
9975                    // The rolling window catches a budget that THROTTLES; the
9976                    // streak below catches one that starves outright. issue
9977                    // 0736 needed both: the measured case skipped ~3 spins in
9978                    // 4 without ever reaching a streak, so the tier ran at a
9979                    // quarter of its declared rate in silence.
9980                    if let Some((skips, total)) = self
9981                        .sporadic_states
9982                        .get_mut(sc_idx)
9983                        .and_then(|st| st.as_mut())
9984                        .and_then(|st| st.take_budget_window())
9985                    {
9986                        nros_log::log_warn!(
9987                            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
9988                            "sporadic budget throttled sched context {}: {} of the last {} dispatch opportunities were skipped for want of budget. The declared budget_us/period_us cannot sustain this tier's callbacks on this target.",
9989                            sc_idx,
9990                            skips,
9991                            total
9992                        );
9993                    }
9994                    if let Some(streak) = self
9995                        .sporadic_states
9996                        .get_mut(sc_idx)
9997                        .and_then(|st| st.as_mut())
9998                        .and_then(|st| st.note_budget_skip())
9999                    {
10000                        nros_log::log_warn!(
10001                            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
10002                            "sporadic budget exhausted for {} consecutive spins (sched context {}): its callbacks are not being dispatched. Either the callback runtime exceeds the declared budget_us per period_us, or the declaration is unsatisfiable on this target.",
10003                            streak,
10004                            sc_idx
10005                        );
10006                    }
10007                    continue;
10008                }
10009                // Phase 110.E.b follow-up — per-callback runtime
10010                // accounting (replaces this cycle-level attribution)
10011                // is applied at dispatch time below via
10012                // `consume_dispatch_runtime_us`. We only update the
10013                // polled-path `SporadicState` (no_std fallback) here
10014                // because the atomic path now records actual
10015                // wall-clock per-callback runtime. The
10016                // `delta_us` over-attribution that previously hit the
10017                // atomic state was a worst-case bandwidth limiter;
10018                // per-callback measurement is strictly tighter.
10019                #[cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))]
10020                {
10021                    let _ = sc_idx; // polled-state path lives in
10022                    // `sporadic_states`; this branch is a no-op when
10023                    // the atomic path is enabled.
10024                }
10025            }
10026            // Phase 110.F — per-callback OS priority routing. Entries
10027            // bound to an SC with `os_pri > 0` dispatch onto a worker
10028            // thread the OS has elevated to that priority; the
10029            // cooperative path is skipped for those entries. Workers
10030            // are spawned lazily.
10031            #[cfg(all(
10032                feature = "alloc",
10033                feature = "rmw-cffi",
10034                feature = "scheduler-os-priority"
10035            ))]
10036            {
10037                let os_pri = self
10038                    .sched_contexts
10039                    .get(sc_idx)
10040                    .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
10041                    .map(|sc| sc.os_pri)
10042                    .unwrap_or(0);
10043                if os_pri > 0
10044                    && let Some(apply_policy) = self.os_priority_apply_policy
10045                    && let Some(meta) = self.entries[i].as_ref()
10046                {
10047                    // Issue 1705 — a worker still holds this entry (its item is
10048                    // queued or its callback is running). Sending it again, or
10049                    // running it here, would put two threads in one
10050                    // `try_process`; it gets its next turn once the worker lets
10051                    // go.
10052                    let tag = &self.slot_tags[i];
10053                    if tag.set(super::types::SlotTag::WORKER_QUEUED)
10054                        & super::types::SlotTag::WORKER_QUEUED
10055                        != 0
10056                    {
10057                        continue;
10058                    }
10059                    let item = super::os_priority::WorkItem {
10060                        arena_base: arena_ptr as usize,
10061                        arena_offset: meta.offset,
10062                        try_process: meta.try_process,
10063                        delta_us,
10064                        // phase-8 — the worker runs the leaf on a DIFFERENT
10065                        // thread, so it has to carry the slot index with it;
10066                        // nothing on the far side can recover it from the
10067                        // arena address alone.
10068                        desc_idx: i as u8,
10069                        tag: tag as *const super::types::SlotTag as usize,
10070                    };
10071                    // phase-359 W10 — `try_dispatch` now reports whether the
10072                    // entry was actually handed to a worker. It can decline:
10073                    // the mailbox is bounded, the pool is capacity-limited, and
10074                    // a platform without a wake primitive hosts no workers at
10075                    // all. Previously the spawn was infallible (`.expect`) and
10076                    // an unbounded `mpsc` never refused, so this branch always
10077                    // `continue`d. Falling through to the cooperative path is
10078                    // the honest answer to a decline — the callback still runs,
10079                    // just without the OS priority guarantee, which is exactly
10080                    // what an entry got before this feature existed.
10081                    if self
10082                        .os_priority_pool
10083                        .try_dispatch(os_pri, apply_policy, item)
10084                    {
10085                        continue;
10086                    }
10087                    // Declined: no worker took it, so the bit set above is
10088                    // released and the entry runs cooperatively.
10089                    self.slot_tags[i].clear(super::types::SlotTag::WORKER_QUEUED);
10090                }
10091            }
10092            // Phase 110.G — TT window gate, orthogonal to class.
10093            // Skips dispatch when the SC has a TT window AND the
10094            // current monotonic time is outside it. Both gates apply
10095            // independently — a Sporadic SC with a TT window must
10096            // pass both.
10097            if self.major_frame_us > 0 {
10098                let sc_opt = self.sched_contexts.get(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_ref());
10099                if let Some(sc) = sc_opt {
10100                    let off = sc.tt_window_offset_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()).unwrap_or(0);
10101                    let dur = sc
10102                        .tt_window_duration_us
10103                        .get()
10104                        .map(|nz| nz.get())
10105                        .unwrap_or(0);
10106                    if dur > 0 {
10107                        // Compute current phase within the major
10108                        // frame using the accumulated `delta_us` clock
10109                        // (std-only precise; no_std uses `delta_us`
10110                        // approximation from spin cadence).
10111                        // phase-359 W4 — the shared read. The no_std arm used
10112                        // to be `now_us = delta_us`, i.e. a per-spin INTERVAL
10113                        // used as an absolute phase clock, which the comment
10114                        // above called an approximation. It is now the real
10115                        // clock when one is injected, and falls back to the old
10116                        // approximation only when none is.
10117                        let now_us = now_us_this_spin.unwrap_or(delta_us);
10118                        let phase = (now_us % self.major_frame_us as u64) as u32;
10119                        let in_window = if off + dur <= self.major_frame_us {
10120                            phase >= off && phase < off + dur
10121                        } else {
10122                            // Window wraps the major frame boundary.
10123                            let end = (off as u64 + dur as u64) % self.major_frame_us as u64;
10124                            phase >= off || (phase as u64) < end
10125                        };
10126                        if !in_window {
10127                            continue;
10128                        }
10129                    }
10130                }
10131            }
10132            let is_edf = matches!(sc_class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Edf);
10133            let job = super::types::ActiveJob {
10134                sort_key: if is_edf { deadline_us } else { i as u32 },
10135                desc_idx: i as super::types::DescIdx,
10136            };
10137            if is_edf {
10138                let _ = edf.insert_into(bucket, job);
10139            } else {
10140                let _ = fifo.insert_into(bucket, job);
10141            }
10142        }
10143
10144        // SAFETY: each `desc_idx` we pop was set above only when the
10145        // corresponding `entries[i]` slot was `Some`; no Executor
10146        // mutation happens between that scan and this dispatch.
10147        let mut dispatch_one = |meta: &CallbackMeta,
10148                                desc_idx: usize,
10149                                arena_ptr: *mut u8,
10150                                delta_us: u64,
10151                                result: &mut SpinOnceResult| {
10152            // Phase 141.B.2 — capture T1 at subscription dispatch
10153            // entry. Probe pairs it with the most recent T0 from
10154            // `nros_rmw_runtime_wake_cb` (std + alloc variants)
10155            // and pushes `T1 - T0` onto the ring buffer 141.C
10156            // drains. No-op when the probe feature is off or
10157            // no cycle reader is installed. Other entry kinds
10158            // (Service / Timer / GuardCondition) skip the probe
10159            // because the 141 acceptance is specifically
10160            // wake-to-subscription-dispatch latency.
10161            #[cfg(feature = "wake-latency-probe")]
10162            if matches!(meta.kind, EntryKind::Subscription) {
10163                super::wake_probe::on_dispatch();
10164            }
10165            let data_ptr = unsafe { arena_ptr.add(meta.offset) };
10166            // phase-8 — `desc_idx` is the entry slot index, threaded through so
10167            // the leaf hooks in `arena.rs` can name the callback they bracket.
10168            // `MAX_CALLBACK_SLOTS` is 64 (enforced by the `u64` ready-set
10169            // bitmask), so the `as u8` cannot truncate a live slot.
10170            // phase-463 W7 — time the dispatch and attribute its publishes
10171            // (host `profile-mode` only). ONE call site for both builds, so no
10172            // second `unsafe` block; the binding is the only change an RTOS
10173            // image sees, and its loadable bytes measured identical (phase-463
10174            // W5 I3c, Zephyr cpp/talker).
10175            #[cfg(feature = "profile-mode")]
10176            super::profile::dispatch_begin(arena_ptr as usize, desc_idx);
10177            let processed = unsafe { (meta.try_process)(data_ptr, delta_us, desc_idx as u8) };
10178            #[cfg(feature = "profile-mode")]
10179            super::profile::dispatch_end(matches!(processed, Ok(true)));
10180            match processed {
10181                Ok(true) => match meta.kind {
10182                    EntryKind::Subscription => result.subscriptions_processed += 1,
10183                    EntryKind::Service
10184                    | EntryKind::ServiceClient
10185                    | EntryKind::ActionServer
10186                    | EntryKind::ActionClient => result.services_handled += 1,
10187                    EntryKind::Timer => result.timers_fired += 1,
10188                    EntryKind::GuardCondition => {}
10189                },
10190                Ok(false) => {}
10191                Err(e) => {
10192                    // phase-427 — the first one is kept, the rest are counted.
10193                    // `stop_on_first_error` is what reads it; when nobody
10194                    // asked, the `Option` is a local the optimiser drops.
10195                    if first_error.is_none() {
10196                        *first_error = Some(e);
10197                    }
10198                    match meta.kind {
10199                        EntryKind::Subscription => result.subscription_errors += 1,
10200                        EntryKind::Service
10201                        | EntryKind::ServiceClient
10202                        | EntryKind::ActionServer
10203                        | EntryKind::ActionClient => result.service_errors += 1,
10204                        EntryKind::Timer | EntryKind::GuardCondition => {}
10205                    }
10206                }
10207            }
10208        };
10209
10210        // Phase 110.E.b follow-up — per-callback runtime accounting
10211        // for Sporadic SCs. Wall-clock-measure each dispatch and
10212        // consume the elapsed microseconds from the bound SC's
10213        // atomic budget. This replaces the cycle-level over-
10214        // attribution that previously charged the FULL `delta_us`
10215        // against every Sporadic SC regardless of which entries
10216        // actually fired — accurate per-callback measurement is the
10217        // shape the design doc's per-callback runtime acceptance
10218        // calls out.
10219        //
10220        // phase-359 W10 — this was `feature = "std"`-gated, because it "needs a
10221        // `core::time::Instant`-equivalent monotonic clock ... until a
10222        // board-side monotonic-microsecond accessor lands". That accessor
10223        // landed: `now_us()` reads the platform monotonic counter on every
10224        // flavour. So per-callback sporadic accounting is no longer something
10225        // only a hosted build gets, and the no_std fallback to polled
10226        // `SporadicState` cycle deltas is no longer the only option on target.
10227        let consume_dispatch_runtime_us =
10228            |desc_idx: usize,
10229             elapsed_us: u32,
10230             sched_context_bindings: &[super::sched_context::SchedContextId],
10231             sched_contexts: &[Option<super::sched_context::SchedContext>],
10232             sporadic_states: &mut [Option<super::sched_context::SporadicState>],
10233             alive_slots: &mut [super::monitor::AliveSlot],
10234             #[cfg(feature = "alloc")] sporadic_atomic_states: &[Option<(
10235                portable_atomic_util::Arc<super::sched_context::AtomicSporadicState>,
10236                OpaqueTimerHandle,
10237            )>]| {
10238                let sc_idx = sched_context_bindings[desc_idx].0 as usize;
10239                // Alive supervision counts EVERY dispatch, before the class
10240                // gate below: a Fifo or time-triggered context can fall
10241                // silent exactly as a sporadic one can, and the rule that
10242                // notices must not be scoped to the class that happens to
10243                // carry a budget.
10244                if let Some(slot) = alive_slots.get_mut(sc_idx) {
10245                    slot.dispatches = slot.dispatches.wrapping_add(1);
10246                }
10247                let sc_class = sched_contexts
10248                    .get(sc_idx)
10249                    .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
10250                    .map(|sc| sc.class)
10251                    .unwrap_or(super::sched_context::SchedClass::Fifo);
10252                if !matches!(sc_class, super::sched_context::SchedClass::Sporadic) {
10253                    return;
10254                }
10255                #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
10256                if let Some((state, _)) =
10257                    sporadic_atomic_states.get(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
10258                {
10259                    state.consume(elapsed_us);
10260                    // Unconditional, unlike the overrun record below: the
10261                    // budget is sized FROM this number, so it has to exist
10262                    // before the budget is right rather than only after it
10263                    // is wrong.
10264                    state.record_exec(elapsed_us);
10265                    // Phase 110.E.b — overrun detection. Cooperative
10266                    // single-thread can't preempt a runaway callback,
10267                    // so post-dispatch wall-clock comparison delivers
10268                    // the same observable signal as the design's
10269                    // oneshot-IRQ-and-cancel pattern, without needing
10270                    // a separate timer per SC. `budget_capacity_us` is
10271                    // the per-period budget the SC was sized against;
10272                    // any callback exceeding that has run past its
10273                    // bandwidth allotment.
10274                    if elapsed_us > state.budget_capacity_us {
10275                        state.record_overrun(elapsed_us - state.budget_capacity_us);
10276                    }
10277                }
10278                // issue 0736 — the POLLED state is charged unconditionally,
10279                // and it is the one that matters: `has_budget` prefers the
10280                // atomic state only when a refill timer was registered, which
10281                // no board or entry does. Before this, the alloc arm charged a
10282                // state nothing populated and the no_std arm discarded the
10283                // measurement outright (`let _ = (sc_idx, elapsed_us)`), so no
10284                // shipped image recorded per-callback runtime anywhere — while
10285                // the comment above claimed it did.
10286                if let Some(state) = sporadic_states.get_mut(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_mut()) {
10287                    state.consume(elapsed_us);
10288                }
10289            };
10290
10291        // W3b.5 — post-dispatch contract checks. `lat_active` gates the
10292        // per-dispatch publish-count snapshot (attribution of dispatch
10293        // elapsed time to monitored publishers whose counter advanced);
10294        // `dl_active` gates elapsed measurement for deadline actions. The third
10295        // term used to be `cfg!(feature = "std")` — "std measures anyway for
10296        // the sporadic path" — which made a COMPILE-TIME flavour stand in for
10297        // "is there a clock". It is now the runtime question it always was.
10298        let mon_table = self.monitor_table;
10299        let lat_active = mon_table.iter().any(|m| m.max_latency_ms > 0);
10300        let dl_active = self.sched_contexts.iter().flatten().any(|sc| {
10301            sc.deadline_us.is_some()
10302                && !matches!(
10303                    sc.deadline_action,
10304                    super::sched_context::DeadlineAction::Ignore
10305                )
10306        });
10307        let mon_clock = self.clock_us_fn;
10308        // phase-359 W4 — one predicate, no cfg block. `cfg!` is an expression,
10309        // so the flavour difference stays a value instead of a branch: std
10310        // measures unconditionally because the sporadic runtime accounting
10311        // below (itself std-only) consumes the result, which is exactly what
10312        // the comment above described and what the four-arm sites encoded.
10313        let measure_us = lat_active || dl_active || mon_clock.is_some();
10314        // phase-359 W4 — ONE hoisted µs reader for the per-dispatch latency
10315        // measurement below. Hoisted because `now_us()` takes `&mut self` and
10316        // the dispatch loop already holds borrows; the std arm copies the epoch
10317        // (a `Copy` `Instant`) so reading inside the loop touches no `self`.
10318        // This is the last cfg pair in the timing path: the two call sites it
10319        // serves each had FOUR arms (start + elapsed, per flavour).
10320        let read_us = move || mon_clock.map(|c| c()).unwrap_or(0);
10321        // Deferred deadline-miss violations (the loop body holds an
10322        // immutable borrow of `self.entries`, so the ring is fed after).
10323        let mut deadline_misses: heapless::Vec<
10324            super::monitor::Violation,
10325            { super::monitor::MAX_VIOLATIONS },
10326        > = heapless::Vec::new();
10327        // SCs whose remaining callbacks this cycle are skipped
10328        // (`DeadlineAction::Skip`) — bitmask over SC slots.
10329        let mut skipped_scs: u64 = 0;
10330
10331        // For each priority bucket (Critical → Normal → BestEffort),
10332        // drain EDF first then FIFO so an EDF callback in this bucket
10333        // beats a FIFO peer at the same priority, but no lower-priority
10334        // entry runs while a higher-priority bucket has work pending.
10335        // Strict static priority across buckets; non-preemptive within
10336        // an in-flight callback (see Phase 110.D).
10337        for bucket in 0..NB {
10338            while let Some(job) = edf.pop_from(bucket) {
10339                let i = job.desc_idx as usize;
10340                let sc_idx = self.sched_context_bindings[i].0 as usize;
10341                if sc_idx < 64 && skipped_scs & (1u64 << sc_idx) != 0 {
10342                    continue; // W3b.5 DeadlineAction::Skip containment
10343                }
10344                if let Some(meta) = self.entries[i].as_ref()
10345                    && !Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i)
10346                {
10347                    let counts_before = snapshot_pub_counts(mon_table, lat_active);
10348                    // Measured only when a consumer wants it, matching the
10349                    // no_std arm this replaces — the std arm used to measure
10350                    // unconditionally.
10351                    let start_us = measure_us.then(read_us);
10352                    Self::begin_dispatch(self.slot_tags, i);
10353                    dispatch_one(meta, i, arena_ptr, delta_us, &mut result);
10354                    let elapsed_us: Option<u32> = start_us
10355                        .map(|t0| read_us().saturating_sub(t0))
10356                        .map(|d| d.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32);
10357                    if let Some(elapsed_us) = elapsed_us {
10358                        consume_dispatch_runtime_us(
10359                            i,
10360                            elapsed_us,
10361                            &self.sched_context_bindings[..],
10362                            &self.sched_contexts[..],
10363                            &mut self.sporadic_states[..],
10364                            &mut self.alive_slots[..],
10365                            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
10366                            &self.sporadic_atomic_states[..],
10367                        );
10368                    }
10369                    if let Some(elapsed_us) = elapsed_us {
10370                        attribute_latency(mon_table, lat_active, &counts_before, elapsed_us);
10371                        check_deadline_miss(
10372                            self.sched_contexts.get(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_ref()),
10373                            sc_idx,
10374                            elapsed_us,
10375                            &mut deadline_misses,
10376                            &mut skipped_scs,
10377                            self.fault_fn,
10378                        );
10379                    }
10380                    self.finish_dispatch(i);
10381                }
10382            }
10383            while let Some(job) = fifo.pop_from(bucket) {
10384                let i = job.desc_idx as usize;
10385                let sc_idx = self.sched_context_bindings[i].0 as usize;
10386                if sc_idx < 64 && skipped_scs & (1u64 << sc_idx) != 0 {
10387                    continue; // W3b.5 DeadlineAction::Skip containment
10388                }
10389                if let Some(meta) = self.entries[i].as_ref()
10390                    && !Self::slot_held(self.slot_tags, i)
10391                {
10392                    let counts_before = snapshot_pub_counts(mon_table, lat_active);
10393                    // Measured only when a consumer wants it, matching the
10394                    // no_std arm this replaces — the std arm used to measure
10395                    // unconditionally.
10396                    let start_us = measure_us.then(read_us);
10397                    Self::begin_dispatch(self.slot_tags, i);
10398                    dispatch_one(meta, i, arena_ptr, delta_us, &mut result);
10399                    let elapsed_us: Option<u32> = start_us
10400                        .map(|t0| read_us().saturating_sub(t0))
10401                        .map(|d| d.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32);
10402                    if let Some(elapsed_us) = elapsed_us {
10403                        consume_dispatch_runtime_us(
10404                            i,
10405                            elapsed_us,
10406                            &self.sched_context_bindings[..],
10407                            &self.sched_contexts[..],
10408                            &mut self.sporadic_states[..],
10409                            &mut self.alive_slots[..],
10410                            #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
10411                            &self.sporadic_atomic_states[..],
10412                        );
10413                    }
10414                    if let Some(elapsed_us) = elapsed_us {
10415                        attribute_latency(mon_table, lat_active, &counts_before, elapsed_us);
10416                        check_deadline_miss(
10417                            self.sched_contexts.get(sc_idx).and_then(|s| s.as_ref()),
10418                            sc_idx,
10419                            elapsed_us,
10420                            &mut deadline_misses,
10421                            &mut skipped_scs,
10422                            self.fault_fn,
10423                        );
10424                    }
10425                    self.finish_dispatch(i);
10426                }
10427            }
10428        }
10429
10430        // W3b.5 — feed deferred deadline misses into the violation ring.
10431        for v in deadline_misses {
10432            self.violations.record(v);
10433        }
10434
10435        // Issue #505 — same ring, same cycle. This runs AFTER dispatch,
10436        // unlike the windowed rate/age/latency rules at the top of the
10437        // spin: the activations it reports were dropped by the dispatch
10438        // that just happened, and a tier that is stalling should not have
10439        // to wait for the next spin to say so.
10440        self.check_timer_overruns();
10441        self.check_release_jitter_rule();
10442        self.check_stack_headroom_rule();
10443        self.check_alive_supervision();
10444        // phase-474 I7 -- the queued /diagnostics reports, after this spin's
10445        // dispatches and rules, when the next timer leaves room for them.
10446        self.flush_violation_reports();
10447        // phase-474 I1 -- the opt-in drain-and-report hook, after every rule of
10448        // this spin has had its say.
10449        self.violations.drain_and_report();
10450
10451        // Process parameter services (outside the arena)
10452        #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
10453        let mut handled = 0usize;
10454        #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
10455        if let Some(params) = &mut self.params {
10456            {
10457                let crate::parameter_services::ParamState {
10458                    server,
10459                    services,
10460                    buffers,
10461                    ..
10462                } = &mut **params;
10463                // phase-426 W3 -- one set per node; see the sibling site above,
10464                // including why nothing here can discard an error (1270/1271).
10465                if let Some(buffers) = buffers {
10466                    for set in services.iter_mut() {
10467                        let n = set.process_services(server, buffers);
10468                        result.services_handled += n;
10469                        handled += n;
10470                    }
10471                }
10472            }
10473        }
10474        #[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
10475        self.note_param_services_ran(handled);
10476
10477        // Process lifecycle services (outside the arena).
10478        //
10479        // SAFETY: `change_state` dispatches a user-supplied C callback through a
10480        // raw function pointer stored in `LifecyclePollingNodeCtx`. The caller
10481        // of `register_lifecycle_services` guarantees the callback/context pair
10482        // stays live for as long as the executor (see that method's docs).
10483        #[cfg(feature = "lifecycle-services")]
10484        if let Some(lc) = &mut self.lifecycle {
10485            if let Ok(n) = unsafe { lc.process() } {
10486                result.services_handled += n;
10487            }
10488        }
10489
10490        // Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — executor-owned component tick pass.
10491        // Mirrors `ExecutorNodeRuntime::run_ticks`: after the transport +
10492        // callbacks have been pumped, drive each enrolled component's `tick`
10493        // (service-client/action poll, etc.). `exec_ctx` hands the component
10494        // the whole executor as a raw `*mut Executor` so its tick can
10495        // reborrow it (the same disjoint-field raw-ptr pattern run_ticks
10496        // uses). Index-iterate over `Copy` slots so no borrow of
10497        // `self.component_slots` is held while `tick` runs (which aliases
10498        // `self` through `exec_ctx`).
10499        let exec_ctx = self as *mut Executor as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
10500        let slot_count = self.component_slots.len();
10501        for i in 0..slot_count {
10502            let slot = self.component_slots[i];
10503            // SAFETY: `slot.state` is the leaked cell the matching `tick`
10504            // expects (enrolled via `enroll_component`); `exec_ctx` is a live
10505            // `*mut Executor` for `self`. The slot was copied out, so no
10506            // borrow of `component_slots` is outstanding during the call.
10507            unsafe {
10508                (slot.tick)(slot.state, exec_ctx);
10509            }
10510        }
10511
10512        result
10513    }
10514
10515    /// Drive I/O and dispatch callbacks forever — the body of an RTOS task.
10516    ///
10517    /// EXTENSION (RFC-0089). Not a rename of upstream's `spin`: the `!` is the
10518    /// point. A bare-metal entry has no shutdown source to return TO, and
10519    /// declaring that lets the compiler drop the epilogue and lets the caller
10520    /// write it as the last expression of a `-> !` task body with no
10521    /// `unreachable!()`. [`spin`](Self::spin) is the verb that can end, and it
10522    /// is upstream's.
10523    ///
10524    /// phase-427 — was `spin(Duration) -> !`, which squatted on rclrs's name
10525    /// with a different contract (a ported `executor.spin(SpinOptions)` line
10526    /// had to be renamed by hand, the one edit on the tutorial's happy path
10527    /// that no real difference forced). `spin_default()` went with it: it named
10528    /// a 50 ms poll interval and had zero call sites, and the interval is now
10529    /// [`SpinOptions::poll_interval`], defaulting to
10530    /// [`DEFAULT_SPIN_POLL_INTERVAL`](super::types::DEFAULT_SPIN_POLL_INTERVAL).
10531    ///
10532    /// **Envelope.** Only `poll_interval` and `stop_on_first_error` can mean
10533    /// anything here; `timeout`, `only_next` and `max_callbacks` are ENDING
10534    /// conditions and this verb does not end. Passing one is a caller error and
10535    /// says so at `LOG_ERR` on entry rather than being quietly dropped — a
10536    /// discarded ending condition is precisely the "compiles and differs" case
10537    /// RFC-0089 exists to make loud, and a `-> !` signature has no other
10538    /// channel. `stop_on_first_error` likewise cannot RETURN the error; it
