10539    /// logs it and keeps spinning, because a task body has nowhere to put it.
10540    ///
10541    /// ```ignore
10542    /// let mut executor = Executor::open(&config)?;
10543    /// executor.register_subscription::<Int32, _>("/topic", |msg| { /* ... */ })?;
10544    /// executor.spin_forever(SpinOptions::default()); // never returns
10545    /// ```
10546    pub fn spin_forever(&mut self, opts: SpinOptions) -> ! {
10547        if opts.timeout.is_some() || opts.only_next || opts.max_callbacks.is_some() {
10548            nros_log::log_error!(
10549                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
10550                "spin_forever: an ending condition (timeout / only_next / max_callbacks) \
10551                 was supplied to a verb that never returns and is being IGNORED \
10552                 -- use `Executor::spin` for a loop that can end"
10553            );
10554        }
10555        let poll = opts.poll_interval;
10556        let report_errors = opts.stop_on_first_error;
10557        loop {
10558            let mut first_error = None;
10559            self.spin_once_capturing(poll, &mut first_error);
10560            if report_errors && let Some(e) = first_error {
10561                nros_log::log_error!(
10562                    nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
10563                    "spin_forever: a callback failed ({:?}); `stop_on_first_error` cannot \
10564                     end a `-> !` loop, so this is a report, not a stop",
10565                    e
10566                );
10567            }
10568        }
10569    }
10570
10571    /// Drive I/O and dispatch callbacks asynchronously.
10572    ///
10573    /// Runs forever, yielding between poll cycles so that other async tasks
10574    /// (e.g., [`Promise`](super::handles::Promise)) can make progress.
10575    ///
10576    /// Uses only `core::future` — no external async runtime dependency.
10577    ///
10578    /// ADOPT-BOUNDED against rclrs's
10579    /// `spin_async(SpinOptions) -> impl Future<Output = Vec<RclrsError>>`:
10580    ///
10581    /// * **It never returns and reports no errors** — the output is `!`, and it
10582    ///   takes no `SpinOptions`. To stop, `select` it against the thing you are
10583    ///   waiting for (pattern 1 below).
10584    /// * **It does not sleep on RMW I/O.** Each cycle is `spin_once(1 ms)` and then
10585    ///   a yield that wakes itself before returning `Pending`, so any runtime that
10586    ///   honours wakes polls it again at once. It is CPU-bound by construction;
10587    ///   the 1 ms `spin_once` budget is its only wait. Do not read `async` as idle.
10588    ///
10589    /// # Usage patterns
10590    ///
10591    /// ```ignore
10592    /// // Pattern 1: select with a promise (embassy-futures)
10593    /// use embassy_futures::select::{select, Either};
10594    /// let promise = client.call(&req)?;
10595    /// let Either::Second(reply) = select(executor.spin_async(), promise).await
10596    ///     else { unreachable!() };
10597    ///
10598    /// // Pattern 2: manual polling (no async runtime)
10599    /// let mut promise = client.call(&req)?;
10600    /// loop {
10601    ///     executor.spin_once(core::time::Duration::from_millis(10));
10602    ///     if let Ok(Some(r)) = promise.take() { break r; }
10603    /// }
10604    /// ```
10605    pub async fn spin_async(&mut self) -> ! {
10606        loop {
10607            self.spin_once(core::time::Duration::from_millis(1));
10608            core::future::poll_fn::<(), _>(|cx| {
10609                cx.waker().wake_by_ref();
10610                core::task::Poll::Pending
10611            })
10612            .await;
10613        }
10614    }
10615
10616    /// Execute the work that is ready NOW and return — rclcpp's
10617    /// `Executor::spin_some(max_duration)`.
10618    ///
10619    /// ADOPT-BOUNDED (RFC-0089). Upstream's drain verb: collect what is ready,
10620    /// execute it, come back. It never waits for new work — that is
10621    /// [`spin_once`](Self::spin_once), which takes a budget and blocks on the
10622    /// transport until it expires.
10623    ///
10624    /// **Envelope, two ways it is weaker than rclcpp's:**
10625    ///
10626    /// * rclcpp collects the ready set ONCE and executes it. One
10627    ///   `spin_once(0)` here is already that whole set (RFC-0002 §3), so this
10628    ///   would be a single call — except a callback may enqueue work for
10629    ///   another entity, which rclcpp's `spin_all` re-collects and its
10630    ///   `spin_some` leaves for the next call. Ours re-drains until a pass does
10631    ///   NO work, which is `spin_all`'s answer, because the alternative is
10632    ///   work sitting in the arena until someone spins again. Bounded by
10633    ///   `max`, so a callback that feeds itself cannot wedge the caller.
10634    /// * `max` is checked BETWEEN passes, never inside one, so it is a floor on
10635    ///   when this returns and not a ceiling: a single long callback overruns
10636    ///   it. There is no preemption here to make it a ceiling.
10637    ///
10638    /// `max` of [`Duration::ZERO`](core::time::Duration::ZERO) means no limit —
10639    /// rclcpp's own default — and is the spelling a build with no clock must
10640    /// use. A non-zero `max` on a clockless build is an ERROR rather than an
10641    /// unbounded drain (issue 0709, the same rule as `spin`'s `timeout`).
10642    ///
10643    /// The `Result` is about that PRECONDITION and nothing else. A failed
10644    /// callback is counted in each pass's `SpinOnceResult` and does not end the
10645    /// drain, matching `spin`'s default (`SpinOptions::stop_on_first_error` is
10646    /// `false`); rclcpp's `spin_some` returns `void` and reports callback
10647    /// failures nowhere at all.
10648    ///
10649    /// # Example
10650    ///
10651    /// ```ignore
10652    /// // Drain the ready set, then get on with the caller's own work.
10653    /// executor.spin_some(core::time::Duration::ZERO)?;
10654    /// ```
10655    pub fn spin_some(&mut self, max: core::time::Duration) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
10656        let bounded = !max.is_zero();
10657        let start_us = self.now_us();
10658        if bounded && start_us.is_none() {
10659            nros_log::log_error!(
10660                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
10661                "spin_some: a max duration was requested but this build has no clock \
10662                 - install one with `ExecutorConfig::clock_us`, or pass \
10663                 `Duration::ZERO` for rclcpp's unbounded default (issue 0709)"
10664            );
10665            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
10666        }
10667        let max_us = max.as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;
10668
10669        // No `enter_spin_loop` here, deliberately: `is_spinning` answers "a
10670        // blocking loop is running that a peer's `cancel()` has to reach", and
10671        // this verb returns on its own. Raising the flag for the length of a
10672        // drain would make a `cancel()` from another task look acted-upon when
10673        // nothing was waiting for it.
10674        loop {
10675            let result = self.spin_once(core::time::Duration::ZERO);
10676            if !result.any_work() {
10677                break;
10678            }
10679            if bounded
10680                && let (Some(start), Some(now)) = (start_us, self.now_us())
10681                && now.saturating_sub(start) >= max_us
10682            {
10683                break;
10684            }
10685        }
10686        Ok(())
10687    }
10688
10689    // ========================================================================
10690    // spin_one_period (no_std)
10691    // ========================================================================
10692
10693    /// Process one iteration and return remaining sleep time.
10694    ///
10695    /// This is `no_std` compatible — the caller is responsible for the actual
10696    /// delay using platform-specific sleep.
10697    ///
10698    /// # Arguments
10699    /// * `period_ms` - Target period in milliseconds
10700    /// * `elapsed_ms` - Time elapsed since last call (used for timer ticking)
10701    ///
10702    /// # Example
10703    ///
10704    /// ```ignore
10705    /// loop {
10706    ///     let r = executor.spin_one_period(10, elapsed_ms);
10707    ///     platform_sleep_ms(r.remaining_ms);
10708    /// }
10709    /// ```
10710    pub fn spin_one_period(&mut self, period_ms: u64, elapsed_ms: u64) -> SpinPeriodPollingResult {
10711        let result = self.spin_once(core::time::Duration::from_millis(elapsed_ms));
10712        SpinPeriodPollingResult {
10713            work: result,
10714            remaining_ms: period_ms.saturating_sub(elapsed_ms),
10715        }
10716    }
10717}
10718
10719// ============================================================================
10720// Parameter services (cfg param-services)
10721// ============================================================================
10722
10723#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
10724impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
10725    /// Register the 6 ROS 2 parameter services for this node.
10726    ///
10727    /// Creates service servers for `get_parameters`, `set_parameters`,
10728    /// `set_parameters_atomically`, `list_parameters`, `describe_parameters`,
10729    /// and `get_parameter_types`.
10730    ///
10731    /// The service names follow the ROS 2 convention: `/{namespace}/{node_name}/{suffix}`.
10732    /// For the default namespace `/`, this becomes `/{node_name}/{suffix}` (e.g.
10733    /// `/sentinel/list_parameters`).
10734    ///
10735    /// Parameter services are stored outside the arena and don't consume
10736    /// callback slots.
10737    ///
10738    /// # Example
10739    ///
10740    /// ```ignore
10741    /// let config = ExecutorConfig::from_env().node_name("talker");
10742    /// let mut executor = Executor::open(&config)?;
10743    /// executor.register_parameter_services()?;
10744    /// executor.declare_parameter("start_value", ParameterValue::Integer(0));
10745    /// ```
10746    pub fn register_parameter_services(&mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
10747        // Issue 1706 -- six services over a store that does not exist would
10748        // answer every request with "not declared"; say what went wrong
10749        // instead (`report_parameter_store_refused` has named the size).
10750        if !self.ensure_parameter_store() {
10751            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
10752        }
10753        if let Some(params) = &mut self.params {
10754            params.requested = true;
10755        }
10756        // phase-426 W3 — with no node yet, RECORD the request and stop. The
10757        // reconcile's no-node fallback publishes under the executor's own
10758        // identity, and taking it here would pin node 0 to that name before the
10759        // node that IS node 0 has been built — which is the pre-W3 behaviour
10760        // this work item exists to remove. Every generated entry arrives in
10761        // exactly this state (`apply_param_services` runs ahead of the per-node
10762        // `register` calls, by design), so the fallback belongs on the spin
10763        // path, where "no node" has stopped being merely "not yet".
10764        if self.nodes.is_empty() {
10765            return Ok(());
10766        }
10767        self.reconcile_parameter_services()
10768    }
10769
10770    /// phase-426 W3 — is there a node whose six services are not up yet?
10771    ///
10772    /// The cheap half of the reconcile, kept separate so `spin_once` can test
10773    /// it without carrying the reconcile's frame (see below).
10774    #[inline]
10775    pub(crate) fn parameter_services_pending(&self) -> bool {
10776        self.params.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| {
10777            p.requested
10778                && p.services.len() < self.nodes.len().max(1)
10779                // Issue 1268 — a failure that cannot change is not pending
10780                // work. This used to retry six `create_service` calls on EVERY
10781                // spin, for the life of an image that would never serve them,
10782                // and the result was discarded; 1271 made it say so once, which
10783                // left the retrying. An explicit
10784                // `register_parameter_services()` still tries, because that is
10785                // a caller asking rather than the spin guessing.
10786                && p.reconcile_failure.as_ref().is_none_or(|f| !f.permanent)
10787        })
10788    }
10789
10790    /// Issue 1271 -- say, once, that the parameter services could not be
10791    /// created, instead of discarding the result on every spin.
10792    ///
10793    /// The spin keeps retrying (a node registered later, or a transport that
10794    /// comes up late, may still succeed); this only decides whether anyone is
10795    /// told. Cold and out of line: it formats, and `spin_once`'s frame must
10796    /// not carry that.
10797    #[cold]
10798    #[inline(never)]
10799    fn report_parameter_service_reconcile_failure(&mut self, e: NodeError) {
10800        let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut() else {
10801            return;
10802        };
10803        if params.reconcile_failure_reported {
10804            return;
10805        }
10806        params.reconcile_failure_reported = true;
10807        // Issue 1268 — name the node and the service. "could not be created
10808        // ({:?})" named neither, so a reader could not tell a name too long for
10809        // one node from a backend that will serve none of the six.
10810        let (node_fqn, service, permanent) = match params.reconcile_failure.as_ref() {
10811            Some(f) => (f.node_fqn.as_str(), f.service, f.permanent),
10812            None => ("<unknown node>", "<unknown service>", false),
10813        };
10814        nros_log::log_error!(
10815            nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
10816            "parameter services could not be created for node {} at service {}: {:?}. \
10817             `ros2 param` cannot reach {} of this image's {} node(s). {} (issues 1271, 1268).",
10818            node_fqn,
10819            service,
10820            e,
10821            self.nodes.len().max(1) - params.services.len(),
10822            self.nodes.len().max(1),
10823            if permanent {
10824                "Not retrying: this failure cannot change without a rebuild."
10825            } else {
10826                "Retrying on every spin; logged once."
10827            }
10828        );
10829    }
10830
10831    /// phase-426 W3 — publish one set of six under every node that does not
10832    /// have one yet.
10833    ///
10834    /// **Why a reconcile and not a registration.** `nros::main!` emits
10835    /// `apply_param_services` BEFORE its per-node `register` calls, by design:
10836    /// the store has to exist when each component cell captures it. So at the
10837    /// moment the request is made the node table is EMPTY and there is no FQN
10838    /// to publish under — registering there is how the six ended up pinned to
10839    /// the executor's own identity in the first place. The request is recorded
10840    /// and satisfied here, at the head of every spin, exactly as
10841    /// `reconcile_ros_time_source` does for `use_sim_time` and for the same
10842    /// reason.
10843    ///
10844    /// **An executor with no registered node still gets one set**, under its
10845    /// own `node_name`/`namespace` and keyed `NodeId::PRIMARY` — the identity
10846    /// [`declare_parameter`](Self::declare_parameter) writes to. That is the
10847    /// pre-W3 behaviour, preserved for the direct-API images that never call
10848    /// `node_builder` (`param-chatter-talker` is one), and it is keyed the same
10849    /// as the first node record, so a node registered later inherits the set
10850    /// rather than getting a second one under a different name.
10851    ///
10852    /// Cheap in the settled case: one length comparison — but the FRAME is not
10853    /// cheap, so it is `inline(never)` and the spin site tests
10854    /// [`parameter_services_pending`](Self::parameter_services_pending) first.
10855    /// Building one set used to materialise six `EmbeddedServiceServer`s by
10856    /// value (2 x `PARAM_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE` each, ~48 KiB at the 4096
10857    /// default) before they were boxed; inlined into `spin_once` that landed
10858    /// on every spin frame whether or not the branch was taken. Issue 1270
10859    /// took the buffers out of the set -- one pair per executor, allocated on
10860    /// the heap directly -- but the set still carries six backend handles and
10861    /// a name, so the frame stays out of `spin_once`. Issue 0756's rule one
10862    /// call up — a parameter-service frame does not fit an embedded thread
10863    /// stack, and `test_open_threaded_spawn_and_halt` died with a bare SIGSEGV
10864    /// the first time this was reachable from the spin path.
10865    #[inline(never)]
10866    pub(crate) fn reconcile_parameter_services(&mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
10867        let Some(params) = self.params.as_ref() else {
10868            return Ok(());
10869        };
10870        if !params.requested {
10871            return Ok(());
10872        }
10873        // The nodes wanted, minus the ones already served. Collected first
10874        // because building a set borrows `self.session` mutably while
10875        // `self.nodes` / `self.params` are still borrowed by the scan.
10876        let want = self.nodes.len().max(1);
10877        if params.services.len() >= want {
10878            return Ok(());
10879        }
10880        let mut todo: heapless::Vec<
10881            (u8, heapless::String<64>, heapless::String<64>),
10882            { crate::param_sizing::MAX_SERVICE_SETS },
10883        > = heapless::Vec::new();
10884        for index in 0..want {
10885            let key = nros_params::NodeKey::new(index as u8);
10886            if params.services.iter().any(|set| set.param_node() == key) {
10887                continue;
10888            }
10889            let (name, namespace) = match self.nodes.get(index) {
10890                Some(record) => (record.name.clone(), record.namespace.clone()),
10891                // No node table entry: the executor's own implicit primary
10892                // identity, which is what `NodeId::PRIMARY` means.
10893                None => (self.node_name.clone(), self.namespace.clone()),
10894            };
10895            if todo.push((index as u8, name, namespace)).is_err() {
10896                return Err(NodeError::NodeTableFull);
10897            }
10898        }
10899        // Issue 1270 -- the ONE buffer pair every set is answered through,
10900        // allocated with the first set so an image that declares parameters
10901        // and serves none pays nothing for it. `params` is `Some` here: the
10902        // scan above returned early otherwise.
10903        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut()
10904            && params.buffers.is_none()
10905        {
10906            // Issue 1551 — an exhausted heap is an error this fn returns, not
10907            // an abort through libstd's OOM hook.
10908            params.buffers = Some(
10909                crate::parameter_services::ParamServiceBuffers::try_with_capacity(
10910                    crate::parameter_services::param_service_buffer_bytes(),
10911                )
10912                .ok_or(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc))?,
10913            );
10914        }
10915        for (index, name, namespace) in todo {
10916            let servers = match self.build_parameter_service_set(
10917                nros_params::NodeKey::new(index),
10918                &name,
10919                &namespace,
10920            ) {
10921                Ok(servers) => servers,
10922                Err((e, service)) => {
10923                    // Issue 1268 — keep WHAT failed and WHERE, for the one log
10924                    // line, and decide once whether retrying could ever help.
10925                    // `Unsupported` from the transport is a property of the
10926                    // build (the backend has no descriptor for the
10927                    // `rcl_interfaces` types), so a later spin asks the same
10928                    // question and gets the same answer.
10929                    let permanent = matches!(e, NodeError::Transport(TransportError::Unsupported));
10930                    if let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut() {
10931                        let mut node_fqn = heapless::String::<256>::new();
10932                        if let Ok(fqn) = crate::names::fully_qualified_name(&name, &namespace) {
10933                            let _ = node_fqn.push_str(fqn.as_str());
10934                        }
10935                        params.reconcile_failure =
10936                            Some(crate::parameter_services::ParamServiceReconcileFailure {
10937                                node_fqn,
10938                                service,
10939                                permanent,
10940                            });
10941                    }
10942                    return Err(e);
10943                }
10944            };
10945            let services_box: alloc::boxed::Box<
10946                dyn crate::parameter_services::ParamServiceProcessor,
10947            > = alloc::boxed::Box::new(servers);
10948            // Issue 0745 — PRESERVE an already-initialized store: launch-param
10949            // seeding may have run before any node existed (services can't be
10950            // registered that early). Overwriting here would wipe the seeds.
10951            match &mut self.params {
10952                Some(params) => params
10953                    .services
10954                    .push(services_box)
10955                    .map_err(|_| NodeError::NodeTableFull)?,
10956                None => {
10957                    // Issue 0756 — see new_param_state: never build a ParamState
10958                    // by value, it does not fit an embedded thread stack.
10959                    // Issue 1706 -- the store is fallible; the refusal is
10960                    // reported once by `ensure_parameter_store`'s spelling.
10961                    if self.param_store_refused {
10962                        return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
10963                    }
10964                    let Some(mut state) =
10965                        Self::new_param_state(core::mem::take(&mut self.param_slots))
10966                    else {
10967                        self.param_store_refused = true;
10968                        report_parameter_store_refused();
10969                        return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
10970                    };
10971                    state.requested = true;
10972                    let _ = state.services.push(services_box);
10973                    self.params = Some(state);
10974                }
10975            }
10976            // phase-430 W2 — "declare `use_sim_time` on EVERY node, as rclcpp
10977            // does", said where the nodes finally exist. This is the only place
10978            // that knows the full set: `ensure_parameter_store` runs before any
10979            // node record does, so it can only seed the implicit PRIMARY, and
10980            // the further nodes an image composes onto one executor arrive
10981            // later. Seeding as each set of six goes up keeps the two in step —
10982            // the parameter is declared on exactly the nodes a
10983            // `ros2 param set <node> use_sim_time true` can reach.
10984            //
10985            // Idempotent by construction: `declare` refuses a name the node
10986            // already holds and the placeholder flag is only raised on
10987            // acceptance, so re-seeding PRIMARY here neither duplicates the
10988            // entry nor re-marks an application's own declaration as ours.
10989            self.seed_use_sim_time_default(super::node_record::NodeId::from_raw(index));
10990        }
10991        // Issue 1271 -- every node is served now, so a later failure (a node
10992        // registered after this one) is news again and earns its own line.
10993        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut() {
10994            params.reconcile_failure_reported = false;
10995            // Issue 1268 -- and drop the record with it, so a later failure is
10996            // reported against the node it actually happened on.
10997            params.reconcile_failure = None;
10998        }
10999        Ok(())
11000    }
11001
11002    /// phase-426 W3 — create the six service servers for ONE node.
11003    ///
11004    /// Split out of [`register_parameter_services`](Self::register_parameter_services)
11005    /// because there are now N of these per image rather than one, and because
11006    /// the six `create_param_srv` call sites are what
11007    /// `check-infra-queryable-counts` reads to hold `PARAM_SERVICE_QUERYABLES`
11008    /// to the number of queryables a set actually claims.
11009    #[inline(never)]
11010    fn build_parameter_service_set(
11011        &mut self,
11012        node: nros_params::NodeKey,
11013        node_name: &str,
11014        namespace: &str,
11015    ) -> Result<crate::parameter_services::ParameterServiceServers, (NodeError, &'static str)> {
11016        use crate::parameter_services::{
11017            DescribeParameters, GetParameterTypes, GetParameters, ListParameters,
11018            ParamServiceHandle as PSrv, ParameterServiceServers, SetParameters,
11019            SetParametersAtomically,
11020        };
11021        use nros_core::RosService;
11022
11023        // The node FQN, from the one implementation. This was the third
11024        // hand-rolled copy of the same join (`crate::names::fully_qualified_name`
11025        // is the first, `Node::fully_qualified_name` was the second) — and the
11026        // three did not agree: this one absolutised a bare namespace, that one
11027        // did not. A join with three spellings has no answer to "what does the
11028        // tree do with `my_ns`".
11029        let node_fqn = crate::names::fully_qualified_name(node_name, namespace)
11030            .map_err(|()| (NodeError::NameTooLong, "get_parameters"))?;
11031        // The service names below still take the two halves separately.
11032        let ns: &str = namespace;
11033        let nn: &str = node_name;
11034
11035        /// Build a service name like `{node_fqn}/{suffix}` and create the server handle.
11036        ///
11037        /// Issue 1268 — the error carries the SUFFIX, so a failure can name the
11038        /// service a tool would have called instead of "one of six".
11039        fn create_param_srv<Svc>(
11040            session: &mut session::ConcreteSession,
11041            domain_id: u32,
11042            node_fqn: &str,
11043            namespace: &str,
11044            node_name: &str,
11045            suffix: &'static str,
11046        ) -> Result<session::RmwServiceServer, (NodeError, &'static str)>
11047        where
11048            Svc: RosService,
11049            Svc::Request: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
11050            Svc::Reply: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
11051        {
11052            // Issue 1268 — REGISTER THE TYPES FIRST, exactly as a typed user
11053            // service does (`register_service_sized`). A backend that keys
11054            // topics on a registered type descriptor — Cyclone does — fails
11055            // `create_service` with `Unsupported` for a type it has never been
11056            // told about, and nothing else in the image registers the
11057            // `rcl_interfaces` service types: the generated typesupport of a
11058            // downstream covers ITS OWN message packages, and the backend bakes
11059            // in only `ParticipantEntitiesInfo` for the graph. So the six
11060            // parameter services failed on every spin while the image's own
11061            // services worked, which is what made the cause look like "no
11062            // service support" for two phases (the issue-0745 comment).
11063            //
11064            // A no-op on backends that need no descriptors (zenoh, xrce), which
11065            // is why zenoh served this same image all along.
11066            let register = |e: NodeError| (e, suffix);
11067            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Request>().map_err(register)?;
11068            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Reply>().map_err(register)?;
11069            let mut name = heapless::String::<256>::new();
11070            name.push_str(node_fqn)
11071                .map_err(|_| (NodeError::NameTooLong, suffix))?;
11072            name.push_str("/")
11073                .map_err(|_| (NodeError::NameTooLong, suffix))?;
11074            name.push_str(suffix)
11075                .map_err(|_| (NodeError::NameTooLong, suffix))?;
11076            let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(&name, Svc::SERVICE_NAME, Svc::SERVICE_HASH)
11077                // issue 0824 follow-up — `domain_id` is a PARAMETER, not `self.domain_id`:
11078                // this is a nested `fn`, not a method, so `self` is not in scope and
11079                // the original spelling was E0434. It only fails under feature sets
11080                // that compile this arm, which is why `--all-features` caught it and
11081                // the narrower lanes did not.
11082                .with_domain(domain_id)
11083                .with_namespace(namespace);
11084            if !node_name.is_empty() {
11085                info = info.with_node_name(node_name);
11086            }
11087            // issue 0793 — the parameter services get the PARAMETER profile
11088            // (`rmw_qos_profile_parameters`: KEEP_LAST(1000), reliable,
11089            // volatile), not the generic services one. `QOS_PROFILE_PARAMETERS`
11090            // existed with the right depth and had no caller, so every parameter
11091            // server ran on a depth-10 queue while ROS 2 gives them 1000 — which
11092            // matters exactly when a tool sets many parameters at once, the case
11093            // the deep queue is for.
11094            session
11095                .create_service(&info, QoSProfile::parameter_services_default())
11096                .map_err(|e| (NodeError::Transport(e), suffix))
11097        }
11098
11099        let get_handle = create_param_srv::<GetParameters>(
11100            &mut self.session,
11101            self.domain_id,
11102            &node_fqn,
11103            ns,
11104            nn,
11105            "get_parameters",
11106        )?;
11107        let set_handle = create_param_srv::<SetParameters>(
11108            &mut self.session,
11109            self.domain_id,
11110            &node_fqn,
11111            ns,
11112            nn,
11113            "set_parameters",
11114        )?;
11115        let set_atomic_handle = create_param_srv::<SetParametersAtomically>(
11116            &mut self.session,
11117            self.domain_id,
11118            &node_fqn,
11119            ns,
11120            nn,
11121            "set_parameters_atomically",
11122        )?;
11123        let list_handle = create_param_srv::<ListParameters>(
11124            &mut self.session,
11125            self.domain_id,
11126            &node_fqn,
11127            ns,
11128            nn,
11129            "list_parameters",
11130        )?;
11131        let desc_handle = create_param_srv::<DescribeParameters>(
11132            &mut self.session,
11133            self.domain_id,
11134            &node_fqn,
11135            ns,
11136            nn,
11137            "describe_parameters",
11138        )?;
11139        let types_handle = create_param_srv::<GetParameterTypes>(
11140            &mut self.session,
11141            self.domain_id,
11142            &node_fqn,
11143            ns,
11144            nn,
11145            "get_parameter_types",
11146        )?;
11147
11148        Ok(ParameterServiceServers::new(
11149            // phase-426 W3 — the set carries the node whose parameters it
11150            // serves, so a handler can never read the store without saying
11151            // whose parameters it means.
11152            node,
11153            // Issue 1271 -- carried so a dropped request is reported against
11154            // the service a tool actually called.
11155            node_fqn,
11156            // Issue 1270 -- handles only. The buffers are the executor's one
11157            // shared pair (`ParamState::buffers`), not six per node.
11158            PSrv::<GetParameters>::new(get_handle),
11159            PSrv::<SetParameters>::new(set_handle),
11160            PSrv::<SetParametersAtomically>::new(set_atomic_handle),
11161            PSrv::<ListParameters>::new(list_handle),
11162            PSrv::<DescribeParameters>::new(desc_handle),
11163            PSrv::<GetParameterTypes>::new(types_handle),
11164        ))
11165    }
11166
11167    /// phase-426 W3 — the node FQNs this executor publishes parameter services
11168    /// under, in registration order.
11169    ///
11170    /// The acceptance question for W3 ("does a two-node image expose both
11171    /// FQNs?") answered without a wire: the six services are created from
11172    /// exactly this list, so asserting it asserts what `ros2 param list` will
11173    /// enumerate. The wire assertion is W6.
11174    pub fn parameter_service_node_names(
11175        &self,
11176    ) -> heapless::Vec<crate::names::ResolvedName, { crate::param_sizing::MAX_SERVICE_SETS }> {
11177        let mut out = heapless::Vec::new();
11178        let Some(params) = self.params.as_ref() else {
11179            return out;
11180        };
11181        for set in params.services.iter() {
11182            let index = set.param_node().raw() as usize;
11183            let (name, namespace) = match self.nodes.get(index) {
11184                Some(record) => (record.name.as_str(), record.namespace.as_str()),
11185                None => (self.node_name.as_str(), self.namespace.as_str()),
11186            };
11187            if let Ok(fqn) = crate::names::fully_qualified_name(name, namespace) {
11188                let _ = out.push(fqn);
11189            }
11190        }
11191        out
11192    }
11193
11194    // phase-359 W10 / issue 0080 — `enable_parameter_persistence{,_with}` are
11195    // GONE with the seam they attached. Issue 0080 ruled on-device parameter
11196    // persistence a non-goal in July and listed both by name; nothing in the
11197    // tree ever called them, and the only backend that could be passed
11198    // (`FileParamStore`) is deleted. Runtime get/set/describe stay — it is the
11199    // PERSISTENCE half that was dropped.
11200}
11201
11202// ============================================================================
11203// Lifecycle services (cfg lifecycle-services)
11204// ============================================================================
11205
11206#[cfg(feature = "lifecycle-services")]
11207impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
11208    /// Register the five REP-2002 lifecycle services on this executor.
11209    ///
11210    /// After this call, `ros2 lifecycle set|get|list|nodes` can drive the
11211    /// stored [`LifecyclePollingNodeCtx`](crate::lifecycle::LifecyclePollingNodeCtx)
11212    /// through the node's lifecycle. The state machine is created fresh
11213    /// (starting in `Unconfigured`); callers register their transition
11214    /// callbacks via [`Executor::lifecycle_state_machine_mut`].
11215    ///
11216    /// # Safety
11217    /// Registered callbacks on the state machine are C FFI function pointers.
11218    /// The caller must keep the callback code and any context it captures
11219    /// valid for as long as the executor processes services.
11220    pub fn register_lifecycle_services(&mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
11221        use crate::{
11222            lifecycle::LifecyclePollingNodeCtx,
11223            lifecycle_services::{
11224                ChangeState, GetAvailableStates, GetAvailableTransitions, GetState,
11225                LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE, LifecycleRuntimeState, LifecycleServiceServers,
11226            },
11227        };
11228        use nros_core::RosService;
11229
11230        type LcSrv<Svc> = super::handles::EmbeddedServiceServer<
11231            Svc,
11232            LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE,
11233            LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE,
11234        >;
11235
11236        // Build the node FQN from namespace + node_name (same convention as
11237        // register_parameter_services).
11238        let mut node_fqn = heapless::String::<256>::new();
11239        let ns: &str = &self.namespace;
11240        let nn: &str = &self.node_name;
11241        if ns.is_empty() || ns == "/" {
11242            node_fqn.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11243            node_fqn.push_str(nn).map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11244        } else {
11245            node_fqn.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11246            node_fqn
11247                .push_str(ns.trim_matches('/'))
11248                .map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11249            node_fqn.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11250            node_fqn.push_str(nn).map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11251        }
11252
11253        fn create_lc_srv<Svc>(
11254            session: &mut session::ConcreteSession,
11255            domain_id: u32,
11256            node_fqn: &str,
11257            namespace: &str,
11258            node_name: &str,
11259            suffix: &str,
11260        ) -> Result<session::RmwServiceServer, NodeError>
11261        where
11262            Svc: RosService,
11263            Svc::Request: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
11264            Svc::Reply: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw,
11265        {
11266            // Issue 1293 — register both halves first, as `create_param_srv`
11267            // does since issue 1268: Cyclone creates a topic only for a type it
11268            // holds a descriptor for. Three of the five request types are
11269            // EMPTY, and an empty schema had no descriptor until codegen gave
11270            // it rosidl's `structure_needs_at_least_one_member` byte. A no-op
11271            // on backends that need no descriptors (zenoh, xrce).
11272            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Request>()?;
11273            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Svc::Reply>()?;
11274            let mut name = heapless::String::<256>::new();
11275            name.push_str(node_fqn)
11276                .map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11277            name.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11278            name.push_str(suffix).map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11279            let mut info = ServiceInfo::new(&name, Svc::SERVICE_NAME, Svc::SERVICE_HASH)
11280                .with_domain(domain_id)
11281                .with_namespace(namespace);
11282            if !node_name.is_empty() {
11283                info = info.with_node_name(node_name);
11284            }
11285            session
11286                .create_service(&info, QoSProfile::services_default())
11287                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)
11288        }
11289
11290        /// Issue 1587 — the ONE publisher the REP-2002 family claims,
11291        /// `~/transition_event`. Shaped like `create_lc_srv` beside it both
11292        /// because the naming rule is the same (node FQN + suffix) and
11293        /// because `check-infra-queryable-counts` counts the creation sites
11294        /// to hold `LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_PUBLISHERS` to them, exactly as it
11295        /// already holds `LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_QUERYABLES` to the five above.
11296        fn create_lc_pub<Msg: crate::rmw_type_registry::MessageForRmw>(
11297            session: &mut session::ConcreteSession,
11298            domain_id: u32,
11299            node_fqn: &str,
11300            namespace: &str,
11301            node_name: &str,
11302            suffix: &str,
11303            qos: QoSProfile,
11304        ) -> Result<session::RmwPublisher, NodeError> {
11305            // Issue 1293 — same rule as `create_lc_srv`: Cyclone needs the
11306            // `TransitionEvent` descriptor before it can create the topic.
11307            crate::rmw_type_registry::register_type::<Msg>()?;
11308            let mut name = heapless::String::<256>::new();
11309            name.push_str(node_fqn)
11310                .map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11311            name.push_str("/").map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11312            name.push_str(suffix).map_err(|_| NodeError::NameTooLong)?;
11313            let mut info = TopicInfo::new(
11314                &name,
11315                <Msg as nros_core::RosMessage>::TYPE_NAME,
11316                Msg::TYPE_HASH,
11317            )
11318            .with_domain(domain_id)
11319            .with_namespace(namespace);
11320            if !node_name.is_empty() {
11321                info = info.with_node_name(node_name);
11322            }
11323            session
11324                .create_publisher(&info, qos)
11325                .map_err(NodeError::Transport)
11326        }
11327
11328        let cs_handle = create_lc_srv::<ChangeState>(
11329            &mut self.session,
11330            self.domain_id,
11331            &node_fqn,
11332            ns,
11333            nn,
11334            "change_state",
11335        )?;
11336        let gs_handle = create_lc_srv::<GetState>(
11337            &mut self.session,
11338            self.domain_id,
11339            &node_fqn,
11340            ns,
11341            nn,
11342            "get_state",
11343        )?;
11344        let gas_handle = create_lc_srv::<GetAvailableStates>(
11345            &mut self.session,
11346            self.domain_id,
11347            &node_fqn,
11348            ns,
11349            nn,
11350            "get_available_states",
11351        )?;
11352        let gat_handle = create_lc_srv::<GetAvailableTransitions>(
11353            &mut self.session,
11354            self.domain_id,
11355            &node_fqn,
11356            ns,
11357            nn,
11358            "get_available_transitions",
11359        )?;
11360        let gtg_handle = create_lc_srv::<GetAvailableTransitions>(
11361            &mut self.session,
11362            self.domain_id,
11363            &node_fqn,
11364            ns,
11365            nn,
11366            "get_transition_graph",
11367        )?;
11368
11369        // Issue 1587 — REP-2002's communication interface is the five
11370        // services PLUS this. VOLATILE, so it costs a publisher slot and a
11371        // liveliness token and NO queryable; see
11372        // `LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_PUBLISHERS` for the measurement that settled it.
11373        let te_handle = create_lc_pub::<nros_lifecycle_msgs::msg::TransitionEvent>(
11374            &mut self.session,
11375            self.domain_id,
11376            &node_fqn,
11377            ns,
11378            nn,
11379            crate::lifecycle_services::TRANSITION_EVENT_SUFFIX,
11380            crate::lifecycle_services::transition_event_qos(),
11381        )?;
11382
11383        let servers = LifecycleServiceServers::new(
11384            LcSrv::<ChangeState> {
11385                handle: cs_handle,
11386                req_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11387                reply_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11388                _phantom: core::marker::PhantomData,
11389            },
11390            LcSrv::<GetState> {
11391                handle: gs_handle,
11392                req_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11393                reply_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11394                _phantom: core::marker::PhantomData,
11395            },
11396            LcSrv::<GetAvailableStates> {
11397                handle: gas_handle,
11398                req_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11399                reply_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11400                _phantom: core::marker::PhantomData,
11401            },
11402            LcSrv::<GetAvailableTransitions> {
11403                handle: gat_handle,
11404                req_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11405                reply_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11406                _phantom: core::marker::PhantomData,
11407            },
11408            LcSrv::<GetAvailableTransitions> {
11409                handle: gtg_handle,
11410                req_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11411                reply_buffer: [0u8; LIFECYCLE_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE],
11412                _phantom: core::marker::PhantomData,
11413            },
11414        );
11415
11416        self.lifecycle = Some(alloc::boxed::Box::new(LifecycleRuntimeState {
11417            state_machine: LifecyclePollingNodeCtx::new(),
11418            services: alloc::boxed::Box::new(servers),
11419            transition_event: te_handle,
11420        }));
11421
11422        Ok(())
11423    }
11424
11425    /// The `~/transition_event` publisher, for the tests that assert what
11426    /// reached the wire. Not a public capability: the executor announces, and
11427    /// a second publisher on the same topic would be a second source of truth.
11428    #[cfg(test)]
11429    pub(crate) fn lifecycle_transition_event_publisher(&self) -> Option<&session::RmwPublisher> {
11430        self.lifecycle.as_ref().map(|lc| &lc.transition_event)
11431    }
11432
11433    /// Mutable access to the lifecycle state machine, if registered.
11434    ///
11435    /// Used to register transition callbacks before spinning and to read the
11436    /// current state from application code.
11437    pub fn lifecycle_state_machine_mut(
11438        &mut self,
11439    ) -> Option<&mut crate::lifecycle::LifecyclePollingNodeCtx> {
11440        self.lifecycle.as_mut().map(|lc| &mut lc.state_machine)
11441    }
11442
11443    /// Immutable access to the lifecycle state machine, if registered.
11444    pub fn lifecycle_state_machine(&self) -> Option<&crate::lifecycle::LifecyclePollingNodeCtx> {
11445        self.lifecycle.as_ref().map(|lc| &lc.state_machine)
11446    }
11447
11448    /// Register a safe lifecycle node (issue 0335 / phase-317).
11449    ///
11450    /// Binds the five REP-2002 lifecycle services and wires each transition to
11451    /// the [`LifecycleCallbacks`](crate::lifecycle::LifecycleCallbacks) trait
11452    /// impl — the safe Rust counterpart to the C++ `nros::LifecycleNode`. No
11453    /// `unsafe` in user code; alloc-free (monomorphized trampolines).
11454    ///
11455    /// `node` must outlive this executor's lifecycle registration: the context
11456    /// pointer stored here is dereferenced on every transition until the
11457    /// executor is finalized. The executor spins single-threaded, so the
11458    /// `&mut node` reconstituted inside a callback is never aliased.
11459    pub fn register_lifecycle_node<T: crate::lifecycle::LifecycleCallbacks>(
11460        &mut self,
11461        node: &mut T,
11462    ) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
11463        use crate::lifecycle::{LifecycleCallbackSlot as Slot, trampolines};
11464
11465        self.register_lifecycle_services()?;
11466        let sm = self
11467            .lifecycle_state_machine_mut()
11468            .ok_or(NodeError::NotInitialized)?;
11469        sm.set_context(node as *mut T as *mut core::ffi::c_void);
11470        sm.register(Slot::Configure, Some(trampolines::on_configure::<T>));
11471        sm.register(Slot::Activate, Some(trampolines::on_activate::<T>));
11472        sm.register(Slot::Deactivate, Some(trampolines::on_deactivate::<T>));
11473        sm.register(Slot::Cleanup, Some(trampolines::on_cleanup::<T>));
11474        sm.register(Slot::Shutdown, Some(trampolines::on_shutdown::<T>));
11475        sm.register(Slot::Error, Some(trampolines::on_error::<T>));
11476        Ok(())
11477    }
11478}
11479
11480// ============================================================================
11481// phase-446 W6 -- the contract's declared parameters (cfg param-services)
11482// ============================================================================
11483
11484#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
11485impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
11486    /// Hand the executor the parameters each node's contract declares.
11487    ///
11488    /// The entry calls this before any node registers. It only RECORDS the
11489    /// table: the check runs where an application declares a parameter (the
11490    /// `nros` node runtime), not in [`Self::declare_parameter_on`], because
11491    /// that funnel also carries the launch seed, whose value type is still
11492    /// inferred from text and was already held to the contract by the
11493    /// resolver.
11494    pub fn set_declared_params(&mut self, declared: nros_params::DeclaredParams) {
11495        self.declared_params = declared;
11496    }
11497
11498    /// The table [`Self::set_declared_params`] recorded (empty by default).
11499    pub fn declared_params(&self) -> nros_params::DeclaredParams {
11500        self.declared_params
11501    }
11502}
11503
11504// ============================================================================
11505// Parameter declaration API (cfg param-services)
11506// ============================================================================
11507
11508#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]
11509impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
11510    /// Issue 0745 — lazily create the parameter STORE (no services yet).
11511    /// Launch-param seeding runs before any node is constructed; the six
11512    /// service servers attach later in `register_parameter_services`,
11513    /// which preserves this store.
11514    /// `true` when the store exists afterwards. `false` only when the platform
11515    /// heap refused its allocation (issue 1706), which is reported once, here,
11516    /// with the size it asked for.
11517    fn ensure_parameter_store(&mut self) -> bool {
11518        if self.params.is_none() {
11519            if self.param_store_refused {
11520                return false;
11521            }
11522            let Some(state) = Self::new_param_state(core::mem::take(&mut self.param_slots)) else {
11523                self.param_store_refused = true;
11524                report_parameter_store_refused();
11525                return false;
11526            };
11527            self.params = Some(state);
11528            // phase-430 W2 — the executor's implicit PRIMARY node exists the
11529            // moment the store does, whether or not a node record has been
11530            // built yet, so it is seeded here. The other node keys are seeded
11531            // in `reconcile_parameter_services`, as each one's set of six goes
11532            // up.
11533            self.seed_use_sim_time_default(super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY);
11534        }
11535        true
11536    }
11537
11538    /// phase-430 W2 — declare `use_sim_time = false`, as rclcpp does on EVERY
11539    /// node.
11540    ///
11541    /// Upstream auto-declares the parameter in `rclcpp::Node`'s constructor, so
11542    /// `ros2 param list` shows it and `ros2 param set <node> use_sim_time true`
11543    /// reaches a node whose author never wrote a line about simulated time.
11544    /// Ours honoured the parameter only if the APP had declared it: the store
11545    /// refuses an undeclared set (`allow_undeclared` is false), so the runtime
11546    /// switch worked on exactly the nodes that least needed it.
11547    ///
11548    /// The seed is a PLACEHOLDER, tracked by `ParamState::sim_time_seeded`,
11549    /// because the store refuses a duplicate name: without that flag, seeding
11550    /// here would turn an application's own `declare_parameter("use_sim_time",
11551    /// Bool(true))` into a refusal and the auto-declared default would silently
11552    /// beat the app. `yield_seeded_use_sim_time` steps the placeholder aside
11553    /// for the first real declaration, whatever value or descriptor it carries.
11554    ///
11555    /// PER NODE, both here and in the flag. phase-426 keyed the store and the
11556    /// six services by node, so "every node" is now literally expressible and
11557    /// this is where it is said: `ensure_parameter_store` seeds the executor's
11558    /// implicit PRIMARY, and `reconcile_parameter_services` seeds each further
11559    /// node key as its set of six goes up — which is exactly the set of nodes a
11560    /// `ros2 param set <node> use_sim_time true` can reach.
11561    ///
11562    /// It deliberately does NOT go through `note_reserved_parameter`, so
11563    /// `sim_time_stated` stays false: an auto-declared default is not a
11564    /// STATEMENT by anyone. Recording it as one would make every executor with
11565    /// parameter services write `set_active(false)` onto a PROCESS-GLOBAL gate
11566    /// on its first spin — switching off a simulated clock another executor in
11567    /// the same image installed, which is exactly the collision
11568    /// `sim_time_stated` was added for (issue 1104). That property is per node
11569    /// too: seeding N nodes must still be N statements by nobody.
11570    ///
11571    /// Gated on `sim-time` as well as `param-services`: an image that cannot
11572    /// act on the parameter should not advertise it, because a settable knob
11573    /// that does nothing is worse than an absent one.
11574    fn seed_use_sim_time_default(&mut self, node: super::node_record::NodeId) {
11575        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
11576        if let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut()
11577            && let Some(seeded) = params.sim_time_seeded.get_mut(node.index())
11578            && params.server.declare(
11579                node.into(),
11580                crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM,
11581                nros_params::ParameterValue::Bool(false),
11582            )
11583        {
11584            *seeded = true;
11585        }
11586        let _ = node;
11587    }
11588
11589    /// phase-430 W2 — step the seeded `use_sim_time` aside for an application
11590    /// that declares it itself on `node`. Returns whether it did.
11591    ///
11592    /// The app's declaration must WIN — its own default, its own descriptor —
11593    /// and a declaration is refused when the name is already taken, so the
11594    /// placeholder has to leave before the real one arrives. Only ever the
11595    /// placeholder: once a real declaration has landed the flag is false and a
11596    /// second declaration is refused exactly as it was before W2.
11597    ///
11598    /// Only ever THIS node's placeholder, too: an app that names
11599    /// `use_sim_time` on one node of an image has said nothing about the
11600    /// others, and their seeds stay placeholders for whoever declares next.
11601    fn yield_seeded_use_sim_time(&mut self, node: super::node_record::NodeId, name: &str) -> bool {
11602        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
11603        if name == crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM
11604            && let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut()
11605            && let Some(seeded) = params.sim_time_seeded.get_mut(node.index())
11606            && core::mem::replace(seeded, false)
11607        {
11608            return params.server.remove(node.into(), name);
11609        }
11610        let _ = (node, name);
11611        false
11612    }
11613
11614    /// The HEAP home for the parameter slot table, used only when the
11615    /// executor's backing carved none.
11616    ///
11617    /// phase-382 W2' — `ParameterServer` no longer OWNS its slots; it borrows
11618    /// a caller-placed [`nros_params::ParameterTable`]. phase-382 W3' carves
11619    /// that table out of the caller's executor backing whenever the build
11620    /// KNOWS the image builds a store ([`ExecutorSizing::params`](super::storage::ExecutorSizing::params), from
11621    /// `nros_params::IMPLIED_STORE_SLOTS`); this function is what remains for a
11622    /// store the build could not see — one reached only from application
11623    /// code — and for an executor opened with a sizing that carves none. It
11624    /// makes a single heap allocation, leaked, one per such executor that
11625    /// touches parameters. The leak is what buys the `'static`
11626    /// the borrow needs without making `ParamState` self-referential (a
11627    /// `ParamState` that owned the storage AND a server borrowing it is not
11628    /// expressible), and it is bounded — `ensure_parameter_store` runs this
11629    /// at most once per executor.
11630    ///
11631    /// Issue 0756 — the placement dance is still here because the SIZE is
11632    /// still here; it only moved off `ParameterServer` and onto
11633    /// `ParameterStorage`. That storage is 285,184 bytes at the default
11634    /// `MAX_PARAMETERS=32` and 2,281,472 at 256 (`ParameterValue` is sized by
11635    /// its `StringArray` variant, so every slot costs ~8.5 KiB regardless of
11636    /// what it holds). `Box::new(ParameterStorage::new())` materialises all of
11637    /// that on the caller's stack before copying it into the allocation,
11638    /// because Rust has no placement-new. On the Zephyr lane that silently
11639    /// overran the thread stack: an image built with 256 slots boots to
11640    /// `dds_create_participant` and hangs with no fault and no output, while
11641    /// 32 — which fits the 512 KiB main stack the cyclonedds snippet asks for
11642    /// — runs clean. Initialising through the allocation bounds the largest
11643    /// stack temporary at one slot, so the knob no longer decides whether boot
11644    /// survives.
11645    ///
11646    /// Issue 1706 -- FALLIBLE. This is the one allocation every parameter
11647    /// declaration reaches, in every language and on every RTOS, and it is the
11648    /// largest single request most images make. `Box::new_uninit` sent a
11649    /// failure to the OOM handler: Zephyr printed `HEAP EXHAUSTED` and died in
11650    /// issue 0589's recursion, FreeRTOS heap_4 hung in `MALLOC FAILED`. Every
11651    /// caller already has a refusal to return (`declare_parameter` is a
11652    /// `bool`), so the failure is now one, named by
11653    /// [`report_parameter_store_refused`] with the size it asked for.
11654    fn leak_parameter_storage() -> Option<nros_params::ParameterTable<'static>> {
11655        #[cfg(all(test, feature = "std"))]
11656        if RefuseParameterStore::armed() {
11657            return None;
11658        }
11659        let mut uninit = nros_rmw::fallible::try_box_uninit::<nros_params::ParameterStorage>()?;
11660        // Safety: `try_box_uninit` gives a correctly-sized, correctly-aligned
11661        // allocation for exactly this type, and `init_in_place` writes every
11662        // slot exactly once before `assume_init` observes it.
11663        unsafe {
11664            nros_params::ParameterStorage::init_in_place(uninit.as_mut_ptr());
11665            Some(alloc::boxed::Box::leak(uninit.assume_init()).as_table())
11666        }
11667    }
11668
11669    /// Build the executor's `ParamState`.
11670    ///
11671    /// phase-382 W2' — this is a plain `Box::new` again: `ParameterServer` is
11672    /// now a table borrow plus a count, so `ParamState` is tens of bytes and
11673    /// nothing about constructing one depends on `MAX_PARAMETERS`. The bulk
11674    /// (and issue 0756's placement requirement with it) lives in
11675    /// [`leak_parameter_storage`](Self::leak_parameter_storage).
11676    ///
11677    /// phase-382 W3' — `carved` are the backing's store slots: non-empty, they
11678    /// ARE the store and the heap is not asked; empty, the store falls back to
11679    /// [`leak_parameter_storage`](Self::leak_parameter_storage).
11680    fn new_param_state(
11681        carved: &'s mut [MaybeUninit<nros_params::ParameterSlot>],
11682    ) -> Option<alloc::boxed::Box<crate::parameter_services::ParamState<'s>>> {
11683        let table = if carved.is_empty() {
11684            Self::leak_parameter_storage()?
11685        } else {
11686            // Said once per store, so a boot log answers "where did the store
11687            // come from" without a debugger: issue 1706's measurements were
11688            // all heap-peak arithmetic, and this line is the direct answer.
11689            nros_log::log_info!(
11690                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
11691                "parameter store: {} slots ({} B) carved from the executor backing",
11692                carved.len(),
11693                core::mem::size_of_val(carved)
11694            );
11695            nros_params::ParameterTable::init_in(carved)
11696        };
11697        Some(alloc::boxed::Box::new(
11698            crate::parameter_services::ParamState {
11699                server: nros_params::ParameterServer::new_in(table),
11700                argv_overrides: alloc::vec::Vec::new(),
11701                // phase-426 W3 — the sets attach in `reconcile_parameter_services`,
11702                // one per node, once the node table is populated.
11703                services: heapless::Vec::new(),
11704                requested: false,
11705                // Issue 1270 -- allocated with the first set of services, not here.
11706                buffers: None,
11707                reconcile_failure_reported: false,
11708                reconcile_failure: None,
11709                // phase-430 W2 — no node has been auto-declared yet; the caller
11710                // (`ensure_parameter_store`) seeds PRIMARY immediately after.
11711                #[cfg(feature = "sim-time")]
11712                sim_time_seeded: [false; crate::param_sizing::MAX_SERVICE_SETS],
11713            },
11714        ))
11715    }
11716
11717    /// Install `-p` / `--params-file` parameter overrides — phase-482 W5.
11718    ///
11719    /// They are applied when a parameter is DECLARED: the declaration's value
11720    /// is replaced by the override's, typed by it (`apply_argv_param_override`).
11721    /// So an override reaches a parameter on every road that declares through
11722    /// this executor — C, C++ and Rust — including the launch file's baked
11723    /// values, which the generated entry declares through the same seam.
11724    ///
11725    /// That makes argv WIN over a launch-baked parameter, the opposite of the
11726    /// remap tiers, deliberately: overriding a baked value at run time without
11727    /// a rebuild is what RFC-0015 §9 asks for ("a runtime override has
11728    /// identical effect to a `set_parameter` request after boot"), and upstream
11729    /// agrees — a launch file's parameters reach the node as command-line
11730    /// arguments themselves, where the later one wins.
11731    ///
11732    /// Overrides accumulate in argv order and the LAST one that matches a
11733    /// declaration wins, as rcl's do. A `node:` override matches the node of
11734    /// that NAME; one without matches every node.
11735    ///
11736    /// Fails only when the parameter store could not be allocated (issue 1706),
11737    /// in which case nothing is installed.
11738    pub fn install_argv_params<'p, I>(&mut self, params: I) -> Result<usize, NodeError>
11739    where
11740        I: IntoIterator<Item = crate::ros_args::ParamArg<'p>>,
11741    {
11742        if !self.ensure_parameter_store() {
11743            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
11744        }
11745        let Some(state) = self.params.as_mut() else {
11746            return Err(NodeError::Transport(TransportError::BadAlloc));
11747        };
11748        let mut n = 0;
11749        for p in params {
11750            state
11751                .argv_overrides
11752                .push(crate::parameter_services::ArgvParamOverride {
11753                    node: p.node.map(alloc::string::String::from),
11754                    name: alloc::string::String::from(p.name),
11755                    value: alloc::string::String::from(p.value),
11756                });
11757            n += 1;
11758        }
11759        Ok(n)
11760    }
11761
11762    /// The value a declaration of `name` on `node` should take — the last
11763    /// matching argv override, typed by `declared`, or `declared` itself — and
11764    /// whether an override was applied.
11765    ///
11766    /// An override whose text does not parse as the declared type is NOT
11767    /// applied: it is logged at error severity, naming the parameter, the text
11768    /// and the type, and the declared default stands (RFC-0015 §9.6 — "log +
11769    /// ignore, never panic"). An array-typed declaration takes no override yet.
11770    fn apply_argv_param_override(
11771        &self,
11772        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
11773        name: &str,
11774        declared: nros_params::ParameterValue,
11775    ) -> (nros_params::ParameterValue, bool) {
11776        let Some(state) = self.params.as_ref() else {
11777            return (declared, false);
11778        };
11779        if state.argv_overrides.is_empty() {
11780            return (declared, false);
11781        }
11782        let node_name = self.node(node).map(|r| r.name.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
11783        let Some(o) = state
11784            .argv_overrides
11785            .iter()
11786            .rev()
11787            .find(|o| o.name == name && o.node.as_deref().is_none_or(|n| n == node_name))
11788        else {
11789            return (declared, false);
11790        };
11791        match typed_param_override(&o.value, &declared) {
11792            Some(v) => (v, true),
11793            None => {
11794                nros_log::log_error!(
11795                    nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
11796                    "parameter override `{}:={}` is not a {:?}; the declared default stands",
11797                    name,
11798                    o.value,
11799                    declared.param_type()
11800                );
11801                (declared, false)
11802            }
11803        }
11804    }
11805
11806    /// Declare a parameter with a value on the executor's PRIMARY node.
11807    ///
11808    /// phase-426 W1 — the store is keyed by node, and this is the spelling for
11809    /// the executor's implicit primary node (`NodeId::PRIMARY`), which is the
11810    /// identity `register_parameter_services` publishes and the one every
11811    /// single-node entry means. Name a different node with
11812    /// [`declare_parameter_on`](Self::declare_parameter_on).
11813    ///
11814    /// phase-428 W6 — `#[must_use]`, for the reason `[[nodiscard]]` went on
11815    /// C++'s `Result`: the `else { false }` arm is silently discarded at a
11816    /// call site that drops the value, and `Node::logger` two files over
11817    /// already carries the attribute — so this was inconsistency, not house
11818    /// style. A declare that failed and was ignored is a parameter the program
11819    /// believes it has.
11820    #[must_use]
11821    pub fn declare_parameter(&mut self, name: &str, value: nros_params::ParameterValue) -> bool {
11822        self.declare_parameter_on(super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY, name, value)
11823    }
11824
11825    /// Declare a parameter with a value on a named node.
11826    pub fn declare_parameter_on(
11827        &mut self,
11828        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
11829        name: &str,
11830        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
11831    ) -> bool {
11832        self.ensure_parameter_store();
11833        let (value, _) = self.apply_argv_param_override(node, name, value);
11834        // phase-430 W2 — an application declaring `use_sim_time` itself wins
11835        // over the auto-declared default, so the placeholder leaves first.
11836        let yielded = self.yield_seeded_use_sim_time(node, name);
11837        let accepted = match &mut self.params {
11838            Some(params) => params.server.declare(node.into(), name, value),
11839            None => false,
11840        };
11841        if yielded && !accepted {
11842            // The app's own declaration was refused on its own terms (a full
11843            // store, an ill-formed range). Put the rclcpp default back rather
11844            // than leaving the name undeclared — that is a state neither the
11845            // app nor upstream asked for, and it would silently un-do W2 for
11846            // this node.
11847            self.seed_use_sim_time_default(node);
11848        }
11849        // phase-425 W3b — `use_sim_time` is RESERVED, exactly as in ROS 2: its
11850        // value is not a value the app reads, it is the switch that attaches the
11851        // time source. This is the one seam every language funnels through
11852        // (`nros::main!`'s launch bakes via `apply_param_services`, nros-c's
11853        // `nros_parameter_declare_*`, nros-cpp's `params_shim`), so hooking it
11854        // here covers all of them instead of once per entry path.
11855        //
11856        // phase-430 W3 / issue 1202 — the hook runs AFTER the store's verdict
11857        // and only on acceptance. It used to run first and unconditionally, so
11858        // a re-declaration the store REFUSES (the name is already there) still
11859        // flipped the switch: the store kept `use_sim_time = true` while the
11860        // `/clock` source detached, leaving an executor with sim time recorded
11861        // as on and no source attached, which is neither of the two states the
11862        // parameter can name.
11863        if accepted {
11864            self.note_reserved_parameter(name);
11865        }
11866        accepted
11867    }
11868
11869    /// phase-425 W3b — record a reserved parameter's effect. Today that is
11870    /// `use_sim_time` and nothing else: it is the tree's only reserved name,
11871    /// and [`time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM`](crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM)
11872    /// is the only such constant.
11873    ///
11874    /// Called only after the store ACCEPTED a declaration, and it reads the
11875    /// value back OUT of the store instead of taking the caller's: what the
11876    /// switch must follow is what the store holds, and the two are the same
11877    /// thing only while every write succeeds (issue 1202). The read is
11878    /// [`refresh_use_sim_time_from_store`](Self::refresh_use_sim_time_from_store),
11879    /// the same one the runtime `ros2 param set` path uses, so the declare path
11880    /// and the wire path cannot disagree about the value.
11881    ///
11882    /// A non-bool `use_sim_time` is IGNORED rather than rejected: parameter
11883    /// declaration has no channel to report a complaint on (it returns "did the
11884    /// store take it"), and refusing the declaration outright would fail a node
11885    /// for a parameter ROS 2 lets it declare. The time source simply does not
11886    /// attach, which is the same outcome as `false`.
11887    ///
11888    /// Not covered: [`Executor::parameter`](Self::parameter)'s
11889    /// [`ParameterBuilder`](nros_params::ParameterBuilder) borrows the server
11890    /// and declares through it, so the executor never sees the write and
11891    /// `use_sim_time` named that way attaches nothing — issue 1203.
11892    fn note_reserved_parameter(&mut self, name: &str) {
11893        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
11894        if name == crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM {
11895            self.refresh_use_sim_time_from_store();
11896        }
11897        let _ = name;
11898    }
11899
11900    /// phase-425 W3b — a parameter service handled `n` requests this spin.
11901    ///
11902    /// The hook exists so `use_sim_time` can be re-read after a runtime
11903    /// `ros2 param set`, WITHOUT a per-spin scan of the store. It takes the
11904    /// count unconditionally and ignores it when `sim-time` is off, rather than
11905    /// the call sites carrying the feature test: `handled` was then assigned and
11906    /// never read in the `param-services`-without-`sim-time` combo, which is a
11907    /// `-D warnings` error `check-build` catches and the narrower per-crate
11908    /// clippy runs do not.
11909    #[inline]
11910    fn note_param_services_ran(&mut self, handled: usize) {
11911        #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
11912        if handled > 0 {
11913            self.refresh_use_sim_time_from_store();
11914        }
11915        let _ = handled;
11916        self.report_truncated_descriptions();
11917    }
11918
11919    /// phase-446 F2 -- log each parameter whose description did not fit
11920    /// `NROS_MAX_PARAM_DESCRIPTION_LEN`, once, naming the knob.
11921    ///
11922    /// `nros-params` has no logger, so it truncates, records the truncation on
11923    /// the stored descriptor, and hands it over here. Asked on every spin
11924    /// because a declaration can arrive through builders this executor never
11925    /// sees the end of (`parameter::<T>()` returns the store's own builder);
11926    /// while nothing is pending the store answers from one flag, without
11927    /// walking its table.
11928    #[cold]
11929    fn report_truncated_descriptions(&mut self) {
11930        let Some(params) = self.params.as_mut() else {
11931            return;
11932        };
11933        let nodes = &self.nodes;
11934        params.server.take_truncated_descriptions(|key, name| {
11935            let (ns, node) = nodes
11936                .get(key.index())
11937                .map_or(("", "?"), |r| (r.namespace.as_str(), r.name.as_str()));
11938            nros_log::log_warn!(
11939                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
11940                "parameter `{}` on node {}/{}: its description is longer than \
11941                 NROS_MAX_PARAM_DESCRIPTION_LEN ({} bytes), so `ros2 param describe` \
11942                 answers it truncated at a character boundary. Raise \
11943                 NROS_MAX_PARAM_DESCRIPTION_LEN to keep it whole; 0 stores no \
11944                 descriptions. Logged once for this parameter (phase-446 F2).",
11945                name,
11946                ns.trim_end_matches('/'),
11947                node,
11948                nros_params::MAX_PARAM_DESCRIPTION_LEN
11949            );
11950        });
11951    }
11952
11953    /// Declare a parameter with a value and descriptor on the PRIMARY node.
11954    /// Returns `true` if successful.
11955    ///
11956    /// phase-428 W6 remainder — the sibling of [`Self::declare_parameter`],
11957    /// with the identical `else { false }` arm and no attribute. W6 marked the
11958    /// one method its audit named; this is the site three lines below it, which
11959    /// is the shape CLAUDE.md's "fix the CLASS, not the reported site" rule
11960    /// exists for.
11961    #[must_use]
11962    pub fn declare_parameter_with_descriptor(
11963        &mut self,
11964        name: &str,
11965        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
11966        descriptor: nros_params::ParameterDescriptor,
11967    ) -> bool {
11968        self.declare_parameter_with_descriptor_on(
11969            super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY,
11970            name,
11971            value,
11972            descriptor,
11973        )
11974    }
11975
11976    /// Declare a parameter with a value and descriptor on a named node.
11977    pub fn declare_parameter_with_descriptor_on(
11978        &mut self,
11979        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
11980        name: &str,
11981        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
11982        descriptor: nros_params::ParameterDescriptor,
11983    ) -> bool {
11984        self.ensure_parameter_store();
11985        // phase-430 W2 — same rule as the sibling above: the app's own
11986        // declaration, descriptor and all, replaces the auto-declared default.
11987        let yielded = self.yield_seeded_use_sim_time(node, name);
11988        // phase-482 W5 — an argv override that the DESCRIPTOR refuses (out of
11989        // range, or read-only with a different value) must not cost the
11990        // parameter its existence: log it, then declare the code's default.
11991        let (overridden, differs) = self.apply_argv_param_override(node, name, value.clone());
11992        let mut accepted = match &mut self.params {
11993            Some(params) => params.server.declare_with_descriptor(
11994                node.into(),
11995                name,
11996                overridden,
11997                Some(descriptor.clone()),
11998            ),
11999            None => false,
12000        };
12001        if !accepted && differs {
12002            nros_log::log_error!(
12003                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
12004                "parameter override for `{}` was refused by its descriptor; the declared \
12005                 default stands",
12006                name
12007            );
12008            accepted = match &mut self.params {
12009                Some(params) => params.server.declare_with_descriptor(
12010                    node.into(),
12011                    name,
12012                    value,
12013                    Some(descriptor),
12014                ),
12015                None => false,
12016            };
12017        }
12018        if yielded && !accepted {
12019            self.seed_use_sim_time_default(node);
12020        }
12021        // phase-430 W3 / issue 1202 — the sibling declare path, which had NO
12022        // reserved hook at all: `declare_parameter_with_descriptor` stored
12023        // `use_sim_time` and attached nothing, so the same declaration meant
12024        // two different things depending on whether the app passed a
12025        // descriptor. Same seam, same verdict ordering, one shared hook.
12026        if accepted {
12027            self.note_reserved_parameter(name);
12028        }
12029        accepted
12030    }
12031
12032    /// THE writer — phase-426 W2.
12033    ///
12034    /// Set an ALREADY-DECLARED parameter on the executor's primary node, with
12035    /// the same rules a remote `ros2 param set` gets: read-only, type, range
12036    /// (min/max/step), and issue 1151's refusal of a name the node never
12037    /// declared unless that node opted in through
12038    /// [`allow_undeclared_parameters_on`](Self::allow_undeclared_parameters_on).
12039    ///
12040    /// It routes through [`ParameterServer::apply`](nros_params::ParameterServer::apply),
12041    /// which is what makes the C and C++ facades, the by-value oracle, the
12042    /// streaming service path and the atomic pre-check agree — a facade that
12043    /// wrote the slot directly would be a second answer to "may this set
12044    /// happen", which is the class RFC-0019/0020 forbids. An in-image caller
12045    /// that genuinely wants declare-on-write names
12046    /// `params_mut()`/`set_or_declare` and has opted in by naming it.
12047    ///
12048    /// Returns [`SetParameterResult::NotFound`] when the store does not exist
12049    /// yet (no parameter has been declared and no services registered).
12050    pub fn set_parameter(
12051        &mut self,
