12052        name: &str,
12053        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
12054    ) -> nros_params::SetParameterResult {
12055        self.set_parameter_on(super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY, name, value)
12056    }
12057
12058    /// [`set_parameter`](Self::set_parameter) on a named node.
12059    pub fn set_parameter_on(
12060        &mut self,
12061        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
12062        name: &str,
12063        value: nros_params::ParameterValue,
12064    ) -> nros_params::SetParameterResult {
12065        // Reserved parameters (`use_sim_time`) take effect on a set exactly as
12066        // they do on a declare — this is the seam every language funnels
12067        // through, so hooking it once here covers all of them.
12068        //
12069        // AFTER the store's verdict and only on `Success`, for the reason issue
12070        // 1202 gives one function up: the hook used to run first and off the
12071        // caller's value, so a write the store REFUSED still moved the switch
12072        // and left sim time recorded as on with no source attached. `apply` has
12073        // more ways to refuse than `declare` does — read-only, type, range,
12074        // undeclared-without-the-node-option — so a writer that hooked first
12075        // would reach that state from four directions instead of one.
12076        let result = match &mut self.params {
12077            Some(params) => params.server.apply(node.into(), name, value),
12078            None => nros_params::SetParameterResult::NotFound,
12079        };
12080        if result == nros_params::SetParameterResult::Success {
12081            self.note_reserved_parameter(name);
12082        }
12083        result
12084    }

12086    /// May a remote set DECLARE a name this node never declared? Upstream's
12087    /// `allow_undeclared_parameters` node option (issue 1151), per node since
12088    /// phase-426 W1: switching it on for one node leaves its siblings
12089    /// refusing.
12090    pub fn allow_undeclared_parameters_on(
12091        &mut self,
12092        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
12093        allow: bool,
12094    ) {
12095        self.ensure_parameter_store();
12096        if let Some(params) = &mut self.params {
12097            params.server.set_allow_undeclared(node.into(), allow);
12098        }
12099    }

12141    /// Returns a [`ParameterBuilder`] for fluent parameter declaration with

12143    /// `.mandatory()`, `.optional()`, or `.read_only()`.
12144    ///
12145    /// Returns [`NodeError::NotInitialized`] if parameter services have
12146    /// not been registered yet — call [`register_parameter_services`]
12147    /// first.
12148    ///
12149    /// # Example
12150    ///
12151    /// ```ignore
12152    /// let max_speed = executor.parameter::<f64>("max_speed")?
12153    ///     .default(25.0)
12154    ///     .description("Maximum velocity (m/s)")
12155    ///     .read_only()?;
12156    /// ```
12157    ///
12158    /// [`ParameterBuilder`]: nros_params::ParameterBuilder
12159    /// [`register_parameter_services`]: Self::register_parameter_services
12160    pub fn parameter<'a, T: nros_params::ParameterVariant>(
12161        &'a mut self,
12162        name: &'a str,
12163    ) -> Result<nros_params::ParameterBuilder<'a, 's, T>, NodeError> {
12164        self.parameter_on(super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY, name)
12165    }

12167    /// [`parameter`](Self::parameter) on a named node.
12168    pub fn parameter_on<'a, T: nros_params::ParameterVariant>(
12169        &'a mut self,
12170        node: super::node_record::NodeId,
12171        name: &'a str,
12172    ) -> Result<nros_params::ParameterBuilder<'a, 's, T>, NodeError> {
12173        let server = self
12174            .params
12175            .as_mut()
12176            .map(|p| &mut p.server)
12177            .ok_or(NodeError::NotInitialized)?;
12178        Ok(nros_params::ParameterBuilder::new(
12179            server,
12180            node.into(),
12181            name,
12182        ))
12183    }

12491
12492// ============================================================================
12493// Executor lifecycle — cancel / is_spinning (phase-417 W4.c)
12494// ============================================================================
12495
12496// Issue 1177 -- UN-GATED. This block was `#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]` because
12497// `halt_flag` and `spinning` were `alloc` fields, and neither needed to be: the
12498// allocator is required to SHARE the halt flag (`halt_flag()` hands out a
12499// refcounted handle), never to hold it.
12500//
12501// Gating it meant a no_std executor could not be stopped, and worse, that
12502// `nros-c`'s spin loop -- which calls `cancel`, `is_halted`, `is_spinning`,
12503// `enter_spin_loop` and `exit_spin_loop` with no cfg of its own -- did not
12504// COMPILE for an embedded image. The safety island found that; no
12505// merge-gating lane builds this crate without `alloc`.
12506impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
12507    /// Request the executor to stop spinning — `rclcpp::Executor::cancel`.
12508    ///
12509    /// # ADOPT-BOUNDED (RFC-0089)
12510    ///
12511    /// `cancel` sets a flag the spin loop observes at the NEXT POLL BOUNDARY,
12512    /// so it returns BEFORE spinning has actually stopped;
12513    /// [`is_spinning()`](Self::is_spinning) is the observable that tells you
12514    /// when it has. rclcpp makes the same promise in the same shape, but the
12515    /// boundary here is one `spin_once` timeout wide (a backend's `drive_io`
12516    /// blocks up to the poll interval), so "next boundary" is a duration a
12517    /// caller can measure rather than an implementation detail. The wake flag
12518    /// below shortens it; it does not remove it.
12519    ///
12520    /// Nothing here tears down the session: an executor that has been cancelled
12521    /// is still initialised, still owns its entities, and can be spun again.
12522    /// Teardown is a different verb (`fini` / `shutdown`), and collapsing the
12523    /// two costs a full discovery round on every mode change.
12524    ///
12525    /// Safe to call from another thread or a signal handler.
12526    ///
12527    /// Also raises the Phase 104.C.6 wake flag so a `spin_once` already blocked
12528    /// inside a backend's `drive_io` falls through to the cancel check on its
12529    /// next loop iteration instead of waiting out its full `timeout_ms` first.
12530    pub fn cancel(&self) {
12531        self.halt_flag
12532            .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
12533        // The wake flag is the `Arc` half and still needs an allocator. A
12534        // core-only image simply waits out the poll interval, which is the
12535        // bounded behaviour the envelope above already promises.
12536        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
12537        self.wake_flag
12538            .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
12539    }
12540
12541    /// Has a [`cancel()`](Self::cancel) been REQUESTED?
12542    ///
12543    /// Not the same question as [`is_spinning()`](Self::is_spinning), and both
12544    /// are kept because both have callers:
12545    ///
12546    /// * `is_halted()` — "someone asked this executor to stop." True the instant
12547    ///   `cancel()` returns, and it stays true until the next spin loop clears
12548    ///   it on entry. This is the flag a hand-rolled `while !exec.is_halted()`
12549    ///   loop polls, which is what a BSP that drives `spin_once` itself writes.
12550    /// * `is_spinning()` — "a spin loop is running right now." Answers the other
12551    ///   half of the envelope: whether the cancel has been ACTED on yet.
12552    ///
12553    /// The two are true together for as long as one poll takes, which is exactly
12554    /// the window the ADOPT-BOUNDED envelope on `cancel()` describes. Neither is
12555    /// derivable from the other: an executor that was never spun is neither
12556    /// halted nor spinning, and one cancelled mid-poll is both.
12557    ///
12558    /// The name is the pre-rename spelling and is deliberately NOT deprecated —
12559    /// `cancel`'s rclcpp pair is a `spinning` observable, not an
12560    /// `is_cancel_requested` one, so there is no ROS 2 name to adopt here and a
12561    /// third spelling would buy nothing.
12562    pub fn is_halted(&self) -> bool {
12563        self.halt_flag.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
12564    }
12565
12566    /// Is a spin loop running on this executor right now?
12567    ///
12568    /// rclcpp spells this `Executor::is_spinning()`. True between the entry and
12569    /// the exit of [`spin`](Self::spin),
12570    /// [`spin_period`](Self::spin_period), the `open_threaded` worker loop, and
12571    /// the C / C++ API loops — every construct that owns its own iteration.
12572    ///
12573    /// A bare `spin_once` does NOT set it: one poll is not a spin, and a caller
12574    /// running its own `while` around `spin_once` is the one who knows it is
12575    /// looping. Such a caller can say so with
12576    /// [`enter_spin_loop`](Self::enter_spin_loop).
12577    ///
12578    /// See [`is_halted()`](Self::is_halted) for why this is a different question
12579    /// from "was cancel requested".
12580    pub fn is_spinning(&self) -> bool {
12581        self.spinning.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
12582    }
12583
12584    /// Declare that the caller is entering a spin loop it drives itself.
12585    ///
12586    /// The seam the C and C++ APIs use so their loops answer
12587    /// [`is_spinning()`](Self::is_spinning) without keeping a flag of their own
12588    /// (RFC-0019: ergonomics may live in the wrapper, state may not). Also
12589    /// CLEARS any pending cancel, matching what `spin` does on entry:
12590    /// a cancel requested before a spin started is not a cancel of THIS spin.
12591    ///
12592    /// Pair it with [`exit_spin_loop`](Self::exit_spin_loop) on EVERY exit path,
12593    /// `break` and early `return` alike — a loop that leaves without it reports
12594    /// `is_spinning() == true` forever. It is a method pair rather than an RAII
12595    /// guard on purpose: a guard would have to borrow the executor for the whole
12596    /// loop, and every caller needs `&mut` inside the body to poll.
12597    ///
12598    /// Takes `&self` (the flags are atomics), so the borrow ends at the call.
12599    pub fn enter_spin_loop(&self) {
12600        self.halt_flag
12601            .store(false, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
12602        self.spinning
12603            .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
12604    }
12605
12606    /// End the scope opened by [`enter_spin_loop`](Self::enter_spin_loop).
12607    ///
12608    /// Idempotent. Leaves the cancel flag alone: "someone asked me to stop" is
12609    /// the caller's answer to keep or clear, and clearing it here would lose the
12610    /// reason the loop exited.
12611    pub fn exit_spin_loop(&self) {
12612        self.spinning
12613            .store(false, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
12614    }
12615}
12616
12617// ============================================================================
12618// std-gated spin and halt methods
12619// ============================================================================
12620
12621// phase-359 W10 — this impl used to be ONE `#[cfg(feature = "std")]` block.
12622// Only the wall-clock spin loops in it need `std` (`Instant`, `thread::sleep`,
12623// `thread::spawn`); `halt` / `is_halted` / `wake` are plain atomic stores on
12624// flags the struct already owns, and `halt_flag` / `wake_handle` only need
12625// `Arc`. Gating the BLOCK rather than the items made a no_std image unable to
12626// stop its own executor — `ExecutorNodeRuntime::spin` carried a matching `std`
12627// gate for no reason but this one.
12628// phase-359 W10 — `alloc`, not `std`. The wall-clock spin loops were the
12629// reason this block was std-gated: `Instant` for the deadline and
12630// `thread::sleep` for the pacing. Both now go through the platform — the
12631// executor's own `now_us()` and `nros_platform_sleep_us` — so a no_std
12632// image can run the same blocking loops a hosted one does instead of
12633// hand-rolling them in its BSP.
12634#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
12635impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
12636    /// Blocking spin loop with configurable exit conditions — rclrs's
12637    /// `Executor::spin(SpinOptions)`.
12638    ///
12639    /// ADOPT-BOUNDED (RFC-0089). Same name, same argument, same meaning: run
12640    /// until an exit condition in `opts` says stop. Two bounds, both visible in
12641    /// the signature:
12642    ///
12643    /// * **The error channel is one error, not all of them.** rclrs returns
12644    ///   `Vec<RclrsError>` and the caller writes `.first_error()?`; there is no
12645    ///   allocator here, so ours returns `Result<(), NodeError>` carrying the
12646    ///   FIRST failing callback's error and drops the rest (they are still
12647    ///   counted in each pass's [`SpinOnceResult`]). Ported line for line, the
12648    ///   edit is `.first_error()?` -> `?`, which the compiler points at.
12649    /// * **The loop is a poll loop**, so `opts.poll_interval` is the quantum at
12650    ///   which every exit condition is observed — a `cancel()` from another
12651    ///   task, the `timeout` expiring, `max_callbacks` being reached. Requesting
12652    ///   a `timeout` on a build with no clock is an ERROR, not a silent
12653    ///   never-ending loop (issue 0709).
12654    ///
12655    /// phase-427 — this method was `spin_blocking`. `spin` was taken by the
12656    /// `-> !` task body, which is now [`spin_forever`](Self::spin_forever).
12657    ///
12658    /// Runs until one of:
12659    /// - [`cancel()`](Self::cancel) is called (from
12660    ///   another thread or signal handler)
12661    /// - `opts.timeout` expires (if set)
12662    /// - `opts.max_callbacks` is reached (if set)
12663    /// - `opts.only_next` is true (single iteration)
12664    /// - a callback failed and `opts.stop_on_first_error` is set
12665    ///
12666    /// # Example
12667    ///
12668    /// ```ignore
12669    /// // Spin until cancelled
12670    /// executor.spin(SpinOptions::default())?;
12671    ///
12672    /// // Spin with 5-second timeout
12673    /// executor.spin(SpinOptions::new().timeout(core::time::Duration::from_secs(5)))?;
12674    ///
12675    /// // Single iteration
12676    /// executor.spin(SpinOptions::spin_once())?;
12677    /// ```
12678    pub fn spin(&mut self, opts: SpinOptions) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
12679        // phase-427 — was a private `POLL_INTERVAL` const; it is
12680        // `SpinOptions::poll_interval` now, defaulting to the same 10 ms, so
12681        // `spin` and `spin_forever` read one value instead of two literals.
12682        let poll_interval = opts.poll_interval;
12683
12684        // phase-359 W10 — the executor's own clock. `now_us()` reads the
12685        // PLATFORM's monotonic counter, and nothing else: the platform API is
12686        // the clock, so a build with a port has one and a build without has
12687        // none. There is no `std::time::Instant` third answer any more, which
12688        // is what used to make "what time is it" depend on whether some crate
12689        // in the graph happened to name `std`.
12690        //
12691        // `None` means this build has NO clock at all — and issue 0709 is what
12692        // the previous answer here cost. It read: "a timeout cannot be honoured
12693        // then, and pretending otherwise would exit immediately or never; the
12694        // honest reading is no deadline". It then picked NEVER. A caller that
12695        // asked for 50 ms got an infinite loop, silently, in the one API whose
12696        // whole contract is "returns after N ms" — ten hours of a CI lane
12697        // before anyone read it as stuck rather than slow.
12698        //
12699        // Neither of the two silent readings is honest. An unmet precondition
12700        // is an ERROR (repo rule, fail-loud): the caller supplied a time
12701        // quantity this build cannot measure, and only they can decide what to
12702        // do about it. An UNTIMED `spin` still runs until halt, which
12703        // is a promise this build can keep.
12704        let start_us = self.now_us();
12705        if opts.timeout.is_some() && start_us.is_none() {
12706            nros_log::log_error!(
12707                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
12708                "spin: a timeout was requested but this build has no clock \
12709                 — install one with `ExecutorConfig::clock_us` (issue 0709)"
12710            );
12711            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
12712        }
12713        // `as_micros()` rather than a hand-rolled `ms * 1_000`: the multiply
12714        // was unchecked, and the unit conversion is `Duration`'s job.
12715        let timeout_us = opts.timeout.map(|d| d.as_micros() as u64);
12716        let mut total_callbacks = 0usize;
12717
12718        // phase-417 W4.c — clears the cancel flag AND raises `is_spinning`. The
12719        // clear is the pre-existing behaviour (a cancel requested before this
12720        // spin is not a cancel of this spin); the raise is what lets a peer
12721        // thread see that its `cancel()` has not been acted on yet. Every exit
12722        // below is a `break` to the single tail, which is where the scope ends.
12723        self.enter_spin_loop();
12724
12725        loop {
12726            if self.halt_flag.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {
12727                break;
12728            }
12729
12730            if let (Some(start), Some(limit)) = (start_us, timeout_us)
12731                && self
12732                    .now_us()
12733                    .is_some_and(|now| now.saturating_sub(start) >= limit)
12734            {
12735                break;
12736            }
12737
12738            let mut callback_error = None;
12739            let result = self.spin_once_capturing(poll_interval, &mut callback_error);
12740            total_callbacks += result.total();
12741
12742            // phase-427 — the first error, and only the first: rclrs's
12743            // `Vec<RclrsError>` needs an allocator we do not have. The scope is
12744            // closed before returning so a caller that reads `is_spinning()`
12745            // after an error sees `false`, exactly as after a clean exit.
12746            if opts.stop_on_first_error
12747                && let Some(e) = callback_error
12748            {
12749                self.exit_spin_loop();
12750                return Err(NodeError::Transport(e));
12751            }
12752
12753            if opts.max_callbacks.is_some_and(|max| total_callbacks >= max) {
12754                break;
12755            }
12756
12757            if opts.only_next {
12758                break;
12759            }
12760        }
12761
12762        self.exit_spin_loop();
12763        Ok(())
12764    }
12765
12766    /// Execute one period with wall-clock overrun detection.
12767    ///
12768    /// Calls [`spin_once()`](Self::spin_once), measures wall-clock time, sleeps
12769    /// for the remainder if under budget.
12770    ///
12771    /// # Example
12772    ///
12773    /// ```ignore
12774    /// let period = core::time::Duration::from_millis(10);
12775    /// let result = executor.spin_one_period_timed(period);
12776    /// if result.overrun {
12777    ///     log::warn!("Period overrun: {:?}", result.elapsed);
12778    /// }
12779    /// ```
12780    pub fn spin_one_period_timed(
12781        &mut self,
12782        period: core::time::Duration,
12783    ) -> super::types::SpinPeriodResult {
12784        let start_us = self.now_us();
12785        let result = self.spin_once(period);
12786        // With no clock there is nothing to measure and nothing to sleep off;
12787        // report zero elapsed and no overrun, which is what an unmeasured
12788        // period is.
12789        let elapsed = start_us
12790            .zip(self.now_us())
12791            .map(|(s, e)| core::time::Duration::from_micros(e.saturating_sub(s)))
12792            .unwrap_or_default();
12793        let overrun = elapsed > period;
12794        if !overrun && start_us.is_some() {
12795            platform_sleep(period - elapsed);
12796        }
12797        super::types::SpinPeriodResult {
12798            work: result,
12799            overrun,
12800            elapsed,
12801        }
12802    }
12803
12804    /// Spin at a fixed rate with drift compensation. Blocks until halted.
12805    ///
12806    /// Uses wall-clock time to maintain the target rate. The next invocation
12807    /// time is accumulated (not reset to `now + period`) to prevent cumulative
12808    /// drift.
12809    ///
12810    /// # Example
12811    ///
12812    /// ```ignore
12813    /// // 100Hz control loop — blocks until halt() is called
12814    /// executor.spin_period(core::time::Duration::from_millis(10))?;
12815    /// ```
12816    pub fn spin_period(&mut self, period: core::time::Duration) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
12817        let period_us = period.as_micros().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64;
12818        // Absolute next-deadline in the executor's own clock. issue 0709 — the
12819        // sibling of `spin`'s guard above: with no clock there is no
12820        // pacing, and the loop would run as fast as `spin_once` returns while
12821        // the caller believes it is running at `period`. A requested period
12822        // this build cannot honour is a configuration error, not a silent
12823        // busy-loop.
12824        let Some(start_us) = self.now_us() else {
12825            nros_log::log_error!(
12826                nros_log::get_logger("nros"),
12827                "spin_period: a period was requested but this build has no clock \
12828                 — install one with `ExecutorConfig::clock_us` (issue 0709)"
12829            );
12830            return Err(NodeError::NotInitialized);
12831        };
12832        // phase-417 W4.c — after the clock guard, not before it: a call that
12833        // returns an error never spun, and must not report that it did. (This
12834        // also moved the cancel-flag clear past the guard, which is the same
12835        // correction.)
12836        self.enter_spin_loop();
12837        let mut next_us = Some(start_us + period_us);
12838
12839        loop {
12840            if self.halt_flag.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {
12841                break;
12842            }
12843
12844            self.spin_once(period);
12845
12846            if let Some(next) = next_us {
12847                // Jitter is recorded in `spin_once` above, which this loop
12848                // calls every iteration -- counting it here as well would
12849                // double every wake on this one driver.
12850                if let Some(now) = self.now_us()
12851                    && now < next
12852                {
12853                    platform_sleep(core::time::Duration::from_micros(next - now));
12854                }
12855                // Accumulate to prevent drift (not = now + period)
12856                next_us = Some(next + period_us);
12857            }
12858        }
12859        self.exit_spin_loop();
12860        Ok(())
12861    }
12862}
12863
12864#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
12865impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
12866    /// Phase 110.D.b — move this Executor onto a fresh OS thread,
12867    /// apply a per-thread scheduling policy via the caller-supplied
12868    /// `apply_policy` function, and run the spin loop until
12869    /// `ThreadHandle::halt` fires.
12870    ///
12871    /// The function-pointer indirection on `apply_policy` lets the
12872    /// caller pass any platform's `PlatformScheduler::set_current_thread_policy`
12873    /// without forcing `Executor` to be generic over the platform —
12874    /// keeps the existing `Executor` type stable.
12875    ///
12876    /// Multi-executor preemption (the actual hard-RT win) comes from
12877    /// the OS scheduler — call `open_threaded` once per criticality
12878    /// tier, each with its own policy / priority. The kernel handles
12879    /// preemption across executors; within a single executor,
12880    /// dispatch remains non-preemptive (110.A–C bucketed sets).
12881    ///
12882    /// # Safety
12883    ///
12884    /// Moves `self` across thread boundaries. `Executor` contains a
12885    /// raw `*mut session::ConcreteSession` when constructed via
12886    /// `from_session_ptr`; the caller must ensure that pointer's
12887    /// referent stays valid across the lifetime of the spawned thread
12888    /// and that no other thread mutates the session concurrently.
12889    /// `from_session` (Owned) is safer — `ConcreteSession` ownership
12890    /// transfers cleanly into the thread.
12891    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
12892    pub unsafe fn open_threaded(
12893        self,
12894        policy: nros_platform_api::SchedPolicy,
12895        apply_policy: fn(
12896            nros_platform_api::SchedPolicy,
12897        ) -> Result<(), nros_platform_api::SchedError>,
12898        spin_period: core::time::Duration,
12899    ) -> ThreadHandle
12900    where
12901        // phase-271 — the spawned thread owns `self` for an unbounded lifetime,
12902        // so its borrowed storage must be `'static` (a leaked/`static` backing —
12903        // the `alloc` convenience constructors or a program-lifetime region).
12904        's: 'static,
12905    {
12906        let halt = self.halt_flag.clone();
12907        // phase-359 W10 — a platform task, not `std::thread`. The two other
12908        // executor-owned workers moved earlier; this is the third and last, and
12909        // it is the one the ABI fits best: `open_threaded` exists to give a
12910        // spin loop an OS SCHEDULING POLICY, which is not something a build
12911        // without an OS was ever going to get from `std`.
12912        //
12913        // The closure becomes a heap context because the entry point crosses C
12914        // as `*mut c_void`. It is reclaimed by the trampoline on exit rather
12915        // than leaked: unlike a tier task, this loop RETURNS — that is what
12916        // `halt` is for.
12917        let ctx = alloc::boxed::Box::into_raw(alloc::boxed::Box::new(ThreadedCtx {
12918            executor: self,
12919            policy,
12920            apply_policy,
12921            spin_period,
12922        }));
12923        // SAFETY: `ctx` stays live until the trampoline reclaims it, which
12924        // happens on the spawned task and only after the loop exits.
12925        let task = unsafe {
12926            nros_platform_api::task::PlatformTask::spawn(
12927                threaded_spin_trampoline,
12928                ctx as *mut core::ffi::c_void,
12929                OPEN_THREADED_STACK_BYTES,
12930                c"nros-exec".as_ptr(),
12931            )
12932        };
12933        let Some(task) = task else {
12934            // The platform refused (or cannot size) a task. Reclaim the
12935            // context and hand back a handle that owns nothing — `halt` and
12936            // `join` stay callable, which keeps the caller's shape identical to
12937            // the success path.
12938            //
12939            // SAFETY: nothing was spawned, so this pointer has no other owner.
12940            drop(unsafe { alloc::boxed::Box::from_raw(ctx) });
12941            return ThreadHandle { task: None, halt };
12942        };
12943        ThreadHandle {
12944            task: Some(task),
12945            halt,
12946        }
12947    }
12948
12949    /// Phase 104.C.6 — wake the executor from another thread / ISR /
12950    /// signal handler.
12951    ///
12952    /// Sets the shared `wake_flag`. The next `spin_once` swap-clears the
12953    /// flag, skips the blocking wait on the primary session, and polls
12954    /// every session non-blockingly so whatever queued the wake is
12955    /// observed in a single iteration. Idempotent — multiple `wake()`
12956    /// calls collapse into one observed wake per `spin_once`.
12957    pub fn wake(&self) {
12958        self.wake_flag
12959            .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
12960    }
12961}
12962
12963#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
12964impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
12965    /// Get a clone of the halt flag for use in signal handlers or other threads.
12966    ///
12967    /// # Example
12968    ///
12969    /// ```ignore
12970    /// let halt = executor.halt_flag();
12971    /// std::thread::spawn(move || {
12972    ///     std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(5));
12973    ///     halt.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
12974    /// });
12975    /// executor.spin(SpinOptions::default())?;
12976    /// ```
12977    pub fn halt_flag(&self) -> portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool> {
12978        self.halt_flag.clone()
12979    }
12980
12981    /// Phase 104.C.6 — clone of the shared wake flag for cross-thread
12982    /// use (signal handlers, foreign threads, future per-backend vtable
12983    /// wake hooks).
12984    ///
12985    /// # Example
12986    ///
12987    /// ```ignore
12988    /// let wake = executor.wake_handle();
12989    /// std::thread::spawn(move || {
12990    ///     // ... compute something ...
12991    ///     // hand off to executor by setting the flag.
12992    ///     wake.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
12993    /// });
12994    /// loop { executor.spin_once(Duration::from_millis(100)); }
12995    /// ```
12996    pub fn wake_handle(&self) -> portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool> {
12997        self.wake_flag.clone()
12998    }
12999}
13000
13001/// Phase 110.E.b — opaque per-platform timer handle. Stores the
13002/// raw platform handle (POSIX `timer_t` boxed via `PosixTimerHandle`,
13003/// FreeRTOS `TimerHandle_t`, etc.) plus a destroy thunk so the
13004/// Executor can clean up without being generic over the platform.
13005///
13006/// Caller of `register_sporadic_timer` builds this via
13007/// `OpaqueTimerHandle::new(handle, destroy_fn)` after their
13008/// `PlatformTimer::create_periodic` call returns.
13009#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13010pub struct OpaqueTimerHandle {
13011    handle: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
13012    destroy_fn: extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void),
13013}
13014
13015#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13016unsafe impl Send for OpaqueTimerHandle {}
13017#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13018unsafe impl Sync for OpaqueTimerHandle {}
13019
13020#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13021impl OpaqueTimerHandle {
13022    /// # Safety
13023    /// `handle` must be a live platform-specific timer handle that
13024    /// `destroy_fn` knows how to drop. Caller surrenders ownership
13025    /// of the underlying handle to the Executor.
13026    pub unsafe fn new(
13027        handle: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
13028        destroy_fn: extern "C" fn(*mut core::ffi::c_void),
13029    ) -> Self {
13030        Self { handle, destroy_fn }
13031    }
13032}
13033
13034#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13035impl Drop for OpaqueTimerHandle {
13036    fn drop(&mut self) {
13037        if !self.handle.is_null() {
13038            (self.destroy_fn)(self.handle);
13039            self.handle = core::ptr::null_mut();
13040        }
13041    }
13042}
13043
13044/// Handle returned from [`Executor::open_threaded`]. Holds the
13045/// spawned thread's join handle and a clone of the executor's halt
13046/// flag. Drop runs `halt() + join()` so the thread can't outlive the
13047/// handle.
13048#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13049pub struct ThreadHandle {
13050    task: Option<nros_platform_api::task::PlatformTask>,
13051    halt: portable_atomic_util::Arc<portable_atomic::AtomicBool>,
13052}
13053
13054/// Default stack for an `open_threaded` spin loop. `std::thread`'s default was
13055/// 2 MiB; the executor's own storage is caller-carved and lives elsewhere, so
13056/// this carries call frames only — the same reasoning (and size) as the NuttX
13057/// tier spawn, which measured this against a real RTOS default.
13058#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13059const OPEN_THREADED_STACK_BYTES: usize = 65536;
13060
13061/// What [`Executor::open_threaded`] hands its task, in place of a closure's
13062/// captures. Owned by the trampoline, which reclaims it when the loop exits.
13063#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13064struct ThreadedCtx {
13065    executor: Executor<'static>,
13066    policy: nros_platform_api::SchedPolicy,
13067    apply_policy: fn(nros_platform_api::SchedPolicy) -> Result<(), nros_platform_api::SchedError>,
13068    spin_period: core::time::Duration,
13069}
13070
13071/// The spawned spin loop.
13072///
13073/// # Safety
13074/// `arg` must be the `Box<ThreadedCtx>` raw pointer `open_threaded` created,
13075/// passed exactly once.
13076#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13077unsafe extern "C" fn threaded_spin_trampoline(
13078    arg: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
13079) -> *mut core::ffi::c_void {
13080    // SAFETY: the caller's contract — this is the pointer `open_threaded`
13081    // leaked, and the task is the only consumer of it.
13082    let mut ctx = unsafe { alloc::boxed::Box::from_raw(arg as *mut ThreadedCtx) };
13083    // Apply the requested OS scheduling policy to this fresh task. Failure is
13084    // reported but not propagated — a runtime that fails to lift to SCHED_FIFO
13085    // still spins correctly at SCHED_OTHER (just without RT guarantees).
13086    let _ = (ctx.apply_policy)(ctx.policy);
13087    // phase-417 W4.c — this loop owns its own iteration, so it is a spin and
13088    // must say so. NOT `enter_spin_loop()`: that clears the cancel flag, and
13089    // `open_threaded` hands the caller a `ThreadHandle` whose `halt()` may
13090    // already have fired before this task was scheduled. Raising `is_spinning`
13091    // without touching the cancel bit is the honest report here.
13092    ctx.executor
13093        .spinning
13094        .store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
13095    while !ctx.executor.is_halted() {
13096        ctx.executor.spin_once(ctx.spin_period);
13097    }
13098    ctx.executor.exit_spin_loop();
13099    core::ptr::null_mut()
13100}
13101
13102#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13103impl ThreadHandle {
13104    /// Signal the spawned executor thread to stop. The thread exits
13105    /// on its next `spin_once` iteration.
13106    pub fn halt(&self) {
13107        self.halt.store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
13108    }
13109
13110    /// Wait for the spawned task to exit. After `join`, calling it again is a
13111    /// no-op.
13112    ///
13113    /// phase-359 W10 — was `std::thread::Result<()>`, which carried a panic
13114    /// payload this can no longer produce: a platform task has no unwinding
13115    /// join. Same two outcomes, an error type that does not require `std` —
13116    /// the trade `signal_fd` already made in this campaign. `NotInitialized`
13117    /// means the platform refused to host the task at spawn time — nothing was
13118    /// started, so there is nothing to wait for. (An existing variant rather
13119    /// than a new one: `NodeError` is mapped across the C and C++ FFI, so a new
13120    /// variant is a gate-checked ABI change and this needs no new meaning.)
13121    pub fn join(mut self) -> Result<(), NodeError> {
13122        self.halt();
13123        match self.task.take() {
13124            Some(t) => {
13125                t.join();
13126                Ok(())
13127            }
13128            None => Err(NodeError::NotInitialized),
13129        }
13130    }
13131}
13132
13133#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13134impl Drop for ThreadHandle {
13135    fn drop(&mut self) {
13136        self.halt.store(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
13137        if let Some(t) = self.task.take() {
13138            t.join();
13139        }
13140    }
13141}

13143// SAFETY: Phase 110.D.b — `Executor` contains a raw `*mut
13144// session::ConcreteSession` only on the `from_session_ptr` (Borrowed)
13145// path; the `from_session` (Owned) path is plain Send-able. The
13146// `unsafe fn open_threaded` entry point documents the safety
13147// contract for Borrowed sessions; for Owned sessions the Send claim
13148// is unconditional.
13149// phase-359 W10 — `alloc`, not `std`: this assertion exists for
13150// `open_threaded`, which now hands the executor to a PLATFORM task. The
13151// crossing is the same one; only the thing doing the crossing changed.
13152#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13153unsafe impl<'s> Send for Executor<'s> {}
13154
13155// =============================================================================
13156// Phase 110.F — `OsPriorityWorker` + `WorkItem`
13157// =============================================================================
13158
13159// phase-359 W10 — `OsPriorityWorker` / `WorkItem` moved to
13160// `super::os_priority` and were rewritten off `std::thread` + `std::sync::mpsc`
13161// + `HashMap` onto the platform task ABI, a bounded `heapless` mailbox and a
13162// `NodeWake` doorbell. The capability is no longer std-only; see that module
13163// for what changed semantically (bounded mailbox, capacity-limited pool, and
13164// no pool on a platform without a wake primitive).
13165
13166impl<'s> Drop for Executor<'s> {
13167    fn drop(&mut self) {
13168        // Issue 0790 — a teardown that never went through `close()` still gets
13169        // its ordered shutdown hooks, and gets them in the SAME order. The C
13170        // API's `nros_executor_fini` is exactly that path: it drops the
13171        // executor in place and leaves the session to `nros_support_fini`, so
13172        // without this the whole facility would be silently inert for every C
13173        // entry. Entities are still live at the top of `drop` — the component
13174        // cells and the arena entries below are what tears them down — so this
13175        // is the last moment a pre-shutdown hook can do what it exists to do.
13176        //
13177        // After a normal `close()` both tables are already empty and these two
13178        // calls are a pair of `None` scans.
13179        self.run_shutdown_hooks(super::types::ShutdownPhase::Pre);
13180        // Phase 258 (Track 2, 2a) — release executor-owned component cells
13181        // first (before the arena entries), so a component's `drop`
13182        // trampoline can still touch its own (cell-owned) state. Each slot
13183        // owns a leaked `Arc<ComponentCell>`; its `drop` reconstitutes +
13184        // drops that Arc exactly once.
13185        for slot in self.component_slots.iter() {
13186            // SAFETY: `slot.state` is the leaked cell enrolled via
13187            // `enroll_component`; `slot.drop` is its matching trampoline, run
13188            // exactly once here (slots are not removed before Drop).
13189            unsafe {
13190                (slot.drop)(slot.state);
13191            }
13192        }
13193        let arena_ptr = self.arena.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u8;
13194        for meta in self.entries.iter().flatten() {
13195            // SAFETY: each entry was written by `ptr::write` in `add_*` and
13196            // has not been dropped yet. `drop_fn` matches the concrete type.
13197            unsafe {
13198                let data_ptr = arena_ptr.add(meta.offset);
13199                (meta.drop_fn)(data_ptr);
13200            }
13201        }
13202        // Issue 0790 — the post-teardown half, after the entities are gone.
13203        // Same "already empty after `close()`" note as the pre pass above.
13204        self.run_shutdown_hooks(super::types::ShutdownPhase::Post);
13205        // Issue 1385 — LAST in the body, and that is the whole point: the
13206        // context the backend holds is `wake_ctx`, a field, so it is still
13207        // alive for every line above and is freed only after `drop` returns.
13208        // Clearing here is therefore the SHORTEST window in which a callback
13209        // can fire into live state, not the longest — entity teardown above
13210        // may still be talking to the backend.
13211        //
13212        // A no-op after `close()` (the latch), and a no-op for an executor
13213        // that never installed. For the C path this is the only clear there
13214        // is: `rclc_executor_fini` runs this `drop_in_place` and THEN
13215        // zero-fills the storage the callback pointed into.
13216        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
13217        self.clear_wake_signal();
13218        // phase-467 Row 8 — and the graph-change target, before the box it
13219        // names is freed with this executor.
13220        #[cfg(all(feature = "alloc", feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
13221        self.clear_graph_change_signal();
13222    }
13223}

13225#[cfg(all(test, feature = "std", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
13226mod dispatch_registry_tests {
13227    //! Phase 216 follow-up — `Executor::register_dispatch_slot` +
13228    //! `Executor::dispatch_callback` round-trip.
13229    //!
13230    //! Uses `MockSession` (same pattern as
13231    //! `lifecycle_services::tests::mock_integration`) so the test
13232    //! doesn't need a live RMW backend. Gated `not(feature =
13233    //! "rmw-cffi")` because under `rmw-cffi` the `ConcreteSession`
13234    //! type alias resolves to the cffi session, which `MockSession`
13235    //! can't impersonate.
13236
13237    extern crate alloc;
13238
13239    use super::Executor;
13240    use crate::mock::MockSession;
13241    use std::sync::Mutex;
13242
13243    static CAPTURED: Mutex<alloc::vec::Vec<(usize, alloc::vec::Vec<u8>, usize)>> =
13244        Mutex::new(alloc::vec::Vec::new());
13245
13246    /// Test trampoline matching the per-Node
13247    /// `__nros_node_<pkg>_on_callback` ABI shape (Phase 216.A.5).
13248    unsafe extern "C" fn recording_on_callback(
13249        state: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
13250        cb_id_ptr: *const u8,
13251        cb_id_len: usize,
13252        ctx: *mut core::ffi::c_void,
13253    ) {
13254        // SAFETY: caller (test body below) holds storage live;
13255        // `cb_id_ptr..len` points into a `&str` literal.
13256        let cb_id_bytes = unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(cb_id_ptr, cb_id_len).to_vec() };
13257        let mut guard = CAPTURED.lock().expect("CAPTURED poisoned");
13258        guard.push((state as usize, cb_id_bytes, ctx as usize));
13259    }
13260
13261    #[test]
13262    fn register_dispatch_slot_round_trip() {
13263        let session = MockSession::new();
13264        let mut executor: Executor = Executor::from_session(session);
13265
13266        // Pre-condition: empty registry.
13267        assert_eq!(executor.dispatch_slot_count(), 0);
13268
13269        // Two distinct "states" so we prove every slot gets called
13270        // with its OWN state.
13271        let mut state_blob_a: u32 = 0xABCD_0001;
13272        let mut state_blob_b: u32 = 0xABCD_0002;
13273        let state_a_ptr = &mut state_blob_a as *mut u32 as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
13274        let state_b_ptr = &mut state_blob_b as *mut u32 as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
13275
13276        executor
13277            .register_dispatch_slot(state_a_ptr, recording_on_callback)
13278            .expect("register slot A");
13279        executor
13280            .register_dispatch_slot(state_b_ptr, recording_on_callback)
13281            .expect("register slot B");
13282        assert_eq!(executor.dispatch_slot_count(), 2);
13283
13284        let mut ctx_blob: u32 = 0xFEED_BEEF;
13285        let ctx_ptr = &mut ctx_blob as *mut u32 as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
13286        let cb_id = "/talker/timer/publish";
13287
13288        CAPTURED.lock().expect("CAPTURED poisoned").clear();
13289        executor.dispatch_callback(cb_id, ctx_ptr);
13290
13291        let captured = CAPTURED.lock().expect("CAPTURED poisoned").clone();
13292        assert_eq!(
13293            captured.len(),
13294            2,
13295            "every registered slot must be invoked — linear scan, \
13296             no self-filter at the registry layer"
13297        );
13298        // The carved dispatch table iterates in insertion order.
13299        assert_eq!(captured[0].0, state_a_ptr as usize, "slot A's state");
13300        assert_eq!(captured[1].0, state_b_ptr as usize, "slot B's state");
13301        for (idx, capture) in captured.iter().enumerate() {
13302            assert_eq!(
13303                capture.1.as_slice(),
13304                cb_id.as_bytes(),
13305                "slot {idx} cb_id bytes round-trip"
13306            );
13307            assert_eq!(
13308                capture.2, ctx_ptr as usize,
13309                "slot {idx} ctx pointer round-trip"
13310            );
13311        }
13312    }
13313
13314    #[test]
13315    fn register_dispatch_slot_capacity_full() {
13316        let session = MockSession::new();
13317        let mut executor: Executor = Executor::from_session(session);
13318
13319        let mut state_blob: u32 = 0;
13320        let state_ptr = &mut state_blob as *mut u32 as *mut core::ffi::c_void;
13321
13322        // `MAX_NODES` slots fit; the next one must error.
13323        for _ in 0..crate::config::MAX_NODES {

13329        let overflow = executor.register_dispatch_slot(state_ptr, recording_on_callback);
13330        assert!(
13331            overflow.is_err(),

13333             NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_NODES at build time to grow the registry"

13338/// Phase 274.W1 — borrowed-executor session sharing + active-groups gating.
13339///
13340/// Validates three primitives introduced for RFC-0015 Model 1:
13341/// - `session_handle` / `open_with_session_handle` (Borrowed session store —
13342///   the borrowed executor does not own or close the session on drop).
13343/// - `set_active_groups` + `group_active` (callback-group filter gating).
13344///
13345/// Uses `MockSession` (same pattern as `dispatch_registry_tests`); gated
13346/// `not(feature = "rmw-cffi")` for the same reason.
13347#[cfg(all(test, feature = "std", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
13348mod p274_w1_tier_executor_tests {
13349    use super::Executor;
13350    use crate::mock::MockSession;
13351
13352    #[test]
13353    fn session_handle_borrowed_executor_shares_session_ptr() {
13354        // Open the primary executor (session owner).
13355        let session = MockSession::new();
13356        let mut primary = Executor::from_session(session);
13357
13358        // Record the primary's session pointer for later comparison.
13359        let primary_session_ptr = primary.session_ptr();
13360
13361        // Get the opaque session handle (into_raw for C FFI; here we keep it raw).
13362        let handle = primary.session_handle();
13363
13364        // Open a second executor over the SAME session (Borrowed — does not own it).
13365        // SAFETY: `primary` (the session owner) outlives `borrowed` in this scope.
13366        let mut borrowed = unsafe { Executor::open_with_session_handle(handle) };
13367
13368        // Both executors must expose the same session pointer.
13369        assert_eq!(
13370            primary.session_ptr(),
13371            borrowed.session_ptr(),
13372            "borrowed executor must share the primary's session pointer"
13373        );
13374        assert_eq!(
13375            borrowed.session_ptr(),
13376            primary_session_ptr,
13377            "session pointer must be stable across session_handle / open_with_session_handle"
13378        );
13379
13380        // Drop the borrowed executor — the primary's session must remain valid.
13381        drop(borrowed);
13382
13383        // Primary still exposes the same session pointer (session was NOT closed by drop).
13384        assert_eq!(
13385            primary.session_ptr(),
13386            primary_session_ptr,
13387            "primary session pointer must be unchanged after dropping the borrowed executor"
13388        );
13389    }

13391    /// An oversized group name is REFUSED and fails CLOSED.
13392    ///
13393    /// issue 1172 — this used to be `if s.push_str(g).is_ok()`, which dropped
13394    /// the name and left the tier filtering on a set that silently lacked it.
13395    /// Two things are asserted because either alone would let the bug back:
13396    /// the call must REPORT the failure, and the resulting filter must accept
13397    /// NOTHING rather than fall back to the wildcard, which would be

13399    #[test]
13400    fn an_oversized_group_name_is_refused_and_fails_closed() {
13401        let session = MockSession::new();

13403        let handle = primary.session_handle();
13404        // SAFETY: primary outlives borrowed.
13405        let mut borrowed = unsafe { Executor::open_with_session_handle(handle) };
13406
13407        // `GroupName` is `heapless::String<32>`.
13408        let too_long = "g".repeat(33);
13409        assert!(
13410            borrowed
13411                .set_active_groups(&[("n", "/", too_long.as_str())])
13412                .is_err(),
13413            "an oversized group name must be reported, not dropped"
13414        );
13415        assert!(
13416            !borrowed.group_active("n", "/", &too_long),
13417            "the name that did not fit must not be active"
13418        );
13419        assert!(
13420            !borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "anything-else"),
13421            "a refused filter must accept NOTHING — falling back to the \
13422             wildcard would run every callback on this tier"
13423        );

13426    #[test]
13427    fn set_active_groups_gates_group_active() {
13428        let session = MockSession::new();
13429        let mut primary = Executor::from_session(session);
13430        let handle = primary.session_handle();
13431
13432        // SAFETY: primary outlives borrowed.
13433        let mut borrowed = unsafe { Executor::open_with_session_handle(handle) };
13434
13435        // Before gating: wildcard — every group is accepted.
13436        assert!(
13437            borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "ctrl"),
13438            "default (wildcard) must accept every group"
13439        );
13440        assert!(
13441            borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "telem"),
13442            "default (wildcard) must accept every group"
13443        );

13445        // Gate borrowed to only the "ctrl" group (one-tier filter).
13446        borrowed
13447            .set_active_groups(&[("n", "/", "ctrl")])
13448            .expect("fits");
13449
13450        assert!(
13451            borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "ctrl"),
13452            "\"ctrl\" must be active after set_active_groups([\"ctrl\"])"
13453        );
13454        assert!(
13455            !borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "telem"),
13456            "\"telem\" must NOT be active when only \"ctrl\" is gated"
13457        );
13458        assert!(
13459            !borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "planning"),
13460            "\"planning\" must NOT be active when only \"ctrl\" is gated"
13461        );
13462
13463        // Primary is unaffected (it still uses the wildcard).
13464        assert!(
13465            primary.group_active("n", "/", "telem"),
13466            "primary executor must remain unaffected (still wildcard)"
13467        );
13468
13469        // Clear the filter on borrowed — back to wildcard.
13470        borrowed
13471            .set_active_groups(&[])
13472            .expect("the wildcard always fits");
13473        assert!(
13474            borrowed.group_active("n", "/", "telem"),
13475            "after clearing, borrowed must accept all groups again"
13476        );
13477    }
