13504/// W3b.5 — snapshot the monitored publishers' counters before a dispatch
13505/// (only when a latency contract exists; otherwise a zeroed array that
13506/// `attribute_latency` never reads).
13507fn snapshot_pub_counts(
13508    table: &'static [super::monitor::MonitorSpec],
13509    active: bool,
13510) -> [u32; super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS] {
13511    let mut counts = [0u32; super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS];
13512    if active {
13513        for (k, spec) in table.iter().take(super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS).enumerate() {
13514            counts[k] = spec.cell.count.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
13515        }
13516    }
13517    counts
13518}
13519
13520/// W3b.5 — attribute one dispatch's elapsed time to every monitored
13521/// publisher whose counter advanced during it (an upper bound on the
13522/// node-path take → publish latency: the callback deserialized, ran, and
13523/// published within `elapsed_us`).
13524fn attribute_latency(
13525    table: &'static [super::monitor::MonitorSpec],
13526    active: bool,
13527    counts_before: &[u32; super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS],
13528    elapsed_us: u32,
13529) {
13530    if !active {
13531        return;
13532    }
13533    for (k, spec) in table.iter().take(super::monitor::MAX_MONITORS).enumerate() {
13534        if spec.max_latency_ms == 0 {
13535            continue;
13536        }
13537        let now = spec.cell.count.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
13538        if now != counts_before[k] {
13539            spec.cell
13540                .max_latency_us
13541                .fetch_max(elapsed_us, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
13542        }
13543    }
13544}
13545
13546/// W3b.5 — enforce the bound SC's deadline after a dispatch. A miss maps
13547/// through [`DeadlineAction`](super::sched_context::DeadlineAction):
13548/// `Warn`/`Skip`/`Fault` all report; `Skip` additionally masks the SC's
13549/// remaining callbacks for this cycle; `Fault` invokes the fault hook
13550/// (panic when none is registered).
13551fn check_deadline_miss(
13552    sc: Option<&super::sched_context::SchedContext>,
13553    sc_idx: usize,
13554    elapsed_us: u32,
13555    misses: &mut heapless::Vec<super::monitor::Violation, { super::monitor::MAX_VIOLATIONS }>,
13556    skipped_scs: &mut u64,
13557    fault_fn: Option<fn(&super::monitor::Violation)>,
13558) {
13559    use super::sched_context::DeadlineAction;
13560    let Some(sc) = sc else { return };
13561    let Some(deadline_us) = sc.deadline_us.get().map(|nz| nz.get()) else {
13562        return;
13563    };
13564    if matches!(sc.deadline_action, DeadlineAction::Ignore) || elapsed_us <= deadline_us {
13565        return;
13566    }
13567    let v = super::monitor::Violation {
13568        rule: "deadline-miss-runtime",
13569        // Entries carry no name at this altitude; the SC slot stands in.
13570        fqn: "sched-context",
13571        measured: elapsed_us,
13572        declared: deadline_us,
13573    };
13574    match sc.deadline_action {
13575        DeadlineAction::Ignore => {}
13576        DeadlineAction::Warn => {
13577            let _ = misses.push(v);
13578        }
13579        DeadlineAction::Skip => {
13580            if sc_idx < 64 {
13581                *skipped_scs |= 1u64 << sc_idx;
13582            }
13583            let _ = misses.push(v);
13584        }
13585        DeadlineAction::Fault => {
13586            if let Some(f) = fault_fn {
13587                f(&v);
13588                let _ = misses.push(v);
13589            } else {
13590                panic!(
13591                    "nros: deadline fault — dispatch ran {elapsed_us} us past a {deadline_us} us deadline"
13592                );
13593            }
13594        }
13595    }
13596}
13597
13598// Timer-accounting clock default (issue: no_std tiers with no `clock_us`
13599// credited each spin the REQUESTED timeout — spin.rs `delta_us` fallback —
13600// so shared-session wakes made low-rate timers fire early (a 100 ms timer
13601// at ~67 ms on Zephyr native_sim) and tick rounding made fast tiers fire
13602// late. Measured on that native_sim image; mechanism documented at the
13603// fallback site.)
13604//
13605// Every platform port exports `nros_platform_clock_ns` through the same
13606// linkage contract the wake primitives rely on (`nros_platform_export_clock!`
13607// in nros-platform-cffi), so an rmw-cffi no_std build can safely default the
13608// executor clock to it; `ExecutorConfig::clock_us` stays as an override.
13609#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
13610unsafe extern "C" {
13611    fn nros_platform_clock_ns() -> u64;
13612}
13613
13614#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
13615fn default_platform_clock_us() -> u64 {
13616    // SAFETY: bare query of the platform's monotonic ns counter; the symbol
13617    // is guaranteed by whichever platform port linked the binary (the same
13618    // contract `nros_platform_wake_*` already depends on).
13619    //
13620    // RFC-0073 made the ABI nanoseconds; the executor's own accounting is
13621    // still microseconds (`clock_us_fn`, `delta_us`), so the division lives
13622    // here rather than being pushed into every port.
13623    unsafe { nros_platform_clock_ns() / 1_000 }
13624}
13625
13626/// Sleep, through the platform ABI.
13627///
13628/// phase-359 W10 — the spin loops used `std::thread::sleep`. Every port already
13629/// exports `nros_platform_sleep_us` (the ABI's own pacing primitive, the one an
13630/// RTOS build has always used), so a hosted loop and an embedded one now pace
13631/// the same way. The µs entry point is used rather than `_ms` because
13632/// `spin_one_period_timed` sleeps off a remainder, which rounds badly at
13633/// millisecond granularity on short periods.
13634#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
13635pub(crate) fn platform_sleep(d: core::time::Duration) {
13636    unsafe extern "C" {
13637        fn nros_platform_sleep_us(us: usize);
13638    }
13639    let us = d.as_micros().min(usize::MAX as u128) as usize;
13640    if us == 0 {
13641        return;
13642    }
13643    // SAFETY: a bare pacing call with no pointer arguments, guaranteed by
13644    // whichever port linked the binary — the same contract the clock and wake
13645    // symbols in this file already rely on.
13646    unsafe { nros_platform_sleep_us(us) }
13647}
13648
13649/// A monotonic µs reader, or `None` when this build has no clock at all.
13650///
13651/// phase-359 W10 — one provider, chosen by what is LINKED rather than by which
13652/// flavour the crate was built in. W4 unified the executor's clock ACCESSOR and
13653/// said the provider was the last piece; this is it.
13654///
13655/// `rmw-cffi` means a platform port is linked, and every port exports
13656/// `nros_platform_clock_ns` under the same contract the wake primitives use —
13657/// so a hosted build reads the same counter an embedded one does, instead of
13658/// `Instant` on one and the platform on the other. `Instant` survives only
13659/// where there is no port to ask: `std` without `rmw-cffi`.
13660///
13661/// phase-359 W10 follow-up — this comment claimed the metadata PROBE was that
13662/// configuration, and **it is not**. The probe's generated manifest deps
13663/// `nros-platform-cffi` with `posix-c-port` (issue 0288 layer 5, so it links),
13664/// and its `nros` resolves with `rmw-cffi` ON — feature-unified from the
13665/// component's board crate. Measured on a real probe tree: `alloc default
13666/// macros rmw-cffi ros-humble std`. It takes the PORT arm.
13667///
13668/// What is real: `nros-rmw-metadata` and `nros-tests` do resolve `nros` with
13669/// `std` and no `rmw-cffi`, and have no port crate in their graphs. But nothing
13670/// in either uses this arm — deleting it and building the workspace
13671/// `--all-targets` is clean, and there is no in-tree caller of
13672/// `nros::time::now` at all. So the arm serves an OUT-OF-TREE contract only: a
13673/// consumer with `std`, no `rmw-cffi`, and its own `Session`.
13674pub(crate) fn default_clock_us_fn() -> Option<fn() -> u64> {
13675    #[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]
13676    {
13677        Some(default_platform_clock_us)
13678    }
13679    #[cfg(not(feature = "rmw-cffi"))]
13680    {
13681        None
13682    }
13683}
13684
13685// =============================================================================
13686// phase-425 W3b — the `/clock` time source's executor half.
13687//
13688// Its OWN impl block, gated on `sim-time`, because the methods were first
13689// written next to `declare_parameter` — which lives in a
13690// `#[cfg(feature = "param-services")]` block, so `reconcile_ros_time_source`
13691// silently disappeared in every combo without parameter services, including the
13692// one `spin_once` calls it from.
13693// =============================================================================
13694#[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
13695impl<'s> Executor<'s> {
13696    /// phase-425 W3b — bring the `/clock` subscription in line with the last
13697    /// requested `use_sim_time`.
13698    ///
13699    /// Called at the head of every spin, and cheap when there is nothing to do:
13700    /// the common case is one bool comparison. It is a RECONCILE rather than an
13701    /// action at the request site because the request routinely arrives before
13702    /// there is a node to hang the subscription on — `nros::main!` emits
13703    /// `apply_param_services` before its per-node `register` calls, by design,
13704    /// so the store exists when each cell is created.
13705    ///
13706    /// Turning it off stops SAMPLES from being installed; the subscription
13707    /// itself stays, because the executor has no entity removal and inventing
13708    /// one for this would be a much larger change than the switch is worth. The
13709    /// gate is `time_source::set_active`, which the subscription callback reads.
13710    ///
13711    /// Turning it off also does NOT clear the override: a node that stops
13712    /// listening keeps the last simulated time rather than jumping back to the
13713    /// wall clock, which every ROS-time timer would otherwise absorb as a
13714    /// backwards jump.
13715    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
13716    pub(crate) fn reconcile_ros_time_source(&mut self) {
13717        // An executor nobody told about `use_sim_time` has NO opinion, and the
13718        // gate is process-global, so writing its default here is not a no-op --
13719        // it is one executor overruling another. Say nothing until asked.
13720        if !self.sim_time_stated {
13721            return;
13722        }
13723        if self.sim_time_requested == crate::time_source::is_active()
13724            && (!self.sim_time_requested || self.sim_time_source.is_some())
13725        {
13726            return;
13727        }
13728        crate::time_source::set_active(self.sim_time_requested);
13729        if !self.sim_time_requested {
13730            // phase-430 W1 — the source is no longer wanted, so its silence is
13731            // no longer a symptom. Disarming here (rather than only re-arming
13732            // on attach) is what makes a later re-attach start a FRESH
13733            // interval: the watch that was counting is put down, not paused.
13734            self.sim_time_silence.disarm();
13735            return;
13736        }
13737        if self.sim_time_source.is_none() {
13738            // No node yet — stay pending and try again next spin. Not an error:
13739            // it is the ordinary order of a generated entry, which declares
13740            // parameters before it registers components.
13741            if self.nodes.is_empty() {
13742                return;
13743            }
13744            if let Ok(handle) = self.install_ros_time_source(
13745                super::node_record::NodeId::PRIMARY,
13746                crate::time_source::CLOCK_TOPIC,
13747            ) {
13748                self.sim_time_source = Some(handle);
13749                // phase-430 W1 — the interval starts HERE, at attach, and not
13750                // at construction: before the subscription exists there is
13751                // nothing to be silent about, so counting from boot would
13752                // accuse an image that spent the interval bringing a transport
13753                // up.
13754                self.sim_time_silence.arm();
13755            }
13756        } else {
13757            // Re-attached: `use_sim_time` went false and back to true while the
13758            // subscription (which the executor cannot remove) stayed. W1 asks
13759            // for the one-shot to reset in exactly this case.
13760            self.sim_time_silence.arm();
13761        }
13762    }
13763
13764    /// phase-430 W1 — credit one spin's elapsed time to the silence watch and
13765    /// emit the diagnostic if this is the spin that crosses the threshold.
13766    ///
13767    /// `delta_us` is the executor's OWN per-spin elapsed measure — the same one
13768    /// every wall timer on this executor accumulates, including its "no clock,
13769    /// credit the requested timeout" fallback. See
13770    /// [`SILENCE_WARN_US`](crate::time_source::SILENCE_WARN_US) for why that is
13771    /// the unit and not a spin count or an independent wall clock.
13772    ///
13773    /// Scope: the source the EXECUTOR installed for `use_sim_time`. An
13774    /// application that calls
13775    /// [`Node::install_ros_time_source`](super::node::Node::install_ros_time_source)
13776    /// directly is not watched, because the line this would print names
13777    /// `use_sim_time`, and that application never set it — the honest
13778    /// diagnostic for the explicit path would be a different sentence, and
13779    /// inventing one nobody asked for is how a warning becomes noise.
13780    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
13781    fn note_sim_time_silence(&mut self, delta_us: u64) {
13782        if self.sim_time_silence.tick(
13783            delta_us,
13784            nros_core::clock::Clock::is_ros_time_override_active(),
13785        ) {
13786            crate::time_source::report_silence(crate::time_source::CLOCK_TOPIC);
13787        }
13788    }
13789
13790    /// phase-430 W1 — how many times this executor has reported that
13791    /// `use_sim_time` is on with no `/clock` sample.
13792    ///
13793    /// The count rather than a bool, and an accessor rather than a log grep: a
13794    /// diagnostic whose contract is "exactly once" needs an assertion that can
13795    /// tell one from two, and a log sink is not present on every target that
13796    /// runs the test. It is also the question an application supervising its
13797    /// own configuration would ask.
13798    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
13799    pub fn sim_time_silence_warnings(&self) -> u32 {
13800        self.sim_time_silence.reports()
13801    }
13802
13803    /// phase-425 W3b — re-read `use_sim_time` from the parameter store.
13804    ///
13805    /// Called after a parameter service actually handled something, which is
13806    /// what makes a runtime `ros2 param set <node> use_sim_time true` work
13807    /// without a per-spin scan of the store.
13808    ///
13809    /// phase-430 W3 / issue 1202 — the declaration path calls it too, through
13810    /// `note_reserved_parameter`, once the store has accepted the write. It
13811    /// used to record the value directly from the caller's argument, which is
13812    /// the same thing only while the store never refuses. One read for both
13813    /// paths; a second spelling is the drift this function exists to prevent.
13814    /// `pub(crate)` for the same reason: a test that changes the store directly
13815    /// needs the entry point a parameter service uses, not a copy of it.
13816    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", feature = "param-services", any(has_rmw, test)))]
13817    pub(crate) fn refresh_use_sim_time_from_store(&mut self) {
13818        // phase-426 W1 — the store is keyed by NODE, and the simulated clock is
13819        // not. This function is where those two facts meet, so the rule is
13820        // stated here rather than left to whichever call site got there first.
13821        //
13822        // `use_sim_time` is a per-node parameter in ROS 2, and rclcpp means it:
13823        // every `Node` builds its own `TimeSource` over its own `Clock`, so two
13824        // nodes composed into one process CAN be configured differently and
13825        // stamp messages from different clocks at the same instant. This tree
13826        // deliberately does not follow that (phase-425): "the override is
13827        // process-global — one simulated clock per image, the model
13828        // `nros_core::Clock` already documents — so there is nothing to attach
13829        // to and nothing to fan out." That is the right trade for an image with
13830        // a fixed RAM budget, and it makes "whose `use_sim_time`?" a question
13831        // rclcpp never has to answer and this executor now does.
13832        //
13833        // ANY node asking arms the one source. Two reasons, and the second is
13834        // the binding one:
13835        //
13836        //   * it is the only rule the CALLERS can implement. `note_param_
13837        //     services_ran` fires after a runtime `ros2 param set` and knows
13838        //     only that N requests were handled — not which node was written.
13839        //     A last-writer-wins rule would need a writer identity that does
13840        //     not reach here, so it would silently degrade to "whatever node 0
13841        //     says", which is the default-to-primary bug phase-426 W1 exists to
13842        //     remove.
13843        //   * one node still wanting simulated time is a reason to keep the
13844        //     source attached, and detaching is the destructive direction:
13845        //     phase-425 already records that turning it off "stops SAMPLES, not
13846        //     the subscription", precisely so a mid-run change does not read as
13847        //     a clock jump.
13848        //
13849        // The scan is over the executor's own node table, which is the same
13850        // `u8` index space `NodeKey` wraps, so there is one node identity here
13851        // and not two.
13852        let Some(params) = self.params.as_ref() else {
13853            return;
13854        };
13855        let mut stated = false;
13856        let mut enable = false;
13857        // A `NodeId` IS the index into this table (`NodeId::index`), so the
13858        // enumeration is the key space — no second derivation of the number.
13859        //
13860        // `.max(1)` because `NodeId::PRIMARY` is IMPLICIT: the executor's node
13861        // table starts empty and a parameter can be declared on the primary
13862        // node before any `create_node` puts a record in it. Scanning only the
13863        // table would then find nothing and leave `sim_time_stated` false, so a
13864        // `use_sim_time` declared before the first node would never arm the
13865        // source — which `use_sim_time_attaches_and_detaches_the_clock_source`
13866        // catches, since its whole first half runs while "there is still no
13867        // node". Slot 0 is always a legitimate key; at worst the lookup misses.
13868        for idx in 0..self.nodes.len().max(1) {
13869            let key = nros_params::NodeKey::new(idx as u8);
13870            if let Some(v) = params
13871                .server
13872                .get_bool(key, crate::time_source::USE_SIM_TIME_PARAM)
13873            {
13874                stated = true;
13875                enable |= v;
13876            }
13877        }
13878        if stated {
13879            self.sim_time_requested = enable;
13880            self.sim_time_stated = true;
13881        }
13882    }
13883
13884    /// phase-425 W3b — the installed `/clock` subscription, if any.
13885    ///
13886    /// The HANDLE rather than a bool, because "did we subscribe twice" is the
13887    /// question a reconciliation loop has to be able to answer: a second
13888    /// registration takes a new slot, so a stable handle across spins is the
13889    /// evidence that the loop is idempotent.
13890    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
13891    pub fn ros_time_source_handle(&self) -> Option<HandleId> {
13892        self.sim_time_source
13893    }
13894
13895    /// phase-425 W3b — whether a `/clock` subscription is currently installed.
13896    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
13897    pub fn ros_time_source_installed(&self) -> bool {
13898        self.sim_time_source.is_some()
13899    }
13900
13901    /// phase-425 W3 — subscribe `topic` and install every sample as this
13902    /// image's ROS time. The registration behind
13903    /// [`Node::install_ros_time_source`](super::node::Node::install_ros_time_source)
13904    /// and behind the `use_sim_time` reconciliation, so both spell the QoS and
13905    /// the conversion exactly once.
13906    #[cfg(all(feature = "sim-time", any(has_rmw, test)))]
13907    pub(crate) fn install_ros_time_source(
13908        &mut self,
13909        node_id: super::node_record::NodeId,
13910        topic: &str,
13911    ) -> Result<HandleId, NodeError> {
13912        self.register_subscription_buffered_on::<
13913            nros_rosgraph_msgs::msg::Clock,
13914            _,
13915            { crate::config::DEFAULT_RX_BUF_SIZE },
13916        >(
13917            node_id,
13918            topic,
13919            QoSProfile::clock_default(),
13920            |msg: &nros_rosgraph_msgs::msg::Clock| {
13921                // The `use_sim_time` gate is read HERE rather than by removing
13922                // the subscription, because there is no entity removal. An
13923                // image that never touches `use_sim_time` and installs the
13924                // source explicitly is active by default.
13925                if !crate::time_source::is_active() {
13926                    return;
13927                }
13928                if let Some(nanos) =
13929                    crate::time_source::override_nanos(msg.clock.sec, msg.clock.nanosec)
13930                {
13931                    nros_core::clock::Clock::set_ros_time_override(nanos);
13932                }
13933            },
13934            None, // no group — node default
13935            None, // the configured default RX buffer, unchanged
13936        )
13937    }
13938}
13939
13940// ============================================================================
13941// phase-417 W4.c — cancel / is_spinning
13942// ============================================================================
13943//
13944// Same gate as `executor::tests`, exactly: `ConcreteSession` is `MockSession`
13945// only while no rmw-* feature is unified in (see `executor/mod.rs`), and
13946// `from_session_with` / `halt_flag` are `alloc`. No `std` gate — `cfg(test)`
13947// already means a hosted harness, which is why `lib.rs` brings `std` in under
13948// `test` as well. (It said "exactly" while missing `alloc`, and `std` was not in
13949// scope: 20 errors, hidden by feature unification under `--workspace`.)
13950#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc", not(feature = "rmw-cffi")))]
13951mod cancel_tests {
13952    use super::Executor;
13953    use crate::{executor::types::ExecutorConfig, mock::MockSession};
13954
13955    /// The core has no default clock and says so (issue 0709), so a test that
13956    /// measures elapsed time brings its own — the same seam a board uses.
13957    fn test_clock_us() -> u64 {
13958        use std::{sync::OnceLock, time::Instant};
13959        static EPOCH: OnceLock<Instant> = OnceLock::new();
13960        EPOCH.get_or_init(Instant::now).elapsed().as_micros() as u64
13961    }
13962
13963    fn executor() -> Executor<'static> {
13964        let cfg = ExecutorConfig::default().clock_us(test_clock_us);
13965        Executor::from_session_with(MockSession::new(), &cfg)
13966    }
13967
13968    /// A fresh executor is neither cancelled nor spinning — the two questions
13969    /// are independent, and this is the state where both answers are `false`.
13970    #[test]
13971    fn a_fresh_executor_is_neither_cancelled_nor_spinning() {
13972        let exec = executor();
13973        assert!(!exec.is_halted(), "nothing has asked it to stop");
13974        assert!(!exec.is_spinning(), "no spin loop is running");
13975    }
13976
13977    /// `cancel()` raises the request bit without starting or stopping anything.
13978    #[test]
13979    fn cancel_requests_without_spinning() {
13980        let exec = executor();
13981        exec.cancel();
13982        assert!(exec.is_halted(), "cancel() must be observable immediately");
13983        assert!(
13984            !exec.is_spinning(),
13985            "cancel() must not make a non-spinning executor claim to spin"
13986        );
13987    }
13988
13989    /// The load-bearing one: `cancel()` from a peer thread TERMINATES a running
13990    /// `spin`, `is_spinning()` is true while the loop runs, and false
13991    /// once it has returned.
13992    ///
13993    /// The peer asserts `is_spinning()` from OUTSIDE the spinning thread, which
13994    /// is the whole point of the observable — it is what a signal handler or a
13995    /// supervisor sees.
13996    #[test]
13997    fn cancel_terminates_a_spin_and_is_spinning_tracks_it() {
13998        use std::{
13999            sync::{
14000                Arc,
14001                atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
14002            },
14003            thread,
14004            time::{Duration, Instant},
14005        };
14006
14007        let mut exec = executor();
14008        assert!(!exec.is_spinning());
14009
14010        // `Executor` is not `Sync`, so the peer thread cannot hold a reference
14011        // to it. It observes and drives through the two flag handles instead —
14012        // which is the supported cross-thread surface (`halt_flag()`), and
14013        // keeps this test on the same seam a signal handler uses.
14014        let cancel_bit = exec.halt_flag();
14015        let saw_spinning = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
14016        let saw_spinning_peer = Arc::clone(&saw_spinning);
14017
14018        let peer = thread::spawn(move || {
14019            // Give the loop time to enter. Bounded, and the assertion below is
14020            // on what was OBSERVED, so a slow host cannot turn this green by
14021            // accident — it fails instead.
14022            thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
14023            saw_spinning_peer.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
14024            cancel_bit.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
14025        });
14026
14027        let started = Instant::now();
14028        exec.spin(crate::executor::types::SpinOptions::default())
14029            .expect("an untimed spin runs until cancelled");
14030        let elapsed = started.elapsed();
14031
14032        peer.join().expect("peer thread must not panic");
14033
14034        assert!(
14035            saw_spinning.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
14036            "the peer must have run before spin returned"
14037        );
14038        assert!(
14039            !exec.is_spinning(),
14040            "is_spinning() must be false once the loop has returned"
14041        );
14042        assert!(
14043            exec.is_halted(),
14044            "the cancel request survives the loop it ended"
14045        );
14046        // LOWER bound too: a spin that never waited would prove nothing about
14047        // termination. The peer sleeps 50 ms before cancelling.
14048        assert!(
14049            elapsed >= Duration::from_millis(40),
14050            "spin returned in {elapsed:?} — it cannot have spun"
14051        );
14052        // ...and an UPPER bound, because "terminated" is the claim: without the
14053        // cancel check this loop never returns and the test would hang rather
14054        // than fail. 10 s is far past any scheduling noise.
14055        assert!(
14056            elapsed < Duration::from_secs(10),
14057            "spin took {elapsed:?} to observe the cancel"
14058        );
14059    }
14060
14061    /// `is_spinning()` is true from INSIDE the loop. Read from a timer callback,
14062    /// which is the only place the executor is genuinely mid-spin, and asserted
14063    /// after the loop so a callback that never fired cannot pass silently.
14064    #[test]
14065    fn is_spinning_is_true_inside_the_loop() {
14066        use std::time::Duration;
14067
14068        let mut exec = executor();
14069        // `only_next` runs exactly one iteration, so this is a single poll
14070        // inside a spin scope — bounded, no thread, no clock dependency beyond
14071        // the one the fixture installs.
14072        assert!(!exec.is_spinning());
14073        exec.spin(crate::executor::types::SpinOptions::spin_once())
14074            .expect("a single-iteration spin must succeed");
14075        assert!(
14076            !exec.is_spinning(),
14077            "the scope must close when the loop returns"
14078        );
14079
14080        // The inside-the-loop reading needs a second thread to do it, because
14081        // the spinning thread is blocked in the loop and `Executor` is `!Sync`
14082        // so no `&Executor` may cross. What crosses is a pointer to the one
14083        // atomic, which is the same thing the C and C++ APIs hold: they observe
14084        // `is_spinning` through a raw executor handle, and that is the case this
14085        // flag exists to serve.
14086        struct FlagPtr(*const portable_atomic::AtomicBool);
14087        // SAFETY: the pointee is an `AtomicBool`, which is `Sync`; the only
14088        // operation performed through it is a relaxed-or-stronger load. The
14089        // executor outlives the thread — `peer.join()` below happens before
14090        // `exec` is dropped at the end of the test.
14091        unsafe impl Send for FlagPtr {}
14092
14093        let cancel_bit = exec.halt_flag();
14094        let observed = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
14095        let spinning_bit_seen = std::sync::Arc::clone(&observed);
14096        let flag = FlagPtr(&exec.spinning as *const portable_atomic::AtomicBool);
14097        let peer = std::thread::spawn(move || {
14098            let flag = flag;
14099            for _ in 0..500 {
14100                // SAFETY: see the `unsafe impl Send` above.
14101                if unsafe { &*flag.0 }.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {
14102                    spinning_bit_seen.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
14103                    break;
14104                }
14105                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2));
14106            }
14107            cancel_bit.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
14108        });
14109
14110        exec.spin(crate::executor::types::SpinOptions::default())
14111            .expect("an untimed spin runs until cancelled");
14112        peer.join().expect("peer thread must not panic");
14113
14114        assert!(
14115            observed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst),
14116            "is_spinning() must read true while spin is running"
14117        );
14118    }
14119
14120    /// `spin_period` maintains the same scope, and a period this build cannot
14121    /// pace is an error that must NOT leave the executor claiming to spin.
14122    #[test]
14123    fn spin_period_with_no_clock_leaves_is_spinning_false() {
14124        let mut exec = executor();
14125        exec.clock_us_fn = None;
14126        let err = exec
14127            .spin_period(core::time::Duration::from_millis(10))
14128            .expect_err("a period with no clock must fail (issue 0709)");
14129        assert_eq!(err, crate::NodeError::NotInitialized);
14130        assert!(
14131            !exec.is_spinning(),
14132            "a spin that never started must not report that it did"
14133        );
14134    }
14135
14136    /// Entering a spin CLEARS a stale cancel: a cancel requested before this
14137    /// spin is not a cancel of this spin. Documents the ADOPT-BOUNDED envelope's
14138    /// one sharp edge.
14139    #[test]
14140    fn entering_a_spin_clears_a_stale_cancel() {
14141        let exec = executor();
14142        exec.cancel();
14143        assert!(exec.is_halted());
14144        exec.enter_spin_loop();
14145        assert!(
14146            !exec.is_halted(),
14147            "a cancel raised before the loop started must not end it instantly"
14148        );
14149        assert!(exec.is_spinning());
14150        exec.exit_spin_loop();
14151        assert!(!exec.is_spinning());
14152    }
14153}
